children.title: Classical Planning Regimes
children.top_down_role: Deterministic finite-state planning under propositional or finite-domain representations.

assumptions_latex: The fluent set \(F\) and action set \(A\) are finite.
Actions are deterministic and fully observable.
The initial state is complete and the goal is propositional.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A plan exists exactly when some finite applicable action sequence reaches a state satisfying \(G\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic, fully observable, finite-state classical planning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A classical planning instance is a tuple \(P=(F,A,s_0,G)\), where a state is a subset \(s\subseteq F\). Each action \(a\in A\) has precondition \(\operatorname{pre}(a)\subseteq F\), add effects \(\operatorname{add}(a)\subseteq F\), and delete effects \(\operatorname{del}(a)\subseteq F\). It is applicable in \(s\) when \(\operatorname{pre}(a)\subseteq s\), producing \(\gamma(s,a)=(s\setminus\operatorname{del}(a))\cup\operatorname{add}(a)\). A plan is a finite sequence \(\pi=(a_1,\ldots,a_n)\) whose successive actions are applicable from \(s_0\) and whose terminal state \(s_n\) satisfies \(G\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Classical planning asks for a finite sequence of deterministic actions that is applicable from a complete initial state and reaches a propositional goal.
knowledge_statements.title: Classical Planning Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and selected content kind fit the deterministic finite-state classical-planning container, but no source is cited. The precise STRIPS-style tuple, transition semantics, and treatment of the propositional goal require an authoritative planning reference with a specific definition or section locator.

children.title: Metric-Temporal Planning Regimes
children.top_down_role: Planning with durations, concurrency, metric change, and numeric state.

children.title: Temporal Planning Regimes
children.top_down_role: Planning regimes centered on action duration, concurrency, temporal placement, or deadlines.

assumptions_latex: Every action occurrence has a nonnegative start time and positive duration.
Temporal conditions and effects have explicitly specified endpoint or interval scope.
Simultaneous happenings obey a fixed noninterference convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A temporal plan is valid precisely when all timed conditions, effects, and concurrency restrictions hold on its induced trajectory.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Durative deterministic planning with point and interval conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A temporal planning instance extends finite-state planning by assigning each action occurrence \(i\) a start time \(t_i\geq 0\) and duration \(d_i>0\). Conditions may be required at \(t_i\), throughout \([t_i,t_i+d_i]\), or at \(t_i+d_i\); effects occur at declared endpoints. A temporal plan \(\Pi=\{(a_i,t_i,d_i)\\}_{i=1}^n\) is valid when every condition holds at its prescribed times on the induced trajectory \(s(t)\), all simultaneous effects are mutually compatible under the chosen concurrency semantics, and the goal holds after \(T=\max_i(t_i+d_i)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Temporal planning schedules durative action occurrences so that endpoint and interval conditions, concurrent effects, and the final goal are all satisfied.
knowledge_statements.title: Temporal Planning Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the temporal-planning regime container, but validity depends on a particular concurrency and endpoint semantics that is not sourced. In addition, the set expression for the plan contains a malformed `\\` sequence before the closing brace. A specific authoritative temporal-planning semantics and locator are required before the mathematical record can be reliably revised.

children.title: Numeric Planning Regimes
children.top_down_role: Planning regimes centered on numeric state, metric change, or quantitative conditions.

assumptions_latex: The propositional and numeric state dimensions are finite.
Every numeric expression has a defined value whenever it is evaluated.
Action effects are deterministic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A numeric plan is valid exactly when every transition is defined and its terminal mixed state satisfies the goal.

notation.meaning: Boolean and numeric components of a state
Guard and deterministic update of an action

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic planning with finite Boolean state and real-valued variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A numeric planning instance has states \(s=(b,x)\in\{0,1\}^m\times\mathbb{R}^q\). Each action \(a\) has a guard \(g_a(b,x)\) and a deterministic partial update \(U_a\) of Boolean and numeric components. The action is applicable at \(s\) when \(g_a(s)\) is true and every expression in \(U_a(s)\) is defined; its successor is \(U_a(s)\). A numeric plan is a finite sequence \(\pi=(a_1,\ldots,a_n)\) generating defined states \(s_i=U_{a_i}(s_{i-1})\) from the given \(s_0\), with terminal state \(s_n\) satisfying the mixed Boolean-numeric goal predicate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Numeric planning augments Boolean states with real variables and seeks a sequence of guarded, deterministic updates reaching a mixed Boolean-numeric goal.
knowledge_statements.title: Numeric Planning Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and content kind fit the numeric-planning container, but the very general guard-and-partial-update semantics is unsupported by a citation. An authoritative source must establish the intended numeric-planning formalism, expression language, and update semantics.

children.title: Integrated Metric-Temporal Regimes
children.top_down_role: Planning settings where temporal commitments interact with evolving numeric quantities.

assumptions_latex: All action durations, numeric guards, updates, and rates are explicitly defined.
The chosen semantics uniquely determines the trajectory between event times.
Concurrent discrete updates satisfy a fixed compatibility rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Validity requires both temporal consistency and satisfaction of every discrete and continuous numeric constraint along the induced trajectory.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint temporal-numeric planning, including discrete updates and continuous evolution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An integrated metric-temporal planning instance induces a trajectory \((b(t),x(t))\in\{0,1\}^m\times\mathbb{R}^q\) from scheduled durative actions. Each occurrence may impose Boolean or numeric conditions at its endpoints or over its open interval, apply discrete endpoint updates, and prescribe continuous evolution such as \(\dot{x}(t)=f_a(b(t),x(t))\) while active. A schedule \(\Pi\) is valid when its event ordering is temporally consistent, all endpoint conditions and interval invariants hold, simultaneous updates are compatible, every continuous segment satisfies the active evolution laws, and the terminal trajectory value satisfies \(G\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Integrated metric-temporal planning schedules actions whose Boolean and numeric conditions, discrete effects, and continuous evolution must jointly satisfy the goal.
knowledge_statements.title: Integrated Metric-Temporal Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the integrated metric-temporal container, but the statement blends durative actions, discrete numeric updates, and general continuous dynamics without identifying the governing semantics. A specific authoritative source is needed to determine sufficient conditions for trajectory existence, uniqueness, concurrency, and invariant satisfaction.

children.title: Resource-Aware Planning Regimes
children.top_down_role: Planning with reusable, consumable, produced, or capacity-limited resources.

assumptions_latex: The resource set and planning horizon are finite.
Each resource has a specified initial stock or time-dependent capacity.
Every action occurrence has a defined resource profile.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A plan is resource-feasible exactly when its aggregate demand and stock trajectories satisfy all resource constraints throughout execution.

notation.meaning: Capacity of renewable resource r at time t
Stock of consumable or produced resource

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Planning with renewable capacities and consumable or produced stocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A resource-aware planning instance associates every scheduled action occurrence with resource-use profiles. For each renewable resource \(r\), feasibility requires aggregate demand \(D_r(t)=\sum_i d_{ir}(t)\) to satisfy \(0\leq D_r(t)\leq C_r(t)\) for every time \(t\). For each consumable or produced resource, the stock trajectory is \(z_r(t)=z_r(0)+P_r(t)-Q_r(t)\), where \(P_r(t)\) and \(Q_r(t)\) are cumulative production and consumption, and feasibility requires \(0\leq z_r(t)\leq C_r(t)\). A resource-feasible plan must additionally satisfy all ordinary action and goal constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Resource-aware planning requires every plan to respect renewable capacities and keep consumable or produced resource stocks within bounds at all times.
knowledge_statements.title: Resource-Aware Planning Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the resource-aware planning container and distinguishes renewable demand from consumable or produced stock. However, no planning source supports the continuous-time profiles, cumulative-flow equations, capacity bounds, or their relationship to ordinary plan validity.

children.title: Preference-Sensitive Planning Regimes
children.top_down_role: Planning with soft goals, preferences, utilities, and competing quality criteria.

children.title: Oversubscription Planning
children.top_down_role: Planning instances where available resources or achievable capacity cannot satisfy every candidate goal.

assumptions_latex: Each optional goal has a finite nonnegative utility.
Each plan has a finite nonnegative execution cost.
Plan feasibility is defined independently of optional-goal utility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An optimal oversubscription plan maximizes achieved optional-goal utility minus execution cost among all feasible plans.

notation.meaning: Utility assigned to an optional goal

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Net-benefit planning with optional goals and action costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An oversubscription planning instance consists of a planning model, mandatory constraints, a finite set of optional goals \(G_o\), utilities \(u:G_o\to\mathbb{R}_{\geq0}\), and a plan-cost function \(c\). For a feasible plan \(\pi\) with terminal state \(s_\pi\), define \(G_o(\pi)=\{g\in G_o:s_\pi\models g\}\) and net benefit \(B(\pi)=\sum_{g\in G_o(\pi)}u(g)-c(\pi)\). An optimal plan \(\pi^*\) satisfies \(B(\pi^*)=\max\{B(\pi):\pi\text{ is feasible}\}\); optional goals not selected or achieved do not make the plan infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Oversubscription planning chooses a feasible plan that maximizes the utility of achieved optional goals minus its execution cost.
knowledge_statements.title: Oversubscription Planning

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and net-benefit formulation fit oversubscription planning, but no source establishes this exact variant with mandatory constraints, optional goals, additive utilities, and plan costs. A specific authoritative definition or section is required.

children.title: Preference-Based Planning
children.top_down_role: Planning with soft requirements or ranked outcomes that influence plan selection.

assumptions_latex: Each preference is a well-defined predicate on complete plan traces.
Every preference has a finite nonnegative violation weight.
Hard planning constraints remain mandatory.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Preference-based planning minimizes the weighted violation of soft trace conditions, optionally combined with ordinary plan cost.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Soft constraints interpreted over finite plan traces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A preference-based planning instance augments a hard-constrained planning model with a finite family \(\Phi\) of soft trace predicates. For each \(\phi\in\Phi\), let \(v_\phi(\pi)=0\) when the trace induced by feasible plan \(\pi\) satisfies \(\phi\), and \(v_\phi(\pi)=1\) otherwise, with weight \(w_\phi\geq0\). The preference penalty is \(V(\pi)=\sum_{\phi\in\Phi}w_\phi v_\phi(\pi)\). Under additive plan cost \(c(\pi)\), an optimal plan minimizes \(c(\pi)+V(\pi)\) over plans satisfying every hard constraint; violating a soft preference incurs its penalty but does not itself destroy feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Preference-based planning treats trace conditions as weighted soft constraints and optimizes their violation penalties together with any ordinary plan cost.
knowledge_statements.title: Preference-Based Planning

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits preference-based planning, but the binary trace-violation interpretation and additive penalty objective represent a particular preference semantics. No source is supplied to support that formalism or its relationship to hard feasibility.

children.title: Utility-Sensitive Goal Selection
children.top_down_role: Selection among competing goals using rewards, penalties, or aggregate utility.

assumptions_latex: Candidate goals and feasible plans are finite or the displayed maximum is attained.
Goal utilities are finite.
A goal contributes utility only when achieved by the selected plan.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Optimal goal selection chooses an achievable goal subset and supporting plan of maximum total utility, possibly net of plan cost.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selection of jointly achievable goals by additive utility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G\) be a finite set of candidate goals with utilities \(u_g\in\mathbb{R}\), and let \(A(\pi)=\{g\in G:\pi\text{ achieves }g\}\) for each feasible plan \(\pi\). Utility-sensitive goal selection solves \[\max_{\pi\text{ feasible}}\left\{\sum_{g\in A(\pi)}u_g-c(\pi)\right\}.\] Equivalently, it selects variables \(y_g\in\{0,1\}\) and a feasible supporting plan such that \(y_g=1\) implies \(g\in A(\pi)\), maximizing \(\sum_{g\in G}u_g y_g-c(\pi)\). Thus logical or resource incompatibility among goals is enforced through existence of one common supporting plan.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Utility-sensitive goal selection maximizes the utility of a jointly achievable goal subset, optionally subtracting the cost of its supporting plan.
knowledge_statements.title: Utility-Sensitive Goal Selection

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle content kind is appropriate for utility-sensitive goal selection, and the two formulations are coherent under suitable assumptions. No source is provided for the additive-utility formulation, optional cost term, or claimed equivalence between achieved-goal and selection-variable models.

children.title: Competing Plan-Quality Criteria
children.top_down_role: Tradeoffs among multiple criteria governing acceptable or preferred plans.

assumptions_latex: Every feasible plan has a finite criterion vector in \(\mathbb{R}^k\).
All criteria are expressed in minimization orientation.
The dominance comparison uses the componentwise order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A plan is Pareto efficient exactly when no feasible plan weakly improves every criterion and strictly improves at least one.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pareto comparison of multiple plan-quality objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal{P}\) be the feasible plan set and \(f(\pi)=(f_1(\pi),\ldots,f_k(\pi))\in\mathbb{R}^k\) collect criteria such as cost, makespan, risk, or preference penalty, all oriented for minimization. A plan \(\pi'\) dominates \(\pi\) when \(f_j(\pi')\leq f_j(\pi)\) for every \(j\in\{1,\ldots,k\}\) and \(f_j(\pi')<f_j(\pi)\) for at least one \(j\). A feasible plan \(\pi^*\) is Pareto efficient if and only if no \(\pi'\in\mathcal{P}\) dominates it. A scalarization selects one efficient compromise only under the additional properties of the chosen scalarizing function.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With competing quality criteria, a plan is Pareto efficient when no feasible alternative improves one criterion without worsening another.
knowledge_statements.title: Competing Plan-Quality Criteria

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition content kind fits the Pareto-efficiency criterion in the competing-quality container, and the formal dominance statement is standard. Nevertheless, the record has no cited source or inspectable locator connecting this criterion and the scalarization qualification to multiobjective planning.

children.title: Planning Representation-Structure Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Domain and plan representations that determine the available constraint structure and search organization.

children.title: Planning State-Transition Representation Family
children.top_down_role: Alternative representations of states, actions, transitions, and domain invariants.

children.title: Propositional Action Models
children.top_down_role: Boolean state and operator representations for classical planning.

assumptions_latex: The fluent and action sets are finite.
States assign a Boolean value to every fluent.
Action effects are deterministic and internally consistent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The model represents planning as reachability in the finite transition system induced by action applicability and Boolean updates.

notation.meaning: Positive and negative preconditions of action a
Positive and negative effects of action a

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complete Boolean states with deterministic propositional operators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A propositional action model uses a finite fluent set \(F\) and complete states \(s:F\to\{0,1\}\). An action \(a\) is represented by \((P_a^+,P_a^-,E_a^+,E_a^-)\), with positive and negative preconditions and effects contained in \(F\). It is applicable when every fluent in \(P_a^+\) is true and every fluent in \(P_a^-\) is false. Its successor \(s'\) sets fluents in \(E_a^+\) true, fluents in \(E_a^-\) false, and preserves all other values. Consequently, the representation induces a finite labeled transition relation \(s\xrightarrow{a}s'\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A propositional action model represents complete Boolean states and deterministic actions with positive and negative preconditions and effects.
knowledge_statements.title: Propositional Action Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation content kind fits the propositional action-model container, and the Boolean transition semantics is internally coherent. An authoritative source with a specific locator is still required for this positive-and-negative precondition/effect variant and its consistency assumptions.

children.title: Finite-Domain Transition Model Family
children.top_down_role: Multivalued state variables, transition systems, and transition-centered organization.

children.title: Finite-Domain State Models
children.top_down_role: Representations organized around multivalued state variables with finite value sets.

assumptions_latex: The variable set and every variable domain are finite.
Each state assigns exactly one value to every variable.
Operators have deterministic partial assignments.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The finite-domain model induces a finite transition system whose states are total variable assignments and whose arcs are applicable operator updates.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: SAS-style states as total assignments over finite-domain variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A finite-domain state model is specified by variables \(V=\{v_1,\ldots,v_m\}\) with finite domains \(D_v\). A state is a total assignment \(s\in\prod_{v\in V}D_v\). Each operator \(a\) has a partial-assignment precondition \(p_a\) and a partial-assignment effect \(e_a\). It is applicable in \(s\) when \(s(v)=p_a(v)\) for every \(v\in\operatorname{dom}(p_a)\). The successor \(s'\) satisfies \(s'(v)=e_a(v)\) for \(v\in\operatorname{dom}(e_a)\) and \(s'(v)=s(v)\) otherwise. Initial and goal conditions are respectively a total and a partial assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite-domain model represents each state as one value per variable and each operator as a guarded partial reassignment.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Domain State Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation content kind and total-assignment model fit the finite-domain state-model container. No authoritative SAS or finite-domain planning source is cited for the operator semantics, initial-state convention, or partial goal assignment.

children.title: Transition-Centered Planning Models
children.top_down_role: Representations organized around permitted changes between state-variable values.

assumptions_latex: Every state variable has a finite domain.
Each selected transition has an explicit source and target value.
Action-transition support and exclusion constraints are enforced.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A transition-centered encoding is valid when selected variable transitions form consistent paths and are jointly supported by the selected actions.

notation.meaning: Transition of variable v from value d to value d prime
Indicator that transition tau occurs at layer t
Indicator that action a occurs at layer t

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Layered planning represented primarily by finite-domain value transitions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each finite-domain variable \(v\), define transitions \(\tau=(v,d,d')\) between values in \(D_v\), including persistence transitions with \(d=d'\). In a horizon-\(H\) encoding, \(x_{\tau,t}=1\) states that \(\tau\) occurs between layers \(t\) and \(t+1\), while \(y_{a,t}=1\) selects action \(a\). For every variable and layer, selected transitions must form a value-consistent path from the initial value toward a goal-compatible value. Each selected action must imply its required transitions, and every non-persistence transition must be supported by a selected action. Mutually incompatible transitions or action supports cannot share a layer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Transition-centered models encode per-variable value changes directly, constrain them to form consistent paths, and couple each change to supporting actions.
knowledge_statements.title: Transition-Centered Planning Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation content kind fits a transition-centered planning model, but the statement describes a particular layered encoding without specifying its exact formalism. Source support is needed for persistence transitions, path constraints, action-transition support, exclusion constraints, and the strength of the asserted validity condition.

children.title: State-Transition Coupling
children.top_down_role: Interfaces linking state-variable assignments to transition choices across a plan.

assumptions_latex: The planning instance has finite-domain variables \(V\), domains \(D_v\), and actions represented by partial precondition and effect assignments.
A state \(s\) is a total assignment with \(s(v)\in D_v\) for every \(v\in V\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The constraints characterize a state sequence induced by the selected actions.

notation.meaning: value of variable v at layer t
binary selection indicator for action a at layer t

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard finite-domain planning transition encoding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-domain, discrete-time transition coupling with one selected action per step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every layer \(t\), impose \(\sum_{a}y_{a,t}=1\). If \(y_{a,t}=1\), then each precondition is satisfied, \(x_{v,t}=\operatorname{pre}_a(v)\) for every \(v\in\operatorname{dom}(\operatorname{pre}_a)\), and each effect is realized, \(x_{v,t+1}=\operatorname{eff}_a(v)\) for every \(v\in\operatorname{dom}(\operatorname{eff}_a)\). Every unaffected variable obeys the frame condition \(x_{v,t+1}=x_{v,t}\) whenever \(v\notin\operatorname{dom}(\operatorname{eff}_a)\). Thus feasible coupled assignments are exactly the state-action-state triples admitted by the selected finite-domain transition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Selected actions require their preconditions, impose their effects, and preserve every unaffected variable between consecutive state layers.
knowledge_statements.title: State-Transition Coupling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the State-Transition Coupling leaf, but no cited source supports the exact-one-action convention, frame constraints, or claimed exact characterization of admitted transitions.

children.title: Planning Interaction Structure Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Dependency and exclusion structures used to expose planning interactions.

children.title: Causal Dependency Graphs
children.top_down_role: Graph structures exposing dependencies among planning variables, actions, or subgoals.

assumptions_latex: The planning task uses finite variables \(V\) and actions whose preconditions and effects mention variables in \(V\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The directed graph records possible one-step causal influence between state variables.

notation.meaning: precondition and effect variable sets of action a

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard finite-domain planning causal graph
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Variable-level causal graph for finite-domain planning tasks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_a\subseteq V\) and \(E_a\subseteq V\) be the variables tested and changed by action \(a\). The causal dependency graph is \(G_C=(V,E_C)\), where \((u,v)\in E_C\) precisely when some action \(a\) changes \(v\) and either tests \(u\), with \(u\in P_a\), or also changes \(u\), with \(u\in E_a\), and \(u\ne v\). An arc therefore denotes potential direct dependence of a transition of \(v\) on the value or simultaneous transition of \(u\); it does not assert that every reachable transition exhibits that dependence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A causal graph connects variable u to variable v when an action changing v tests or simultaneously changes u.
knowledge_statements.title: Causal Dependency Graphs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the leaf, but planning causal-graph edge conventions vary, particularly for co-effect variables. A planning source with a precise definition and locator is required.

children.title: State Invariant Structures
children.top_down_role: Persistent structural restrictions used to organize reachable planning states.

assumptions_latex: The planning task has state space \(S\), initial state \(s_0\), and deterministic transition relation \(T\subseteq S\times S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An invariant structure denotes a predicate true in every state reachable from \(s_0\).

notation.meaning: set of states reachable from the initial state

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reachability and inductive invariants for deterministic finite-state planning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A state invariant is a predicate \(I:S\to\{0,1\}\) satisfying \(I(s)=1\) for every \(s\in\operatorname{Reach}(s_0)\). It is inductive when \(I(s_0)=1\) and, for all \((s,s')\in T\), the implication \(I(s)=1\Rightarrow I(s')=1\) holds. Any inductive invariant is a state invariant. Cardinality constraints such as \(\sum_{p\in M}\mathbf 1[p\text{ holds in }s]\le 1\), or equality to \(1\), are invariant structures when the corresponding predicate holds throughout the reachable state space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A state invariant holds in every reachable state; an inductive invariant holds initially and is preserved by every transition.
knowledge_statements.title: State Invariant Structures

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and content kind fit State Invariant Structures, but no source supports the reachability, inductiveness, and cardinality-invariant claims in this planning context.

children.title: Mutual-Exclusion Structures
children.top_down_role: Representations of action or fact combinations that cannot coexist.

assumptions_latex: The planning task uses propositional facts \(F\), states \(s\subseteq F\), and actions with precondition, add, and delete sets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Mutex relations identify fact pairs or action pairs forbidden from co-occurring under the chosen semantics.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard propositional planning mutex semantics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic fact mutex and interference-based action mutex are distinguished.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A sound fact mutex relation \(M_F\) satisfies \((p,q)\in M_F\Rightarrow \neg\exists s\in\operatorname{Reach}(s_0):\{p,q\}\subseteq s\). An interference-based action mutex relation \(M_A\) contains \((a,b)\) whenever an effect of either action negates a precondition or effect of the other, or their effects are inconsistent. A parallel action layer \(U\subseteq A\) respects the mutex structure when no distinct \(a,b\in U\) satisfy \((a,b)\in M_A\). Fact mutex is a reachability claim, whereas action mutex depends on the adopted same-layer execution semantics.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fact mutex forbids joint reachability; action mutex forbids same-layer execution when actions interfere or have inconsistent effects.
knowledge_statements.title: Mutual-Exclusion Structures

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition appropriately distinguishes fact and action mutex, but the action-mutex criteria depend on the adopted propositional and same-layer semantics. No inspectable citation is supplied.

children.title: Planning Interaction Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Boundaries separating independent planning components from interacting components.

assumptions_latex: The task variables are partitioned as \(V=V_1\mathbin{\dot\cup}\cdots\mathbin{\dot\cup}V_k\).
Each action has a precondition scope and an effect scope over \(V\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The boundary contains exactly the variables through which different planning components can interact.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: separator-style definition for factored planning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separator boundary induced by actions spanning a fixed variable partition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For component \(V_i\), define its interaction boundary by \(B_i=\{v\in V_i:\exists a,\ \operatorname{scope}(a)\cap V_i\ne\varnothing,\ \operatorname{scope}(a)\cap(V\setminus V_i)\ne\varnothing,\ v\in\operatorname{scope}(a)\}\). An action is internal to component \(i\) when \(\operatorname{scope}(a)\subseteq V_i\); otherwise it is a coupling action. If every coupling action mentions variables only in \(\bigcup_i B_i\), then assignments outside the boundaries affect other components only through boundary assignments and coupling-action choices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An interaction boundary consists of component variables mentioned by actions that also mention variables in another component.
knowledge_statements.title: Planning Interaction Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is plausible for a separator-style boundary, but it is not a uniquely standard planning definition. The final cross-component dependence claim also requires formal supporting assumptions and a cited source.

children.title: Plan-Structure Semantics
children.top_down_role: Plan representations distinguished by ordering, concurrency, and retained temporal flexibility.

children.title: Sequential Plan Structures
children.top_down_role: Totally ordered plans and bounded sequential horizons.

assumptions_latex: The planning task has initial state \(s_0\), goal predicate \(G\), action set \(A\), and a deterministic partial transition function \(\gamma\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A bounded sequential plan is feasible exactly when every successive transition is defined and the final state satisfies the goal.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Totally ordered deterministic plans with a finite horizon bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A sequential plan of length \(m\) is a sequence \(\pi=(a_1,\ldots,a_m)\in A^m\). It is executable from \(s_0\) when states \(s_1,\ldots,s_m\) exist such that \(s_t=\gamma(s_{t-1},a_t)\) is defined for every \(t\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\). It is a solution when additionally \(G(s_m)=1\). Under a horizon bound \(H\), admissible plans satisfy \(m\le H\); padding by a no-op action yields an equivalent representation with exactly \(H\) action layers when the no-op is always applicable and preserves every state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bounded sequential plan is a totally ordered action sequence executable from the initial state and ending in a goal state.
knowledge_statements.title: Sequential Plan Structures

children.title: Plan Concurrency Semantics
children.top_down_role: Plan structures governed by alternative concurrency and interference semantics.

children.title: Parallel Plan Semantics
children.top_down_role: Plan interpretations that group multiple actions into common execution layers.

assumptions_latex: Actions are propositional with precondition, add, and delete sets.
Every same-layer action set is required to be pairwise noninterfering.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A parallel plan is valid when each layer is jointly applicable and its simultaneous update leads to a goal state.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard noninterfering parallel STRIPS semantics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Synchronous propositional parallel plans with pairwise noninterfering actions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A parallel plan of makespan \(H\) is \(\Pi=(U_1,\ldots,U_H)\), where each \(U_t\subseteq A\). Layer \(U_t\) is applicable in \(s_{t-1}\) when every action precondition holds there and its distinct actions are pairwise noninterfering. Its simultaneous successor is \(s_t=(s_{t-1}\setminus\bigcup_{a\in U_t}\operatorname{del}(a))\cup\bigcup_{a\in U_t}\operatorname{add}(a)\). The parallel plan is valid from \(s_0\) when every layer is applicable in sequence and the resulting state satisfies \(G(s_H)=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A parallel plan applies each noninterfering action set simultaneously and must reach the goal after its final layer.
knowledge_statements.title: Parallel Plan Semantics

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits Parallel Plan Semantics and is internally coherent under pairwise noninterference, but the record supplies no source for this particular synchronous STRIPS convention.

children.title: Concurrent Action Semantics
children.top_down_role: Plan interpretations governing temporally overlapping actions.

assumptions_latex: Each action \(a\) has precondition \(P_a\), add effects \(A_a^+\), and delete effects \(A_a^-\).
The semantics evaluates all preconditions in the state preceding the concurrent step.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The concurrent step has a unique successor whenever its joint applicability and consistency conditions hold.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: synchronous set-based STRIPS transition semantics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Synchronous set execution with pre-state condition evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A concurrent action set \(U\subseteq A\) is jointly applicable in state \(s\) when \(P_a\subseteq s\) for every \(a\in U\), its aggregate effects are consistent, \((\bigcup_{a\in U}A_a^+)\cap(\bigcup_{a\in U}A_a^-)=\varnothing\), and any additional interference restrictions of the planning semantics hold. Its synchronous successor is \(\Gamma(s,U)=(s\setminus\bigcup_{a\in U}A_a^-)\cup\bigcup_{a\in U}A_a^+\). All preconditions are read from \(s\); effects produced within the step cannot support another action in the same step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Concurrent actions read one common pre-state and produce one successor by applying their consistent aggregate effects simultaneously.
knowledge_statements.title: Concurrent Action Semantics

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits Concurrent Action Semantics, but the phrase 'additional interference restrictions' leaves joint applicability dependent on an uncited external convention. A precise source is required.

children.title: Interference-Sensitive Concurrency
children.top_down_role: Concurrency regimes classified by conflicts among conditions, effects, or resource use.

assumptions_latex: Actions use propositional precondition, add, and delete sets.
Concurrency follows the no-moving-targets convention: one action may not alter a fact another concurrently reads or writes incompatibly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A layer is interference-safe exactly when every distinct action pair satisfies the displayed disjointness conditions.

notation.meaning: precondition, add, and delete sets of action a

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pairwise STRIPS interference under no-moving-targets concurrency.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A concurrent layer \(U\) is interference-safe when, for all distinct \(a,b\in U\), \(A_a^-\cap(P_b\cup A_b^+)=\varnothing\), \(A_b^-\cap(P_a\cup A_a^+)=\varnothing\), \(A_a^+\cap A_b^-=\varnothing\), and \(A_b^+\cap A_a^-=\varnothing\). Under the no-moving-targets convention one additionally requires \((A_a^+\cup A_a^-)\cap P_b=\varnothing\) and \((A_b^+\cup A_b^-)\cap P_a=\varnothing\). These tests exclude competing effects and concurrent deletion or modification of another action's required facts.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Concurrent actions are allowed only when neither changes a fact the other reads or writes incompatibly.
knowledge_statements.title: Interference-Sensitive Concurrency

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A condition is the correct role for this leaf. The displayed tests contain redundant add-delete exclusions, and the claimed exact characterization depends on the specific no-moving-targets convention; no authoritative source is cited.

children.title: Plan Serializability Regimes
children.top_down_role: Relationships between concurrent plans and valid sequential interpretations.

assumptions_latex: A finite action set \(U\) is jointly applicable in state \(s\).
Sequential execution uses deterministic transition function \(\gamma\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Serializability specifies whether one, every, or a state-independent ordering reproduces the concurrent transition.

notation.meaning: simultaneous successor of action set U

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard existential and universal serializability distinction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existential, universal, and uniform serializability of synchronous action sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The set \(U\) is existentially serializable at \(s\) when some \(\sigma\in\operatorname{Perm}(U)\) is sequentially executable from \(s\) and yields \(\Gamma(s,U)\). It is universally serializable at \(s\) when every \(\sigma\in\operatorname{Perm}(U)\) is executable and yields that same successor. It is uniformly serializable on a state set \(S'\) when one fixed permutation \(\sigma\) works for every \(s\in S'\) at which \(U\) is jointly applicable. Universal serializability implies existential serializability, but the converse need not hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A concurrent set may admit some valid serialization, every serialization, or one ordering that works uniformly across relevant states.
knowledge_statements.title: Plan Serializability Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits Plan Serializability Regimes and distinguishes three coherent quantifier patterns, but the regime names and simultaneous-successor equivalence are convention-dependent and uncited.

children.title: Causal-Link Partial-Order Structures
children.top_down_role: Plans retaining ordering flexibility and explicit causal support.

children.title: Partial-Order Plan Structures
children.top_down_role: Plans retaining unresolved ordering choices among actions.

assumptions_latex: The plan contains a finite set of action occurrences \(O\), including optional start and finish occurrences.
The ordering relation is required to be acyclic and transitive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every linear extension of the ordering relation is a candidate sequential realization of the partial-order plan.

notation.meaning: strict precedence relation on action occurrences

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite partially ordered action occurrences interpreted by linear extensions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A partial-order plan is a pair \(P=(O,\prec)\), where \(O\) is a finite set of action occurrences and \(\prec\) is an irreflexive, transitive precedence relation on \(O\). A total order \(\sigma\) realizes \(P\) when it is a linear extension: \(o\prec o'\) implies that \(o\) precedes \(o'\) in \(\sigma\). The plan is strongly valid when every linear extension is an executable sequential plan achieving the goal; it is weakly valid when at least one such extension is executable and goal-achieving. These validity notions must not be conflated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A partial-order plan constrains only required precedences; its executions are linear extensions, with weak and strong validity distinguished.
knowledge_statements.title: Partial-Order Plan Structures

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits Partial-Order Plan Structures and correctly distinguishes existential from universal validity of linear extensions, but the weak/strong terminology and semantics need a planning source with a precise locator.

children.title: Causal-Link Plan Structures
children.top_down_role: Plans recording explicit support relationships between action effects and later needs.

assumptions_latex: Action occurrences have propositional preconditions and effects.
The plan includes precedence constraints and distinguished start and finish occurrences encoding the initial state and goal.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A causal-link plan explicitly records which earlier occurrence supports each protected condition of a later occurrence.

notation.meaning: causal link from producer o through fact p to consumer o'

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard causal-link partial-order planning structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Propositional causal links embedded in a finite partial-order plan.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A causal-link plan is a triple \((O,\prec,L)\). A link \(o\xrightarrow{p}o'\in L\) requires \(o\prec o'\), occurrence \(o\) to establish fact \(p\), and occurrence \(o'\) to require \(p\). The link asserts that \(p\) must persist after \(o\) and until \(o'\). An occurrence \(q\) threatens the link when \(q\) can negate \(p\) and is not ordered outside its protection interval, meaning neither \(q\prec o\) nor \(o'\prec q\) holds. A complete threat-free causal-link plan supports every open precondition and orders every threat outside the corresponding interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Causal links name the action occurrence supporting each precondition and require all possible deleters to lie outside the protected interval.
knowledge_statements.title: Causal-Link Plan Structures

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and content kind fit Causal-Link Plan Structures, but no cited source supports the protection interval, threat condition, or completeness characterization.

children.title: Threat-Constrained Ordering
children.top_down_role: Ordering commitments introduced to protect causal support from interference.

assumptions_latex: The plan contains finitely many action instances and a strict partial order \(\prec\).
Every causal link \(a_i\xrightarrow{p}a_j\) requires \(p\) after \(a_i\) and until \(a_j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every threat is separated from the protected interval by an ordering constraint.
review_flags: No supplied source locator directly supports causal-link threat resolution.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical causal-link partial-order planning with propositional effects.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a causal link \(a_i\xrightarrow{p}a_j\), an action \(a_k\) is a threat when it has an effect inconsistent with \(p\) and the current order permits \(a_i\prec a_k\prec a_j\). The link is threat-protected precisely when the ordering constraints entail at least one separation, \(a_k\prec a_i\) or \(a_j\prec a_k\). A causal-link plan satisfies threat-constrained ordering when every threat to every causal link is protected.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A causal-link plan is valid only when every action capable of destroying a supported condition is ordered before its producer or after its consumer.
knowledge_statements.title: Threat-Constrained Ordering

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits the Threat-Constrained Ordering leaf, and the statement is mathematically plausible for classical causal-link planning. However, no source reference or inspectable locator is supplied for the threat definition and promotion/demotion separation criterion, so the record cannot pass source review.

children.title: Least-Commitment Plan Structure
children.top_down_role: Plan organization preserving flexibility until additional commitments become necessary.

assumptions_latex: Plan validity is invariant under any linear extension satisfying all causal, threat-resolution, and temporal constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The plan commits only to order relations entailed by validity constraints.

notation.meaning: valid linear extensions of the partial order

review_flags: No supplied source locator directly supports least-commitment planning.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Least commitment concerns ordering, not necessarily action selection or variable binding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\) be the selected actions and let \(C\) contain the causal, threat-resolution, and temporal constraints required for validity. A least-commitment plan structure uses a strict partial order \(\prec\) such that every relation in \(\prec\) is entailed by \(C\). It does not add \(a_i\prec a_j\) when both relative orders occur among valid linearizations. Thus its represented executions are exactly \(\mathcal L(\prec)\), rather than one arbitrarily chosen total order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A least-commitment plan imposes only orderings forced by validity, retaining every feasible linear execution consistent with those constraints.
knowledge_statements.title: Least-Commitment Plan Structure

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle role fits the Least-Commitment Plan Structure leaf. The exact characterization using relations entailed by C and all valid linearizations depends on the adopted planning formalism, and no source or locator is supplied to support it.

children.title: Timeline-Chronicle Representation Family
children.top_down_role: Temporal planning representations centered on state-variable timelines, chronicles, synchronization, and flexible temporal commitments.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Temporal Planning; Planning with Chronicles

children.title: State-Variable Timelines
children.top_down_role: Temporal evolution represented through value intervals and transitions.

assumptions_latex: Time ranges over a totally ordered domain \(T\).
Each state variable has a finite value domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A timeline is a temporally ordered, transition-consistent sequence of value intervals for one state variable.

notation.meaning: state variable with value domain D_x
token assigning value v on an interval

review_flags: No supplied source locator addresses timeline-based planning semantics.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite token timelines for discrete-valued state variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A timeline for state variable \(x\) is a finite sequence \((\tau_1,\ldots,\tau_m)\), where \(\tau_i=(v_i,[s_i,e_i))\), \(s_i<e_i\), and \(e_i\le s_{i+1}\). Each token asserts \(x(t)=v_i\) for every \(t\in[s_i,e_i)\). Consecutive tokens are transition-consistent when \((v_i,v_{i+1})\in R_x\). If the modeled interval requires complete coverage, then additionally \(e_i=s_{i+1}\) and the first and last endpoints equal the horizon boundaries.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A state-variable timeline is an ordered sequence of value-holding intervals whose adjacent values obey the variable's allowed transitions.
knowledge_statements.title: State-Variable Timelines

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Representation is the correct role for this leaf, and the statement consistently describes discrete-valued token timelines. Whether gaps are permitted and how complete horizon coverage and transitions are defined varies across timeline formalisms; no source with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Chronicle Models
children.top_down_role: Optional temporal assertions and constraints used to represent actions and plans.

assumptions_latex: All variables have declared finite or bounded domains.
Temporal constraints are interpreted over a totally ordered time domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A chronicle denotes every assignment satisfying its presence-guarded assertions and constraints.
review_flags: Chronicle formalisms vary in assertion and support semantics.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optional finite chronicles with guarded constraints and temporal assertions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A chronicle is a tuple \(C=(o_C,V_C,K_C,A_C)\). The Boolean \(o_C\) states whether the chronicle is present; \(V_C\) contains its object, value, and time variables; \(K_C\) contains constraints over those variables; and \(A_C\) contains temporally qualified conditions and effects on state variables. Its semantics is guarded: if \(o_C=1\), every constraint in \(K_C\) must hold and every assertion in \(A_C\) must receive the required consistency and support; if \(o_C=0\), those obligations are inactive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A chronicle is an optional bundle of variables, constraints, conditions, and effects whose planning obligations apply exactly when the bundle is selected.
knowledge_statements.title: Chronicle Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Definition is an appropriate role for Chronicle Models. The tuple components, presence guarding, consistency, and support obligations are formalism-dependent, and the record supplies no authoritative source or inspectable locator.

children.title: Timeline Coordination-Flexibility Tradeoff
children.top_down_role: Coordination among timelines while preserving executable slack.

children.title: Timeline Synchronization Constraints
children.top_down_role: Cross-timeline temporal commitments coordinating state-variable behavior.

assumptions_latex: Tokens belong to finitely many state-variable timelines.
Every endpoint is a decision variable over the common time domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A synchronization rule holds exactly when each trigger token has witnesses satisfying one designated temporal-value pattern.
review_flags: Synchronization-rule syntax differs among timeline formalisms.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Trigger-and-witness synchronization over token values and endpoints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(T_r\) be the tokens matching a rule's trigger predicate. A timeline synchronization constraint has the form \[\forall \tau\in T_r,
\quad \bigvee_{j=1}^{r}\exists \omega_1,\ldots,\omega_{k_j}:
\Phi_j(\tau,\omega_1,\ldots,\omega_{k_j}).\] Each \(\Phi_j\) is a conjunction of value predicates and endpoint relations, such as bounded start differences, containment, precedence, or overlap. A set of timelines satisfies the rule when the displayed formula holds for every trigger token.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every triggering token must have witness tokens whose values and endpoints satisfy at least one permitted synchronization pattern.
knowledge_statements.title: Timeline Synchronization Constraints

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits the synchronization-constraint leaf, and the quantified trigger-witness formula is internally coherent. Its syntax and semantics vary among timeline-based planning systems, so a specifically located source is required.

children.title: Temporal Flexibility Windows
children.top_down_role: Admissible timing ranges retained around activities or timeline tokens.

assumptions_latex: The temporal constraints form a feasible system of difference constraints \(t_j-t_i\le c_{ij}\).
A distinguished origin time is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each event may occur at any time in its projected feasible interval, subject to joint consistency with the remaining events.

notation.meaning: earliest feasible time of event i
latest feasible time of event i

review_flags: No supplied source locator supports simple temporal network projection.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection windows for events in a feasible simple temporal network.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P\) be the set of assignments satisfying all temporal difference constraints. For event time \(t_i\), define \[E_i=\inf_{t\in P}t_i,
\qquad L_i=\sup_{t\in P}t_i.\] The temporal flexibility window is the projection \([E_i,L_i]\) when both extrema are attained. Its width \(L_i-E_i\) is the event's marginal slack. Membership \(u\in[E_i,L_i]\) alone does not guarantee that independently selected times for different events are jointly feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An event's flexibility window spans its earliest and latest feasible times, but independently chosen times from different windows may be incompatible.
knowledge_statements.title: Temporal Flexibility Windows

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Representation fits the Temporal Flexibility Windows leaf. The projection-based statement is plausible for a feasible simple temporal network and correctly warns that marginal choices need not be jointly feasible, but no source or locator supports the adopted definitions of window and marginal slack.

children.title: Slack-Preserving Coordination
children.top_down_role: Coordination choices evaluated by how much executable temporal slack they retain.

assumptions_latex: The original temporal constraint system has nonempty feasible set \(P\).
Coordination adds constraints but does not remove existing ones.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Coordination is slack-preserving at level \(\delta\) exactly when the coordinated feasible region retains the required projected widths.
review_flags: Slack-preserving coordination is not uniquely standardized.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A local projected-slack criterion for coordinated temporal networks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each protected event \(i\), let \([E_i',L_i']\) be the projection of the coordinated feasible region \(P'\) onto its time coordinate. Coordination is \(\delta\)-slack-preserving when \[P'\ne\varnothing
\quad\text{and}\quad
L_i'-E_i'\ge\delta_i\quad\text{for every protected }i.\] The choice \(\delta_i=L_i-E_i\) preserves all original marginal slack, while \(\delta_i=\rho_i(L_i-E_i)\), with \(0\le\rho_i\le1\), preserves a prescribed fraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coordination preserves slack when it remains feasible and every protected event retains at least its prescribed temporal-window width.
knowledge_statements.title: Slack-Preserving Coordination

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits the leaf, but delta-slack-preserving coordination is presented as a particular projected-width definition rather than a uniquely standard notion. A domain source with a specific locator is needed to establish that this is the intended local meaning.

children.title: Synchronization Rigidity Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Regimes where cross-timeline commitments eliminate useful timing flexibility.

assumptions_latex: Two event times initially satisfy bounded feasible windows.
Synchronization is imposed as an exact offset equality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact synchronization can collapse positive temporal freedom to a singleton and can make disjoint shifted windows infeasible.
review_flags: The displayed boundary is elementary but lacks a supplied temporal-planning source.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rigidity induced by one exact-offset synchronization constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(t_a\in I_a=[E_a,L_a]\), \(t_b\in I_b=[E_b,L_b]\), and impose \(t_b=t_a+d\). The synchronized choices for \(t_a\) are exactly \[I_a\cap(I_b-d).\] Synchronization is infeasible precisely when this intersection is empty, and it is rigid precisely when the intersection is a singleton. Thus even when both original windows have positive width, an exact synchronization can eliminate all common slack; replacing equality by a bounded offset may avoid this collapse.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact offset synchronization is infeasible when shifted windows do not intersect and becomes rigid when their intersection contains exactly one time.
knowledge_statements.title: Synchronization Rigidity Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Failure boundary is the correct role for this leaf. The shifted-window intersection criterion is mathematically coherent, but no temporal-planning or temporal-reasoning source with a specific locator is supplied for its use as a synchronization rigidity boundary.

children.title: Planning as Constraint Compilation
children.top_down_role: Families compiling plan existence or quality into logical, constraint, or optimization formalisms.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Propositional Satisfiability Techniques; Constraint Satisfaction Techniques

children.title: Planning as Satisfiability
children.top_down_role: Bounded propositional planning organized by horizon, transition representation, concurrency semantics, and incremental solving.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Planning Problems as Satisfiability Problems; Planning by Satisfiability; Different Encodings

children.title: Bounded-Horizon SAT Encodings
children.top_down_role: Layered encodings indexed by a candidate plan horizon.

assumptions_latex: The planning instance is finite, propositional, and deterministic.
The horizon \(H\in\mathbb N\) bounds the number of transition layers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The bounded planning instance has a plan exactly when its horizon-indexed formula is satisfiable.
review_flags: No supplied source locator directly supports planning-as-SAT encodings.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-horizon SAT compilation for deterministic propositional planning.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bounded planning problem is compiled into a layered SAT formula whose models correspond exactly to valid plans within the chosen horizon.
knowledge_statements.title: Bounded-Horizon SAT Encodings

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Representation fits Bounded-Horizon SAT Encodings. The soundness-and-completeness equivalence depends on the precise layer, horizon, and concurrency semantics, including whether H denotes exactly H steps or at most H steps; no supporting planning-as-SAT source or locator is supplied.

children.title: Planning Primitive Encoding Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Encoding families organized around different primitive planning relations.

children.title: Action-Centered Encodings
children.top_down_role: Planning encodings whose primary decision structure concerns action occurrence.

assumptions_latex: Actions are ground and have propositional preconditions and effects.
A fixed horizon and concurrency semantics are given.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Truth assignments to action variables select the plan, while clauses enforce applicability, effects, persistence, goals, and exclusions.

notation.meaning: action a is selected at step t
fact p holds at layer t

review_flags: No supplied source locator identifies an action-centered SAT encoding.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Action variables are the primary plan-selection variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An action-centered encoding introduces \(A_{a,t}\) for each action \(a\) and step \(0\le t<H\). It includes implications from \(A_{a,t}\) to every precondition at layer \(t\) and every effect at layer \(t+1\), together with frame or explanatory clauses connecting unchanged facts across layers. Clauses exclude action sets forbidden by the concurrency semantics. Under sound and complete auxiliary fact constraints, models of \(\Phi_H\) project to exactly the executable action sequences or parallel steps of horizon \(H\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Action-centered SAT encodings make action occurrence primary and constrain each selected action's preconditions, effects, persistence interactions, and concurrency.
knowledge_statements.title: Action-Centered Encodings

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Representation is appropriate for Action-Centered Encodings. The claimed exact projection to executable sequential or parallel plans depends on the auxiliary fact, frame, and concurrency clauses, and no specifically located source is supplied.

children.title: Fact-Centered Encodings
children.top_down_role: Planning encodings organized around propositional facts across bounded horizons.

assumptions_latex: The planning state is a valuation of finitely many propositional facts.
A fixed horizon \(H\) is given.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Layer valuations constitute a valid state trajectory exactly when all initial, goal, transition-support, and consistency clauses hold.

notation.meaning: fact p holds at layer t

review_flags: Fact-centered encodings admit several distinct support conventions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fact-layer variables are primary; action or support variables may be auxiliary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A fact-centered encoding introduces \(F_{p,t}\) for each fact \(p\) and layer \(0\le t\le H\). Clauses fix the initial valuation and require the goal valuation. For every change between \(F_{p,t}\) and \(F_{p,t+1}\), support clauses require an applicable producer or deleter, while persistence clauses permit unchanged values. State-consistency clauses forbid incompatible fact combinations. The encoding is adequate when each satisfying layered valuation extends to action or support choices realizing exactly those transitions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fact-centered encodings primarily describe successive state valuations and require every fact change to have valid action support.
knowledge_statements.title: Fact-Centered Encodings

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Representation fits Fact-Centered Encodings. The support, persistence, state-consistency, and extension requirements are plausible but vary across fact-centered SAT formulations; no source with a section, theorem, definition, or page locator is supplied.

children.title: Transition-Centered Encodings
children.top_down_role: Planning encodings organized around state-variable transitions.

assumptions_latex: Each finite-domain state variable has an explicit transition relation.
A fixed horizon and transition concurrency semantics are given.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Selected transition variables form a consistent state path and are linked to actions capable of realizing those transitions.

notation.meaning: variable x changes from value u to value v at step t

review_flags: No supplied source locator identifies transition-centered planning encodings.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-domain transition variables are the primary encoding primitives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A transition-centered encoding introduces \(T_{x,u,v,t}\) only for \((u,v)\in R_x\). For each variable \(x\) and step \(t\), clauses select exactly one compatible transition, including persistence \(u=v\), and adjacent steps satisfy flow conservation: a transition ending at \(v\) must be followed by one starting at \(v\). Action-linking clauses require each selected action's transitions and require each non-persistence transition to be supported by at least one selected action. Initial and goal clauses constrain path endpoints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Transition-centered encodings choose finite-domain value transitions, enforce path continuity, and link each genuine change to actions that realize it.
knowledge_statements.title: Transition-Centered Encodings

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Representation is appropriate for Transition-Centered Encodings. Exact-one transition selection, persistence treatment, flow conservation, and action support depend on the selected finite-domain encoding and concurrency semantics, and no inspectable source locator is supplied.

children.title: Primitive-Selection Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Structural consequences of choosing actions, facts, or transitions as encoding primitives.

assumptions_latex: \(\Pi=(F,A,I,G)\) is a finite propositional planning instance.
\(H\in\mathbb{N}\) is a fixed horizon.
Each encoding is sound and complete for the same concurrency semantics.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{SAT}(E_H^{\mathrm{act}})\iff\operatorname{SAT}(E_H^{\mathrm{fact}})\iff\operatorname{SAT}(E_H^{\mathrm{trans}})\), while their variable counts, clause widths, and propagation strengths may differ.

notation.meaning: Action-, fact-, and transition-centered bounded encodings.
Set of plans of horizon at most \(H\).

review_flags: Planning-specific authoritative source and exact encoding-size comparisons are missing.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates semantic equivalence from encoding size and inference strength at a fixed horizon.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E_H^{\mathrm{act}}\), \(E_H^{\mathrm{fact}}\), and \(E_H^{\mathrm{trans}}\) encode the same bounded planning problem using action, fluent, and state-transition primitives, respectively. If each satisfying assignment projects onto exactly one member of \(\mathcal P_H(\Pi)\), possibly with auxiliary-variable multiplicity, then all three formulas are equisatisfiable. Primitive selection may nevertheless change the numbers of variables and constraints, maximum constraint arity or clause width, and deductions obtained by local consistency or unit propagation. Thus semantic completeness fixes the represented plan set, whereas computational behavior depends on the chosen primitive vocabulary and linking constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sound and complete primitive families represent the same bounded plans, but can differ substantially in size, constraint arity, and propagation strength.
knowledge_statements.title: Primitive-Selection Tradeoffs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle and content kind fit the leaf, but no cited source supports the equivalence assumptions or the claims about encoding size and propagation strength.

children.title: Persistence-Support-Exclusion Encoding Family
children.top_down_role: Encoding families for persistence, causal support, interference, and concurrency.

children.title: Frame Encodings
children.top_down_role: Encoding structures representing persistence across planning layers.

assumptions_latex: \(x_{f,t}\in\{0,1\}\) denotes fluent truth and \(y_{a,t}\in\{0,1\}\) denotes action selection.
Parallel actions in one layer obey the encoding's chosen compatibility semantics.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{f,t+1}\leftrightarrow\bigl(\bigvee_{a:f\in\operatorname{add}(a)}y_{a,t}\bigr)\lor\bigl(x_{f,t}\land\neg\bigvee_{a:f\in\operatorname{del}(a)}y_{a,t}\bigr)\).

notation.meaning: Boolean truth variable for fluent \(f\) at layer \(t\).
Boolean selection variable for action \(a\) at layer \(t\).

review_flags: Planning-specific source for successor-state and explanatory-frame variants is missing.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses a complete successor-state form of frame encoding for finite propositional planning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every fluent \(f\) and transition \(t=0,\ldots,H-1\), a complete frame encoding equates its next-layer truth with either an adding action or persistence without deletion:
\[x_{f,t+1}\leftrightarrow\left(\bigvee_{a:f\in\operatorname{add}(a)}y_{a,t}\right)\lor\left(x_{f,t}\land\neg\bigvee_{a:f\in\operatorname{del}(a)}y_{a,t}\right).\]
Empty disjunctions are false. Together with action precondition constraints and compatible-effect constraints, these equivalences exclude spontaneous fluent changes and characterize the state sequence induced by the selected actions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fluent is true in the next layer exactly when an action adds it or it persists without any selected action deleting it.
knowledge_statements.title: Frame Encodings

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation is coherent under compatible-effect semantics, but the complete successor-state/frame formulation has no planning-specific citation.

children.title: Causal-Support Encodings
children.top_down_role: Encoding structures connecting required facts to supporting actions or transitions.

assumptions_latex: \(I\subseteq F\) is the initial state.
Every required fluent occurrence is assigned a producer earlier than its consumer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s_{i,j,p}=1\Rightarrow\bigl(p\in\operatorname{add}(a_i)\land p\in\operatorname{pre}(a_j)\land i<j\bigr)\), and every required \((j,p)\) has exactly one selected supporter.

notation.meaning: Support variable asserting that occurrence \(i\) supports precondition \(p\) of occurrence \(j\).
Distinguished initial producer for initially true fluents.

review_flags: Planning-specific source for direct and fact-layer causal-support encodings is missing.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct support-variable encoding with a distinguished initial producer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each selected action occurrence \(j\) and each \(p\in\operatorname{pre}(a_j)\), impose
\[\sum_{i\in P(j,p)}s_{i,j,p}=1,\qquad s_{i,j,p}\Rightarrow(i<j),\]
where \(P(j,p)\) contains the initial producer \(0\) when \(p\in I\) and earlier occurrences whose actions add \(p\). Each implication \(s_{i,j,p}\Rightarrow z_i\land z_j\) activates both endpoint occurrences. Additional protection constraints must ensure that no selected occurrence deleting \(p\) lies between producer \(i\) and consumer \(j\). These constraints make every selected precondition explicitly causally supported.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every selected action precondition chooses an initial or earlier adding occurrence, and the chosen causal link must be protected from deletion.
knowledge_statements.title: Causal-Support Encodings

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits causal-support encodings, but no source establishes the exactly-one supporter convention and required protection constraints.

children.title: Mutex Encodings
children.top_down_role: Encoding structures excluding incompatible actions, facts, or transitions.

assumptions_latex: \(y_{a,t},y_{b,t}\in\{0,1\}\) indicate actions placed in the same layer.
\(M_t\subseteq A\times A\) is the symmetric incompatibility relation required by the concurrency semantics.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\forall (a,b)\in M_t:\;\neg y_{a,t}\lor\neg y_{b,t}\).

notation.meaning: Pairs of actions forbidden from sharing layer \(t\).
Selection variable for action \(a\) in layer \(t\).

review_flags: Planning-specific source for competing-needs, interference, and effect mutex variants is missing.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pairwise Boolean encoding of a precomputed action incompatibility relation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given an incompatibility relation \(M_t\), impose for every \((a,b)\in M_t\) the clause
\[\neg y_{a,t}\lor\neg y_{b,t}.\]
The relation must include every pair excluded by the intended step semantics, such as inconsistent effects, an effect negating the other's precondition, or competing preconditions when applicable. Conversely, pairs not in \(M_t\) may coexist only if the remaining transition constraints jointly define a valid successor state. Hence the clauses encode mutual exclusion, while the definition of \(M_t\) determines the represented concurrency model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each incompatible action pair receives a binary clause forbidding simultaneous selection; the mutex relation determines which concurrency semantics is represented.
knowledge_statements.title: Mutex Encodings

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The pairwise mutex condition is mathematically coherent, but the planning-specific construction of the incompatibility relation and its concurrency interpretation are uncited.

children.title: Concurrency Encoding Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Differences in permitted concurrency induced by support, frame, or exclusion choices.

assumptions_latex: The initial state contains \(p\) and \(q\).
Action \(a\) deletes \(q\), while action \(b\) requires \(q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The step \(\{a,b\}\) is valid under existential serialization because \(b\prec a\), but invalid under universal serialization because \(a\prec b\) disables \(b\).

notation.meaning: Two actions proposed for the same parallel layer.
Strict execution order within a serialization.

review_flags: Planning-specific source establishing existential-step and universal-step boundaries is missing.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete boundary between existentially and universally serializable parallel steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q\in\operatorname{pre}(b)\cap\operatorname{del}(a)\), and suppose both actions are otherwise applicable initially and have compatible final effects. The concurrent set \(\{a,b\}\) has a valid serialization \(b\prec a\), so an existential-step encoding may admit it. The reverse serialization \(a\prec b\) is invalid because executing \(a\) destroys the precondition \(q\) of \(b\). Therefore the set is not valid under universal-step semantics. An encoding that omits this interference pair from its mutex relation cannot represent universal serializability, even if its final-state effects are consistent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two actions may admit one valid order but not every order, separating existential-step concurrency from universal-step concurrency.
knowledge_statements.title: Concurrency Encoding Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The example correctly distinguishes existential from universal serialization under the stated assumptions, and failure_boundary fits the leaf, but no authoritative source supports the semantics used.

children.title: Incremental SAT Optimization Family
children.top_down_role: Reuse across horizons and integration with plan-quality search.

children.title: Incremental-Horizon SAT Planning
children.top_down_role: SAT-planning regimes that reuse information while extending the planning horizon.

assumptions_latex: \(E_H(\Pi)\) is satisfiable exactly when \(\Pi\) has a plan of horizon at most \(H\).
A finite starting horizon \(L\) and optional finite upper bound \(U\) are given.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm returns a plan decoded from the first satisfiable \(E_H(\Pi)\), or reports failure after \(U\) when no tested horizon is satisfiable.

notation.meaning: Sound and complete SAT encoding at horizon \(H\).

review_flags: Planning-specific source for incremental horizon construction and solver assumptions is missing.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear horizon growth for bounded propositional SAT planning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a planning instance \(\Pi\), lower horizon \(L\), and optional upper horizon \(U\). Initialize \(H:=L\). Construct \(E_H(\Pi)\) and invoke a SAT solver. If satisfiable, decode and return the selected action variables as a plan. If unsatisfiable and \(H<U\), set \(H:=H+1\), extend the encoding with the next transition layer, and solve again; otherwise report that no plan exists within \(U\). Without a finite \(U\), the procedure terminates exactly when some tested horizon is satisfiable, unless independent unsolvability detection is supplied.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve sound bounded encodings at increasing horizons, returning the first decoded plan or failure at a specified upper horizon.
knowledge_statements.title: Incremental-Horizon SAT Planning

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm appropriately describes increasing-horizon SAT planning and states its termination boundary, but incremental construction and decoding have no supporting citation.

children.title: Optimal SAT Planning
children.top_down_role: SAT-planning regimes organized around proving or improving plan quality.

assumptions_latex: \(E_H(\Pi)\) is sound and complete for plans of makespan at most \(H\).
Horizons are tested in strictly increasing order from a valid lower bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(H^*=\min\{H:E_H(\Pi)\text{ is satisfiable}\}\), every plan decoded from \(E_{H^*}(\Pi)\) has minimum encoded makespan \(H^*\).
review_flags: Planning-specific source for makespan optimality of first satisfiable horizon is missing.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Makespan optimality only; it does not imply minimum action count or cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Assume \(E_H(\Pi)\) is satisfiable if and only if \(\Pi\) admits a plan whose encoded makespan is at most \(H\). Let
\[H^*=\min\{H\in\mathbb N:E_H(\Pi)\text{ is satisfiable}\}.\]
Then any plan decoded from a satisfying assignment of \(E_{H^*}(\Pi)\) is makespan-optimal under the encoding's concurrency semantics. Indeed, soundness gives a plan of makespan at most \(H^*\), while unsatisfiability of every smaller horizon excludes any plan of smaller encoded makespan. This conclusion does not establish optimality for action count, accumulated cost, or another objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The first satisfiable sound and complete horizon yields a makespan-optimal plan, but not necessarily a minimum-cost or minimum-action plan.
knowledge_statements.title: Optimal SAT Planning

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The makespan-optimality claim is appropriately limited and theorem is the correct kind, but it lacks a source. The sentence beginning “Indeed” is proof text and must be removed before acceptance.

children.title: Bound-Driven SAT Planning
children.top_down_role: SAT-planning searches controlled by horizon, cost, or quality bounds.

assumptions_latex: \(E_{H,B}(\Pi)\) is satisfiable exactly when a horizon-\(H\) plan has cost at most \(B\).
Plan costs are integral and known bounds \(L\le C^*\le U\) are available.
