knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: On termination the returned plan has cost \(C^*=U=L\); an unsatisfiable query at \(B\) certifies \(C^*>B\).

notation.meaning: SAT encoding with horizon and cost bounds.
Current lower and upper objective bounds.

review_flags: Planning-specific source for cost-bound SAT optimization and bound updates is missing.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary bound search for integral plan cost at a fixed complete horizon.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input \(\Pi\), a horizon \(H\) known to contain an optimal-cost plan, and integral bounds \(L\le C^*\le U\), with an incumbent of cost \(U\). While \(L<U\), set \(B:=\lfloor(L+U)/2\rfloor\) and solve \(E_{H,B}(\Pi)\). If satisfiable, decode an incumbent of cost \(C\le B\) and set \(U:=C\); if unsatisfiable, set \(L:=B+1\). Return the incumbent when \(L=U\). Soundness and completeness of each bounded query make the final common bound equal to the minimum representable cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Binary search over integral cost bounds, tightening the incumbent after satisfiable queries and the lower bound after unsatisfiable queries.
knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Driven SAT Planning

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The binary-search algorithm is coherent given a fixed horizon containing a globally optimal-cost plan, but that completeness premise and the bound-update result require a planning-specific source.

children.title: Cross-Horizon Reuse
children.top_down_role: Reusable compilation structure or learned information shared across successive horizons.

assumptions_latex: Each horizon formula is expressed as persistent clauses plus clauses guarded by activation literals.
A reused learned clause is logically implied by clauses active in every later query where it is retained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Retaining persistent clauses and such learned clauses preserves satisfiability of every later horizon query.
review_flags: Planning-specific source for incremental SAT clause reuse and activation-literal conditions is missing.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical safety condition for retaining clauses across increasing planning horizons.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent a horizon query by a shared clause set \(P\) and guarded horizon clauses \(\neg\alpha_H\lor C\), solving under the assumption \(\alpha_H\). When moving from \(H\) to \(H+1\), retain \(P\), append the new layer, and change the assumptions rather than deleting clauses. A learned clause may be reused only when it follows from clauses retained and active in the later query, or when its dependence on obsolete assumptions is represented explicitly. Under this condition, reuse changes solver state and search effort but neither creates nor removes satisfying assignments of the later bounded encoding.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Persistent and learned clauses can be reused across horizons only when their logical dependencies remain active or are explicitly guarded.
knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Horizon Reuse

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated logical dependency condition is suitable for cross-horizon reuse, but activation-literal handling and learned-clause retention are unsupported by any citation.

children.title: Planning as Constraint Satisfaction
children.top_down_role: Finite-domain and global-constraint formulations of bounded, partial-order, or temporal planning.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Planning Problems as CSPs; Extended CSP Models; CSP Techniques in Planning

children.title: State-Layered Planning CSPs
children.top_down_role: Bounded models with explicit state and action layers.

assumptions_latex: \(F\) and \(A\) are finite, and \(H\in\mathbb N\).
Actions have propositional preconditions and deterministic add-delete effects.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: CSP solutions are in one-to-one correspondence, up to auxiliary variables, with valid length-\(H\) state-action trajectories satisfying \(S_0=I\) and \(G\subseteq S_H\).

notation.meaning: State variable for fluent \(f\) at layer \(t\).
Selection variable for action \(a\) at transition \(t\).

review_flags: Supplied CP locator is too general to support this planning-CSP representation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit Boolean state and action layers for deterministic bounded planning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A state-layered planning CSP has variables \(X_{f,t}\) for \(f\in F\), \(t=0,\ldots,H\), and \(Y_{a,t}\) for \(a\in A\), \(t=0,\ldots,H-1\). Initial constraints fix \(X_{f,0}=1\) exactly for \(f\in I\); goal constraints require \(X_{g,H}=1\) for \(g\in G\). Reified precondition constraints make \(Y_{a,t}=1\) imply every precondition at layer \(t\). Transition constraints apply selected effects and preserve unaffected fluents, while exclusion constraints enforce the selected concurrency semantics. Solutions therefore encode precisely the valid bounded trajectories.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Boolean state and action layers, joined by precondition, transition, frame, goal, and exclusion constraints, represent bounded deterministic plans.
knowledge_statements.title: State-Layered Planning CSPs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits state-layered planning CSPs, but the claimed trajectory correspondence depends on unspecified transition and exclusion constraints and has no planning-CSP source.

children.title: Causal-Protection Planning CSPs
children.top_down_role: Models centered on causal support, ordering, and threat resolution.

children.title: Causal-Support Planning CSPs
children.top_down_role: Planning CSPs centered on selecting support for action conditions or goals.

assumptions_latex: Selected occurrence \(j\) requires fluent \(p\).
Candidate producers are the initial state or selected occurrences adding \(p\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_j=1\Rightarrow\sum_{i\in P(j,p)}s_{i,j,p}=1\), with every selected support satisfying endpoint selection, precedence, and protection constraints.

notation.meaning: Reified choice of producer \(i\) for requirement \((j,p)\).

review_flags: Planning-specific source for reified causal-support CSP constraints is missing.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reified exactly-one support condition for optional action occurrences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every occurrence \(j\) and precondition \(p\in\operatorname{pre}(a_j)\), introduce support variables indexed by \(P(j,p)\). Impose
\[z_j\Rightarrow\sum_{i\in P(j,p)}s_{i,j,p}=1,\qquad s_{i,j,p}\Rightarrow z_i\land z_j\land(i\prec j).\]
For the distinguished initial producer, replace \(z_i\) by the condition \(p\in I\). Each selected support variable also activates protection constraints excluding any selected deleter of \(p\) between \(i\) and \(j\). When \(z_j=0\), all associated support variables are fixed to zero. Thus every active commitment has one protected producer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each active precondition chooses exactly one earlier active producer, and selecting that producer activates ordering and protection constraints.
knowledge_statements.title: Causal-Support Planning CSPs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition matches the leaf and consistently treats optional occurrences, but the exactly-one support and protection formulation lacks an authoritative planning-CSP citation.

children.title: Threat-Resolution Planning CSPs
children.top_down_role: Planning CSPs centered on resolving interference with causal commitments.

assumptions_latex: \(s_{i,j,p}=1\) selects a causal link from producer \(i\) to consumer \(j\).
Selected occurrence \(k\) deletes \(p\), and the precedence relation is strict and transitive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s_{i,j,p}\land z_k\Rightarrow(k\prec i)\lor(j\prec k)\).
review_flags: Planning-specific source for promotion-demotion threat-resolution constraints is missing.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Disjunctive ordering resolution of a delete threat to a selected causal link.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \(s_{i,j,p}=1\) establishes that occurrence \(i\) produces \(p\) for occurrence \(j\), and occurrence \(k\) has \(p\in\operatorname{del}(a_k)\). If \(k\) is selected, the CSP must impose
\[s_{i,j,p}\land z_k\Rightarrow(k\prec i)\lor(j\prec k).\]
The first disjunct demotes the threat before the producer; the second promotes it after the consumer. Together with \(i\prec j\), transitivity, and acyclicity of \(\prec\), this constraint prevents \(k\) from occurring strictly between the endpoints of the active causal link. An unselected occurrence creates no threat.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A selected deleter threatening a causal link must be ordered before its producer or after its consumer.
knowledge_statements.title: Threat-Resolution Planning CSPs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The promotion-or-demotion disjunction is coherent for a selected deleter threatening a causal link, but the formulation has no planning-specific source.

children.title: Ordering-Protection CSPs
children.top_down_role: Planning CSPs using ordering decisions to protect causal relationships.

assumptions_latex: A finite partial-order plan contains actions with start and finish events and designated causal links.
The strict precedence relation \(\prec\) is acyclic.
A threat to a causal link is an action whose effect can negate the protected literal while the link is open.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every protected causal link is immune to every selected threat.

notation.meaning: A causal link asserting that action \(i\) establishes literal \(p\) for action \(j\).
Set of actions threatening the indicated causal link.

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite partial-order planning with promotion-or-demotion threat protection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every selected causal link \(i\xrightarrow{p}j\) and every selected threat \(k\in T_{ipj}\), an ordering-protection CSP imposes the disjunction
\[
k\prec i\;\lor\;j\prec k.
\]
If actions have start and finish events, the two alternatives mean that the threatening effect occurs before the support is established or after the supported precondition is consumed. Together with acyclicity of \(\prec\), satisfaction of all such disjunctions is exactly the ordering-based protection condition for the designated causal links.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each action threatening a causal link must be ordered either before the supporter or after the consumer, while all resulting precedences remain acyclic.
knowledge_statements.title: Ordering-Protection CSPs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind and promotion-or-demotion condition fit the leaf, but no planning source supports the asserted exact characterization, especially for actions represented by start and finish events.

children.title: Unsupported-Commitment Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Model boundaries where selected commitments lack compatible causal support.

assumptions_latex: A candidate plan selects actions and designates precondition occurrences that must be supported.
Each designated support must come from the initial state or a selected producer.
Threat protection is evaluated only after a support is chosen.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A plan containing an unsupported commitment cannot satisfy the causal-support planning CSP.

notation.meaning: Admissible selected producers of \(p\) for action \(j\), including the initial state when applicable.

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary separating missing causal support from failures of threat resolution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An unsupported commitment occurs when some selected action \(j\in A^+\) requires a literal \(p\), but
\[
S_{jp}=\varnothing.
\]
Equivalently, if support indicators \(y_{ijp}\in\{0,1\}\) are defined for admissible producers \(i\), the required constraint \(\sum_{i\in S_{jp}}y_{ijp}=1\) has no feasible assignment. This is a causal-support infeasibility, not an ordering-protection failure: adding promotion or demotion constraints cannot create a missing producer. The boundary also applies when all nominal producers are excluded by action-selection or reachability constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A required precondition is beyond repair by threat ordering when no selected initial or action effect can serve as its causal supporter.
knowledge_statements.title: Unsupported-Commitment Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role and empty-support infeasibility are coherent, but the planning-specific support model and claimed boundary lack a cited source.

children.title: Time-Resource Planning CSP Coupling
children.top_down_role: Models coupling action choice to temporal networks and resource constraints.

children.title: Temporal Planning CSPs
children.top_down_role: Planning CSPs coupling action choices to temporal variables or networks.

assumptions_latex: A finite set of selected actions has nonnegative durations.
Temporal requirements are conjunctions or finite disjunctions of difference constraints.
Time is represented over \(\mathbb{R}\), unless an explicitly discrete domain is imposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Temporal feasibility is equivalent to satisfiability of the compiled difference constraints and their selected disjunctive branches.

notation.meaning: Start and finish times of action \(i\).
Binary selector for branch \(r\) of a temporal disjunction.

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite temporal plans compiled into difference and disjunctive constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A temporal planning CSP represents each selected action \(i\) by variables \(s_i,f_i\in\mathbb{R}\) satisfying \(f_i-s_i=d_i\) and \(s_i\ge 0\). Every required lag \(\ell_{ij}\le s_j-f_i\le u_{ij}\) is compiled as two difference constraints. Each alternative temporal requirement is represented by selectors \(z_r\in\{0,1\}\) with \(\sum_r z_r=1\), activating exactly one admissible branch. A temporal assignment is feasible precisely when it satisfies all duration, lag, horizon, and activated-branch constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Start and finish variables, duration equations, lag bounds, and selected temporal alternatives jointly represent a temporally feasible plan.
knowledge_statements.title: Temporal Planning CSPs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits the leaf, but no source supports this particular compilation, including exactly-one selectors for temporal alternatives and the claimed feasibility equivalence.

children.title: Resource Planning CSPs
children.top_down_role: Planning CSPs coupling action choices to capacity or consumption constraints.

assumptions_latex: A finite set of selected actions has specified renewable or consumable resource demands.
Each resource has a stated capacity or initial inventory.
Resource usage is evaluated over all relevant times or event intervals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Resource feasibility holds exactly when every renewable capacity and consumable balance constraint is satisfied.

notation.meaning: Capacity or initial inventory of resource \(r\).
Indicator that action \(i\) is executing at time \(t\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Renewable-capacity and consumable-balance constraints for finite plans.

source_refs.locator: 1.2.1 Resource allocation in production planning p. 4

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each renewable resource \(r\), feasibility requires
\[
\sum_i q_{ir}a_i(t)\le C_r
\]
at every relevant time \(t\). For each consumable resource, let \(b_{ir}\) be the signed inventory change caused by action \(i\); then every event prefix \(P\) must satisfy \(0\le C_r+\sum_{i\in P}b_{ir}\), together with any upper storage bound. A resource planning CSP consists of these constraints plus action-selection links forcing unselected actions to contribute zero demand and zero inventory change.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A plan is resource-feasible when concurrent renewable demand never exceeds capacity and every event prefix maintains valid consumable inventory.
knowledge_statements.title: Resource Planning CSPs

source_witnesses.locator: 1.2.1 Resource allocation in production planning p. 4

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited production-allocation section does not adequately support the combined renewable-profile, consumable-prefix, and action-selection characterization of a resource planning CSP.

children.title: Coupled Time-Resource CSPs
children.top_down_role: Planning CSPs where resource feasibility depends on temporal placement.

assumptions_latex: Actions have temporal variables and resource demands as in the component CSPs.
Whether an action consumes a renewable resource depends on its scheduled execution interval.
All coupling indicators are constrained to agree with action selection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A satisfying assignment simultaneously determines a temporally feasible plan and a capacity-feasible resource profile for that same schedule.

notation.meaning: Start and finish times of action \(i\).
Indicator that action \(i\) executes at time \(t\).

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Integrated temporal and resource feasibility with shared action variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A coupled time-resource CSP contains the temporal constraints on \(s_i,f_i\), the resource constraints, and channeling constraints
\[
a_i(t)=1\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad s_i\le t<f_i
\]
for each selected action and relevant time point, with \(a_i(t)=0\) for unselected actions. Thus the renewable constraint \(\sum_i q_{ir}a_i(t)\le C_r\) is evaluated on the same intervals determined by the temporal solution. Consumable balance constraints are analogously indexed by the event order induced by the temporal variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Channeling constraints make resource usage depend on the same action intervals and event order that satisfy the temporal planning constraints.
knowledge_statements.title: Coupled Time-Resource CSPs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits the coupled leaf, but the domain of relevant times is not defined sufficiently to determine whether the indicator biconditionals form a finite CSP, and no source supports the formulation.

children.title: Resource-Temporal Conflict Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Infeasibility regimes caused by interactions between timing commitments and resource limits.

assumptions_latex: Two selected actions require the same unary renewable resource.
Their execution intervals are nonpreemptive.
No alternative resource assignment or capacity increase is permitted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If temporal bounds force the two actions to overlap, the coupled CSP is infeasible.

notation.meaning: Start and finish times of action \(i\).
Earliest start and latest finish bounds of action \(i\).
The exclusive resource shared by actions \(i\) and \(j\).

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unary-resource conflict made unavoidable by temporal windows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For actions \(i\) and \(j\) sharing a unary resource, feasibility requires the separation disjunction
\[
f_i\le s_j\;\lor\;f_j\le s_i.
\]
A resource-temporal conflict lies beyond feasible resolution when the remaining temporal domains make both branches impossible, namely when \(E_j<L_i\) forces \(f_j>s_i\) for every assignment and \(E_i<L_j\) forces \(f_i>s_j\) for every assignment, after duration bounds are applied. More generally, infeasibility occurs whenever every resource-admissible ordering contradicts the temporal constraint closure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coupled conflict becomes fatal when temporal windows rule out every ordering that could separate actions competing for an exclusive resource.
knowledge_statements.title: Resource-Temporal Conflict Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits, but the stated inequalities involving earliest starts and latest finishes do not by themselves force overlap. Duration-aware start and finish bounds and a supporting scheduling source are required.

Binary indicator that fluent \(p\) holds at time \(t\).

Goal constraints are imposed on \(y_{p,H}\). Projection of an integral feasible point onto the positive \(x_{a,t}\) variables yields its scheduled plan.

children.title: Event-Based Planning Formulations
children.top_down_role: Compact planning formulations organized around selected events.

assumptions_latex: At most \(K\) ordered event positions are available.
Each selected action is assigned start and finish events with start preceding finish.
State changes and resource changes occur only at event positions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A feasible integral assignment determines an event sequence whose induced intervals and state transitions constitute a valid bounded-event plan.

notation.meaning: Binary assignment of event \(e\) to position \(k\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounded-event mixed-integer representation without a full time grid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An event-based formulation uses ordered times \(0\le\tau_1\le\cdots\le\tau_K\) and binary variables \(z_{e,k}\) satisfying \(\sum_k z_{e,k}=1\) for each selected event \(e\), with capacity constraints on each position. Channeling constraints assign every selected action's start and finish to positions \(k<\ell\), impose its duration through \(\tau_\ell-\tau_k\), and update logical and numeric state between consecutive positions. Preconditions are enforced at the assigned start position and goals after the final used position.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Actions are assigned to a bounded ordered sequence of timed events, with state transitions enforced only between consecutive event positions.

children.title: Relative-Ordering Planning Formulations
children.top_down_role: Planning formulations organized around precedence choices between selected events.

assumptions_latex: The selected event set is finite.
Every required precedence relation is strict and acyclic.
Continuous event times are used only when metric separation must be recovered.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The binary order variables encode a strict partial order, extendable to a valid total event order.

notation.meaning: Binary indicator that event \(e\) precedes event \(f\).

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pairwise event-order encoding for finite partial-order plans.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A relative-ordering formulation introduces \(o_{ef}\in\{0,1\}\) for distinct selected events \(e,f\in E\). Required comparability is expressed by \(o_{ef}+o_{fe}=1\), and transitivity by
\[
o_{ef}+o_{fg}-1\le o_{eg}.
\]
Fixed causal, duration, and threat-resolution precedences set the corresponding variables to one. When metric times are present, \(o_{ef}=1\) activates \(\tau_e+\delta_{ef}\le\tau_f\). Consequently, any integral feasible assignment defines an acyclic precedence relation and admits a topological event sequence respecting all activated planning constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pairwise binary variables encode event precedence; antisymmetry, transitivity, and activated planning constraints produce a valid extendable event order.
knowledge_statements.title: Relative-Ordering Planning Formulations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The constraints impose pairwise comparability and therefore encode a strict total order, although the conclusion describes a partial order extendable to a total order. The intended formulation requires clarification and a source.

children.title: Disjunctive Planning Formulations
children.top_down_role: Planning formulations representing alternative orderings or mutually exclusive choices.

assumptions_latex: Each planning alternative is representable by a finite system of linear inequalities.
At least one alternative must hold for every modeled conflict or choice.
Finite valid variable bounds are available when a big-\(M\) encoding is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Integral selector assignments satisfy exactly one or more admissible planning alternatives, according to the stated selector constraint.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite union-of-polyhedra encoding of planning choices and conflicts.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 5. Disjunctive Programming and Extended Formulations p. 69

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let each planning alternative be \(P_r=\{x:A_rx\le b_r\}\). The disjunctive requirement is
\[
x\in\bigcup_{r=1}^m P_r.
\]
With valid row bounds \(M_r\), a mixed-integer encoding uses \(z_r\in\{0,1\}\), \(\sum_r z_r\ge1\), and \(A_rx\le b_r+M_r(1-z_r)\). Replacing the selector inequality by equality enforces exactly one branch. Typical branches represent competing event orders, alternative supporters, or mutually exclusive action modes; validity requires each \(M_r\) to dominate the maximum possible row violation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Binary selectors activate one or more polyhedral alternatives representing choices such as event order, causal support, or action mode.
knowledge_statements.title: Disjunctive Planning Formulations

children.title: Compactness Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Size and structural tradeoffs among event-based, ordering-based, or disjunctive formulations.

assumptions_latex: A time-indexed formulation uses \(H\) periods and \(|A|\) action types.
A relative-order formulation uses \(|E|\) selected events.
Both formulations encode the same bounded planning semantics after projection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Smaller formulation size does not imply a stronger linear relaxation or faster solution.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Size-strength tradeoff between time-indexed and compact event-order encodings.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 5. Disjunctive Programming and Extended Formulations p. 69

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under direct indexing, action-start variables in a time-expanded formulation number \(O(|A|H)\), whereas pairwise order variables in a compact event formulation number \(O(|E|^2)\), independently of the numeric horizon. This syntactic compactness has no monotone implication for relaxation strength: big-\(M\) order or disjunction constraints may admit fractional points excluded by a larger time-expanded or convex-hull extended formulation. Conversely, an ideal extended disjunctive formulation may use more variables while projecting to the convex hull of the same integer plans.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Event-order models can avoid horizon-sized variable sets, but fewer variables may come with weaker relaxations; larger extended formulations can be tighter.
knowledge_statements.title: Compactness Tradeoffs

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 5. Disjunctive Programming and Extended Formulations p. 69

children.title: Planning Decomposition Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Separation of plan structure from temporal, resource, or numeric feasibility.

assumptions_latex: Planning decisions split into structural variables \(x\) and feasibility variables \(y\).
For fixed \(x\), temporal, resource, or numeric feasibility is decidable by a subproblem.
Any returned feasibility or optimality cut is valid for every admissible structural assignment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Iterating valid master cuts preserves every globally feasible plan and terminates on finite structural domains unless no feasible structure exists.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent the integrated model as structural constraints \(x\in X\) and subordinate constraints \(F(x,y)\le0\). A master problem proposes \(\bar x\in X\); the subproblem either returns \(\bar y\) with \(F(\bar x,\bar y)\le0\), or a valid cut \(g(x)\le0\) violated by \(\bar x\) but satisfied by every \(x\) admitting some feasible \(y\). Adding such cuts creates an exact planning interface: structural choices remain in the master, while temporal, resource, or numeric feasibility remains in the subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A master chooses plan structure; subordinate solvers either complete it with feasible timing and resources or return a globally valid rejecting cut.

children.title: Theory-Coupled Planning Interface
children.top_down_role: Planning interfaces combining Boolean structure with arithmetic, temporal, or transition theories.

children.title: SMT Planning
children.top_down_role: Planning compilations combining Boolean structure with selected background theories.

knowledge_statements.title: SMT Planning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounded deterministic planning compiled into satisfiability modulo theories.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each horizon \(h\in\{0,\ldots,H\}\), introduce state copies \(X^0,\ldots,X^h\) and action-selection variables \(U^0,\ldots,U^{h-1}\), and define \[\Phi_h:=I(X^0)\land G(X^h)\land\bigwedge_{t=0}^{h-1}\operatorname{Step}_T(X^t,U^t,X^{t+1}),\] where \(\operatorname{Step}_T\) enforces action choice, preconditions, theory-valued effects, and frame constraints. Define \[\Phi_{\leq H}:=\bigvee_{h=0}^{H}\Phi_h.\] A \(T\)-model of \(\Phi_{\leq H}\) decodes to an executable action sequence of length at most \(H\) reaching \(G\); conversely, every such plan induces a \(T\)-model. Thus bounded plan existence is equivalent to \(T\)-satisfiability of \(\Phi_{\leq H}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: SMT planning encodes every permitted plan length from zero through H so that satisfying theory models correspond exactly to executable plans of length at most H.
assumptions_latex: \(P=(X,A,I,G)\) is a deterministic finite-horizon planning instance.
Each action transition and state constraint is expressible in a fixed background theory \(T\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P\) has a plan of length at most \(H\) if and only if \(\Phi_{\leq H}\) is \(T\)-satisfiable.

notation.meaning: planning instance with variables, actions, initial condition, and goal
bounded SMT encoding for plan lengths at most H

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: bounded planning is routinely represented by satisfiability modulo a background theory

children.title: Hybrid Constraint Planning
children.top_down_role: Planning models spanning discrete choices plus richer temporal, numeric, or continuous structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Constraint Planning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-horizon planning over discrete modes and continuous state variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A hybrid constraint planning instance has states \((q,x)\in Q\times\mathbb{R}^n\), an initial state set \(I\), a goal set \(G\), and guarded action relations \(R_a\subseteq(Q\times\mathbb{R}^n)^2\). A length-\(H\) hybrid plan is a sequence \((a_0,\ldots,a_{H-1})\) together with states \((q_t,x_t)\) satisfying \[(q_0,x_0)\in I,\qquad ((q_t,x_t),(q_{t+1},x_{t+1}))\in R_{a_t}\ \text{for all }t<H,\qquad(q_H,x_H)\in G.\] Discrete action selection and continuous witnesses are therefore solved jointly rather than in separate, independently validated stages.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hybrid constraint planning jointly chooses discrete actions and continuous state witnesses satisfying guarded transitions from an initial set to a goal set.
assumptions_latex: The planning state is \((q,x)\in Q\times\mathbb{R}^n\), with finite mode set \(Q\).
Each action supplies a guarded continuous-state transition relation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A hybrid plan is feasible exactly when every selected guarded transition and the terminal goal constraint hold.

notation.meaning: guarded transition relation for action a

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: hybrid planning combines discrete action choices with continuous feasibility relations

children.title: Theory-Coupled Planning
children.top_down_role: Planning architectures classified by the theory solvers attached to their Boolean layer.

assumptions_latex: \(B\) is a finite set of Boolean planning atoms.
\(T\) is a background theory with a decidable satisfiability procedure for the selected fragment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The coupled encoding is feasible exactly when its Boolean plan skeleton has a jointly consistent \(T\)-theory assignment.

notation.meaning: theory constraint activated by literal l

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: theory coupling links propositional planning decisions to constraints interpreted by a background theory
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interface between propositional plan structure and background-theory feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A theory-coupled planning model consists of a Boolean planning skeleton over \(B\), a background theory \(T\), and a mapping assigning selected literals \(l\) theory formulas \(C_l\). For a Boolean assignment \(\beta\), its induced theory context is \[C(\beta):=\bigwedge_{l:\,\beta(l)=1}C_l.\] The assignment represents a feasible bounded plan precisely when it satisfies the propositional initial, transition, frame, and goal constraints and \(C(\beta)\) is satisfiable in \(T\). A theory conflict is any clause validly excluding a Boolean selection whose induced context is \(T\)-inconsistent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Theory-coupled planning accepts a propositional plan skeleton only when all theory constraints activated by its selected literals are jointly satisfiable.
knowledge_statements.title: Theory-Coupled Planning

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the theory-coupled planning interface and is internally coherent, but no citation is supplied. The local inventory contains optimization sources rather than inspectable planning or SMT-planning support for this formulation.

children.title: Mixed Discrete-Continuous Planning
children.top_down_role: Planning regimes involving discrete actions plus continuous quantities or dynamics.

knowledge_statements.title: Mixed Discrete-Continuous Planning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint finite-horizon feasibility model with discrete decisions and continuous trajectories.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z\in D^m\) encode finite-domain action or mode choices and let \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\) collect continuous states, controls, durations, or resources across horizon \(H\). Mixed discrete-continuous planning represents plan existence by \[z\in D^m,\qquad x\in\mathbb{R}^n,\qquad F(z,x),\qquad I(z,x),\qquad G(z,x),\] where \(F\) contains transition, coupling, and invariant constraints. A feasible pair \((z,x)\) decodes to a discrete plan skeleton and a compatible continuous trajectory. Fixing \(z\) leaves its continuous feasibility subproblem; infeasibility of that subproblem invalidates the skeleton.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mixed discrete-continuous planning seeks discrete action choices and continuous trajectories that jointly satisfy transition, coupling, initial, and goal constraints.
assumptions_latex: The horizon \(H\) is finite.
Discrete choices are encoded by \(z\), and continuous states or controls by \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A plan exists exactly when the mixed-domain constraint system has a feasible point satisfying the initial and goal restrictions.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: mixed discrete-continuous planning is represented by joint finite-domain and real-valued feasibility constraints

children.title: Native Planning Search Families
children.top_down_role: Planning-specific search spaces, reachability structures, and heuristic families that complement constraint compilation.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: State-Space Planning; Plan-Space Planning; Planning-Graph Techniques; Heuristics

children.title: State-Space Planning
children.top_down_role: Search over explicit or symbolic representations of reachable states.

children.title: Progression Planning
children.top_down_role: Forward exploration from the initial state.

knowledge_statements.title: Progression Planning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic forward state-space search with duplicate detection over a finite reachable state space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize the frontier by \(F:=\{s_0\}\), record an empty predecessor map, and maintain a closed set \(C:=\varnothing\). Repeatedly remove a state \(s\) from \(F\). If \(G(s)\) holds, follow predecessor labels back to \(s_0\) and return the resulting action sequence. Otherwise add \(s\) to \(C\); for every action \(a\) satisfying \(\operatorname{app}(a,s)\), compute \(s':=\gamma(s,a)\) and insert any undiscovered \(s'\) into \(F\) with predecessor \((s,a)\). Return failure when \(F=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Progression planning searches forward through a finite reachable state space, generating applicable-action successors until it reaches a goal or exhausts all reachable states.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is a state set with initial state \(s_0\), and only finitely many states are reachable from \(s_0\).
Each action \(a\) has applicability predicate \(\operatorname{app}(a,s)\) and deterministic successor \(\gamma(s,a)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm terminates and returns an action sequence reaching \(G\), or failure after exhausting all states reachable from \(s_0\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: progression is the standard forward state-space planning procedure

children.title: Regression Planning
children.top_down_role: Backward exploration from goal conditions.

assumptions_latex: States are sets of true propositional atoms under closed-world semantics.
Each action \(a\) has preconditions \(\operatorname{pre}(a)\), additions \(\operatorname{add}(a)\), and deletions \(\operatorname{del}(a)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Regression yields predecessor conditions whose satisfaction guarantees that applying the selected action establishes the current subgoal.

notation.meaning: regression of Y through action a

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: STRIPS regression is the standard backward state-space planning operation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Backward search for propositional STRIPS planning with conjunctive subgoals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize the backward frontier with the goal atom set \(Y_0:=G\). An action \(a\) is relevant and consistent for \(Y\) when \(\operatorname{add}(a)\cap Y\neq\varnothing\) and \(\operatorname{del}(a)\cap Y=\varnothing\). Its regressed subgoal is \[\operatorname{Reg}(Y,a):=(Y\setminus\operatorname{add}(a))\cup\operatorname{pre}(a).\] Search over such subgoals, recording the chosen actions. When some generated \(Y\) satisfies \(Y\subseteq I\), return the recorded actions in forward order. If every backward frontier is exhausted, return failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Regression planning works backward from the goal, replacing supported goal atoms by an action's preconditions until the initial state satisfies the subgoal.
knowledge_statements.title: Regression Planning

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The STRIPS regression rule, relevance and consistency conditions, algorithm role, and local scope are mutually consistent. No source with an inspectable planning locator is supplied, so the precise rule and algorithm cannot be accepted as sourced candidate-review knowledge.

children.title: Compressed-Frontier Planning Search
children.top_down_role: Set-based or two-frontier exploration of planning state spaces.

children.title: Symbolic State-Set Planning
children.top_down_role: Planning search over compact representations of state sets.

assumptions_latex: The planning state space is represented by valuations of finitely many variables.
A symbolic transition relation \(T(X,U,X')\) and initial formula \(I(X)\) are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The iteration returns the least reachable-state layers and detects a plan when a layer intersects the goal set.

notation.meaning: symbolic reached set through depth k

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: symbolic reachability computes image sets rather than enumerating individual states
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Forward planning by symbolic image computation over finite-state valuations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Set \(F_0(X):=I(X)\) and \(R_0(X):=F_0(X)\). For \(k\geq0\), test whether \(F_k(X)\land G(X)\) is satisfiable. If so, recover a plan by retaining transition witnesses or by backward image extraction. Otherwise compute \[F_{k+1}(X'):=\left(\exists X,U\;[F_k(X)\land T(X,U,X')]\right)\land\neg R_k(X'),\qquad R_{k+1}:=R_k\lor F_{k+1}.\] Stop with failure when \(F_{k+1}\) is unsatisfiable. Each formula denotes a set of states, so the frontier is manipulated without explicit state enumeration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Symbolic state-set planning advances whole sets of states by quantified image computation, removes previously reached states, and tests each frontier against the goal.
knowledge_statements.title: Symbolic State-Set Planning

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The symbolic-image algorithm fits the leaf and correctly distinguishes frontier and reached sets under the stated finite-state assumption. It lacks a cited symbolic-planning or symbolic-reachability source with a specific locator.

children.title: Bidirectional Planning Search
children.top_down_role: Planning search using forward and backward exploration frontiers.

assumptions_latex: The transition system is finite and deterministic actions admit a sound predecessor relation.
Forward and backward search use compatible state or condition representations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A compatible frontier intersection yields a valid concatenation of a forward prefix and a backward suffix.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: bidirectional planning combines forward progression and backward regression at a compatible meeting point
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-state search combining progression from the initial state and regression from the goal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize a forward frontier at \(I\) and a backward frontier at \(G\), with reached sets \(R_f\) and \(R_b\). Repeatedly expand one frontier using progression or regression, commonly choosing the smaller estimated expansion. After each expansion, test whether there exist \(s\in R_f\) and \(Y\in R_b\) with \(s\sim Y\), where compatibility means that \(s\) satisfies the backward condition \(Y\). At the first accepted meeting, concatenate the recorded forward action sequence with the recorded backward suffix. Return failure only after the finite reachable search regions are exhausted without a compatible pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bidirectional planning alternates forward and backward expansion until a reached state satisfies a regressed goal condition, then joins the two action sequences.
knowledge_statements.title: Bidirectional Planning Search

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm appropriately combines progression and regression using satisfaction-based compatibility. No inspectable source is supplied for the stated joining and exhaustion claims.

children.title: Frontier-Meeting Conditions
children.top_down_role: Compatibility criteria governing when opposing planning frontiers can be joined.

assumptions_latex: Every forward node stores a valid prefix from the initial state.
Every backward node stores a sufficient condition and a valid suffix to the goal.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A pair \((s,Y)\) is a sound meeting point when \(s\models Y\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: state satisfaction of a regressed goal condition is the canonical sound meeting test
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sound compatibility test for joining progression and regression frontiers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a forward node contain a state \(s\) reached by prefix \(\pi_f\), and let a backward node contain a condition \(Y\) with suffix \(\pi_b\) such that every state satisfying \(Y\) can execute \(\pi_b\) and reach the goal. The frontier-meeting condition is \[s\models Y.\] Under the stored-node invariants, this condition certifies that \(\pi_f\cdot\pi_b\) is a valid complete plan. For set-valued frontiers represented by formulas \(F(X)\) and \(B(X)\), existence of a meeting is equivalently satisfiability of \(F(X)\land B(X)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Forward and backward frontiers meet when a forward-reached state satisfies a backward condition that guarantees execution of the stored goal-reaching suffix.
knowledge_statements.title: Frontier-Meeting Conditions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition content kind matches the exact leaf, and the state-satisfaction test is sound under the explicitly stated stored-node invariants. A planning-specific citation with a section, theorem, or page locator is absent.

children.title: Symbolic Frontier Compression
children.top_down_role: Compact organization of reachable or predecessor frontiers during planning search.

assumptions_latex: The state space consists of valuations over finitely many variables \(X\).
The representation language supports Boolean operations and satisfiability testing.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A formula \(F(X)\) is an exact frontier compression when its models are precisely the frontier states.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: characteristic formulas canonically compress finite state sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact characteristic-formula representation of a finite planning frontier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an explicit frontier \(\mathcal{F}\) of states over variables \(X\), a symbolic frontier compression is a formula \(F(X)\) satisfying \[\operatorname{Mod}(F)=\{\nu_s:s\in\mathcal{F}\}.\] Equivalently, for every state \(s\), \(s\in\mathcal{F}\) if and only if \(\nu_s\models F\). The formula may share subexpressions, omit irrelevant variables, or use a canonical decision structure; exactness concerns only its model set. Union, intersection, and exclusion of frontiers are then represented by \(\lor\), \(\land\), and conjunction with negation, respectively.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Symbolic frontier compression replaces an explicit state collection by a formula whose satisfying valuations are exactly those frontier states.
knowledge_statements.title: Symbolic Frontier Compression

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exact characteristic-formula representation fits symbolic frontier compression and is internally consistent. No cited source supports the representation and its Boolean operations in the planning context.

children.title: Causal-Link Plan-Space Refinement
children.top_down_role: Refinement search over partial plans and causal commitments.

children.title: Partial-Plan Refinement
children.top_down_role: Refinement through open-condition, action, binding, and ordering choices.

assumptions_latex: Actions have preconditions and effects, and plans permit partial ordering.
A partial plan records steps, bindings, ordering constraints, and causal links.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Refinement terminates successfully at a consistent partial plan with no open conditions or unresolved threats.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: partial-order planning refines flaws by adding support, bindings, and ordering constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Least-commitment causal-link refinement for deterministic partial-order plans.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(P\) with distinguished start and finish steps, ordering start before finish, and the goal literals as finish preconditions. While \(\operatorname{Open}(P)\neq\varnothing\), select an open condition \(p\) of a consumer step, choose or introduce a step whose effect unifies with \(p\), and add the required binding, ordering, and causal-link constraints. While \(\operatorname{Threat}(P)\neq\varnothing\), resolve a selected threat by a sound ordering or binding refinement. Reject any refinement with inconsistent bindings or cyclic ordering. Output \(P\) when both flaw sets are empty; report failure when no refinement branch remains.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partial-plan refinement repeatedly supports open conditions and resolves threats while preserving consistent bindings and acyclic orderings, stopping when no flaws remain.
knowledge_statements.title: Partial-Plan Refinement

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits partial-plan refinement, and the open-condition and threat refinements match the stated deterministic partial-order scope. No authoritative plan-space planning citation with a specific locator is provided.

children.title: Causal-Commitment Protection Calculus
children.top_down_role: Maintenance of causal links and resolution of interfering commitments.

children.title: Causal-Support Management
children.top_down_role: Maintenance of support commitments within partial plans.

assumptions_latex: \(P\) is a partial-order plan with steps and ordering relation \(\prec\).
Every supported precondition is represented by a causal link.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Causal-support management is complete for the current partial plan when every precondition has a protected supporting link.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: causal-link planning requires support for every precondition and protection against intervening deletion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Support and protection predicate for causal-link partial-order plans.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A precondition literal \(p\) of step \(s_j\) is causally supported when there exists a step \(s_i\) such that \(p\in\operatorname{eff}(s_i)\), \(s_i\prec s_j\), and the plan contains the link \(s_i\xrightarrow{p}s_j\). The link is protected when every step \(s_k\) capable of making \(p\) false is constrained by \[s_k\prec s_i\quad\text{or}\quad s_j\prec s_k,\] or is excluded by inconsistent bindings. Causal-support management is complete exactly when every step precondition has at least one such protected link and all associated ordering and binding constraints are jointly consistent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Causal-support management requires each step precondition to have an earlier supporting effect whose causal link is protected from every possible intervening deleter.

children.title: Planning Threat Detection
children.top_down_role: Identification of actions or commitments that can disrupt causal support.

knowledge_statements.title: Planning Threat Detection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Threat predicate for a causal link in a partially ordered plan.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(a_p\xrightarrow{p}a_c\) be a causal link, meaning that action \(a_p\) establishes literal \(p\) for consumer \(a_c\), and let \(\prec\) be the plan's strict precedence relation. An action \(a_t\) is a threat to this link exactly when it has an effect inconsistent with \(p\) and can occur between the producer and consumer:
\[
\operatorname{Threat}(a_t,a_p,p,a_c)\iff \neg p\in\operatorname{Eff}(a_t)\ \land\ \neg(a_t\prec a_p)\ \land\ \neg(a_c\prec a_t).
\]
For non-ground actions, the effect condition means that some consistent binding unifies an effect of \(a_t\) with \(\neg p\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An action threatens a causal link when it can negate the supported literal and the current ordering still permits it between the link's producer and consumer.
assumptions_latex: \(\prec\) is a consistent strict partial order on plan actions.
Effects are literals, with inconsistency represented by complementation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Threat}(a_t,a_p,p,a_c)\) holds exactly under the displayed effect and ordering conditions.

notation.meaning: Causal link whose producer establishes literal p for its consumer.

review_flags: No supplied locator addresses partial-order causal-link planning; an authoritative planning reference is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits threat detection and is plausible, but no cited source or locator supports its ground and lifted formulations.

children.title: Planning Threat Resolution
children.top_down_role: Resolution families based on ordering, separation, binding, or plan refinement.

knowledge_statements.title: Planning Threat Resolution
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard promotion, demotion, and separation refinements for detected threats.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a consistent partial plan containing a threat \(a_t\) to \(a_p\xrightarrow{p}a_c\), generate one child for each applicable repair: promotion adds \(a_c\prec a_t\); demotion adds \(a_t\prec a_p\); and, for lifted actions, separation adds binding constraints that prevent every threatening effect from unifying with \(\neg p\). Reject any child whose ordering or binding constraints are inconsistent. Continue refining unresolved threats; output a plan only when every causal link is threat-free. The branching rule is
\[
\mathcal R=\{a_c\prec a_t,\ a_t\prec a_p,\ \text{separating bindings}\}\cap\{\text{consistent refinements}\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Resolve a threat by ordering it after the consumer, before the producer, or by imposing bindings that eliminate the threatening unification; discard inconsistent refinements.
assumptions_latex: The input partial plan has a detected threat to \(a_p\xrightarrow{p}a_c\).
Ordering and binding consistency are decidable for the planning language.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every retained refinement excludes the identified action from threatening the specified causal link.

notation.meaning: Set of applicable consistent threat repairs.

review_flags: No supplied locator supports causal-link threat-resolution refinements.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithmic role and promotion, demotion, and separation branches fit the leaf, but no inspectable planning reference is cited.

children.title: Causal-Commitment Protection
children.top_down_role: Constraint structures preserving established causal support during refinement.

knowledge_statements.title: Causal-Commitment Protection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity condition protecting every causal commitment in a partial-order plan.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A partial plan \(P=(A,\prec,L,B)\), with actions \(A\), ordering constraints \(\prec\), causal links \(L\), and binding constraints \(B\), protects its causal commitments when
\[
\forall(a_p\xrightarrow{p}a_c)\in L\ \forall a_t\in A:\quad
\neg p\in\operatorname{Eff}(a_t)\Rightarrow
(a_t\prec a_p)\lor(a_c\prec a_t)\lor\operatorname{Sep}_B(a_t,\neg p).
\]
Here \(\operatorname{Sep}_B(a_t,\neg p)\) means that \(B\) makes every complementary effect of \(a_t\) non-unifiable with \(p\). Thus no linearization or binding completion admitted by the partial plan places an effective clobberer between a link's endpoints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every causal link is protected when each possible clobberer is forced before its producer, after its consumer, or separated by binding constraints.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) has consistent ordering and binding constraints.
Every causal support commitment is represented in \(L\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P\) admits no unresolved threat to any link in \(L\).

notation.meaning: Partial plan with actions, ordering, causal links, and bindings.

review_flags: No supplied locator covers the causal-commitment protection invariant.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The protection condition fits the container, but its quantified binding-completion interpretation requires an authoritative causal-link planning source.

children.title: Planning-Graph Methods

children.title: Planning-Graph Reachability
children.top_down_role: Layered approximations of reachable facts and actions.

knowledge_statements.title: Planning-Graph Reachability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Leveled Graphplan reachability relaxation for propositional planning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For initial fact set \(F_0=I\), define alternating fact and action layers by
\[
A_i=\{a:\operatorname{Pre}(a)\subseteq F_i\},\qquad
F_{i+1}=F_i\cup\bigcup_{a\in A_i}\operatorname{Add}(a),
\]
including persistence actions. A literal first appearing in \(F_i\) is relaxed-reachable by level \(i\). A set \(S\subseteq F_i\) is planning-graph reachable at level \(i\) only if no pair in \(S\) is mutex there. Consequently, absence of a goal literal from every layer, or persistent mutex among goals after leveling, certifies impossibility within this planning-graph relaxation; presence alone does not certify a plan.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Alternating fact and action layers overapproximate reachability; goals are layer-reachable only when present together without pairwise mutex, but this condition need not yield a plan.
assumptions_latex: The planning task is finite and propositional.
Actions have conjunctive preconditions and add/delete effects.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_i\) overapproximates facts attainable by depth \(i\), while nonmutex co-occurrence is a necessary extraction condition.

notation.meaning: Action layer applicable from fact layer i.

review_flags: The supplied optimization locators do not support Graphplan reachability semantics.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation broadly matches propositional planning graphs, but the reachability and stabilized-mutex impossibility claims have no supporting citation.

children.title: Planning-Graph Mutex Structure
children.top_down_role: Layered exclusion information supporting pruning and compilation.

knowledge_statements.title: Planning-Graph Mutex Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recursive Graphplan mutex relations on action and fact layers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At action layer \(A_i\), distinct actions are mutex if they have inconsistent effects, one deletes an effect or precondition of the other, or some pair of their preconditions is mutex in \(F_i\). At fact layer \(F_{i+1}\), distinct literals \(p,q\) are mutex if every pair \((a,b)\) satisfying \(p\in\operatorname{Add}(a)\) and \(q\in\operatorname{Add}(b)\) is action-mutex. Formally,
\[
\operatorname{Mutex}_{F_{i+1}}(p,q)\iff
\forall a\in\operatorname{Ach}_i(p)\ \forall b\in\operatorname{Ach}_i(q):
\operatorname{Mutex}_{A_i}(a,b).
\]
Persistence actions participate as ordinary achievers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Action mutex records interference or competing needs; fact mutex records inconsistent support when every possible pair of achievers is mutually exclusive.
assumptions_latex: The leveled graph includes persistence actions.
Action and literal layers are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed recursion uniquely determines pairwise mutex relations layer by layer.

notation.meaning: Actions at layer i that add literal p.

review_flags: The supplied source inventory has no planning-graph mutex reference.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The recursive mutex definition fits the leaf and is mathematically plausible, but no planning-graph source with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Graphplan Extraction Algorithm Family
children.top_down_role: Plan extraction and extensions of planning-graph semantics.

children.title: Graphplan Plan Extraction
children.top_down_role: Backward extraction of plans from leveled planning graphs.

knowledge_statements.title: Graphplan Plan Extraction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Backward Graphplan extraction from a fixed nonmutex goal layer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input a planning graph and a level \(k\) where goal set \(G\subseteq F_k\) is pairwise nonmutex. Set \(G_k=G\). For \(i=k-1,\ldots,0\), choose a nonmutex action set \(U_i\subseteq A_i\) such that
\[
G_{i+1}\subseteq\bigcup_{a\in U_i}\operatorname{Add}(a),
\qquad
G_i=\bigcup_{a\in U_i}\operatorname{Pre}(a).
\]
Require \(G_i\) to be pairwise nonmutex in \(F_i\); otherwise backtrack over achiever choices. Memoize failed pairs \((i,G_i)\). Stop successfully when \(G_0\subseteq I\), and output the non-persistence actions in \((U_0,\ldots,U_{k-1})\); report failure after exhausting choices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Work backward from nonmutex goals, selecting nonmutex achievers and replacing goals by their preconditions; backtrack on mutex subgoals and succeed upon reaching the initial state.
assumptions_latex: The input is a finite leveled planning graph.
\(G\subseteq F_k\) is pairwise nonmutex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Success returns a parallel plan of horizon \(k\); exhaustive failure proves that none is represented at that level.

notation.meaning: Subgoal set at fact layer i.
Selected nonmutex actions at action layer i.

review_flags: No supplied locator supports the Graphplan backward-extraction algorithm.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content is appropriately an algorithm and describes standard backward extraction, but its completeness and fixed-horizon conclusion require a cited source.

children.title: Alternative Extraction Policies
children.top_down_role: Variants in candidate selection, conflict handling, or extraction ordering.

knowledge_statements.title: Alternative Extraction Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sound policy variations for ordering Graphplan's backward search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At an extraction state \((i,G_i)\), a policy chooses an unresolved goal \(g\in G_i\) and orders its candidate achievers \(a\in\operatorname{Ach}_{i-1}(g)\). It may prefer, for example, the goal with fewest compatible achievers and the action adding the most unresolved goals. After selecting \(a\), remove every candidate action mutex with \(a\), update the covered goals, and backtrack upon an empty achiever domain. The policy is complete at level \(i\) provided it eventually enumerates every nonmutex achiever set satisfying
\[
G_i\subseteq\bigcup_{a\in U_{i-1}}\operatorname{Add}(a).
\]
Only enumeration order may change; feasibility tests remain unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Alternative policies reorder goals and achievers to reduce search, while completeness is retained only if every feasible nonmutex achiever set can eventually be explored.
assumptions_latex: Candidate achievers and mutex relations are those of a fixed planning graph.
Backtracking is exhaustive unless a sound pruning rule applies.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any policy satisfying exhaustive feasible enumeration returns exactly the same existence answer as standard extraction at the fixed level.

notation.meaning: Candidate achievers of goal g in the preceding action layer.

review_flags: No supplied locator identifies or validates Graphplan extraction-policy variants.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithmic role fits, but the proposed policy examples and equivalence under exhaustive enumeration lack an inspectable source.

children.title: Extended Planning-Graph Semantics
children.top_down_role: Planning-graph extensions supporting richer actions, constraints, or plan criteria.

knowledge_statements.title: Extended Planning-Graph Semantics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conservative extension criterion for enriched planning-graph layers and extraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let an extended planning graph use layer labels \(X_i\) and compatibility relation \(M_i\), possibly carrying numeric, temporal, resource, or conditional-effect information. Its semantics are extraction-sound when every accepted layer transition corresponds to an executable parallel action set:
\[
\operatorname{Accept}_i(U,X_i,M_i)\Rightarrow
\exists s_i,s_{i+1}:\ s_i\models X_i,\ U\text{ is jointly applicable in }s_i,\ s_{i+1}=\gamma(s_i,U).
\]
Backward extraction must propagate all extended preconditions and reject every set violating \(M_i\). If projection \(\pi\) forgets the added annotations, conservativity additionally requires every extended layer and mutex judgment to project to a valid ordinary planning-graph judgment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An enriched planning graph is sound only when accepted action sets denote executable transitions, extraction propagates all added constraints, and forgetting annotations recovers valid ordinary semantics.
assumptions_latex: The transition function \(\gamma\) is defined for jointly applicable action sets.
The extension supplies a projection \(\pi\) to ordinary propositional planning.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Accepted extended extractions project to ordinary valid extractions and denote executable transitions under the enriched semantics.
review_flags: The node does not specify which extended planning-graph formalism is intended.
No supplied locator supports temporal, numeric, resource, or conditional-effect extensions.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The generic representation does not identify a particular extended planning-graph formalism, and its projection and extraction conclusions are not secured by cited semantics.

children.title: Extraction Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Graph levels or support structures from which no compatible plan can be extracted.

knowledge_statements.title: Extraction Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes fixed-level extraction failure from global planning unsolvability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(E(k,G)\) denote exhaustive Graphplan extraction for goals \(G\) from fact layer \(F_k\). Failure of \(E(k,G)\) establishes only that no plan of parallel horizon \(k\) is represented by that graph prefix:
\[
E(k,G)=\operatorname{fail}\ \not\Rightarrow\ \text{the planning task is unsolvable}.
\]
A longer plan may exist, so the graph must be extended. Global failure is justified only after the graph has leveled off—fact layers and mutex relations are unchanged—and exhaustive extraction has failed without producing any new subgoal sets beyond previously memoized failures. Pairwise nonmutex goals at \(F_k\) likewise do not guarantee extraction success because higher-order support conflicts may remain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Failure at one layer excludes only that horizon. Unsolvability follows only after graph and failed-subgoal information stabilize; pairwise nonmutex goals alone need not be jointly achievable.
assumptions_latex: Extraction at each tested level is exhaustive.
The planning task and resulting planning graph are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Fixed-level failure is horizon-relative; stabilized graph and memoized-failure conditions are required for a global negative conclusion.

notation.meaning: Exhaustive extraction of goals G at level k.

review_flags: No supplied locator supports Graphplan's fixed-point termination and extraction-failure conditions.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind is correct, but the global-unsolvability criterion involving graph and memoized-failure stabilization needs a specific Graphplan reference.

children.title: Heuristic Planning Search
children.top_down_role: Planning search guided by relaxations, abstractions, landmarks, novelty, or learned estimates.

children.title: Delete-Relaxation Heuristics
children.top_down_role: Heuristic families derived from monotone relaxations of action effects.

knowledge_statements.title: Delete-Relaxation Heuristics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Heuristics obtained by removing negative effects from a classical planning task.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a finite classical planning task \(\Pi=(F,A,I,G,c)\), its delete relaxation \(\Pi^+\) replaces each action \(a\) by one having the same preconditions, add effects, and cost, but no delete effects. For state \(s\), define
\[
h^+(s)=\min\left\{\sum_{a\in P}c(a):P\text{ achieves }G\text{ from }s\text{ in }\Pi^+\right\},
\]
with value \(+\infty\) if no relaxed plan exists. Practical delete-relaxation heuristics such as maximum, additive, and relaxed-plan heuristics approximate this value by different cost-propagation or plan-extraction rules. Because every original plan is a relaxed plan, \(h^+(s)\) is a lower bound on optimal original plan cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Delete relaxation removes all negative effects. Its optimal relaxed-plan cost lower-bounds true plan cost, while common heuristics approximate it by propagation or relaxed extraction.
assumptions_latex: Action costs satisfy \(c(a)\ge 0\).
The task is finite, deterministic, and propositional.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(h^+(s)\le h^*(s)\) for every state \(s\).

notation.meaning: Optimal cost in the original task.

review_flags: The supplied relaxation sources concern mathematical programming rather than delete-relaxed planning heuristics.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and lower-bound claim fit delete-relaxation heuristics, but the supplied inventory contains no planning source supporting them.

children.title: Abstract-State Pattern Heuristic Family
children.top_down_role: Heuristic families derived from abstract state spaces and pattern databases.

children.title: Planning Abstraction Heuristics
children.top_down_role: Heuristics derived from simplified planning state spaces.

knowledge_statements.title: Planning Abstraction Heuristics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Admissible heuristic induced by a cost-preserving state-space homomorphism.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let a planning task induce a weighted transition system \((S,T,c)
i(s,a,s')\), and let \(\alpha:S\to\bar S\) map concrete states to abstract states. Suppose every concrete transition \((s,a,s')\) has an abstract transition \((\alpha(s),a,\alpha(s'))\) of cost at most \(c(a)\), and every concrete goal maps to an abstract goal. Define
\[
h_\alpha(s)=\operatorname{dist}_{\bar T}(\alpha(s),\bar G).
\]
Then \(h_\alpha(s)\le h^*(s)\) for all \(s\). Moreover, the abstract distance satisfies consistency: for every concrete transition \((s,a,s')\),
\[
h_\alpha(s)\le c(a)+h_\alpha(s').
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Shortest distance to an abstract goal is admissible and consistent when every concrete transition and goal has a no-more-expensive abstract image.
assumptions_latex: The abstraction preserves every concrete transition with no greater cost.
Concrete goal states map into \(\bar G\).
All transition costs are nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(h_\alpha\) is an admissible and consistent planning heuristic.
review_flags: No supplied locator addresses state-space abstraction heuristics for planning.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property role fits abstraction heuristics, and the assumptions plausibly imply admissibility and consistency, but no authoritative locator is supplied.

children.title: Pattern-Database Heuristics
children.top_down_role: Heuristics based on stored distances for selected state-variable patterns.

knowledge_statements.title: Pattern-Database Heuristics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact abstract distances stored for a selected pattern of planning variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a finite-domain planning task with variables \(V\), choose a pattern \(P\subseteq V\) and let \(\alpha_P(s)=s|_P\) be projection onto the pattern variables. Construct the projected transition system by retaining every projected image of a concrete transition with cost no greater than its concrete cost. The pattern database stores, for each abstract state \(x\),
\[
\operatorname{PDB}_P(x)=\operatorname{dist}(x,\bar G_P).
\]
The heuristic is \(h_P(s)=\operatorname{PDB}_P(\alpha_P(s))\). With nonnegative action costs and this transition-preserving projection, \(h_P\) is admissible and consistent; unreachable abstract goals give value \(+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pattern database precomputes exact goal distances after projecting states onto selected variables; table lookup yields an admissible, consistent heuristic under cost-preserving projection.
assumptions_latex: The planning task has finitely many finite-domain variables.
Projected transitions cost no more than their concrete antecedents.
Action costs are nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(h_P(s)\le h^*(s)\) and \(h_P(s)\le c(a)+h_P(s')\) for every transition \((s,a,s')\).

notation.meaning: Table of exact abstract goal distances.

review_flags: No supplied locator supports pattern-database construction or its admissibility conditions.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits pattern-database heuristics, but construction, admissibility, consistency, and infinite-value conventions require a cited planning reference.

children.title: Additive Pattern Collections
children.top_down_role: Collections of patterns whose heuristic contributions can be combined under suitable independence structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Additive Pattern Collections
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Admissibility of summed pattern-database estimates under action-cost partitioning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let patterns be \(P_1,\ldots,P_m\), let \(c(a)\ge 0\) be each concrete action cost, and assign abstract costs \(c_i(a)\ge 0\) satisfying \(\sum_{i=1}^m c_i(a)\le c(a)\) for every action \(a\). If \(h_i(s)\) is the optimal goal distance from the abstraction of \(s\) for pattern \(P_i\), computed using \(c_i\), then the additive pattern heuristic \(h_{\mathrm{add}}(s)=\sum_{i=1}^m h_i(s)\) is admissible: \[h_{\mathrm{add}}(s)\le h^*(s).\] Disjoint affected-variable patterns with each action cost assigned to at most one pattern are a sufficient special case.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pattern estimates may be summed admissibly when their abstract action costs form a nonnegative partition dominated by each concrete action cost.
assumptions_latex: \(c(a)\ge 0\) for every concrete action \(a\).
Each pattern abstraction is transition preserving and goal respecting.
\(\sum_i c_i(a)\le c(a)\) for every action \(a\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(h_{\mathrm{add}}(s)=\sum_i h_i(s)\le h^*(s)\).

notation.meaning: Cost allocated to action a in pattern i.
Optimal concrete cost from state s to a goal.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: cost-partitioned sums of abstraction distances are standard admissible planning heuristics
