children.title: Abstraction-Loss Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Regimes where removed planning structure weakens heuristic discrimination.

knowledge_statements.title: Abstraction-Loss Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantifies the potentially unbounded information loss of transition-preserving planning abstractions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a goal-respecting transition abstraction \(\alpha:S\to\bar S\), the abstract optimal distance satisfies \(h_\alpha(s)\le h^*(s)\), but no nontrivial multiplicative accuracy follows from transition preservation alone. For each \(n\ge 1\), consider the unit-cost chain \(s_0\to s_1\to\cdots\to s_n\), with sole goal \(s_n\). Map \(s_0,\ldots,s_{n-1}\) to one abstract non-goal state and map \(s_n\) to an abstract goal. Then \(h^*(s_0)=n\) while \(h_\alpha(s_0)=1\). Thus the additive loss is \(n-1\), and the ratio \(h^*(s_0)/h_\alpha(s_0)=n\) is unbounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A transition-preserving abstraction remains admissible but can underestimate arbitrarily badly by merging states at very different concrete goal distances.
assumptions_latex: All chain transitions have unit cost.
The abstraction preserves induced transitions and distinguishes the goal image from the merged non-goal image.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(h_\alpha(s_0)=1\le n=h^*(s_0)\), with unbounded ratio as \(n\to\infty\).

notation.meaning: Optimal distance in the abstract transition system.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: homomorphic relaxation yields admissibility but not bounded approximation quality

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The chain example correctly expresses an abstraction-loss boundary, but the admissibility premise and unbounded-loss claim have no cited source or locator.

children.title: Landmark-Ordering Heuristic Family
children.top_down_role: Guidance based on necessary subgoals and their ordering relations.

children.title: Landmark Heuristics
children.top_down_role: Planning guidance based on necessary facts, actions, or disjunctive subgoals.

knowledge_statements.title: Landmark Heuristics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An admissible weighted landmark lower bound using achiever-cost constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal L_s\) be landmarks not yet accepted on a search path to state \(s\), where every completion from that path must achieve each \(L\in\mathcal L_s\). Let \(A(L)\) contain actions capable of achieving \(L\). Choose weights \(y_L\ge 0\) such that \(\sum_{L\in\mathcal L_s:a\in A(L)}y_L\le c(a)\) for every action \(a\). Then \[h_{\mathrm{LM}}(s)=\sum_{L\in\mathcal L_s}y_L\le h^*(s).\] The action inequalities prevent charging one action more than its cost when it can achieve several landmarks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative landmark weights give an admissible lower bound when every action covers no more total landmark weight than its cost.
assumptions_latex: Every \(L\in\mathcal L_s\) is necessary for every valid completion.
Action costs satisfy \(c(a)\ge 0\).
The displayed achiever-cost inequalities hold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(h_{\mathrm{LM}}(s)=\sum_{L\in\mathcal L_s}y_L\le h^*(s)\).

notation.meaning: Landmarks still required from the current search path.
Actions capable of achieving landmark L.
Nonnegative cost assigned to landmark L.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: landmark cost partitioning is a standard admissible lower-bound construction

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The overlap-aware landmark weighting is a plausible admissible property and matches the container, but authoritative support for the precise achiever-cost formulation is absent.

children.title: Landmark-Ordering Heuristics
children.top_down_role: Planning guidance derived from precedence relations among landmarks.

knowledge_statements.title: Landmark-Ordering Heuristics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Path-dependent search guidance from sound precedence relations among landmarks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a landmark set \(\mathcal L\), a sound precedence relation \(\prec\), and a search node carrying state \(s\) and accepted set \(X\subseteq\mathcal L\). Initialize \(X\) with initially satisfied landmarks. After each transition, add every satisfied landmark \(L\) whose predecessors under \(\prec\) are already accepted. Define \(R=\mathcal L\setminus X\), \(E=\{L\in R: \operatorname{Pred}(L)\subseteq X\}\), and the ordering key \(k(s,X)=(|R|,-|E|)\). Expand nodes lexicographically by \(k\), subject to the underlying search algorithm's primary cost key, and return a plan when a goal node is selected.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Track accepted landmarks along each path and prefer nodes with fewer remaining landmarks and more precedence-eligible next landmarks.
assumptions_latex: \(\prec\) contains only sound necessary precedence relations.
The accepted set is stored per search path rather than inferred solely from the current state.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(k(s,X)=(|\mathcal L\setminus X|,-|\{L\notin X:\operatorname{Pred}(L)\subseteq X\}|)\) defines the guidance order.

notation.meaning: Landmarks accepted along the current search path.
Remaining landmarks whose predecessors are accepted.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind and path-dependent landmark-ordering role fit, but the particular lexicographic key is an unsupported local algorithmic construction rather than a cited standard method.

children.title: Necessary-Subgoal Guidance
children.top_down_role: Search guidance emphasizing subgoals required by every admissible plan.

knowledge_statements.title: Necessary-Subgoal Guidance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses sound landmark precedences to expose necessary next-subgoal candidates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be the landmarks accepted along a partial plan and let \(R=\mathcal L\setminus X\). If every \(L\in\mathcal L\) is a landmark and every relation \(K\prec L\) means that \(K\) must be first achieved before \(L\), then each valid completion must achieve all members of \(R\). Moreover, any landmark first achieved next must belong to the frontier \[F_X=\{L\in R:\operatorname{Pred}(L)\subseteq X\}.\] Prioritizing actions that progress toward \(F_X\) is therefore sound guidance. Pruning every action that does not immediately achieve a frontier landmark is not justified by necessity alone and may destroy completeness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unaccepted landmarks are necessary future subgoals, and sound ordering exposes an eligible frontier, but frontier guidance alone does not justify pruning.
assumptions_latex: All members of \(\mathcal L\) are valid landmarks.
Every edge of \(\prec\) is a sound strict first-achievement precedence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every completion achieves \(R\), and its next first-achieved landmark lies in \(F_X\).

notation.meaning: Accepted landmarks on the partial plan.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: sound landmarks are necessary subgoals while heuristic prioritization does not imply safe pruning

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The necessary-subgoal and no-safe-pruning distinction fits the principle container, but the precise first-achievement frontier claim requires authoritative support.

children.title: Landmark Interaction Conflicts
children.top_down_role: Regimes where landmark orderings or achievement choices interfere.

knowledge_statements.title: Landmark Interaction Conflicts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shows why independently counted landmarks require overlap-aware cost allocation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Individual landmark necessity does not make the sum of their separate achievement costs admissible. Consider facts \(p,q\), an empty initial state, goal \(p\land q\), and one action \(a\) of cost \(1\) whose effects add both \(p\) and \(q\). Each singleton \(\{p\}\) and \(\{q\}\) is a fact landmark, and assigning unit cost independently to each gives the estimate \(2\). Nevertheless, the plan \(\langle a\rangle\) achieves both landmarks with optimal cost \(1\). Thus landmark overlap through a shared achiever must be represented by cost partitioning or another interaction constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Summing separate landmark costs can overestimate when one action achieves several landmarks; overlap-aware cost allocation is required.
assumptions_latex: The initial state satisfies neither \(p\) nor \(q\).
Action \(a\) is applicable initially, costs \(1\), and adds both facts.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(h_{\mathrm{naive}}=2>1=h^*\).

notation.meaning: Goal facts that are individually landmarks.
Shared unit-cost achiever of both landmarks.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: shared achievers invalidate naive additive landmark counting

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The shared-achiever counterexample is internally coherent and fits a failure-boundary container, but it is uncited.

children.title: Diversified Planning Guidance Family
children.top_down_role: Guidance based on feature novelty, portfolios, or learned estimates.

children.title: Novelty-Based Planning Guidance
children.top_down_role: Search guidance favoring states with previously unseen feature combinations.

knowledge_statements.title: Novelty-Based Planning Guidance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Width-based guidance using newly observed tuples of true state features.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a feature set \(F\), width bound \(w\), and optional partition map \(b\). For each bucket maintain previously generated states \(H_b\). For a newly generated state \(s\), set \[\operatorname{nov}(s)=\min\{|T|:T\subseteq F(s),\ |T|\le w,\ \forall t\in H_{b(s)},\ T\nsubseteq F(t)\},\] with value \(\infty\) if no such tuple exists. Rank states by increasing novelty, or in iterative-width search retain exactly states with \(\operatorname{nov}(s)\le w\). Insert \(s\) into \(H_{b(s)}\) after testing it, and stop upon selecting a goal; otherwise report failure when the retained frontier is empty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A state is novel when it makes a small feature tuple true that no earlier state in its partition made jointly true.
assumptions_latex: The feature set \(F\) and width bound \(w\ge 1\) are finite.
Novelty histories are maintained separately for each chosen partition bucket.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: States are ordered or retained according to \(\operatorname{nov}(s)\).

notation.meaning: Previously generated states in bucket b.
Size of the smallest newly observed true-feature tuple.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: tuple novelty is the standard basis of width-based planning guidance

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The novelty definition is plausible, but the record combines partitioned novelty ranking and iterative-width retention; a source is needed to validate the exact conventions and algorithmic variant.

children.title: Learned Planning Guidance
children.top_down_role: Search guidance derived from trained value, policy, ranking, or cost estimators.

knowledge_statements.title: Learned Planning Guidance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Completeness boundary for learned scores used only to order an exhaustive search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f_\theta(s)\in\mathbb R\) be any learned score used solely to order nodes in \(\mathrm{OPEN}\). Suppose the reachable state space is finite, duplicate handling does not discard every path to any reachable state, and the base search eventually expands every retained node unless it first finds a goal. Then replacing its tie-breaking or secondary ordering by \(f_\theta\) preserves completeness, independently of prediction accuracy. This conclusion fails if the learned component permanently prunes nodes, suppresses applicable actions, or imposes a finite cutoff: without an additional safety guarantee, a necessary path may then be removed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Arbitrary learned rankings preserve completeness when they only reorder exhaustive search; learned pruning requires a separate safety guarantee.
assumptions_latex: The reachable state space is finite.
The base search is exhaustive over retained nodes.
\(f_\theta\) changes ordering only and never changes retention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Learned reordering preserves completeness; learned pruning need not preserve it.

notation.meaning: Learned priority score for state s.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: ordering does not alter exhaustive-search completeness whereas unsafe pruning can

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The ordering-only completeness boundary is logically plausible and appropriately classified as a property, but no cited search or learned-guidance source supports the stated conditions.

children.title: Portfolio-Based Planning Guidance
children.top_down_role: Search guidance based on selecting or combining multiple planning strategies.

knowledge_statements.title: Portfolio-Based Planning Guidance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Time-sliced coordination of heterogeneous planners with incumbent sharing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input planners \(P_1,\ldots,P_m\), a schedule of nonnegative time slices \((i_j,\tau_j)_{j\ge1}\), and a total budget \(B\). Initialize the incumbent cost \(U=\infty\). Run \(P_{i_j}\) for \(\tau_j\), passing it \(U\) when supported; whenever it returns a valid plan \(\pi\), replace the incumbent if \(c(\pi)<U\). Stop when budget \(B\) is exhausted and return the best incumbent, or failure if none exists. For an unbounded schedule, the portfolio is complete if some complete planner receives unbounded cumulative runtime and resumes without losing required search progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Schedule multiple planners, share the best plan bound, and return the best valid incumbent; completeness requires sustained time for a complete member.
assumptions_latex: Every reported incumbent plan is independently validated.
Time slices satisfy \(\tau_j\ge0\).
For the completeness claim, one complete planner receives unbounded cumulative runtime.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The finite-budget output is \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{\pi\ \mathrm{returned}}c(\pi)\); the stated unbounded schedule is complete.

notation.meaning: Cost of the best validated incumbent plan.
Planner index and duration of schedule slice j.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: fair scheduling transfers completeness from a resumable complete portfolio member

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The portfolio procedure fits the algorithm container, but the incumbent-sharing method and resumable-member completeness condition lack an authoritative citation.

children.title: Guidance Generalization Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Problem regimes where learned or selected guidance transfers poorly.

knowledge_statements.title: Guidance Generalization Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Zero training error alone gives no search-efficiency guarantee outside the training support.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the training support be \(T\) and let \(u\notin T\) be an unseen branching state. Agreement of a learned score \(f\) with all target rankings on \(T\) places no constraint on its ranking at \(u\). For every \(N\ge1\), construct at \(u\) one branch reaching a goal in one step and another traversing \(N\) distinct non-goal states before failure. A score with zero ranking error on \(T\) may rank every state of the failing branch ahead of the goal successor. Best-first search guided by that score then performs at least \(N\) unnecessary expansions, although its training error is zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Perfect training rankings do not bound search effort after distribution shift; unseen states can induce arbitrarily bad expansion orders.
assumptions_latex: The unseen branch state \(u\) is outside the training support \(T\).
Search priority is determined by the learned score on tied primary keys.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(N\), zero training error is compatible with at least \(N\) avoidable expansions.

notation.meaning: Support of the guidance training data.
Length of the misleading failing branch.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: empirical error on observed support does not constrain arbitrary off-support rankings

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The off-support counterexample fits a generalization failure boundary, but neither the construction nor its search-expansion conclusion is sourced.

children.title: Planning Complexity-Certificate System
children.top_down_role: Complexity boundaries and checkable artifacts associated with plan existence, bounded planning, and plan quality.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Complexity of Classical Planning

children.title: Plan-Length Complexity Regimes
children.top_down_role: Complexity regimes separated by plan-length bounds and representation restrictions.

children.title: Bounded-Length Planning Complexity
children.top_down_role: Complexity of plan existence under an explicit plan-length or horizon bound.

knowledge_statements.title: Bounded-Length Planning Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical propositional STRIPS plan existence with a polynomially bounded horizon.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite propositional STRIPS instance \(I\) and a bound \(K\) encoded in unary, deciding whether \(I\) has a plan of at most \(K\) actions is \(\mathrm{NP}\)-complete. Membership uses an action sequence of length at most \(K\) as a certificate; applicability, successor states, and goal satisfaction are checkable in time polynomial in \(|I|+K\). The same classification holds when \(K\) is guaranteed polynomial in \(|I|\). It does not automatically extend to a binary-encoded bound that may be exponential in the instance size.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unary or polynomial-horizon propositional STRIPS plan existence is NP-complete because a bounded action sequence is a polynomially verifiable certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(I\) is a finite propositional STRIPS instance with explicit operators.
\(K\) is unary encoded or polynomially bounded in \(|I|\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\textsc{Bounded-Plan-Existence}\) is \(\mathrm{NP}\text{-complete}\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: polynomial-length plans are NP certificates and bounded STRIPS planning is standard NP-hard

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The unary or polynomial-horizon NP-completeness classification is standard and correctly placed as a complexity bound, but a planning-specific authoritative citation is required.

children.title: Unbounded-Length Planning Complexity
children.top_down_role: Complexity of plan existence without a supplied plan-length bound.

knowledge_statements.title: Unbounded-Length Planning Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical propositional STRIPS plan existence without an explicit horizon.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite propositional STRIPS instance \(I\) with no plan-length bound, deciding whether any plan reaches a goal state is \(\mathrm{PSPACE}\)-complete. The state graph can contain exponentially many states, so a shortest plan may have exponential length, while a state and a depth-first reachability computation require only polynomial space in \(|I|\). Consequently, unbounded plan existence is not represented by a polynomial-length plan certificate unless an additional polynomial-horizon guarantee is imposed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unbounded propositional STRIPS plan existence is PSPACE-complete, and solvable instances may require exponentially long plans despite polynomial state descriptions.
assumptions_latex: \(I\) is a finite propositional STRIPS instance with explicitly represented facts and operators.
No polynomial plan-length bound is promised.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\textsc{Plan-Existence}\) is \(\mathrm{PSPACE}\text{-complete}\).

notation.meaning: Bit length of the planning-instance representation.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: unbounded propositional STRIPS reachability is the standard PSPACE-complete planning problem

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The PSPACE-completeness classification and exponential-plan-length qualification are standard and fit the container, but no planning-specific source or locator is supplied.

children.title: Representation-Sensitive Complexity Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Complexity changes induced by planning representation choices or encoding restrictions.

knowledge_statements.title: Representation-Sensitive Complexity Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary induced by polynomially equivalent versus exponentially more succinct planning representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R_1\) and \(R_2\) represent planning instances, and let \(L_i\) be the corresponding plan-existence language under \(R_i\). If polynomial-time translations \(T_{12}\) and \(T_{21}\) preserve plan existence and produce polynomial-size outputs, then \(L_1\) and \(L_2\) are polynomial-time many-one equivalent. Consequently, standard polynomial-time complexity classifications are representation-invariant within this equivalence class. This conclusion need not hold when one representation is exponentially more succinct: an algorithm polynomial in the expanded \(R_1\)-size may require exponential time measured against the succinct \(R_2\)-input size.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complexity classifications are preserved by polynomial-size, polynomial-time translations, but an exponentially succinct representation can move a planning problem across apparent complexity boundaries.
assumptions_latex: \(T_{12}\) and \(T_{21}\) preserve yes-instances.
Both translations run in polynomial time and have polynomial output size.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_1\equiv_m^p L_2\); without polynomial output size, this equivalence conclusion is unavailable.

notation.meaning: translation from representation i to representation j

children.title: Bound-Encoding Regimes
children.top_down_role: Complexity distinctions arising from how plan-length bounds are represented.

knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Encoding Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Input-size and certificate consequences of unary and binary plan-length bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an integer plan-length bound \(K\geq 0\), unary encoding contributes \(\Theta(K+1)\) symbols to the input, whereas binary encoding contributes \(\Theta(\log(K+1))\) bits. An explicit plan containing at most \(K\) action identifiers has size \(O(K\log |A|)\). Hence explicit bounded-plan certificates are polynomial in the total input size when \(K\) is unary encoded, or when a binary-encoded \(K\) is polynomially bounded in the remaining instance size. With unrestricted binary encoding, the certificate may be exponential in the encoded bound length.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unary bounds make explicit bounded plans polynomial-size; unrestricted binary bounds may describe exponentially long plans and therefore invalidate that certificate-size argument.
assumptions_latex: Actions are named using \(O(\log |A|)\) bits.
Certificates list actions explicitly rather than by a compressed program.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The explicit certificate size is \(O(K\log |A|)\), polynomial under the stated unary or polynomial-bound regimes.

children.title: Structural-Parameterized Tractability Regimes
children.top_down_role: Restricted causal graphs, action interactions, domains, and parameterized regimes.

children.title: Structural Planning Tractability
children.top_down_role: Planning tractability arising from restricted domain or interaction structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Structural Planning Tractability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Slice-wise polynomial tractability induced by a numerical structural measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal P\) be a planning formalism, let \(|I|\) denote the encoded size of an instance \(I\), and let \(s(I)\in\mathbb N\) be a computable structural measure such as causal-graph width. Plan existence is structurally tractable with respect to \(s\) if there is an algorithm and a computable function \(g\) such that every instance is decided in time \(|I|^{g(s(I))}\). Equivalently, for every fixed \(k\), the restriction \(\{I:s(I)\leq k\}\) is decidable in polynomial time, with the polynomial degree allowed to depend on \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A planning problem is structurally tractable when every fixed structural-width slice is polynomial-time decidable, although the polynomial degree may depend on the width.
assumptions_latex: \(s\) is a computable map from encoded planning instances to \(\mathbb N\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For each fixed \(k\), plan existence on \(s(I)\leq k\) is decidable in polynomial time.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: definition is the standard slice-wise polynomial or XP tractability convention
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A planning or parameterized-complexity source is required. Moreover, slice-wise polynomial decidability is equivalent to the displayed XP form only with an appropriate uniformity condition; the current equivalence is otherwise overstated.

children.title: Parameterized Planning Tractability
children.top_down_role: Planning complexity organized by selected structural or solution parameters.

knowledge_statements.title: Parameterized Planning Tractability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-parameter tractability for plan existence under a declared planning parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(k(I)\in\mathbb N\) be a computable parameter of a planning instance \(I\). The parameterized plan-existence problem is fixed-parameter tractable with respect to \(k\) if an algorithm decides whether \(I\) has a plan in time \(f(k(I))|I|^c\), where \(f:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N\) is computable and the constant \(c\) is independent of both \(I\) and \(k(I)\). The definition concerns decision time; plan construction additionally requires time proportional to the produced plan.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Parameterized planning is fixed-parameter tractable when all super-polynomial dependence is confined to the parameter and the input-size exponent is constant.
assumptions_latex: \(k\) is computable from the encoded instance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Plan existence is decidable in \(f(k(I))|I|^c\) time for a parameter-independent constant \(c\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard definition of fixed-parameter tractability
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The FPT definition and content kind are appropriate, but no inspectable source supports its application to parameterized plan existence or the plan-construction qualification.

children.title: Causal-Graph Restrictions
children.top_down_role: Tractability regimes classified by causal-graph topology.

knowledge_statements.title: Causal-Graph Restrictions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Causal graph for finite-domain planning and common graph-class restrictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite-domain planning instance with variable set \(V\), its directed causal graph is \(G_I=(V,E)\), where \((u,v)\in E\) for distinct \(u,v\) exactly when some action changes \(v\) and either tests or changes \(u\). A causal-graph restriction is a class \(\mathcal G\) of directed graphs, and the associated planning class is \(\{I:G_I\in\mathcal G\}\). Examples of predicates defining \(\mathcal G\) include acyclicity, bounded indegree, bounded directed-path length, or bounded treewidth of the underlying undirected graph; these predicates are distinct and must be stated separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The causal graph links variables that jointly influence an action transition; tractability claims must name the precise restricted graph class.
assumptions_latex: Actions have finite-domain preconditions and effects over \(V\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Membership in the restricted planning class is exactly the predicate \(G_I\in\mathcal G\).

notation.meaning: directed causal graph of instance I

review_flags: causal-graph edge conventions vary between planning formalisms

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Causal-graph edge conventions differ across finite-domain planning formalisms, particularly for co-effects. An authoritative source defining the selected convention is necessary.

children.title: Interaction-Width Regimes
children.top_down_role: Planning regimes classified by bounded interaction width or related decomposability measures.

knowledge_statements.title: Interaction-Width Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dynamic-programming bound for bounded-width finite-domain planning compilations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a bounded-horizon planning instance be compiled soundly and completely into a constraint network with \(N\) variables, maximum domain size \(d\), and primal-graph treewidth \(w\). Given a width-\(w\) tree decomposition, satisfiability can be decided by table-based dynamic programming in time \(O(Nd^{w+1})\) up to polynomial factors for constraint processing, and space \(O(Nd^{w+1})\). Thus the compiled regime is polynomial-time decidable when \(d\) and \(w\) are fixed and the compilation size is polynomial in the planning input and horizon encoding.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polynomial-size planning compilation with fixed domain size and interaction width is decidable by tree-decomposition dynamic programming in polynomial time.
assumptions_latex: The compilation preserves bounded-horizon plan existence.
A width-\(w\) tree decomposition is supplied or computable within the stated bound.
The compiled network has polynomial size.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Constraint satisfiability, and hence bounded-horizon plan existence, is decidable in \(O(Nd^{w+1})\) time up to polynomial constraint-processing factors.
review_flags: exact complexity depends on constraint representation and decomposition model

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The treewidth dynamic-programming bound depends on the constraint representation, constraint arity, table access model, and decomposition assumptions. A source is required to establish the stated bound and its transfer through the planning compilation.

children.title: Planning Feasibility-Refutation Certificate System
children.top_down_role: Plans and compilation-level artifacts supporting feasibility or bounded nonexistence claims.

children.title: Plan-Validity Certificates
children.top_down_role: Checkable artifacts supporting feasibility claims for supplied plans.

knowledge_statements.title: Plan-Validity Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit action sequence certifying reachability of a planning goal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a deterministic planning instance \(I=(S,A,s_0,G)\), a plan-validity certificate is a finite sequence \(\pi=(a_1,\ldots,a_m)\) of actions. A verifier initializes \(s:=s_0\); for each \(i=1,\ldots,m\), it rejects unless \(a_i\) is applicable in \(s\), and otherwise replaces \(s\) by the successor \(a_i(s)\). It accepts exactly when the final state satisfies \(G\). Acceptance certifies that every transition is defined and that executing \(\pi\) from \(s_0\) reaches a goal state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An explicit action sequence certifies validity when each action is applicable in succession and the resulting final state satisfies the goal.
assumptions_latex: Action applicability, successor computation, and goal testing are decidable in polynomial time.
\(I\) is deterministic and uses sequential plan semantics.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Verifier acceptance implies that \(\pi\) is a valid plan for \(I\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct operational definition of sequential plan verification
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate role and operational statement are standard, but no cited planning-formalism source fixes the deterministic sequential semantics, action representation, or polynomial-time verification assumptions.

children.title: Bounded-Nonexistence Certificates
children.top_down_role: Checkable artifacts supporting the absence of plans within a stated bound.

knowledge_statements.title: Bounded-Nonexistence Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Refutation certificate excluding every plan up to a specified horizon.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(I,K)\) be a sound and complete propositional encoding satisfying \(F(I,K)\) if and only if planning instance \(I\) has a plan of length at most \(K\). A bounded-nonexistence certificate is a refutation \(\rho\) of \(F(I,K)\) in a proof system with a deterministic checker. If the checker verifies that every inference in \(\rho\) follows from encoding clauses or earlier lines and that the final line is contradiction, then \(F(I,K)\) is unsatisfiable; therefore no plan for \(I\) of length at most \(K\) exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A checkable refutation of a sound and complete horizon encoding certifies that no plan exists within the stated bound.
assumptions_latex: \(F(I,K)\) is sound and complete for plans of length at most \(K\).
The proof checker is sound for the selected refutation system.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Verified refutation of \(F(I,K)\) implies that \(I\) has no plan of length at most \(K\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: sound refutation composed with an equisatisfiable bounded-planning encoding
specific encoding and proof-system source requested
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conclusion is valid under the stated assumptions, but the nontrivial encoding correspondence and refutation-checking interface require a concrete, inspectable source.

children.title: Compilation-Level Refutations
children.top_down_role: Unsatisfiability or infeasibility artifacts produced by planning compilations.

knowledge_statements.title: Compilation-Level Refutations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Refutations whose meaning is transferred through a planning-to-constraint compilation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) compile a planning query \(Q(I)\) into a constraint formula \(C(I)\), with the certified correspondence \(Q(I)\iff C(I)\text{ is satisfiable}\). A compilation-level refutation consists of \(C(I)\), a derivation \(\rho\) accepted by a sound refutation checker, and sufficient mapping data to verify that the checked formula is exactly the output of \(C\) on \(I\). If compilation checking and refutation checking both succeed, then \(C(I)\) is unsatisfiable and the planning query \(Q(I)\) is false.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A solver refutation becomes a planning refutation only when both the proof and the semantics-preserving compilation are checkably linked to the original instance.
assumptions_latex: The compilation equivalence \(Q(I)\iff C(I)\text{ is satisfiable}\) holds.
The refutation checker is sound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Successful compilation and refutation checks certify \(\neg Q(I)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: certificate soundness follows from checked compilation equivalence and proof-checker soundness
source for concrete compilation interface requested

children.title: Certificate Verification Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Interfaces connecting planning claims to independent certificate checking.

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate Verification Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract interface separating certificate production, checking, and semantic interpretation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A planning-certificate verification interface is a tuple \((\mathsf{Emit},\mathsf{Check},\mathsf{Meaning})\). For an instance \(I\), \(\mathsf{Emit}\) may produce a byte string \(c\); the total deterministic procedure \(\mathsf{Check}(I,c)\) returns accept or reject; and \(\mathsf{Meaning}(I,c)\) is the planning claim represented by \(c\). Interface soundness requires \(\mathsf{Check}(I,c)=\mathsf{accept}\Rightarrow\mathsf{Meaning}(I,c)\). Relative completeness for a claim class requires that whenever a supported claim is true, some finite \(c\) is accepted and denotes that claim. Polynomial verification additionally requires runtime polynomial in \(|I|+|c|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A certificate interface defines emitted data, a total checker, and its planning meaning, with explicit soundness, relative completeness, and verification-cost obligations.
assumptions_latex: Certificates and instances have finite encodings.
\(\mathsf{Check}\) is deterministic and total.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Acceptance is semantically valid exactly under the stated soundness implication; polynomial verification is measured in \(|I|+|c|\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: abstract proof-certificate interface with standard soundness and completeness obligations
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits the leaf, but the proposed interface and its relative-completeness obligation are an unsourced abstraction rather than an inspectably established planning-certificate interface.

children.title: Plan-Quality Certificate System
children.top_down_role: Bound, dominance, and exhaustive-search artifacts supporting quality claims.

children.title: Plan-Quality Certificates
children.top_down_role: Checkable artifacts supporting a stated plan-quality value or threshold.

knowledge_statements.title: Plan-Quality Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate that a valid plan meets a declared objective threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q_I(\pi)\) be a polynomial-time computable quality measure for valid plans of instance \(I\), with smaller values preferred. A threshold-quality certificate for bound \(B\) is an explicit plan \(\pi\) together with any data needed to evaluate \(q_I(\pi)\). The verifier checks plan validity and computes the quality value, accepting exactly when \(q_I(\pi)\leq B\). Acceptance certifies existence of a valid plan meeting the threshold; it does not by itself certify that \(\pi\) is optimal or dominates every alternative plan.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A plan and checkable objective value certify attainment of a quality threshold, but not global optimality.
assumptions_latex: \(q_I(\pi)\) is defined for valid plans and computable in polynomial time.
Lower objective values are preferred.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Acceptance implies that \(\pi\) is valid and \(q_I(\pi)\leq B\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: feasibility certificate augmented by direct objective evaluation
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The distinction between threshold quality and optimality is mathematically sound, but an authoritative source is needed for the planning-quality semantics and certificate-verification claim.

children.title: Planning Optimality Certificates
children.top_down_role: Checkable artifacts supporting the absence of a strictly better admissible plan.

knowledge_statements.title: Planning Optimality Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combined feasibility and strict-improvement refutation for minimization planning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q_I\) be a minimization objective and let \(\pi\) be a valid plan with value \(v=q_I(\pi)\). An optimality certificate consists of a plan-validity certificate for \(\pi\) and a soundly checkable refutation of a complete encoding \(F_{<v}(I)\) whose satisfying assignments correspond exactly to valid plans \(\pi'\) with \(q_I(\pi')<v\). If both components verify, then \(\pi\) is feasible and no strictly better plan exists, so \(q_I(\pi)=\min\{q_I(\pi'): \pi'\text{ is a valid plan for }I\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimality is certified by validating the proposed plan and refuting the existence of every strictly better plan.
assumptions_latex: \(F_{<v}(I)\) is sound and complete for valid plans of value below \(v\).
The selected refutation checker is sound.
The minimum is taken over all valid plans admitted by the planning semantics.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Successful verification implies \(q_I(\pi)=\min_{\pi'\text{ valid for }I}q_I(\pi')\).

notation.meaning: quality value of the certified plan
encoding of existence of a strictly better plan

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: optimality decomposes into incumbent feasibility and certified absence of strict improvement
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The feasibility-plus-refutation structure fits an optimality certificate, but the complete strict-improvement encoding and sound refutation system are substantial unsourced assumptions.

children.title: Planning Dominance Certificates
children.top_down_role: Artifacts supporting dominance comparisons between plans or plan classes.

assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal P(I)=\bigcup_{k=1}^m R_k\).
Each \(b^k\) is a valid componentwise lower bound on \(R_k\).
All components of \(q\) are minimized.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q(\pi^*)\preceq q(\pi)\quad\text{for every }\pi\in\mathcal P(I).\)

notation.meaning: feasible plans for planning instance I
search region and its valid lower-bound vector

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A bound-based certificate that one feasible plan is componentwise no worse than every plan represented by a finite search cover.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal P(I)\) be the feasible plans of instance \(I\), let \(q:\mathcal P(I)\to\mathbb R^d\) be a vector of minimized quality criteria, and let \(\preceq\) denote componentwise inequality. A dominance certificate for \(\pi^*\in\mathcal P(I)\) consists of regions \(R_1,\ldots,R_m\) covering \(\mathcal P(I)\) and vectors \(b^1,\ldots,b^m\in\mathbb R^d\) such that \(b^k\preceq q(\pi)\) for every \(k\in\{1,
\ldots,m\}\) and every \(\pi\in R_k\). If \(q(\pi^*)\preceq b^k\) for every \(k\in\{1,
\ldots,m\}\), then \(q(\pi^*)\preceq q(\pi)\) for every \(\pi\in\mathcal P(I)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible plan is componentwise no worse than every alternative when certified regional lower bounds cover all feasible plans and the plan's quality vector is no larger than every regional bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Planning Dominance Certificates

children.title: Exhaustive-Bound Certificates
children.top_down_role: Artifacts showing that relevant cost, horizon, or quality bounds have been exhausted.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a finite encoded search domain and \(X_F\subseteq X\) is its nonempty feasible subset.
\(X=\bigcup_{k=1}^m R_k\).
Each nonempty feasible terminal region has a valid lower bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x^*)=\min_{x\in X_F}f(x).\)

notation.meaning: feasible encoded plans within the search domain
terminal region and its valid lower bound when feasible points remain

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A finite branch-and-bound search-cover certificate for globally optimal feasible plan quality.

source_refs.locator: 2.2.1 Outline of the general branch-and-bound method p. 15

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be a finite encoded search domain, let \(X_F\subseteq X\) be the nonempty set of feasible encoded plans, and let \(f:X_F\to\mathbb R\) be minimized. An exhaustive-bound certificate consists of a feasible incumbent \(x^*\in X_F\) with \(U=f(x^*)\) and terminal regions \(R_1,
\ldots,R_m\) satisfying \(X=igcup_{k=1}^m R_k\). For each \(k\), the terminal record independently certifies either \(R_k\cap X_F=
\varnothing\), or a value \(L_k\) satisfying \(L_k\leq\inf\{f(x):x\in R_k\cap X_F\}\) and \(L_k\geq U\). These records exclude every feasible point with objective value below \(U\), so \(x^*\) is globally optimal over \(X_F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible incumbent is globally optimal when certified terminal regions cover the encoded search domain and each region is either feasibly empty or has a valid lower bound at least as large as the incumbent value.
knowledge_statements.title: Exhaustive-Bound Certificates

source_witnesses.locator: 2.2.1 Outline of the general branch-and-bound method p. 15

children.title: Plan Revision Method Family
children.top_down_role: Constraint-driven responses to execution failures, changed goals, changed resources, and model revisions.

children.title: Local Plan Repair
children.top_down_role: Restricted changes around detected conflicts while retaining unaffected plan structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Local Plan Repair
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Neighborhood optimization that preserves a designated unaffected portion of an existing plan.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given planning instance \(I\), incumbent plan \(\pi^0\), detected conflict set \(C\), and frozen structure \(F\), construct a repair neighborhood \(N_F(\pi^0)\) containing exactly the plans that retain every action, binding, and ordering designated by \(F\). Solve \[\min_{\pi\in N_F(\pi^0)}\;c_I(\pi)+\lambda d(\pi,\pi^0)\quad\text{subject to }\pi\text{ being feasible for }I.\] Return an optimizer \(\widehat\pi\) after validating its transitions and goals. Return failure if the neighborhood is infeasible; enlarging \(N_F(\pi^0)\) is then a separate repair iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local repair optimizes only within a neighborhood preserving frozen plan structure, returning a validated feasible revision or neighborhood-infeasibility failure.
assumptions_latex: \(\pi^0\) is an encoded incumbent plan.
\(F\) identifies structure that must remain unchanged.
\(d\) is a nonnegative deviation measure and \(\lambda\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat\pi\in\operatorname*{argmin}\{c_I(\pi)+\lambda d(\pi,\pi^0):\pi\in N_F(\pi^0),\ \pi\text{ feasible for }I\}.\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role and frozen-neighborhood interpretation fit Local Plan Repair, but the cited general constraint-programming section does not support this planning-specific repair algorithm, its exact objective, or its failure semantics. The statement also requests an optimizer without an attainment assumption and introduces the conflict set without using it to define the neighborhood.

children.title: Plan Transfer-Adaptation Family
children.top_down_role: Transformation of prior plans or plan fragments for revised instances.

children.title: Plan Reuse
children.top_down_role: Use of prior complete plans or plan components in revised instances.

knowledge_statements.title: Plan Reuse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct use of an existing plan in a new planning instance without structural editing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I'=(S,A,T,s_0',G')\) be a deterministic planning instance and let \(\pi=(a_1,\ldots,a_n)\) be a plan obtained previously. The plan is reusable without adaptation for \(I'\) if every action is successively applicable from \(s_0'\), the induced trajectory satisfies \(s_i=T(s_{i-1},a_i)\) for \(i=1,\ldots,n\), and the terminal state satisfies \(s_n\in G'\). Parameter rebinding is allowed only when it preserves the action sequence and all transition constraints; inserting, deleting, or reordering actions constitutes adaptation rather than direct reuse.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A previous plan is directly reusable when its unchanged action sequence remains executable from the new initial state and reaches the new goal.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is deterministic on applicable state-action pairs.
\(\pi\) is a finite action sequence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\pi\text{ is reusable for }I'\iff a_i\text{ is applicable at }s_{i-1}\text{ for all }i\text{ and }s_n\in G'.\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition role and unchanged-sequence validity condition fit Plan Reuse, but no source supports the asserted boundary under which parameter rebinding remains reuse while insertion, deletion, or reordering becomes adaptation.

children.title: Plan Adaptation
children.top_down_role: Transformation of a prior plan to accommodate changed goals, states, or constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Plan Adaptation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimum-change transformation of a source plan into a valid plan for a target instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a target instance \(I'\), source plan \(\pi^0\), admissible edit set \(E\), edit cost \(d_E\), and plan cost \(c_{I'}\), initialize the candidate with \(\pi^0\). Search over plans reachable by finitely many edits from \(E\), enforcing action applicability, transition, ordering, resource, and goal constraints of \(I'\). Return \[\widehat\pi\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\pi}\{d_E(\pi,\pi^0)+\lambda c_{I'}(\pi):\pi\text{ is feasible for }I'\}.\] If no reachable feasible plan exists, report adaptation failure. Every returned plan must be validated independently against \(I'\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Plan adaptation finds a valid target plan reachable from a source plan while minimizing edits and, optionally, target-plan cost.
assumptions_latex: \(E\) specifies admissible insertions, deletions, substitutions, and reorderings.
\(d_E\geq0\) measures edit cost.
\(\lambda\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat\pi\text{ is feasible for }I'\text{ and minimizes the stated adaptation objective over the edit-reachable set}.\)

notation.meaning: edit-induced distance from the source plan

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits Plan Adaptation, but the edit-reachable scalarized optimization model is one possible formulation rather than a source-backed general adaptation algorithm. Finiteness or attainment of the stated argmin is also not established.

children.title: Plan-Fragment Recombination
children.top_down_role: Assembly of reusable plan fragments into a plan for a revised instance.

knowledge_statements.title: Plan-Fragment Recombination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraint-based assembly of compatible partial plans drawn from a fragment library.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a fragment library \(\mathcal F\), initial state \(s_0\), goal set \(G\), and resource limits, introduce variables selecting fragments, binding their parameters, and ordering selected fragments. Impose that the first selected precondition holds at \(s_0\), each fragment's postcondition entails the next fragment's precondition under the chosen bindings, all causal threats and resource conflicts are resolved, and the final postcondition entails \(G\). Optimize a stated cost over selections and orderings. Concatenate the chosen fragments using the certified interfaces, validate the resulting action-level plan, and return it; report failure when the recombination constraints are infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compatible plan fragments are selected, bound, ordered, and validated so their interfaces connect the initial state to the goal without conflicts.
assumptions_latex: Each \(F\in\mathcal F\) has certified preconditions, postconditions, actions, and resource profile.
Fragment interfaces use a common state vocabulary.
The selected ordering is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\pi=F_{i_1}\circ\cdots\circ F_{i_r}\text{ is returned only if it is feasible from }s_0\text{ and reaches }G.\)

notation.meaning: a partial plan with an interface contract

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the recombination leaf, but no source defines the certified fragment interfaces or establishes that the stated entailment, threat, and resource checks are sufficient for valid action-level composition.

children.title: Case-Based Plan Transfer
children.top_down_role: Selection and transfer of plans from structurally related prior cases.

knowledge_statements.title: Case-Based Plan Transfer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Retrieval, adaptation, and validation of plans from solved cases.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal C=\{(I_j,\pi_j)\\}\) be a library of solved planning cases and let \(I'\) be a target instance. Compute a declared instance distance \(\delta(I',I_j)\), retrieve the \(k\) nearest cases, and for each retrieved plan run a fixed adaptation operator \(A(I',\pi_j)\). Discard failures and candidates that do not validate against \(I'\). Among the remaining plans, return one minimizing \(c_{I'}(\pi)+\alpha\delta(I',I_j)+\beta d(\pi,\pi_j)\). If none validates, report transfer failure and invoke a separate plan-generation procedure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Case-based transfer retrieves similar solved instances, adapts their plans, validates the results, and selects the best successful transfer.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal C\) contains plans valid for their recorded instances.
\(\delta\) and \(d\) are declared nonnegative dissimilarity measures.
\(k\geq1\) and \(\alpha,\beta\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat\pi\text{ is a validated target plan minimizing the stated score among successful retrieved adaptations}.\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits Case-Based Plan Transfer, but no source supports the nearest-case retrieval and scoring procedure. The opening expression for the case library also contains an erroneous line-break command before the closing set delimiter, so its LaTeX is malformed.

children.title: Execution-Triggered Replanning Interface
children.top_down_role: Detection of execution divergence and renewed planning from an updated state.

children.title: Plan Execution Monitoring
children.top_down_role: Observation of execution progress relative to expected plan states or events.

knowledge_statements.title: Plan Execution Monitoring
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Online comparison of observed execution with predicted plan states and constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given plan \(\pi=(a_1,\ldots,a_n)\), predicted states \(\widehat s_0,\ldots,\widehat s_n\), observation map \(h\), and tolerances \(\varepsilon_i\), initialize \(i=0\). After each executed action, obtain observation \(y_i\), update an estimated state \(\widetilde s_i\), and evaluate action status, invariant constraints, and discrepancy \(D_i=d(h(\widetilde s_i),h(\widehat s_i))\). Emit a divergence event if an action fails, an invariant is violated, or \(D_i>\varepsilon_i\). Otherwise advance to \(i+1\). Stop successfully when \(i=n\) and the observed or estimated state satisfies the goal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Execution monitoring updates state estimates after actions and emits divergence whenever failures, invariant violations, or excessive deviations from predicted states occur.
assumptions_latex: Observations can be mapped to state estimates.
\(d\) is a declared discrepancy measure.
Each \(\varepsilon_i\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{diverge}_i\iff\text{action-failure}_i\lor\text{invariant-violation}_i\lor D_i>\varepsilon_i.\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits Plan Execution Monitoring, but the observation, estimation, and threshold model lacks a source. The procedure initializes at step zero yet describes obtaining the indexed observation after each executed action, leaving the action/state indexing ambiguous.

children.title: Execution Divergence Diagnosis
children.top_down_role: Classification of mismatches between expected and observed execution.

knowledge_statements.title: Execution Divergence Diagnosis
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A verifiable minimal explanation of discrepancies between predicted and observed execution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\) be the detected discrepancy set and \(C\) a finite family of candidate execution causes. For each \(c\in C\), let \(E(c)\subseteq D\) be the discrepancies entailed by inserting cause \(c\) into the execution model. A diagnosis certificate is a set \(H\subseteq C\) together with model evaluations verifying \(D\subseteq\bigcup_{c\in H}E(c)\) and consistency of \(H\) with the observations. It is subset-minimal when, for every \(c\in H\), some discrepancy is not covered by \(H\setminus\{c\}\). These checks certify that \(H\) explains all detected divergence and contains no dispensable cause.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A diagnosis is certified when its modeled causes consistently explain every detected discrepancy and removing any selected cause destroys complete coverage.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) and \(C\) are finite.
Each entailment set \(E(c)\) is independently computable from the execution model.
Joint causes in \(H\) are observation-consistent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D\subseteq\bigcup_{c\in H}E(c)\quad\text{and}\quad\forall c\in H,\ D\nsubseteq\bigcup_{c'\in H\setminus\{c\}}E(c').\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The leaf denotes diagnosis generally, while the record narrows it to a certificate without evidence that this is the intended terminal role. The union of independently explained discrepancy sets does not represent interacting causes, and coverage-minimality alone is not a source-backed general diagnosis criterion.

children.title: State-Triggered Replanning
children.top_down_role: Renewed planning initiated from an updated execution state.

knowledge_statements.title: State-Triggered Replanning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A state predicate that activates replanning when continuation becomes invalid or insufficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At execution step \(i\), let \(s_i\) be the estimated current state and \(\pi_{i:}\) the unexecuted plan suffix. Let \(\operatorname{Valid}(s_i,\pi_{i:})\) mean that the suffix is executable and goal-reaching from \(s_i\), and let \(V(s_i,\pi_{i:})\) be its predicted loss. For threshold \(\tau_i\), the state-triggered replanning predicate is \[R_i=\neg\operatorname{Valid}(s_i,\pi_{i:})\ \lor\ V(s_i,\pi_{i:})>\tau_i\ \lor\ \operatorname{GoalChanged}_i.\] Replanning is invoked exactly when \(R_i\) holds; otherwise execution may retain the suffix subject to continued monitoring.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replanning is triggered when the remaining plan is invalid, its predicted loss exceeds tolerance, or the goal has changed.
assumptions_latex: \(s_i\) is the current state estimate.
Suffix validity and predicted loss are computable under the planning model.
\(\tau_i\) is a declared loss threshold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_i\iff\neg\operatorname{Valid}(s_i,\pi_{i:})\lor V(s_i,\pi_{i:})>\tau_i\lor\operatorname{GoalChanged}_i.\)

notation.meaning: unexecuted suffix of the current plan
replanning trigger at execution step i

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A condition is an appropriate role for a replanning trigger, but the three-disjunct predicate is an application-specific policy presented as an exact general rule. No source establishes these triggers or the meaning of the predicted loss threshold.

children.title: Plan Continuation Decisions
children.top_down_role: Choices among continuing, repairing, replacing, or abandoning the current plan.

knowledge_statements.title: Plan Continuation Decisions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Online choice among retaining, repairing, or replacing the remaining plan.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At state \(s_i\), form candidate set \(K_i\) containing the valid current suffix, any validated local repairs, and any validated replanned suffixes. For each \(\rho\in K_i\), compute \(J_i(\rho)=C(s_i,\rho)+S(\rho,\pi_{i:})+R(s_i,\rho)\), combining predicted execution cost, switching cost, and risk. Remove candidates violating hard goals, safety constraints, or resource limits. Return a minimizer of \(J_i\) over the remaining set. Continue the original suffix precisely when it is feasible and has no larger score than every admissible repair or replacement; report failure if the set is empty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The controller continues, repairs, or replaces the current suffix by minimizing execution, switching, and risk costs over validated feasible alternatives.
assumptions_latex: All candidates are evaluated from the same current state \(s_i\).
Hard feasibility is checked before comparison.
The three score components use compatible declared units or scalarization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_i^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\rho\in K_i\,:\,\rho\text{ admissible}}J_i(\rho).\)

notation.meaning: candidate continuation, repair, and replacement suffixes
cost of switching away from the incumbent suffix

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits Plan Continuation Decisions, but the additive execution, switching, and risk score is a domain-dependent choice without supporting evidence. The construction and completeness of the repair and replanning candidate set are also unspecified.

children.title: Repair-Stability Tradeoff
children.top_down_role: Tradeoffs among restored feasibility, deviation, reuse, quality, and execution continuity.

children.title: Repair Objective Families
children.top_down_role: Objective families governing feasibility restoration, quality recovery, or repair cost.

knowledge_statements.title: Repair Objective Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Three standard representations for balancing repaired-plan quality against deviation from an incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal R\) be the feasible repair set, \(c(\pi)\) the repaired-plan performance cost, and \(d(\pi,\pi^0)\) its deviation from incumbent \(\pi^0\). Common objective families are: weighted scalarization, \(\min_{\pi\in\mathcal R} c(\pi)+\lambda d(\pi,\pi^0)\); deviation-constrained optimization, \(\min_{\pi\in\mathcal R}c(\pi)\) subject to \(d(\pi,\pi^0)\leq\Delta\); and lexicographic optimization of \((d(\pi,\pi^0),c(\pi))\) or its reversed order. Without fixed weights or priorities, the nondominated set consists of repairs for which no feasible alternative weakly improves both criteria and strictly improves one.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repair objectives may use weighted costs, deviation budgets, lexicographic priorities, or the Pareto frontier of quality and stability.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal R\neq\varnothing\).
\(c\) and \(d\) are real-valued and bounded below on \(\mathcal R\).
\(\lambda,\Delta\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Pareto}(\mathcal R;c,d)=\{\pi\in\mathcal R:\nexists\rho\in\mathcal R\text{ with }c(\rho)\leq c(\pi),\ d(\rho,\pi^0)\leq d(\pi,\pi^0)\text{ and one strict}\}.\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation role fits a leaf cataloging repair objective families, and the formulas are mathematically coherent. However, the cited generic objective-modeling section does not specifically support weighted, constrained, lexicographic, and Pareto formulations as standard plan-repair objective families; an authoritative multiobjective repair source is required.

children.title: Plan Stability Criteria
children.top_down_role: Criteria measuring preservation of prior plan commitments.

assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal F\ne\varnothing\).
\(d(P,P^0)\ge 0\) for every \(P\in\mathcal F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The repaired plan \(P\) is \(\varepsilon\)-stable when \(d(P,P^0)\le\varepsilon\), and it is maximally stable within \(\mathcal F\) when \(P\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{Q\in\mathcal F}d(Q,P^0)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Threshold and optimization criteria for stability relative to a baseline plan.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P^0\) be a baseline plan, let \(\mathcal F\) be the set of repaired plans feasible under the updated constraints, and let \(d:\mathcal F\times\{P^0\}\to\mathbb R_{\ge 0}\) measure plan deviation. A repaired plan \(P\in\mathcal F\) is \(\varepsilon\)-stable when \(d(P,P^0)\le\varepsilon\). It is maximally stable within \(\mathcal F\) when \(P\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{Q\in\mathcal F}d(Q,P^0)\). The distance may weight changes to actions, ordering, timing, or resource assignments, but its definition must be fixed before candidate repairs are compared.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A repair is epsilon-stable if its measured deviation from the baseline stays below the specified threshold, and maximally stable if no feasible repair has smaller deviation.
knowledge_statements.title: Plan Stability Criteria

children.title: Deviation-Sensitive Repair
children.top_down_role: Repair regimes penalizing changes relative to the original plan.

assumptions_latex: The optimization method is complete when infeasibility or exact optimality is asserted.
The scalarized problem has an attained minimum when an exact optimum is requested.
\(c\) and \(d\) are evaluable for every feasible plan.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: When the exact solver returns \(P^\star\), the output minimizes \(c(P)+\lambda d(P,P^0)\) over \(P\in\mathcal F\); infeasibility is declared only when the solver proves \(\mathcal F=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Plan repair using an explicit penalty for departures from the baseline.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a baseline plan \(P^0\), an updated feasible set \(\mathcal F\), a repair-cost function \(c:\mathcal F\to\mathbb R\), a deviation measure \(d:\mathcal F\times\{P^0\}\to\mathbb R_{\ge0}\), and a weight \(\lambda\ge0\). Use a complete feasibility or optimization method to solve \[P^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{P\in\mathcal F}\bigl(c(P)+\lambda d(P,P^0)\bigr).\] Declare infeasibility only if the method proves \(\mathcal F=\varnothing\). For an exact result, stop when optimality is proved; under an explicit approximation convention, return an incumbent with its bound. Output the returned plan and the separate values of \(c\) and \(d\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use a complete solver to minimize operational cost plus a weighted baseline-deviation penalty. Declare infeasibility only when proved, and report cost and deviation separately for the returned plan.
knowledge_statements.title: Deviation-Sensitive Repair

children.title: Execution-Continuity Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Tradeoffs between plan modification and continuity of ongoing execution.

knowledge_statements.title: Execution-Continuity Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pareto relation between revised-plan quality and continuity of ongoing execution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal F\) be the feasible repairs, let \(c(P)\) be revised execution cost, and let \(d(P,P^0)\) quantify disruption to the baseline or already committed execution. A repair \(P\in\mathcal F\) is continuity-cost efficient if no \(Q\in\mathcal F\) satisfies \(c(Q)\le c(P)\) and \(d(Q,P^0)\le d(P,P^0)\), with at least one strict inequality. Thus every minimizer of \(c(P)+\lambda d(P,P^0)\) for \(\lambda>0\) is nondominated, although a weighted sum need not recover every nondominated repair when the attainable objective set is nonconvex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A repair is efficient when no feasible alternative improves cost and continuity simultaneously; positive weighted-sum optima are efficient but may omit unsupported tradeoffs.
assumptions_latex: \(c(P)\) and \(d(P,P^0)\) are finite for all compared repairs.
The scalarized minimum is attained for the weighted-sum claim.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every positive-weight scalarized optimum is Pareto efficient in \((c,d)\), but the converse can fail for nonconvex attainable sets.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property role and Pareto statement fit the tradeoff leaf, and the positive weighted-sum claim is mathematically coherent under attainment. However, no plan-repair or multiobjective source with an inspectable locator is cited.
