children.title: Machine-Environment Regimes
children.top_down_role: Canonical machine environments and their structural specializations.

children.title: Single-Machine Scheduling
children.top_down_role: Single-resource sequencing regimes and their objective-dependent structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Single-Machine Scheduling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical nonpreemptive single-resource scheduling model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A nonpreemptive single-machine scheduling instance consists of jobs \(J=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), each having processing time \(p_j>0\), and optionally release date \(r_j\), due date \(d_j\), and weight \(w_j\). A schedule assigns start times \(S_j\) such that \(S_j\ge r_j\) when release dates apply and, for every distinct \(i,j\), either \(S_i+p_i\le S_j\) or \(S_j+p_j\le S_i\). Completion times are \(C_j=S_j+p_j\); an objective such as makespan, total completion time, or weighted tardiness selects the optimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Jobs occupy one machine without overlap; their timing and an objective determine the single-machine scheduling problem.
assumptions_latex: Processing is nonpreemptive unless the instance explicitly states otherwise.
The machine processes at most one job at a time.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Feasible schedules are exactly the start-time assignments satisfying release and pairwise nonoverlap constraints.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition matches the nonpreemptive single-machine regime, but the record has no scheduling reference or specific section, definition, or page locator.

children.title: Parallel-Machine Scheduling
children.top_down_role: Identical, uniform, and unrelated parallel-machine regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Parallel-Machine Scheduling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identical, uniform, and unrelated parallel-machine environments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A parallel-machine scheduling instance has jobs \(J\) and machines \(M=\{1,\ldots,m\}\); each job is assigned to one machine and machine intervals may not overlap. With base work \(p_j\), identical machines have processing time \(p_{ij}=p_j\), while uniform machines with speed \(s_i>0\) have \(p_{ij}=p_j/s_i\). In the unrelated regime, arbitrary eligible processing times \(p_{ij}>0\) are specified for each job-machine pair. For a nonpreemptive assignment \(a(j)\), completion satisfies \(C_j=S_j+p_{a(j)j}\), subject to nonoverlap on every machine.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each job is assigned to one of several machines; processing times are equal, speed-scaled, or machine-job specific in the three standard regimes.
assumptions_latex: Every job has at least one eligible machine.
Processing is nonpreemptive unless explicitly stated otherwise.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The regimes are distinguished by \(p_{ij}=p_j\), \(p_{ij}=p_j/s_i\), or unrestricted eligible \(p_{ij}\), respectively.

notation.meaning: processing time of job j on machine i

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition correctly distinguishes identical, uniform, and unrelated parallel-machine regimes, but no authoritative scheduling source with an inspectable locator is supplied.

children.title: Multioperation Shop Scheduling Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Multioperation scheduling regimes distinguished by routing and machine order.

children.title: Flow-Shop Scheduling
children.top_down_role: Multioperation scheduling with a common machine route across jobs.

assumptions_latex: Operations are nonpreemptive.
Each machine processes at most one operation at a time.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A feasible flow-shop schedule satisfies the common-route precedences and all machine nonoverlap constraints.

notation.meaning: operation of job j on machine k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multioperation shop with a common machine route for every job.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A flow-shop instance has jobs \(J=\{1,\ldots,n\}\) and machines \(M=\{1,\ldots,m\}\). Job \(j\) requires one nonpreemptive operation \((j,k)\) of duration \(p_{jk}>0\) on each machine \(k\), in the common order \(1,\ldots,m\). Start times satisfy \(S_{j,k+1}\ge S_{jk}+p_{jk}\). Operations assigned to the same machine do not overlap. A permutation flow shop additionally requires the jobs to appear in the same order on every machine; the general flow shop does not impose this permutation restriction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every job visits all machines in the same order, with precedence within each job and no overlap on each machine.
knowledge_statements.title: Flow-Shop Scheduling

children.title: Flexible-Flow-Shop Scheduling
children.top_down_role: Flow-shop scheduling with alternative machines available at one or more stages.

knowledge_statements.title: Flexible-Flow-Shop Scheduling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stage-ordered shop with alternative parallel machines at each stage.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A flexible-flow-shop instance has ordered stages \(K=\{1,\ldots,q\}\), stage-specific machine sets \(M_k\), and jobs \(J\). Job \(j\) requires one operation at each required stage in increasing stage order and must be assigned to one eligible machine \(a_{jk}\in M_k\). If its processing time there is \(p_{a_{jk},j,k}>0\), then \(S_{j,k+1}\ge S_{jk}+p_{a_{jk},j,k}\). Operations assigned to the same machine cannot overlap. The model reduces to an ordinary flow shop when every \(M_k\) contains exactly one machine.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Jobs pass through ordered stages, choosing an eligible parallel machine at each stage while respecting precedence and machine capacity.
assumptions_latex: Operations are nonpreemptive.
Every required job-stage operation has an eligible machine.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Feasibility requires one eligible assignment per operation, stage-order precedence, and nonoverlap on every selected machine.

notation.meaning: machine selected for job j at stage k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition matches the flexible-flow-shop leaf and correctly separates stages from alternative machines, but it lacks an authoritative source and inspectable locator.

children.title: Open-Shop Scheduling
children.top_down_role: Multioperation scheduling without a fixed technological order among a job's operations.

knowledge_statements.title: Open-Shop Scheduling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shop model without prescribed within-job operation order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An open-shop instance has jobs \(J=\{1,\ldots,n\}\) and machines \(M=\{1,\ldots,m\}\). For each required pair \((j,k)\), job \(j\) has a nonpreemptive operation of duration \(p_{jk}>0\) on machine \(k\). A feasible schedule assigns start times so that no two operations of the same job overlap and no two operations on the same machine overlap. Unlike flow and job shops, the instance prescribes no precedence order among a job's operations; their order is selected by the schedule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each job requires machine operations in no prescribed order, while neither a job nor a machine may process two operations simultaneously.
assumptions_latex: Operations are nonpreemptive.
A job can undergo at most one operation at a time.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Feasibility consists of job nonoverlap and machine nonoverlap, without fixed within-job precedences.

notation.meaning: operation of job j on machine k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition matches the standard nonpreemptive open-shop regime, but no supporting scheduling source with a specific locator is provided.

children.title: Job-Shop Scheduling
children.top_down_role: Multioperation scheduling with job-specific machine routes.

knowledge_statements.title: Job-Shop Scheduling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multioperation shop with a job-specific prescribed machine route.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A job-shop instance gives each job \(j\in J\) an ordered operation list \((j,1),\ldots,(j,q_j)\). Operation \((j,h)\) has duration \(p_{jh}>0\) and requires a specified machine \(\mu_{jh}\). Start times satisfy \(S_{j,h+1}\ge S_{jh}+p_{jh}\), and any two operations requiring the same machine occupy disjoint intervals. Machine routes may differ across jobs and may revisit machines if the adopted model permits recirculation. An objective, commonly makespan, is optimized over these feasible schedules.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each job follows its own prescribed machine route; operations respect route precedence and cannot overlap on a shared machine.
assumptions_latex: Operations are nonpreemptive.
Each operation requires exactly one specified machine.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A feasible job-shop schedule satisfies every job-route precedence and every machine nonoverlap constraint.

notation.meaning: number of operations of job j
machine required by operation h of job j

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition matches job-shop scheduling and appropriately qualifies recirculation as model-dependent, but no authoritative source or specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Precedence-Constrained Project Scheduling Family
children.top_down_role: Activity networks, precedence constraints, alternative modes, and project portfolios.

children.title: Project Scheduling
children.top_down_role: Scheduling of activities within project-oriented resource or time constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Project Scheduling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Activity scheduling under technological precedence and renewable-resource limits.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A project-scheduling instance consists of activities \(V\), durations \(p_i\ge0\), a directed acyclic precedence graph \(G=(V,E)\), renewable resources \(R\) with capacities \(K_r\), and demands \(a_{ir}\). Start times satisfy \(S_j\ge S_i+p_i\) for every \((i,j)\in E\). At every time \(t\) and resource \(r\), active activities obey \[\sum_{i:S_i\le t<S_i+p_i}a_{ir}\le K_r.\] A standard objective minimizes project makespan \(C_{\max}=\max_{i\in V}(S_i+p_i)\), though other time or cost objectives may be specified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Activities are timed subject to precedence and renewable-resource capacities, commonly to minimize the project's completion time.
assumptions_latex: The precedence graph is acyclic.
Activities are nonpreemptive in this model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Feasible project schedules satisfy all arc precedences and resource-capacity inequalities.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition gives the standard single-mode resource-constrained project-scheduling model and fits the local family, but it has no project-scheduling source with an inspectable locator.

children.title: Precedence-Constrained Scheduling
children.top_down_role: Scheduling regimes organized around required ordering relations between activities.

knowledge_statements.title: Precedence-Constrained Scheduling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scheduling model defined by a partial order among activities or jobs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V\) be tasks with processing times \(p_i\ge0\), scheduled on a specified machine or resource environment, and let \(G=(V,E)\) be a directed acyclic graph. An arc \((i,j)\in E\) requires task \(i\) to complete before task \(j\) starts, hence \(S_j\ge S_i+p_i\). A precedence-constrained schedule is any resource-feasible start-time assignment satisfying all such inequalities. Equivalently, the realized task order extends the partial order generated by \(E\); resource constraints may impose additional ordering not present in \(G\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible schedule must extend an acyclic task partial order while also satisfying the chosen machine or resource constraints.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is acyclic.
Processing times and the resource environment are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every feasible schedule satisfies \(S_j\ge S_i+p_i\) for all \((i,j)\in E\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition captures precedence-constrained scheduling over a separately specified resource environment, but no authoritative scheduling source or specific locator is cited.

children.title: Multi-Mode Project Scheduling
children.top_down_role: Project scheduling where activities may use alternative execution modes.

knowledge_statements.title: Multi-Mode Project Scheduling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Project scheduling with a discrete execution-mode choice for each activity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A multi-mode project-scheduling instance gives each activity \(i\in V\) a finite mode set \(M_i\). Choosing \(m_i\in M_i\) determines duration \(p_{i m_i}\), renewable-resource demands \(a_{i m_i r}\), and, when modeled, nonrenewable consumption \(b_{i m_i q}\). Start times satisfy \(S_j\ge S_i+p_{i m_i}\) for every precedence arc \((i,j)\). Renewable capacities hold at every time, and nonrenewable budgets satisfy \[\sum_{i\in V}b_{i m_i q}\le B_q.\] A feasible solution jointly selects one mode per activity and schedules all selected operations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each activity chooses one execution mode, which fixes its duration and resource use; mode choices and start times must jointly satisfy all constraints.
assumptions_latex: Every activity has a finite nonempty mode set.
The precedence graph is acyclic.
Activities are nonpreemptive in this model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Feasibility requires one mode per activity together with precedence, renewable-capacity, and nonrenewable-budget compliance.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition matches multi-mode project scheduling and consistently introduces renewable and optional nonrenewable resources, but it lacks an authoritative source with a specific section, definition, theorem, or page locator.

children.title: Project-Portfolio Scheduling
children.top_down_role: Coordinated scheduling across multiple projects sharing resources or objectives.

knowledge_statements.title: Project-Portfolio Scheduling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint selection and resource-feasible scheduling of projects from a finite portfolio.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) be a finite set of candidate projects, and let project \(p\) contain activities \(A_p\). A project-portfolio schedule consists of selection variables \(y_p\in\{0,1\}\) and start times \(S_i\) for activities of selected projects. It is feasible when \(y_p=1\) activates every required temporal, precedence, mode, and renewable or nonrenewable resource constraint of project \(p\), while unselected projects consume no resources. A portfolio-scheduling problem optimizes a specified value function \(V(y,S)\), commonly subject to portfolio-level budget, capacity, or strategic constraints coupling distinct projects.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Project-portfolio scheduling jointly chooses projects and schedules their activities while enforcing project-level constraints and shared portfolio-wide resource, budget, or strategic limits.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) and every \(A_p\) are finite.
Activity requirements are inactive whenever their project is unselected.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((y,S)\) is feasible exactly when all activated project constraints and all portfolio-level coupling constraints hold.

notation.meaning: binary selection variable for project p

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the project-portfolio scheduling leaf and is internally coherent, but no cited source supports the activation semantics or portfolio-level formulation; the inventory's portfolio-selection source is not scheduling-specific.

children.title: Scheduling Processing Regime Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Release dates, deadlines, preemption, migration, setups, calendars, blocking, batching, and no-wait conditions.

children.title: Temporal Availability Regimes
children.top_down_role: Scheduling restrictions arising from temporal availability and calendars.

children.title: Release-Date Regimes
children.top_down_role: Scheduling regimes where jobs or operations become available only after specified times.

knowledge_statements.title: Release-Date Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hard lower bounds on the times at which jobs may begin processing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite job set \(J\), assign each job \(j\) a release date \(r_j\). A schedule is feasible under the release-date regime when its start time satisfies \(S_j\ge r_j\) for every \(j\in J\). In a preemptive model with processing-rate function \(x_j(t)\), the equivalent availability condition is \(x_j(t)=0\) for every \(t<r_j\). A common-release regime has \(r_j=r\) for all jobs; the unrestricted regime is represented by release dates no later than the scheduling origin.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A release date is a hard earliest-availability time: a job cannot start, or receive preemptive processing, before that time.
assumptions_latex: \(J\) is finite.
Release dates are hard feasibility parameters.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every feasible schedule satisfies \(S_j\ge r_j\) for each \(j\in J\).

notation.meaning: processing rate assigned to job j at time t

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition correctly distinguishes nonpreemptive start-time and preemptive processing-availability formulations, but it has no inspectable scheduling citation.

children.title: Deadline Regimes
children.top_down_role: Scheduling regimes with required completion limits.

knowledge_statements.title: Deadline Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hard upper bounds on job completion, distinct from penalized due dates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite job set \(J\), assign each job \(j\) a deadline \(d_j\). A schedule is feasible under the deadline regime precisely when its completion time satisfies \(C_j\le d_j\) for every \(j\in J\). If a deadline instead bounds the start of processing, the constraint must be stated explicitly as \(S_j\le d_j\); it is not equivalent to a completion deadline. A soft due date, whose violation incurs a penalty such as \(\max\{0,C_j-d_j\}\), does not constitute a hard deadline unless feasibility also requires zero tardiness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A completion deadline is a hard latest-finish constraint. Soft due dates permit lateness at a cost and therefore define a different regime.
assumptions_latex: \(J\) is finite.
Each \(d_j\) is interpreted as a hard completion deadline unless stated otherwise.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Feasibility requires \(C_j\le d_j\) for every \(j\in J\).
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The hard completion-deadline condition and distinction from soft due dates are mathematically appropriate, but no source with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Calendar Regimes
children.top_down_role: Scheduling regimes governed by machine, workforce, or resource calendars.

knowledge_statements.title: Calendar Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Time-dependent resource or job availability represented by admissible time sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\) be the scheduling horizon and let \(K\) be a finite set of resources. A calendar assigns each resource \(k\) an availability function \(a_k:T\to\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}\), or equivalently an admissible-time set when capacity is binary. If \(u_{jk}(t)\) is job \(j\)'s consumption of resource \(k\), calendar feasibility requires \(\sum_j u_{jk}(t)\le a_k(t)\) at every modeled time \(t\). A job-specific calendar \(A_j\subseteq T\) additionally requires all processing of job \(j\) to occur within \(A_j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Calendars make resource capacity or job availability depend on time; processing is feasible only during admissible periods and within available capacity.
assumptions_latex: The horizon \(T\) and calendar functions or sets are specified.
Resource consumption is defined at every modeled time.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At every time, processing respects both time-varying capacities and applicable job-specific availability sets.

notation.meaning: available capacity of resource k at time t
resource-k consumption by job j at time t
admissible processing times for job j

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record plausibly covers resource and job calendars, but these are distinct calendar variants and require a scheduling source establishing the stated formulation and scope.

children.title: Combined Availability Windows
children.top_down_role: Scheduling restrictions formed by interacting release, completion, or calendar windows.

knowledge_statements.title: Combined Availability Windows
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint earliest-start, latest-completion, and calendar restrictions on processing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each job \(j\), let \(r_j\) be its release date, \(d_j\) its completion deadline, and \(A_j\) its calendar-admissible processing set. A nonpreemptive execution occupying \([S_j,C_j)\) is feasible with respect to its combined availability window exactly when \(S_j\ge r_j\), \(C_j\le d_j\), and \([S_j,C_j)\subseteq A_j\). Under preemption, replace interval containment by the requirement that the support of the processing-rate function \(x_j\) be contained in \([r_j,d_j)\cap A_j\), while its integral supplies the required processing amount.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A combined window enforces release, deadline, and calendar restrictions simultaneously; preemptive processing may use only admissible portions of that window.
assumptions_latex: Each job has a specified processing requirement.
Release dates, deadlines, and calendars are hard constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Job \(j\) may be processed only within \([r_j,d_j)\cap A_j\), and it must receive its full required processing there.
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The combined release, deadline, and calendar restrictions are coherent for both nonpreemptive and preemptive processing, but no supporting citation is provided.

children.title: Processing Interruption-Mobility Regimes
children.top_down_role: Processing regimes distinguished by whether jobs can be interrupted or reassigned.

children.title: Preemptive Processing Regimes
children.top_down_role: Scheduling regimes permitting processing to pause before later resumption.

knowledge_statements.title: Preemptive Processing Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Processing may be interrupted and resumed without requiring contiguous execution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let job \(j\) require processing amount \(p_j>0\) over horizon \(T\). A preemptive schedule specifies a measurable processing-rate function \(x_j:T\to\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}\) satisfying \(\int_T x_j(t)\,dt=p_j\), together with all resource-capacity constraints. The set \(\{t:x_j(t)>0\}\) need not be a single interval, so execution may be interrupted and resumed. Preemption alone does not authorize migration: if machine assignments are modeled, all positive processing segments must remain on one machine unless migration is separately permitted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Preemption allows a job's processing to be split across time. It does not by itself allow the resumed job to move to another machine.
assumptions_latex: Each job has a positive processing requirement.
Interruptions have zero cost and delay unless separately modeled.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A feasible job may occupy multiple disjoint time intervals whose total delivered processing equals \(p_j\).

notation.meaning: required processing amount of job j
processing rate of job j at time t

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition captures interruption and correctly separates preemption from migration, but the measurable rate-function formulation and its normalization require an authoritative scheduling source.

children.title: Migratory Processing Regimes
children.top_down_role: Scheduling regimes permitting resumed processing on a different eligible resource.

knowledge_statements.title: Migratory Processing Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Preempted jobs may resume on different eligible machines without parallel self-execution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M
eq\varnothing\) be a finite machine set, and let \(x_{jm}(t)\ge0\) denote the processing rate of job \(j\) on machine \(m\). A migratory schedule permits positive processing of the same job on different machines at different times, while imposing \(\sum_{m\in M}x_{jm}(t)\le1\) for every \(j,t\) when simultaneous execution of one job is forbidden. Each job must receive its required work: \(\int_T\sum_{m\in M}x_{jm}(t)\,dt=p_j\). Machine capacities and eligibility restrictions remain binding.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Migration permits a preempted job to continue on another eligible machine, but ordinarily forbids the job from running on several machines simultaneously.
assumptions_latex: \(M\) is finite and machine eligibility is specified.
Processing rates are normalized so one job's total instantaneous rate is at most one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A job may use multiple machines over time, but receives total work \(p_j\) without simultaneous self-parallelism.

notation.meaning: processing rate of job j on machine m at time t

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits migratory processing and explicitly excludes simultaneous self-parallelism, but its normalized rate model is unsupported by a cited source.

children.title: Interruption-Constrained Regimes
children.top_down_role: Scheduling regimes governed by planned or externally imposed processing interruptions.

knowledge_statements.title: Interruption-Constrained Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Preemption is permitted but bounded by counts, segment lengths, or restart penalties.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent job \(j\)'s positive-processing support as a union of maximal disjoint intervals \(I_{j1},\ldots,I_{jq_j}\). An interruption-constrained regime supplements preemptive feasibility with specified restrictions such as \(q_j-1\le K_j\), minimum segment lengths \(|I_{j\ell}|\ge L_j\), or restart delays \(S_{j,\ell+1}-C_{j\ell}\ge\delta_j\). Any combination must be declared as part of the regime. The case \(K_j=0\) forces a single processing interval and hence nonpreemptive execution; unbounded \(K_j\), zero minimum length, and zero restart delay recover unrestricted preemption.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Interruption-constrained scheduling lies between unrestricted preemption and nonpreemption by limiting interruption counts, segment lengths, or restart delays.
assumptions_latex: Processing segments are maximal positive-processing intervals.
All interruption limits are supplied as instance data.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every feasible job decomposition obeys its declared bounds on \(q_j\), \(|I_{j\ell}|\), and restart separation.

notation.meaning: number of processing segments of job j

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A source is needed to fix the intended interruption model. Representing support by finitely many maximal intervals excludes some measurable preemptive schedules, so removing the displayed finite restrictions does not automatically recover unrestricted preemption without an explicit finite-segment assumption.

children.title: Nonpreemptive Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Feasibility or performance boundaries created when processing cannot be interrupted.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonpreemptive Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary at which every job must occupy one uninterrupted processing interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a job \(j\) of processing time \(p_j>0\), nonpreemptive feasibility requires a start time \(S_j\) such that its processing support is exactly \([S_j,S_j+p_j)\). Equivalently, the number of maximal processing segments is \(q_j=1\). Removing this contiguity requirement enlarges the feasible set to preemptive schedules and can restore feasibility: on one unit-capacity machine, jobs with \((r_1,p_1,d_1)=(0,2,3)\) and \((r_2,p_2,d_2)=(1,1,2)\) admit the preemptive sequence consisting of job \(1\) on \([0,1)\), job \(2\) on \([1,2)\), and job \(1\) on \([2,3)\), but no nonpreemptive schedule meets both deadlines.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonpreemption forces each job into one contiguous interval. In the displayed two-job instance, preemption permits both deadlines to be met, whereas every nonpreemptive schedule misses at least one deadline.
assumptions_latex: A single unit-capacity machine is used in the example.
Deadlines are hard completion bounds.
Jobs cannot execute simultaneously.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Contiguous execution is strictly more restrictive than preemptive execution for the displayed instance.

notation.meaning: release date and hard completion deadline of job j

children.title: Coupled Processing Restriction Regimes
children.top_down_role: Operational restrictions coupling consecutive or simultaneous processing decisions.

children.title: Sequence-Dependent Setup Regimes
children.top_down_role: Setup restrictions coupling consecutive activities or resource assignments.

knowledge_statements.title: Sequence-Dependent Setup Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Setup time depends on the ordered pair of consecutive jobs on a machine.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each machine \(m\) and ordered pair of distinct jobs \((i,j)\), let \(s_{ijm}\ge0\) be the setup time required when job \(j\) immediately follows job \(i\) on \(m\). If \(i\prec_m j\) denotes this immediate-successor relation, feasibility requires \(S_j\ge C_i+s_{ijm}\). An initial setup can be represented by a dummy job \(0\) and values \(s_{0jm}\). Because generally \(s_{ijm}\ne s_{jim}\), setup consumption is determined by the machine sequence and must be included in capacity and timing constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sequence-dependent setup separates consecutive jobs by an ordered-pair-specific duration, so changing their order can change feasibility and completion times.
assumptions_latex: Jobs processed on each machine have a well-defined immediate-successor order.
Setup times are nonnegative and supplied as instance data.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Whenever \(i\prec_m j\), the schedule satisfies \(S_j\ge C_i+s_{ijm}\).

notation.meaning: setup time from job i to job j on machine m
j immediately follows i on machine m
start of j and completion of i

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The immediate-successor setup condition is mathematically appropriate and the condition kind fits the leaf, but no scheduling citation supports the formulation.

children.title: Blocking Regimes
children.top_down_role: Resource occupancy caused by unavailable downstream capacity.

knowledge_statements.title: Blocking Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite or absent downstream buffers can retain a completed job on its current machine.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider successive stages with buffer capacity \(b_k\) between stages \(k\) and \(k+1\). After job \(j\) completes processing at stage \(k\), it may leave machine \(k\) only if it can enter the buffer or begin stage \(k+1\). Otherwise it remains on machine \(k\) and blocks that machine from starting another job. In the zero-buffer case, if \(C_{jk}\) is processing completion and \(S_{j,k+1}\) is the next-stage start, the machine-release time is \(R_{jk}=\max\{C_{jk},S_{j,k+1}\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Blocking occurs when a completed job cannot move downstream and therefore continues occupying its current machine until buffer space or the next machine becomes available.
assumptions_latex: Jobs visit ordered processing stages.
Intermediate buffer capacities are finite and specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Machine \(k\) remains unavailable for another job until the blocked job departs at time \(R_{jk}\).

notation.meaning: processing completion of job j at stage k
time job j releases the stage-k machine

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The zero-buffer blocking description is plausible, but flow-shop blocking has multiple conventions and requires a scheduling-specific source. The listed sources on blocking polyhedra are unrelated.

children.title: Batching Regimes
children.top_down_role: Simultaneous or grouped processing under batch-capacity restrictions.

knowledge_statements.title: Batching Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatible jobs are grouped and processed simultaneously as a capacity-limited batch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(J\) be a finite job set, let \(B
eq\varnothing\) be a partition of \(J\), and let machine capacity be \(Q>0\). A batching schedule assigns each batch \(b\in B\) a common start time \(S_b\), with \(\sum_{j\in b}q_j\le Q\) and all members mutually compatible. Every \(j\in b\) starts and completes with its batch. Under parallel batching, a standard duration rule is \(p_b=\max_{j\in b}p_j\), so \(C_j=S_b+p_b\); other duration rules must be declared explicitly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Batching partitions compatible jobs into capacity-feasible groups processed together; under parallel batching, the batch lasts as long as its longest job.
assumptions_latex: Each job has size \(q_j>0\) and processing time \(p_j>0\).
Batch compatibility and machine capacity are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each job inherits its batch's common interval, and every batch respects compatibility and \(\sum_{j\in b}q_j\le Q\).
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition appropriately identifies parallel batching and declares its maximum-duration rule, but no scheduling source supports that variant or distinguishes it from other batching regimes.

children.title: No-Wait Regimes
children.top_down_role: Immediate-transition requirements between successive operations.

knowledge_statements.title: No-Wait Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: No-wait restriction for a fixed technological route through consecutive operations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each job \(j\), let operations \((j,1),\ldots,(j,m_j)\) follow a fixed order, with start times \(S_{jk}\), processing times \(p_{jk}\ge 0\), and completion times \(C_{jk}=S_{jk}+p_{jk}\). The schedule satisfies the no-wait regime exactly when \[S_{j,k+1}=C_{jk}=S_{jk}+p_{jk}\qquad (j,\ k=1,\ldots,m_j-1).\] Thus no positive idle time may occur between successive operations of the same job; machine-capacity and release constraints remain separately applicable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every operation after the first must start exactly when its predecessor finishes, so a job cannot wait between consecutive processing stages.
assumptions_latex: \(m_j\in\mathbb{N}\) and each job has a fixed operation order.
\(p_{jk}\ge 0\) is fixed for every operation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_{j,k+1}-C_{jk}=0\) for every pair of consecutive operations.

notation.meaning: start time of operation k of job j
processing time of operation k of job j
completion time of operation k of job j

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition is mathematically standard and fits the no-wait-regime leaf, but the record has no citation or inspectable locator.

children.title: Scheduling Objective Families
children.top_down_role: Completion, flow, lateness, tardiness, throughput, inventory, stability, energy, and multiple-criteria objectives.

children.title: Completion-Flow Objective Family
children.top_down_role: Criteria based on completion times, system flow, or terminal completion.

children.title: Completion-Time Objectives
children.top_down_role: Criteria aggregating or prioritizing activity completion times.

knowledge_statements.title: Completion-Time Objectives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted and unweighted total-completion-time objectives for a finite job set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(J\) be a finite set of jobs and \(\mathcal{X}\neq\varnothing\) the feasible schedule set. For each \(x\in\mathcal{X}\), let \(C_j(x)\) be the completion time of job \(j\), and let \(w_j\ge0\). A weighted completion-time objective is \[\min_{x\in\mathcal{X}}F_C(x),\qquad F_C(x)=\sum_{j\in J}w_jC_j(x).\] The unweighted total completion time is obtained by taking \(w_j=1\) for every \(j\). Because absolute completion times are used, shifting the common time origin generally changes the objective value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Over the feasible schedules, minimize the sum of job completion times, optionally weighted by nonnegative job priorities.
assumptions_latex: \(J\) is finite and \(\mathcal{X}\neq\varnothing\).
\(C_j(x)\) is finite for every \(j\in J\) and \(x\in\mathcal{X}\), and \(w_j\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{x\in\mathcal{X}}\sum_{j\in J}w_jC_j(x)\).

notation.meaning: completion time of job j in schedule x

children.title: Flow-Time Objectives
children.top_down_role: Criteria measuring time spent within the scheduled system.

knowledge_statements.title: Flow-Time Objectives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted and unweighted flow-time objectives measured from job release to completion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(J\) be a finite job set and \(\mathcal{X}\neq\varnothing\) the feasible schedule set. For each job \(j\), let \(r_j\) be its release time, let \(C_j(x)\ge r_j\) be its completion time in schedule \(x\in\mathcal{X}\), and let \(w_j\ge0\). Its flow time is \(F_j(x)=C_j(x)-r_j\), and the weighted total-flow-time objective is \[\min_{x\in\mathcal{X}}F_{\mathrm{flow}}(x),\qquad F_{\mathrm{flow}}(x)=\sum_{j\in J}w_j(C_j(x)-r_j).\] Taking \(w_j=1\) gives total flow time; dividing that unweighted sum by \(|J|\) gives average flow time without changing its minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Over the feasible schedules, minimize total or weighted time spent by jobs between release and completion.
assumptions_latex: \(J\) is finite and nonempty, and \(\mathcal{X}\neq\varnothing\).
\(C_j(x)\ge r_j\) and \(w_j\ge0\) for every applicable job and schedule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{x\in\mathcal{X}}\sum_{j\in J}w_j(C_j(x)-r_j)\).

notation.meaning: completion time of job j in schedule x

children.title: Makespan Objectives
children.top_down_role: Criteria focused on the terminal completion time of a schedule.

knowledge_statements.title: Makespan Objectives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Maximum-completion-time objective for a finite collection of scheduled jobs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(J\) be a finite nonempty job set and \(\mathcal{X}\neq\varnothing\) the feasible schedule set. For \(x\in\mathcal{X}\), let \(C_j(x)\) be the completion time of job \(j\). The makespan is \[C_{\max}(x)=\max_{j\in J}C_j(x).\] A makespan objective minimizes \(C_{\max}(x)\) over \(x\in\mathcal{X}\). Equivalently, introduce \(M\), impose \(M\ge C_j(x)\) for every \(j\in J\), and minimize \(M\) over \(x\in\mathcal{X}\); at an optimum, \(M=C_{\max}(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimize the time at which the last job finishes; equivalently, minimize a variable that bounds every job completion time.
assumptions_latex: \(J\) is finite and nonempty, and \(\mathcal{X}\neq\varnothing\).
Every \(x\in\mathcal{X}\) has finite completion times.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{x\in\mathcal{X}}C_{\max}(x)=\min\{M:x\in\mathcal{X},\ M\ge C_j(x)\ \text{for every }j\in J\}\).

notation.meaning: completion time of job j in schedule x
epigraph variable bounding all completion times

children.title: Due-Date Performance Objective Family
children.top_down_role: Criteria based on due-date adherence, lateness, tardiness, and completed demand.

children.title: Due-Date Adherence Objectives
children.top_down_role: Criteria concerning conformance to promised or preferred completion dates.

knowledge_statements.title: Due-Date Adherence Objectives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Symmetric or asymmetric penalties for deviation from prescribed due dates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(J\) be a finite job set and \(\mathcal{X}\neq\varnothing\) the feasible schedule set. For each job \(j\), let \(d_j\) be its due date and \(C_j(x)\) its completion time in schedule \(x\in\mathcal{X}\). A due-date adherence objective is \[\min_{x\in\mathcal{X}}F_D(x),\qquad F_D(x)=\sum_{j\in J}\phi_j(C_j(x)-d_j),\] where \(\phi_j:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}_{+}\) satisfies \(\phi_j(0)=0\). The choice \(\phi_j(z)=w_j\lvert z\rvert\), with \(w_j\ge0\), gives weighted absolute deviation. Different penalties for negative and positive deviations distinguish earliness from tardiness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Over the feasible schedules, minimize nonnegative penalties for finishing before or after due dates, possibly using different earliness and tardiness penalties.
assumptions_latex: \(J\) is finite and \(\mathcal{X}\neq\varnothing\).
Each \(\phi_j\) is nonnegative and satisfies \(\phi_j(0)=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{x\in\mathcal{X}}\sum_{j\in J}\phi_j(C_j(x)-d_j)\).

notation.meaning: completion time of job j in schedule x
nonnegative penalty for job j's due-date deviation

children.title: Lateness Objectives
children.top_down_role: Signed deviations of completion times from due dates.

knowledge_statements.title: Lateness Objectives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Signed due-date deviation and the maximum-lateness scheduling objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(J\) be a finite nonempty job set and \(\mathcal{X}\neq\varnothing\) the feasible schedule set. For each \(x\in\mathcal{X}\) and \(j\in J\), lateness is \(L_j(x)=C_j(x)-d_j\), which is negative for early completion and positive for late completion. Maximum lateness is \[L_{\max}(x)=\max_{j\in J}L_j(x),\] and the maximum-lateness objective minimizes \(L_{\max}(x)\) over \(x\in\mathcal{X}\). Unlike tardiness, lateness does not truncate negative deviations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lateness is completion time minus due date; the maximum-lateness objective minimizes the largest signed due-date deviation.
assumptions_latex: \(J\) is finite and nonempty, and \(\mathcal{X}\neq\varnothing\).
Each job has a finite completion time and a specified due date.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{x\in\mathcal{X}}L_{\max}(x)\), where \(L_{\max}(x)=\max_{j\in J}(C_j(x)-d_j)\).

notation.meaning: signed lateness of job j in schedule x
maximum job lateness in schedule x

children.title: Tardiness Objectives
children.top_down_role: Late-completion penalties, counts, or maximum-delay criteria.

knowledge_statements.title: Tardiness Objectives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonnegative late-completion penalties relative to job due dates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(J\) be a finite job set and \(\mathcal{X}\neq\varnothing\) the feasible schedule set. For each \(x\in\mathcal{X}\) and \(j\in J\), with completion time \(C_j(x)\) and due date \(d_j\), tardiness is \[T_j(x)=\max\{C_j(x)-d_j,0\}.\] Common objectives minimize total weighted tardiness \(\sum_{j\in J}w_jT_j(x)\), maximum tardiness \(\max_{j\in J}T_j(x)\), or the weighted number of tardy jobs \(\sum_{j\in J}w_j\mathbf{1}_{\{T_j(x)>0\}}\), where \(w_j\ge0\). Taking \(w_j=1\) in the last expression gives the number of tardy jobs. Early completion contributes zero tardiness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tardiness is the positive part of completion time minus due date; objectives can penalize its total, maximum, or the weighted count of tardy jobs.
assumptions_latex: \(J\) is finite and \(\mathcal{X}\neq\varnothing\).
Each weight satisfies \(w_j\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_j(x)=(C_j(x)-d_j)_{+}\ge0\) for every \(j\in J\) and \(x\in\mathcal{X}\).

notation.meaning: tardiness of job j in schedule x

children.title: Service-Level Objectives
children.top_down_role: Criteria based on completed demand, responsiveness, or fulfillment targets.

knowledge_statements.title: Service-Level Objectives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Due-date service measured by the weighted fraction of jobs completed on time.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(J\) be a finite job set and \(\mathcal{X}\neq\varnothing\) the feasible schedule set. For \(x\in\mathcal{X}\), define \(y_j(x)=\mathbf{1}_{\{C_j(x)\le d_j\}}\). Choose weights \(w_j\ge0\) satisfying \(\sum_{j\in J}w_j>0\). The weighted service level is \[\mathrm{SL}(x)=\frac{\sum_{j\in J}w_jy_j(x)}{\sum_{j\in J}w_j}.\] Maximizing \(\mathrm{SL}(x)\) over \(\mathcal{X}\) is equivalent to minimizing \(\sum_{j\in J}w_j(1-y_j(x))\) over the same set. A target service constraint is \(\mathrm{SL}(x)\ge\alpha\), where \(\alpha\in[0,1]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Over the feasible schedules, maximize the weighted fraction of jobs completed by their due dates, or require that this fraction meet a target.
assumptions_latex: \(J\) is finite and \(\mathcal{X}\neq\varnothing\).
\(w_j\ge0\), \(\sum_{j\in J}w_j>0\), and \(\alpha\in[0,1]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\max_{x\in\mathcal{X}}\mathrm{SL}(x)\) is equivalent to \(\min_{x\in\mathcal{X}}\sum_{j\in J}w_j(1-y_j(x))\).

notation.meaning: indicator that job j completes on time in schedule x
weighted on-time service level of schedule x

children.title: Resource-Performance Scheduling Objectives
children.top_down_role: Economic, environmental, disruption-sensitive, and multiple-criteria objectives.

children.title: Scheduling Cost Objectives
children.top_down_role: Economic criteria involving operation, setup, inventory, or penalty costs.

knowledge_statements.title: Scheduling Cost Objectives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive monetary objective induced by scheduled activities and resource decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal{X}\neq\varnothing\) be the feasible schedule set, and let \(K\) be a finite index set of modeled monetary cost components, such as resource activation, processing, setup, overtime, inventory, or contractual penalties. If \(c_k(x)\in\mathbb{R}\) is the contribution of component \(k\in K\) under schedule \(x\in\mathcal{X}\), a scheduling cost objective is \[\min_{x\in\mathcal{X}}F_{\mathrm{cost}}(x),\qquad F_{\mathrm{cost}}(x)=\sum_{k\in K}c_k(x).\] Fixed charges can be modeled as \(f_ky_k\) with \(y_k\in\{0,1\}\); time-dependent charges must be defined explicitly as functions of schedule attributes or resource usage.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Over the feasible schedules, minimize the total modeled monetary cost of processing, setup, resources, overtime, inventory, and penalties.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal{X}\neq\varnothing\) and \(K\) is finite.
Every \(c_k(x)\) is defined and finite for \(k\in K\) and \(x\in\mathcal{X}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{x\in\mathcal{X}}F_{\mathrm{cost}}(x)=\min_{x\in\mathcal{X}}\sum_{k\in K}c_k(x)\).

children.title: Scheduling Energy Objectives
children.top_down_role: Energy-consumption, peak-load, or emissions-sensitive criteria.

knowledge_statements.title: Scheduling Energy Objectives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Energy consumption induced by time-varying scheduled resource states.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal{X}\neq\varnothing\) be the feasible schedule set, let \(R\) be a finite resource set, and let \(H<\infty\) be the scheduling horizon. Suppose schedule \(x\in\mathcal{X}\) determines an integrable power draw \(P_r(t;x)\ge0\) for each \(r\in R\) and \(t\in[0,H]\). The total schedule energy is \[E(x)=\sum_{r\in R}\int_0^H P_r(t;x)\,dt,\] and a total-energy objective minimizes \(E(x)\) over \(x\in\mathcal{X}\). Discrete-time models use the corresponding slot-duration-weighted sum of power draws.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Over the feasible schedules, minimize the total energy consumed by scheduled resources across the scheduling horizon.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal{X}\neq\varnothing\), \(R\) is finite, and \(H<\infty\).
Each \(P_r(\cdot;x)\) is nonnegative and integrable on \([0,H]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{x\in\mathcal{X}}E(x)=\min_{x\in\mathcal{X}}\sum_{r\in R}\int_0^H P_r(t;x)\,dt\).

notation.meaning: power draw of resource r under schedule x at time t
total energy consumed under schedule x

children.title: Schedule Stability Objectives
children.top_down_role: Criteria penalizing disruption to baseline or published schedules.

knowledge_statements.title: Schedule Stability Objectives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deviation penalties relative to a previously announced baseline schedule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(J\) be a finite job set, let \(\mathcal{X}\neq\varnothing\) be the revised feasible schedule set, and let \(S_j^0\) be the fixed baseline start time of job \(j\). If \(S_j(x)\) is the start time of job \(j\) in revised schedule \(x\in\mathcal{X}\), a start-time stability objective is \[\min_{x\in\mathcal{X}}D(x),\qquad D(x)=\sum_{j\in J}w_j\lvert S_j(x)-S_j^0\rvert,\quad w_j\ge0.\] More generally, stability can use a specified distance on schedule attributes, including completion-time deviations or sequence changes. The baseline and distance must be fixed before optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Over the revised feasible schedules, minimize weighted changes from a fixed baseline schedule, such as absolute start-time shifts.
assumptions_latex: \(J\) is finite, \(\mathcal{X}\neq\varnothing\), and the baseline schedule is fixed.
\(w_j\ge0\) for every \(j\in J\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{x\in\mathcal{X}}D(x)=\min_{x\in\mathcal{X}}\sum_{j\in J}w_j\lvert S_j(x)-S_j^0\rvert\).

notation.meaning: baseline start time of job j
revised start time of job j under schedule x
distance of schedule x from the baseline

children.title: Multiobjective Scheduling
children.top_down_role: Tradeoffs, priorities, or compromise structures spanning multiple scheduling criteria.

knowledge_statements.title: Multiobjective Scheduling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pareto comparison and scalarization for schedules with several performance criteria.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal{X}\) be the feasible schedule set and let \(f(x)=(f_1(x),\ldots,f_q(x))\in\mathbb{R}^q\) be criteria to minimize, with \(q\ge2\). A schedule \(x^*\in\mathcal{X}\) is Pareto efficient if no \(x\in\mathcal{X}\) satisfies \(f_i(x)\le f_i(x^*)\) for every \(i\) and \(f_k(x)<f_k(x^*)\) for some \(k\). One scalarization minimizes \(\sum_{i=1}^q\lambda_i f_i(x)\), where \(\lambda_i\ge0\) and \(\sum_i\lambda_i=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A schedule is Pareto efficient when no feasible schedule improves one objective without worsening at least one other objective.
assumptions_latex: \(q\ge2\) and all criteria use the minimization convention.
\(\mathcal{X}\ne\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^*\) is efficient exactly when no feasible \(x\) dominates it componentwise with at least one strict improvement.

children.title: Scheduling Constraint Models
children.top_down_role: Temporal, ordering, assignment, resource, and network representations used by scheduling solvers.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Constraint Programming Models for Scheduling
Machine Sequencing via Disjunctive Graphs

children.title: Activity-Interval Representation Pair
children.top_down_role: Activity-centered models carrying optionality, duration, start, end, and presence structure.

children.title: Interval-Based Scheduling Models
children.top_down_role: Scheduling representations centered on bounded processing intervals.

assumptions_latex: A finite activity set \(J\) and scheduling horizon \(H\subseteq\mathbb{R}\) are given.
Each activity \(j\in J\) has an allowed duration set \(D_j\subseteq\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A feasible assignment selects one admissible interval for every activity and satisfies all imposed temporal and resource constraints.

notation.meaning: start, end, and duration of activity j

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mandatory, nonpreemptive interval variables over a continuous or discrete horizon.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An interval-based scheduling model associates with each \(j\in J\) an interval variable \(I_j=(s_j,e_j,d_j)\) whose domain satisfies \(s_j,e_j\in H\), \(d_j\in D_j\), and \(e_j=s_j+d_j\). The activity occupies the half-open interval \([s_j,e_j)\). Temporal relations and resource restrictions are predicates over the collection \((I_j)_{j\in J}\); a schedule is feasible exactly when every interval takes a domain value and all such predicates hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each activity is one interval whose start, end, and duration are coupled; feasibility requires all interval-domain, temporal, and resource constraints to hold.
knowledge_statements.title: Interval-Based Scheduling Models

children.title: Activity-Based Scheduling Models
children.top_down_role: Representations centered on activities with temporal attributes.

knowledge_statements.title: Activity-Based Scheduling Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar-variable representation of mandatory, nonpreemptive activities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An activity-based model represents each \(j\in J\) by scalar variables \(s_j\in S_j\subseteq H\), \(p_j\in D_j\subseteq\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}\), and \(c_j\in H\), constrained by \(c_j=s_j+p_j\). A precedence arc \((i,j)\in A\) is represented by \(c_i\le s_j\). Resource feasibility is imposed by constraints whose arguments are these activity attributes. The represented execution set is \(\{(j,t)\in J\times H:s_j\le t<c_j\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Activities are represented by separate start, duration, and completion variables over a scheduling horizon; coupling, precedence, and resource constraints are imposed directly on those scalar attributes.
assumptions_latex: A finite set \(J\) of mandatory, nonpreemptive activities and a scheduling horizon \(H\subseteq\mathbb{R}\) are given.
Each activity \(j\in J\) has a start-time domain \(S_j\subseteq H\) and a duration domain \(D_j\subseteq\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}\).
The set \(A\subseteq J\times J\) contains the imposed precedence arcs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A schedule is represented by scalar activity attributes satisfying their domains, start-completion coupling, precedence constraints, and resource constraints.

notation.meaning: start time and duration of activity j

children.title: Optional Activity Representations
children.top_down_role: Presence-sensitive representations for activities that may be selected or omitted.

assumptions_latex: A finite activity set \(J\) is given.
For each \(j\), \(S_j\) and \(D_j\) are the start and duration domains when the activity is present.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Absence contributes no occupied time or resource demand, while presence activates the ordinary activity constraints.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Presence-literal semantics for optional nonpreemptive activities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An optional activity \(j\in J\) is represented by a presence variable \(z_j\in\{0,1\}\) together with \((s_j,e_j,d_j)\). Its semantics are \(z_j=1\Rightarrow s_j\in S_j,\ d_j\in D_j,\ e_j=s_j+d_j\). When \(z_j=0\), the activity has no occupied interval and contributes zero resource demand. Any constraint requiring execution of \(j\) must imply \(z_j=1\); a conditional precedence is enforced only under the stated presence literals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Boolean presence variable activates an activity's timing and resource effects; an absent activity occupies no time and consumes no resource.
knowledge_statements.title: Optional Activity Representations

children.title: Start-End-Duration Coupling
children.top_down_role: Structural coupling among activity starts, ends, and durations.

knowledge_statements.title: Start-End-Duration Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basic consistency condition for a nonpreemptive activity interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every activity \(j\), let \(s_j,e_j\in\mathbb{R}\) and \(d_j\in\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}\). Start, end, and duration are consistent exactly when \(e_j=s_j+d_j\). Under the half-open convention, execution occurs at times \(t\in\mathbb{R}\) satisfying \(s_j\le t<e_j\). If duration is fixed at \(p_j\in\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}\), the condition reduces to \(e_j=s_j+p_j\); if the activity is optional with presence indicator \(z_j\in\{0,1\}\), the equality is required whenever \(z_j=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonpreemptive activity has real start and end times and a nonnegative duration, with end equal to start plus duration; for an optional activity this equality is required whenever it is present.
assumptions_latex: Activity \(j\) is nonpreemptive.
The scheduling convention uses the half-open execution interval \([s_j,e_j)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any two of \(s_j\), \(e_j\), and \(d_j\) determine the third through \(e_j=s_j+d_j\).

notation.meaning: real start and end times and nonnegative duration of activity j
fixed nonnegative duration when duration is prescribed

children.title: Disjunctive-Sequence Representation Family
children.top_down_role: Unary-resource, non-overlap, successor, and relative-order representations.

children.title: Disjunctive Resource Models
children.top_down_role: Unary-resource representations based on pairwise or global non-overlap.

knowledge_statements.title: Disjunctive Resource Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pairwise nonoverlap model for positive-duration activities using a unary renewable resource.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The unary-resource condition is the conjunction, for every unordered pair \(\{i,j\}\subseteq J_r\), of the disjunction \(s_i+p_i\le s_j\ \lor\ s_j+p_j\le s_i\). Equivalently, the occupied half-open intervals \([s_i,s_i+p_i)\) and \([s_j,s_j+p_j)\) are disjoint. For optional activities with presence variables \(z_i,z_j\in\{0,1\}\), this disjunction is required whenever \(z_i=z_j=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every pair of positive-duration activities using a unary resource must be ordered so that one finishes before the other starts; for optional activities this is required only when both are present.
assumptions_latex: A finite set \(J_r\) of nonpreemptive activities requires one unary resource \(r\).
Every activity \(j\in J_r\) has start time \(s_j\in\mathbb{R}\) and duration \(p_j\in\mathbb{R}_{>0}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At most one activity in \(J_r\) executes at any time.

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

source_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

children.title: Sequence Variable Models
children.top_down_role: Representations carrying resource-specific activity order.

assumptions_latex: A finite set \(J_r\) of activities may use unary resource \(r\).
Each present activity has a well-defined execution interval.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Resource feasibility holds when the sequence order and interval times are mutually consistent.

notation.meaning: ordered sequence of present activities on resource r

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: sequence variables conventionally encode a permutation of present unary-resource activities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Permutation representation of activities assigned to a unary resource.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A sequence-variable model assigns to resource \(r\) an ordered list \(\pi_r=(j_1,\ldots,j_m)\) containing each present activity from \(J_r\) exactly once and no absent activity. Feasibility requires \(s_{j_k}+p_{j_k}\le s_{j_{k+1}}\) for \(k=1,\ldots,m-1\), possibly strengthened by sequence-dependent setup times. Hence consecutive-order constraints imply pairwise nonoverlap for all activities appearing in \(\pi_r\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A resource sequence is a permutation of its present activities, and every activity must finish before its listed successor starts.
knowledge_statements.title: Sequence Variable Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The sequence representation is plausible and locally appropriate, but no inspectable source supports the permutation semantics or the claimed implication from consecutive constraints. A scheduling-specific source is required.

children.title: Successor-Based Scheduling Models
children.top_down_role: Representations based on immediate predecessor or successor structure.

assumptions_latex: A finite activity set \(J_r\) is assigned to a unary resource.
Dummy vertices \(0\) and \(n+1\) denote the beginning and end of the resource route.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected arcs form one path through every scheduled activity, and each selected arc enforces temporal succession.

notation.meaning: indicator that j immediately succeeds i

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: immediate-successor arcs are the standard path encoding of a machine sequence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directed-path encoding of a unary-resource activity order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(V=J_r\cup\{0,n+1\}\), let \(x_{ij}\in\{0,1\}\) indicate that \(j\) immediately follows \(i\). A mandatory-activity model imposes \(\sum_{i\in V\setminus\{j\}}x_{ij}=1\) and \(\sum_{k\in V\setminus\{j\}}x_{jk}=1\) for each \(j\in J_r\), one arc leaving \(0\), one entering \(n+1\), and no subtour on \(J_r\). Every selected arc satisfies \(x_{ij}=1\Rightarrow s_j\ge s_i+p_i+q_{ij}\), where \(q_{ij}\ge0\) is a setup time.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Binary immediate-successor arcs form a single activity path; each selected arc forces the successor to start after processing and setup.

start and duration of activity i

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For distinct \(i,j\in J_r\), let \(y_{ij}\in\{0,1\}\) mean that \(i\) precedes \(j\). A relative-order representation imposes \(y_{ij}+y_{ji}=1\) and transitivity, for example \(y_{ij}+y_{jk}-1\le y_{ik}\) for distinct \(i,j,k\). Temporal compatibility requires \(y_{ij}=1\Rightarrow s_i+p_i\le s_j\). These conditions encode a strict total order whose timing realization satisfies unary-resource nonoverlap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pairwise precedence binaries, antisymmetry, transitivity, and timing implications encode a total order of activities on a unary resource.

children.title: Cumulative Resource Models
children.top_down_role: Renewable-capacity representations for overlapping activities.

knowledge_statements.title: Cumulative Resource Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Time-indexed capacity condition for a renewable cumulative resource.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The cumulative-resource constraint for \(r\) is \[\sum_{j\in J_r:\,s_j\le t<s_j+p_j}a_j\le C_r\qquad\text{for every }t\in H.\] For optional activities with presence indicators \(z_j\in\{0,1\}\), the summation includes only indices satisfying \(z_j=1\). Under the half-open interval convention, an activity ending at \(t\) releases its capacity before an activity starting at \(t\) consumes capacity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At every time in the scheduling horizon, the sum of demands from executing activities cannot exceed the renewable resource capacity; absent optional activities contribute no demand.
assumptions_latex: A scheduling horizon \(H\subseteq\mathbb{R}\) and a finite activity set \(J_r\) are given.
Each activity \(j\in J_r\) has start time \(s_j\in H\), duration \(p_j\in\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}\), and renewable-resource demand \(a_j\in\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}\).
Resource \(r\) has constant capacity \(C_r\in\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Aggregate simultaneous demand never exceeds \(C_r\) at any \(t\in H\).

notation.meaning: activities that use renewable resource r
resource demand of activity j while executing
start time and duration of activity j

children.title: Reservoir Resource Models
children.top_down_role: Level-evolution representations with consuming or producing events.

assumptions_latex: A reservoir has initial level \(L_0\).
Each event \(k\) occurs at time \(\tau_k\) and changes the level by \(\Delta_k\).
Permitted levels satisfy \(L_{\min}\le L\le L_{\max}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every event-time prefix level remains within the reservoir bounds.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: reservoir feasibility is characterized by bounded prefix sums of event changes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Discrete-event balance model for a bounded consumable-replenishable resource.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Order the events so that \(\tau_1\le\cdots\le\tau_m\), using a fixed convention for simultaneous events. The level after event \(k\) is \(L_k=L_0+\sum_{h=1}^{k}\Delta_h\). The reservoir model is feasible exactly when \(L_{min}\le L_k\le L_{max}\) for every \(k=0,\ldots,m\), where positive \(\Delta_h\) replenishes and negative \(\Delta_h\) consumes the resource. Optional events contribute their change only when present.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from an initial level, ordered event changes are accumulated, and every resulting prefix level must remain between lower and upper bounds.
knowledge_statements.title: Reservoir Resource Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A scheduling-specific source is required. Ordering simultaneous changes by an arbitrary fixed convention can introduce intermediate levels that are not part of an aggregate event-time model, so the exact semantics must be sourced. The record also inconsistently writes the bounds as L_min/L_max and L_{min}/L_{max}.

children.title: Inventory Scheduling Models

assumptions_latex: Inventory is tracked at ordered periods or event epochs \(t=1,\ldots,T\).

Inventory bounds \(\underline I_t\le\overline I_t\) are given.

Equivalently, \(I_t=I_0+\sum_{h=1}^{t}(u_h-v_h)\). When production or consumption is caused by scheduled activities, the corresponding \(u_t\) or \(v_t\) is activated at the activity's designated start, completion, or processing epoch according to the model convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inventory equals previous stock plus supply minus demand, stays within bounds, and links scheduled activities to their production or consumption epochs.

children.title: Hybrid Resource-Flow Models

assumptions_latex: Activities have execution intervals and renewable demands.
A finite resource-flow network has initial supplies and activity-induced production or consumption.
All timing conventions for flow events are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A schedule is feasible only if both instantaneous capacity constraints and inter-event flow balances hold.

notation.meaning: flow sent from event i to event j

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: hybrid models conjunct renewable-capacity and conserved-flow constraints through shared activity decisions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint interval, cumulative-capacity, and conserved-flow representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A hybrid resource-flow model uses common activity times in two constraint systems. Renewable feasibility requires \(\sum_{j:\,s_j\le t<s_j+p_j}a_j\le C\) for every \(t\). Flow feasibility requires nonnegative transfers \(f_{ij}\ge0\), event-wise conservation of incoming supply plus production against outgoing flow plus consumption, and stock bounds \(L_{min}\le L_k\le L_{max}\). A transfer arc \((i,j)\) may carry positive flow only when the associated temporal order permits resource released or produced at \(i\) to reach \(j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Shared activity times must satisfy renewable capacity limits, bounded material balances, flow conservation, and temporal compatibility of positive transfers.

children.title: Execution-Choice Representation Family
children.top_down_role: Choice among machines, modes, routes, skills, or processing alternatives.

children.title: Processing Alternative Models
children.top_down_role: Choice structures spanning alternative machines, routes, or realizations.

knowledge_statements.title: Processing Alternative Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Alternative-interval representation for selecting exactly one processing realization of each mandatory activity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every activity \(i\in I\), let \(A_i\) be its finite nonempty set of processing alternatives. Introduce a master interval \(X_i\), optional alternative intervals \(X_{ia}\), and selectors \(x_{ia}\in\{0,1\}\). The processing-alternative representation is defined by \[\sum_{a\in A_i}x_{ia}=1,\qquad \operatorname{pres}(X_{ia})=x_{ia},\qquad \operatorname{start}(X_{ia})=\operatorname{start}(X_i),\qquad \operatorname{end}(X_{ia})=\operatorname{end}(X_i)\] whenever \(x_{ia}=1\), together with \(\operatorname{length}(X_{ia})=p_{ia}\). Thus the selected alternative determines the realized duration while all unselected intervals are absent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each activity chooses exactly one optional processing alternative; the chosen interval shares the activity’s start and end and supplies its processing duration.
assumptions_latex: \(I\) and every \(A_i\) are finite.
\(p_{ia}>0\) is fixed for each alternative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exactly one alternative interval realizes each activity and determines its duration.

notation.meaning: processing alternatives available to activity i
optional interval for activity i under alternative a

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation and content kind fit the leaf, but the cited general constraint-programming section does not inspectably support this exact alternative-interval formulation.

children.title: Resource Assignment Models
children.top_down_role: Representations linking activities to eligible resources or skills.

knowledge_statements.title: Resource Assignment Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary assignment representation for activities requiring one eligible unary resource.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R_i\subseteq R\) be the nonempty set of resources eligible for activity \(i\). Introduce \(y_{ir}\in\{0,1\}\) and impose \[\sum_{r\in R_i}y_{ir}=1\qquad(i\in I).\] If \(S_i\) and \(p_{ir}>0\) denote the start and resource-dependent processing time, then activities assigned to the same unary resource satisfy \[y_{ir}=y_{jr}=1\ \Longrightarrow\ S_i+p_{ir}\le S_j\ \lor\ S_j+p_{jr}\le S_i.\] Hence assignment and nonoverlap jointly represent resource selection and resource-feasible execution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each activity is assigned to exactly one eligible resource, and activities assigned to the same unary resource cannot overlap.
assumptions_latex: \(I\) and \(R\) are finite.
Every activity requires exactly one unary resource throughout processing.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected assignments satisfy eligibility, uniqueness, and unary-resource nonoverlap.

notation.meaning: binary assignment of activity i to resource r

children.title: Execution Mode Models
children.top_down_role: Mode choices affecting duration, demand, cost, or resource use.

knowledge_statements.title: Execution Mode Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Discrete-mode representation coupling an activity’s duration and renewable-resource demands.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\) be a finite activity set and \(R\) a finite renewable-resource set. For each \(i\in I\), let \(M_i\) be a finite nonempty mode set and let \(S_i\in\mathbb{R}\) be its start time. Mode \(m\in M_i\) specifies duration \(p_{im}>0\) and demand \(q_{imr}\ge 0\) on every \(r\in R\). With selectors \(z_{im}\in\{0,1\}\), impose \[\sum_{m\in M_i}z_{im}=1,\qquad p_i=\sum_{m\in M_i}p_{im}z_{im},\qquad q_{ir}=\sum_{m\in M_i}q_{imr}z_{im}\qquad(i\in I,r\in R).\] For constant capacities \(Q_r\ge0\), renewable-resource feasibility requires \[\sum_{i\in I:\,S_i\le t<S_i+p_i}q_{ir}\le Q_r\qquad(r\in R,t\in\mathbb{R}).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exactly one execution mode is chosen for each activity. The selected mode simultaneously determines duration and renewable-resource demands, and the demands of activities executing at any time cannot exceed capacity.
assumptions_latex: \(I\), \(R\), and every \(M_i\) are finite.
Activities are nonpreemptive and consume their selected demands throughout execution.
Renewable resource \(r\) has constant capacity \(Q_r\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each activity has one coherent mode-dependent duration and demand vector, and the resulting execution profile respects every renewable-resource capacity.

notation.meaning: binary selector for mode m of activity i

children.title: Coupled Choice Representations
children.top_down_role: Interactions among alternative selection, assignment compatibility, and mode selection.

knowledge_statements.title: Coupled Choice Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shared-selector representation preventing inconsistent processing, mode, and resource choices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K_i\) be the admissible joint configurations for activity \(i\), where each \(k\in K_i\) fixes a processing alternative, execution mode, eligible resource, duration \(p_{ik}\), and demand vector \(q_{ikr}\). Introduce \(w_{ik}\in\{0,1\}\) with \[\sum_{k\in K_i}w_{ik}=1.\] Every marginal selector is derived from the same joint choice; for example, \[x_{ia}=\sum_{k\in K_i:a(k)=a}w_{ik},\qquad y_{ir}=\sum_{k\in K_i:r(k)=r}w_{ik},\qquad z_{im}=\sum_{k\in K_i:m(k)=m}w_{ik}.\] Consequently, incompatible combinations excluded from \(K_i\) cannot be selected.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A single joint configuration selector determines processing alternative, mode, and resource, so independently valid but mutually incompatible choices cannot occur.
assumptions_latex: \(K_i\) is finite, nonempty, and contains exactly the admissible joint configurations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: All marginal execution choices are mutually consistent projections of one selected configuration.

notation.meaning: admissible joint configurations for activity i
alternative, mode, and resource components of configuration k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The shared-selector construction is coherent and correctly classified as a representation, but the generic mathematical-modeling locator does not specifically support this coupled scheduling-choice formulation.

children.title: Time-Indexed Scheduling Models
children.top_down_role: Discrete-time formulations coupling time, assignment, and resource usage.

knowledge_statements.title: Time-Indexed Scheduling Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Discrete-time start-indexed formulation for nonpreemptive renewable-resource scheduling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T=\{0,\ldots,H-1\}\) and let binary variable \(x_{it}\) equal one exactly when activity \(i\) starts at time \(t\). A start-indexed model imposes \[\sum_{t=0}^{H-p_i}x_{it}=1\qquad(i\in I)\] and, for every renewable resource \(r\) and period \(\tau\in T\), \[\sum_{i\in I}q_{ir}\sum_{t=\max\{0,\tau-p_i+1\}}^{\min\{\tau,H-p_i\}}x_{it}\le Q_r.\] Precedence \(i\prec j\) is represented by \[\sum_t(t+p_i)x_{it}\le\sum_t t x_{jt}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Binary variables select each activity’s discrete start period; convolution-style capacity constraints count every activity executing during each period.
assumptions_latex: Processing times \(p_i\) and horizon \(H\) are positive integers.
Activities are nonpreemptive and use constant demands \(q_{ir}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Integral feasible solutions correspond to discrete-time schedules satisfying assignment, precedence, and renewable-resource capacities.

notation.meaning: binary indicator that activity i starts in period t
