children.title: Event-Based Scheduling Models
children.top_down_role: Compact formulations indexed by timing events or event points.

knowledge_statements.title: Event-Based Scheduling Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuous-time formulation assigning activity starts and completions to ordered events.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix event indices \(E=\{0,\ldots,K\}\) with continuous times \(0\le T_0\le\cdots\le T_K\). For each activity \(i\), binary variables \(u_{ik}\) and \(v_{i\ell}\) select one start event and one completion event: \[\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}u_{ik}=1,\qquad \sum_{\ell=1}^{K}v_{i\ell}=1.\] Impose \(u_{ik}+v_{i\ell}\le1\) for \(\ell\le k\), and enforce \[u_{ik}=v_{i\ell}=1\ \Longrightarrow\ T_\ell-T_k\ge p_i.\] Resource constraints are imposed over every event interval \([T_k,T_{k+1})\) using the activities active there.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Activities choose ordered start and completion events whose continuous times provide sufficient duration; resource feasibility is checked between consecutive events.
assumptions_latex: The number \(K+1\) of events is fixed and finite.
Activities are nonpreemptive with durations \(p_i>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every integral solution defines an event-ordered continuous-time schedule.

notation.meaning: indicator that activity i starts at event k
indicator that activity i completes at event l

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record describes an event-based representation in the correct local sense, but the generic modeling locator does not support the particular start-event, completion-event, duration, and resource formulation.

children.title: Position-Based Scheduling Models
children.top_down_role: Formulations indexed by processing positions within resource sequences.

knowledge_statements.title: Position-Based Scheduling Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Permutation-position formulation for nonpreemptive scheduling on one machine.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(n\) jobs and positions \(K=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), let \(z_{ik}\in\{0,1\}\) indicate that job \(i\) occupies position \(k\). Impose \[\sum_{k\in K}z_{ik}=1\quad(i=1,\ldots,n),\qquad \sum_{i=1}^{n}z_{ik}=1\quad(k\in K).\] With completion variables \(C_k\), enforce \[C_1\ge\sum_i p_i z_{i1},\qquad C_k\ge C_{k-1}+\sum_i p_i z_{ik}\quad(k=2,\ldots,n).\] The assignment matrix therefore defines a permutation, and the recurrence constructs a feasible serial schedule in that order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A doubly stochastic binary assignment places each job in one unique sequence position; completion-time recurrences then construct the machine schedule.
assumptions_latex: There are \(n\) mandatory nonpreemptive jobs.
All jobs require the same unary machine and have \(p_i>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Integral position assignments encode a permutation schedule without overlap.

notation.meaning: indicator that job i occupies position k
completion time of the job in position k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The position-based permutation representation is mathematically coherent and correctly classified, but its cited generic modeling section does not inspectably support the formulation.

children.title: Network-Based Scheduling Models
children.top_down_role: Activity-network or route-network representations of scheduling structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Network-Based Scheduling Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Immediate-predecessor network formulation for a single-machine permutation schedule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Augment jobs \(I\) by source \(0\) and sink \(n+1\). Let \(y_{ij}\in\{0,1\}\) indicate that \(j\) immediately follows \(i\). Degree constraints require one incoming and one outgoing selected arc for every job, one arc leaving the source, and one entering the sink; subtour-elimination constraints require the selected arcs to form a single source-to-sink path. With valid \(M_{ij}\), impose \[S_j\ge S_i+p_i-M_{ij}(1-y_{ij})\] for all admissible job-to-job arcs. The selected path and timing inequalities encode a nonoverlapping permutation schedule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Selected immediate-successor arcs form one source-to-sink job path, while conditional timing inequalities schedule each successor after its predecessor.
assumptions_latex: All jobs are mandatory, nonpreemptive, and use one unary machine.
Each \(M_{ij}\) is a valid upper bound for relaxing its timing implication.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every integral path solution induces a feasible job order and corresponding nonoverlapping start times.

notation.meaning: selected immediate-successor arc from i to j

children.title: Compact Formulation Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Representational tradeoffs involving size, strength, symmetry, and temporal resolution.

knowledge_statements.title: Compact Formulation Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Size and relaxation tradeoff between indexed and compact scheduling formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(n\) activities, integer horizon \(H\), and positive integer processing times \(p_i\le H\), a start-indexed formulation containing one binary variable for every admissible start uses \[\sum_{i=1}^{n}(H-p_i+1)\] binary variables before mode or resource indices. This count is \(O(nH)\), and it is \(\Theta(nH)\) when every activity has \(\Theta(H)\) admissible starts. Event-based formulations may use \(O(nK)\) assignment binaries for \(K\) events, while position- and arc-based formulations commonly use \(O(n^2)\) binaries, with neither count directly depending on \(H\). Compactness alone does not imply a stronger linear relaxation: in the relaxation of \[S_j\ge S_i+p_i-M_{ij}(1-y_{ij}),\qquad 0\le y_{ij}\le1,\] a large valid \(M_{ij}\) can substantially relax the timing inequality at fractional \(y_{ij}\). Thus variable count, relaxation strength, symmetry, and propagation are distinct formulation criteria.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A start-indexed model has one variable for each admissible activity-start pair, giving at most order nH variables and order nH only when activities each retain order H possible starts. Compact event, position, or arc models avoid direct horizon dependence, but can still have weak fractional big-M constraints or symmetry, so fewer variables do not establish dominance.
assumptions_latex: The start-indexed model explicitly represents every admissible integer start period.
\(1\le p_i\le H\) for every activity \(i\).
Every big-M constant \(M_{ij}\) is finite and valid for its conditional timing inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Asymptotic compactness alone guarantees neither relaxation dominance nor superior computational behavior.

notation.meaning: valid big-M constant for a conditional timing inequality

children.title: Unary-Resource Propagation

children.title: Unary Profile-Precedence Propagation
children.top_down_role: Profile and precedence inference for unary resources.

children.title: Detectable Precedence Reasoning
children.top_down_role: Unary-resource inference establishing forced relative order.

knowledge_statements.title: Detectable Precedence Reasoning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pairwise unary-resource rule detecting a forced precedence from current time bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider two mandatory activities \(i\) and \(j\) sharing a unary resource, with start domains \([\operatorname{est}_i,\operatorname{lst}_i]\) and \([\operatorname{est}_j,\operatorname{lst}_j]\), and durations \(p_i,p_j>0\). If \[\operatorname{est}_i+p_i>\operatorname{lst}_j,\] then the ordering \(i\prec j\) is impossible: even the earliest completion of \(i\) exceeds the latest start of \(j\). Unary nonoverlap therefore forces \(j\prec i\), allowing the sound updates \[\operatorname{est}_i\leftarrow\max\{\operatorname{est}_i,\operatorname{est}_j+p_j\},\qquad \operatorname{lst}_j\leftarrow\min\{\operatorname{lst}_j,\operatorname{lst}_i-p_j\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If one activity cannot finish before another’s latest start, unary nonoverlap forces the reverse order and permits corresponding bound updates.
assumptions_latex: Activities \(i\) and \(j\) are mandatory and nonpreemptive.
Both activities require the same unary resource.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inequality \(\operatorname{est}_i+p_i>\operatorname{lst}_j\) soundly implies \(j\prec i\).

notation.meaning: earliest start time of activity i
latest start time of activity i
activity i completes before activity j starts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The pairwise inference is coherent and the condition kind fits its triggering inequality, but no citation supports the rule or its bound updates.

children.title: Unary Time-Table Reasoning
children.top_down_role: Unary-resource inference based on compulsory occupancy profiles.

knowledge_statements.title: Unary Time-Table Reasoning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compulsory-part propagation for mandatory activities on a unary resource.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For mandatory activity \(i\) with duration \(p_i>0\), earliest completion \(\operatorname{ect}_i=\operatorname{est}_i+p_i\), and latest start \(\operatorname{lst}_i\), the interval \([\operatorname{lst}_i,\operatorname{ect}_i)\) is compulsory when \(\operatorname{lst}_i<\operatorname{ect}_i\). Every feasible execution of \(i\) occupies the unary resource throughout this interval. Two overlapping compulsory parts certify infeasibility. For another activity \(j\), every candidate start \(s\) satisfying \[[s,s+p_j)\cap[\operatorname{lst}_i,\operatorname{ect}_i)\ne\varnothing\] is forbidden unless \(j=i\); removing all such starts is sound time-table propagation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A task’s compulsory interval is occupied in every schedule; overlapping compulsory intervals are infeasible, and other tasks cannot be placed across them.
assumptions_latex: All considered activities are mandatory and nonpreemptive.
All considered activities require the same unary resource.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Compulsory-part conflicts soundly detect infeasibility and remove conflicting start values.

notation.meaning: earliest completion time of activity i
latest start time of activity i

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The compulsory-part rule is coherent and appropriately classified as a propagation condition, but the record supplies no authoritative locator for the compulsory interval, conflict test, or start-value pruning rule.

children.title: Profile-Precedence Interaction
children.top_down_role: Combined use of occupancy profiles and inferred activity order.

knowledge_statements.title: Profile-Precedence Interaction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-point interaction between compulsory-resource profiles and inferred unary precedences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\) be the vector of current start bounds for mandatory activities on a unary resource. Let \(P(B)\) apply all sound detectable-precedence updates, and let \(T(B)\) apply all sound compulsory-profile exclusions. Both operators are contracting on finite start domains: they delete values or tighten bounds without adding values. Alternating them to a fixed point, \[B^{k+1}=T(P(B^k)),\] is sound because precedence updates can create or enlarge compulsory parts, while profile exclusions can tighten bounds enough to make additional precedences detectable. Termination follows when all start domains are finite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Precedence propagation can strengthen the compulsory profile, and profile pruning can reveal new precedences; alternating both sound operators reaches a stronger finite-domain fixed point.
assumptions_latex: Start domains are finite.

children.title: Unary Edge-Finding

knowledge_statements.title: Unary Edge-Finding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact forced-edge tests for nonpreemptive activities on one unary resource.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U\) be activities with start domains \(S_i\in[r_i,d_i-p_i]\) and durations \(p_i>0\). For every \(i\notin\Omega\subseteq U\), test feasibility after imposing either \(C_i\le S_j\) for every \(j\in\Omega\), or \(C_j\le S_i\) for every \(j\in\Omega\), together with all release, deadline, and unary nonoverlap constraints. If the first restricted problem is infeasible, delete the ordering in which \(i\) precedes all of \(\Omega\); if the second is infeasible, delete the ordering in which \(i\) follows all of \(\Omega\). Propagate any resulting precedence and start-bound consequences, repeating until no domain changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Edge-finding rejects placing an activity wholly before or after a subset whenever that restricted unary schedule is infeasible.
assumptions_latex: \(U\) is finite, and activities are nonpreemptive.
\(C_i=S_i+p_i\) for every \(i\in U\).
Distinct activities cannot overlap on the unary resource.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each rejected extreme ordering has no extension to a feasible unary schedule.

notation.meaning: start and completion times of activity i

children.title: Not-First Reasoning

knowledge_statements.title: Not-First Reasoning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exclusion of an activity from the first position of a unary subset.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonempty subset \(\Omega\subseteq U\) and \(i\in\Omega\), form the restricted unary scheduling problem containing the current time bounds and the constraints \(C_i\le S_j\) for all \(j\in\Omega\setminus\{i\}\). If this restricted problem is infeasible, then \(i\) cannot be first in any feasible ordering of \(\Omega\). Consequently, the first-position value is removed from the positional domain of \(i\); any precedence or start-time bound entailed by the remaining positions may also be propagated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An activity is not first when forcing it before every other activity in the subset makes the unary subproblem infeasible.

\(S_k\in[r_k,d_k-p_k]\) and \(C_k=S_k+p_k\) for every \(k\in\Omega\).

children.title: Positional Exclusion Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Regimes where positional exclusions differ in strength or applicability.

knowledge_statements.title: Positional Exclusion Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact lower and upper feasible-position boundaries within a unary activity subset.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(i\in\Omega\), let \(P_i\subseteq\{1,\ldots,|\Omega|\}\) contain every position occupied by \(i\) in some feasible nonoverlapping schedule of \(\Omega\) satisfying the current time bounds. When \(P_i\ne\varnothing\), define \(\ell_i=\min P_i\) and \(u_i=\max P_i\). Positions \(k<\ell_i\) and \(k>u_i\) are infeasible and may be deleted. In particular, not-first reasoning establishes \(\ell_i\ge2\), while not-last reasoning establishes \(u_i\le|\Omega|-1\). If \(P_i=\varnothing\), the unary subproblem itself is infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The positional boundaries are the earliest and latest ranks an activity attains in any feasible ordering; all exterior ranks are excluded.
assumptions_latex: \(\Omega\) is finite and all its activities require the same unary resource.
Positions are numbered by nondecreasing activity start time.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_i\subseteq[\ell_i,u_i]\cap\mathbb Z\), and every position outside this interval is infeasible.

children.title: Cumulative-Resource Propagation

children.title: Cumulative Time-Table Reasoning
children.top_down_role: Capacity-profile inference from compulsory activity parts.

knowledge_statements.title: Cumulative Time-Table Reasoning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compulsory-part capacity profiling for a nonpreemptive cumulative resource.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each activity \(i\), let \(e_i\) and \(\ell_i\) be its earliest and latest starts. Its compulsory part is \(K_i=[\ell_i,e_i+p_i)\) when \(\ell_i<e_i+p_i\), and is empty otherwise. Construct \(H(t)=\sum_{i:t\in K_i}q_i\). Declare failure if \(H(t)>C\) for some \(t\). For each activity \(i\) and candidate start \(s\in[e_i,\ell_i]\), delete \(s\) if some \(t\in[s,s+p_i)\) satisfies \(q_i+\sum_{j\ne i:t\in K_j}q_j>C\). Recompute compulsory parts after every bound change and iterate to a fixpoint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Time-table propagation profiles compulsory demand, detects overload, and removes starts whose execution would exceed capacity against that profile.
assumptions_latex: Activities are nonpreemptive and have fixed durations \(p_i>0\) and demands \(q_i\ge0\).
The cumulative resource has constant capacity \(C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every deleted start violates \(\sum_{i:S_i\le t<S_i+p_i}q_i\le C\) at some time \(t\).

notation.meaning: compulsory execution interval of activity i

children.title: Energetic Reasoning
children.top_down_role: Aggregate demand reasoning over candidate time intervals.

knowledge_statements.title: Energetic Reasoning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary cumulative-capacity inequality over every candidate time interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every interval \([a,b)\) with \(a<b\), define the minimum duration of activity \(i\) that must execute inside it by \(m_i(a,b)=\max\{0,\min(p_i,b-a,e_i+p_i-a,b-\ell_i)\}\), where \(e_i\) and \(\ell_i\) are the earliest and latest starts. Any feasible cumulative schedule satisfies \[\sum_i q_i m_i(a,b)\le C(b-a).\] Hence an interval violating this inequality certifies infeasibility. Candidate start bounds may be removed whenever conditioning on the candidate makes the same inequality fail for some interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In every interval, the total resource energy that activities must consume cannot exceed capacity times interval length.
assumptions_latex: Activities are nonpreemptive with \(S_i\in[e_i,\ell_i]\), duration \(p_i>0\), and demand \(q_i\ge0\).
The resource capacity is the constant \(C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_i q_i m_i(a,b)>C(b-a)\) for some \([a,b)\) implies infeasibility.

notation.meaning: minimum forced processing of activity i inside the interval
total resource energy of activity i

children.title: Cumulative Edge-Finding

knowledge_statements.title: Cumulative Edge-Finding

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Omega\) be activities sharing capacity \(C\), and let \(i\notin\Omega\). Test the cumulative scheduling subproblem after imposing \(C_i\le S_j\) for every \(j\in\Omega\). If its capacity and time-window constraints are infeasible, then \(i\) cannot precede all activities of \(\Omega\). Symmetrically, infeasibility after imposing \(C_j\le S_i\) for every \(j\in\Omega\) excludes \(i\) from following all of \(\Omega\). These exclusions may be converted into start or completion bound updates whenever the remaining ordering alternatives entail such bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cumulative edge-finding excludes an activity from lying wholly before or after a subset when that extreme ordering cannot respect capacity.
assumptions_latex: Each activity is nonpreemptive with fixed duration and nonnegative resource demand.
At every time \(t\), total executing demand must not exceed \(C\).

children.title: Hybrid Cumulative Propagation

knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Cumulative Propagation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixpoint composition of complementary sound cumulative-resource filters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize a work queue with time-table, energetic, and cumulative edge-finding propagators for each cumulative resource. Apply a queued propagator to the current domains. If it proves overload, return infeasible; if it tightens any start, completion, presence, or ordering domain, enqueue every propagator whose inputs changed. Continue until the queue is empty. The output is the common fixpoint reached by these sound contracting operators under the selected scheduling policy; no value removed by any component can belong to a feasible schedule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hybrid propagation repeatedly combines time-table, energetic, and edge-finding filters until no component can tighten a domain.
assumptions_latex: Every component propagator is sound and contracting on the finite domain lattice.
Changed domains trigger every component that depends on them.

children.title: Propagation Strength Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Tradeoffs involving pruning strength, applicability, and computational effort.

knowledge_statements.title: Propagation Strength Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dominance and computational-cost comparison for cumulative propagators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For contracting propagators \(P\) and \(Q\) on the same domain lattice, define \(P\) to dominate \(Q\) when \(P(D)\subseteq Q(D)\) for every domain state \(D\). Dominance compares pruning strength, not running time: a dominating propagator may require greater worst-case or observed computational cost. If neither inclusion holds for all \(D\), the propagators are incomparable, and their fixpoint composition can prune more than either one alone. Thus selecting a cumulative propagation portfolio requires jointly considering domain reduction, invocation frequency, and computational cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stronger propagator always leaves subsets of another's domains, but may cost more; incomparable filters can gain strength through composition.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) and \(Q\) are sound, monotone, and contracting.
Both operators act on the same ordered collection of domains.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P\succeq Q\iff(\forall D)\,P(D)\subseteq Q(D)\); this relation alone implies no runtime ordering.

children.title: Alternative-Choice Propagation

knowledge_statements.title: Alternative-Choice Propagation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Domain filtering for exactly-one optional scheduling alternatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a master activity have alternatives \(A_1,\ldots,A_m\) with presence variables \(z_k\in\{0,1\}\) and \(\sum_{k=1}^m z_k=1\). For each undecided alternative, temporarily impose \(z_k=1\), channel its start, completion, duration, and resource attributes to the master, and run the relevant constraints. If this restricted state is infeasible, set \(z_k=0\). If only one alternative remains, set its presence to one. If no alternative remains, report infeasibility. Repeat whenever a master or alternative domain changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Alternative propagation removes choices that cannot support the master activity and forces the sole remaining feasible choice.
assumptions_latex: Exactly one alternative must be present.
Channeling equates the selected alternative's scheduling attributes with those of the master activity.
Each feasibility test is sound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_k=0\) is inferred only if the state with \(z_k=1\) has no feasible extension.

children.title: Resource-Assignment Propagation

knowledge_statements.title: Resource-Assignment Propagation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Filtering activity-to-resource assignment domains using conditional scheduling feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every activity \(i\), maintain a finite assignment domain \(R_i\) of eligible resources. For each \(r\in R_i\), condition on \(x_i=r\), post the corresponding resource-demand and no-overlap or cumulative constraints, and run their sound propagators. If the conditioned state is infeasible, delete \(r\) from \(R_i\). If \(R_i=\varnothing\), report infeasibility; if \(|R_i|=1\), fix the assignment and activate its resource constraints. Iterate assignment and scheduling propagation until no domain changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A resource is removed from an activity's assignment domain when assigning it there cannot extend to a feasible schedule.
assumptions_latex: Every activity must receive exactly one resource from its finite eligibility domain.
Conditioned resource propagators are sound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r\notin R_i\) whenever the state conditioned by \(x_i=r\) is infeasible.

children.title: Reservoir-Level Propagation
children.top_down_role: Inference over stock levels induced by consuming or producing events.

knowledge_statements.title: Reservoir-Level Propagation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Envelope-based feasibility and event-time filtering for a bounded reservoir.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let event \(i\) occur at \(T_i\in D_i\) and change the reservoir by \(\Delta_i\). For each relevant time \(t\), compute \(L^-(t)=L_0+\sum_i\min_{\tau\in D_i}\Delta_i\mathbf1_{\{\tau\le t\}}\) and \(L^+(t)=L_0+\sum_i\max_{\tau\in D_i}\Delta_i\mathbf1_{\{\tau\le t\}}\). If \(L^-(t)>U\) or \(L^+(t)<L\), report infeasibility. For each candidate \(\tau\in D_i\), condition on \(T_i=\tau\), recompute the envelopes, and delete \(\tau\) if either test fails at any relevant time. Iterate to a fixpoint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reservoir propagation bounds every possible level trajectory and removes event times whose conditioned envelopes necessarily cross a level bound.
assumptions_latex: The level is \(L_0+\sum_{i:T_i\le t}\Delta_i\).
Every feasible trajectory must satisfy \(L\le L(t)\le U\) at all relevant event times.
Each event-time domain \(D_i\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L^-(t)>U\) or \(L^+(t)<L\) certifies infeasibility; the conditioned form soundly deletes event times.

notation.meaning: minimum and maximum attainable level envelopes

children.title: Choice-Resource Coupling
children.top_down_role: Cross-propagation between activity choice, resource assignment, and stock feasibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Choice-Resource Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optional-mode scheduling with mode-dependent renewable-resource demands and fixed activity durations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\) be a finite activity set and \(R\) a finite renewable-resource set. For each \(i\in I\), let \(M_i\) be its finite nonempty mode set, \(p_i\in\{0,1\}\) its presence indicator, \(s_i\) its start time, and \(d_i\ge 0\) its duration. For every \(m\in M_i\), let \(y_{im}\in\{0,1\}\) indicate selection of mode \(m\), and let \(q_{imr}\ge 0\) be that mode's demand for resource \(r\in R\). Choice-resource coupling imposes \[p_i=\sum_{m\in M_i}y_{im},\qquad u_{ir}=\sum_{m\in M_i}q_{imr}y_{im}\quad(i\in I,\ r\in R).\] Thus an absent activity selects no mode and induces zero demand, whereas a present activity selects exactly one mode. Given resource capacities \(Q_r\ge 0\), renewable-resource feasibility additionally requires \[\sum_{i\in I}u_{ir}\mathbf{1}\{s_i\le t<s_i+d_i\}\le Q_r\quad(r\in R)\] at every relevant time \(t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each present activity selects exactly one mode, while each absent activity selects none. The selected mode determines its renewable-resource demand, and total demand from concurrently executing activities cannot exceed capacity.
assumptions_latex: \(I\) and \(R\) are finite sets.
Each \(M_i\) is finite and nonempty.
\(Q_r\ge 0\) is the capacity of renewable resource \(r\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_i=\sum_{m\in M_i}y_{im}\), the induced demand is \(u_{ir}=\sum_{m\in M_i}q_{imr}y_{im}\), and concurrent usage does not exceed \(Q_r\).

resource-r demand induced for activity i

children.title: Objective-Domain Propagation

knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Domain Propagation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sound propagation of a minimization objective over the current scheduling domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a current domain store \(D\), an objective variable \(z=f(x)\), and sound bounds \(L(D)\le f(x)\le U(D)\) for every feasible completion \(x\in D\), replace its domain by \[D(z)\leftarrow D(z)\cap[L(D),U(D)].\] If an incumbent value \(z^{\mathrm{inc}}\) is known and strict improvement is required, also impose \(z<z^{\mathrm{inc}}\). Report failure when the resulting domain is empty; otherwise return the reduced store and repeat propagation until no bound changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Intersect the objective domain with sound completion bounds and the incumbent cutoff; an empty intersection proves that the current search node cannot improve the incumbent.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is real-valued on every feasible completion in the current store.
\(L(D)\) and \(U(D)\) are valid lower and upper bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every removed objective value is infeasible or cannot satisfy the required incumbent improvement.

children.title: Explanation-Producing Propagators
children.top_down_role: Propagators that expose reasons for pruning or conflict.

knowledge_statements.title: Explanation-Producing Propagators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Propagators that accompany each inference or failure with an entailed reason.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be the constraint set and \(D\) the current domain literals. An explanation-producing propagator maps \((F,D)\) to either a reduced store \(D'\subseteq D\) or failure, together with explanations. For every newly inferred literal \(\ell\), it returns a finite set \(E\subseteq D\) satisfying \[F\land\bigwedge_{e\in E}e\models\ell.\] For failure it returns \(E\subseteq D\) satisfying \[F\land\bigwedge_{e\in E}e\models\bot.\] Thus each pruning or contradiction has a checkable logical antecedent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An explanation-producing propagator returns each pruning or failure together with current literals that logically entail it under the model constraints.
assumptions_latex: Domain restrictions are expressible as logical literals.
The propagator is sound for \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each emitted explanation logically entails its inference or contradiction.

children.title: Bound Explanations

knowledge_statements.title: Bound Explanations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical certificates for propagated lower or upper bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a propagated lower bound \(x\ge a\), a bound explanation is a finite set \(E\) of currently valid literals such that \[F\land\bigwedge_{e\in E}e\models x\ge a.\] For a propagated upper bound \(x\le b\), it analogously satisfies \[F\land\bigwedge_{e\in E}e\models x\le b.\] The certificate is verifiable by checking unsatisfiability of \(F\land\bigwedge E\land(x<a)\), respectively \(F\land\bigwedge E\land(x>b)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bound explanation is a finite set of active literals whose conjunction with the model entails the propagated bound, verifiable by refuting its negation.
assumptions_latex: \(E\) contains literals valid in the current search state.
Entailment is interpreted over the domains of the scheduling model.

children.title: Learning-Enabled Propagation

knowledge_statements.title: Learning-Enabled Propagation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conflict-driven reuse of explanations generated during scheduling propagation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain a constraint set \(F\), current decision literals \(D\), and a learned set \(L\), initially empty. Propagate using \(F\land L\). When an explanation establishes \(E\models\bot\), derive the nogood \[N_E=\neg\!\left(\bigwedge_{e\in E}e\right)=\bigvee_{e\in E}\neg e,\] add \(N_E\) to \(L\), backtrack to a state where \(N_E\) is not falsified, and resume propagation. Learned nogoods may prune only when they are entailed by the original model and previously valid learned constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convert a conflict explanation into an entailed nogood, retain it across backtracking, and use it in later propagation to prevent recurrence of the conflicting assignment.
assumptions_latex: Every conflict explanation is sound under the original model and existing learned constraints.
The search maintains finite decision levels.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Adding each learned nogood preserves all solutions and excludes its explained conflict.

children.title: Constraint-Programming Scheduling Search
children.top_down_role: Propagation-guided branching over activities, resources, orderings, alternatives, and time.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Programming Scheduling Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complete finite-domain search interleaving scheduling propagation and branching.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a finite-domain scheduling model \(F\) and optional objective \(f\). Initialize the root store \(D_0\) and incumbent \(z^{\mathrm{inc}}=+\infty\). At a node, propagate \(F\) to a fixpoint; discard the node on failure or when its valid lower bound is at least \(z^{\mathrm{inc}}\). If all variables are fixed, record the feasible schedule and update the incumbent. Otherwise choose an unfixed activity, resource, ordering, alternative, or time decision and create finitely many child restrictions whose disjunction covers the node domain. Continue until no open node remains.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly propagate, prune infeasible or nonimproving nodes, and branch exhaustively on scheduling decisions; completed assignments update the incumbent.
assumptions_latex: All decision domains and branch partitions are finite.
Propagation and objective bounds are sound.
Every branch family covers its parent domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Termination returns an optimal schedule, or infeasibility if no feasible leaf exists.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited general CP section is insufficient for the complete scheduling branch-and-bound algorithm and optimality claim. The statement also permits an optional objective while concluding that an optimal schedule is always returned.

children.title: Scheduling Branching-Bounding Algorithm Family
children.top_down_role: Problem-specific enumeration driven by schedule bounds, dominance, and branching structure.

children.title: Scheduling Branching Schemes
children.top_down_role: Branching choices based on activities, times, resources, or sequences.

knowledge_statements.title: Scheduling Branching Schemes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exhaustive covering rules for creating children of branch-and-bound scheduling nodes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a search node \(N\), let \(X_N\) denote its feasible completions. A valid scheduling branching scheme selects finitely many representable predicates \(B_1,\ldots,B_k\), with \(k\ge 1\), satisfying \[X_N=\bigcup_{j=1}^{k}\{x\in X_N:B_j(x)\}.\] It creates one child by adding each predicate and then propagates that child. For activities \(i\) and \(j\) with start times \(s_i,s_j\) and durations \(d_i,d_j\), possible binary branches include precedence predicates \(s_i+d_i\le s_j\) and \(s_j+d_j\le s_i\). Other examples include assigning a resource-choice variable \(r_i\) by \(r_i=r\) versus \(r_i\ne r\), or splitting an integral start domain at an integer \(\tau\) by \(s_i\le\tau\) versus \(s_i\ge\tau+1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scheduling branching scheme creates finitely many children whose predicates collectively cover every feasible completion of the parent, then propagates each child.
assumptions_latex: The branch predicates cover every feasible completion of the parent node.
Each child restriction is representable by the solver.
Any example-specific precedence branches are applied where the modeled scheduling disjunction makes them exhaustive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exhaustively searching all generated children preserves completeness relative to node \(N\).

notation.meaning: start time and duration of activity i

review_flags: scheduling-specific branch examples require source confirmation

children.title: Scheduling Bounding Schemes
children.top_down_role: Lower-bound or upper-bound structures used during enumeration.

knowledge_statements.title: Scheduling Bounding Schemes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Computation and use of valid minimization bounds from scheduling relaxations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization scheduling node \(N\), let \(X_N\) be its feasible set and let \(f:X_N\to\mathbb{R}\) be its objective. Choose a relaxation \(R_N\supseteq X_N\) and compute either \[L_N=\inf_{x\in R_N}f(x)\] or any certified value \(L_N\) no greater than that infimum. Then \[L_N\le\inf_{x\in X_N}f(x).\] If an incumbent schedule has value \(z^{\mathrm{inc}}\) and \(L_N\ge z^{\mathrm{inc}}\), discard node \(N\); otherwise retain it for further branching or propagation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compute a certified lower bound from a relaxation of the scheduling node and prune the node when that bound cannot improve upon the incumbent.
assumptions_latex: \(R_N\) contains every feasible schedule represented by node \(N\).
The relaxation value or reported lower bound is certified.
The objective is minimized.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_N\ge z^{\mathrm{inc}}\) certifies that node \(N\) contains no strictly improving schedule.

children.title: Dominance-Based Node Pruning
children.top_down_role: Search-tree pruning based on dominance between partial schedules.

knowledge_statements.title: Dominance-Based Node Pruning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe pruning when another node dominates every continuation of a scheduling state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For minimization, node \(A\) dominates node \(B\) if there exists a mapping \(T:X_B\to X_A\) such that \[f(T(x))\le f(x)\quad\text{for every }x\in X_B.\] Equivalently, every feasible completion represented by \(B\) has a feasible completion represented by \(A\) with no larger objective. If \(A\) has already been retained or completely searched, then \(B\) may be discarded without removing all optimal schedules.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Prune a node when every one of its feasible completions can be matched by a retained node's feasible completion with no worse objective.
assumptions_latex: Nodes \(A\) and \(B\) belong to the same minimization search.
The dominance mapping preserves scheduling feasibility.
Node \(A\) is retained or has been completely searched.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Discarding dominated node \(B\) preserves at least one globally optimal schedule.

notation.meaning: feasible completion sets of nodes A and B

review_flags: locator supports branch-and-bound generally but may not state scheduling dominance

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The dominance condition is coherent, but the cited general branch-and-bound locator does not establish the stated scheduling dominance mapping or its pruning guarantee.

children.title: Incumbent-Guided Enumeration
children.top_down_role: Enumeration behavior shaped by incumbent schedules and objective gaps.

knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent-Guided Enumeration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Enumeration restricted by the best feasible scheduling objective found so far.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an integral minimization objective, initialize \(z^{\mathrm{inc}}=+\infty\). Whenever enumeration finds a feasible schedule \(x\) with \(f(x)<z^{\mathrm{inc}}\), set \(z^{\mathrm{inc}}\leftarrow f(x)\) and impose the cutoff \(f(x')\le z^{\mathrm{inc}}-1\) on every open node. Prune any node with valid lower bound \(L_N\ge z^{\mathrm{inc}}\). When no open node remains, return the incumbent; if none was found, report infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each improving schedule tightens a global objective cutoff, and nodes whose lower bounds cannot beat the incumbent are removed from enumeration.
assumptions_latex: The objective is integer-valued and minimized.
Every node lower bound is valid.
Enumeration without incumbent pruning is complete.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At termination, the incumbent is globally optimal whenever a feasible schedule exists.

notation.meaning: valid lower bound at node N

children.title: Mathematical Programming for Scheduling
children.top_down_role: Integer, disjunctive, and continuous-relaxation approaches to scheduling.

knowledge_statements.title: Mathematical Programming for Scheduling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-horizon mixed-integer representation of scheduling decisions and disjunctions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A finite-horizon scheduling model may be represented as \[\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x+d^{\mathsf T}y:Ax+By\le b,\ x\in\mathbb{R}^{n_c},\ y\in\mathbb{Z}^{n_i}\},\] where designated components encode start or completion times, assignments, selections, and precedence orientations. For two activities \(i\) and \(j\) sharing a unary resource, let \(s_i,s_j\) be their start times, \(d_i,d_j\ge 0\) their durations, and \(y_{ij}\in\{0,1\}\) an ordering indicator. Their nonoverlap disjunction can be encoded by \[s_i+d_i\le s_j+M(1-y_{ij}),\qquad s_j+d_j\le s_i+My_{ij}.\] The constant \(M\ge 0\) must be large enough, relative to the finite variable bounds, to make each inactive inequality redundant without excluding a feasible schedule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite-horizon schedule can be represented by a mixed-integer program whose variables encode times, assignments, selections, and orders; binary ordering variables and valid big-M constraints encode unary-resource nonoverlap.
assumptions_latex: The scheduling horizon and all variables used in a big-M constraint have finite valid bounds.
Each big-M constant makes its inactive inequality redundant over those bounds.
Designated integer variables have the required binary or discrete domains.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Integer-feasible model points satisfy the scheduling constraints encoded by the mixed-integer formulation.

notation.meaning: start time and duration of activity i
binary ordering indicator for activities i and j

children.title: State-Space Dynamic Programming Family
children.top_down_role: Exact and relaxed state-space methods for structured scheduling families.

children.title: Scheduling Dynamic Programming
children.top_down_role: Exact state-based approaches for structured scheduling families.

knowledge_statements.title: Scheduling Dynamic Programming
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite-state recursion for constructing an optimal schedule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\) be a finite scheduling state set, \(s_0\in S\) the initial state, and \(S_T\subseteq S\) the terminal states. For every nonterminal state \(s\in S\setminus S_T\), let \(A(s)\) be a finite nonempty set of admissible decisions, \(T(s,a)\in S\) the successor state, and \(g(s,a)\in\mathbb{R}\) the incremental cost. Let \(h(s)\in\mathbb{R}\) be the terminal cost for \(s\in S_T\). Set \(V(s)=h(s)\) on \(S_T\), and otherwise compute \[V(s)=\min_{a\in A(s)}\{g(s,a)+V(T(s,a))\}.\] Evaluate states in an acyclic topological order, or according to a terminating stage index, store a minimizing action at every reachable nonterminal state, and follow the stored actions from \(s_0\) to construct a schedule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Represent partial schedules by finite states, minimize immediate cost plus the optimal successor value over a finite action set, and follow stored minimizing actions to reconstruct an optimal schedule.
assumptions_latex: The transition graph is finite and acyclic, or has a valid terminating stage index.
Every nonterminal action set \(A(s)\) is finite and nonempty.
The state contains all information affecting feasible continuations and future costs.
Every admissible action preserves scheduling feasibility and every generated path reaches a terminal state.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V(s_0)\) is the optimal represented schedule value, and the stored actions yield a schedule attaining it.

notation.meaning: finite admissible action set at state s

children.title: State-Space Relaxation
children.top_down_role: Relaxed state representations used for bounds or compact exploration.

assumptions_latex: The original finite-horizon scheduling dynamic program has states \(s\in S_t\), feasible actions \(A_t(s)\), transitions \(T_t(s,a)\), stage costs \(c_t(s,a)\), and terminal cost \(g(s)\).
The problem is a minimization problem, and every original state-action trajectory remains admissible in the relaxed model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\underline V_0(\rho_0(s_0))\le V_0(s_0)\).

notation.meaning: Original and relaxed cost-to-go functions at stage t.
Map from original states to relaxed states.
Relaxed action set and transition map.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-horizon minimization dynamic programs; relaxation yields a lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A state-space relaxation consists of maps \(\rho_t:S_t\to\underline S_t\), enlarged action sets satisfying \(A_t(s)\subseteq\underline A_t(\rho_t(s))\), and transitions satisfying \(\rho_{t+1}(T_t(s,a))=\underline T_t(\rho_t(s),a)\) for every original feasible pair \((s,a)\). If relaxed costs obey \(\underline c_t(\rho_t(s),a)\le c_t(s,a)\) and \(\underline g(\rho_H(s))\le g(s)\), define \(\underline V_H=\underline g\) and \(\underline V_t(z)=\min_{a\in\underline A_t(z)}\{\underline c_t(z,a)+\underline V_{t+1}(\underline T_t(z,a))\}\). Then \(\underline V_0(\rho_0(s_0))\le V_0(s_0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relaxed state model retains every original trajectory at no greater cost, so its optimal value is a lower bound for minimization scheduling.
knowledge_statements.title: State-Space Relaxation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The formulation is mathematically plausible, but the cited section concerns continuous-relaxation branch-and-bound rather than state-space relaxation of finite-horizon scheduling dynamic programs. A direct source is needed to validate the precise simulation and lower-bound conditions; the horizon index H should also be introduced explicitly.

children.title: State Aggregation
children.top_down_role: Grouping of scheduling states to control representation size.

assumptions_latex: A finite-horizon scheduling dynamic program is defined on state sets \(S_t\).
The aggregation maps \(\alpha_t:S_t\to Z_t\) are surjective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The aggregated recursion is well defined exactly when costs, feasible actions, transitions, and terminal values are constant on each aggregation class in the stated sense.
review_flags: no supplied locator directly addresses dynamic-programming state aggregation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact aggregation of finite-horizon scheduling states.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An aggregation \(\alpha_t:S_t\to Z_t\) is recursion-preserving when, for all \(s,s'\in S_t\) with \(\alpha_t(s)=\alpha_t(s')\), one has \(A_t(s)=A_t(s')\), \(c_t(s,a)=c_t(s',a)\), and \(\alpha_{t+1}(T_t(s,a))=\alpha_{t+1}(T_t(s',a))\) for every common feasible action \(a\). At the horizon, \(g(s)=g(s')\) whenever \(\alpha_H(s)=\alpha_H(s')\). These conditions define unambiguously \(\bar A_t\), \(\bar c_t\), \(\bar T_t\), and \(\bar g\) on \(Z_t\), and imply \(V_t(s)=\bar V_t(\alpha_t(s))\) for every \(t\) and \(s\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: States may be merged exactly when their actions, costs, aggregated successors, and terminal values agree, making the value function constant on every aggregate.
knowledge_statements.title: State Aggregation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed fiber conditions suffice to induce representative-independent Bellman data and exact aggregation, but the plain statement's 'exactly when' can be read as claiming they are necessary for all value-preserving mergers, which is false without a stronger definition of exact aggregation. A direct source is required to settle the intended equivalence.

children.title: Exactness-Relaxation Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Structural regimes governing loss of exact state distinction.

assumptions_latex: The original and reduced models are finite-horizon minimization dynamic programs.
A surjective state map \(\alpha_t:S_t\to Z_t\) is used at each stage.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact aggregation requires Bellman-equivalent fibers; otherwise an outer relaxation only guarantees a lower bound and may have a positive gap.
review_flags: no supplied locator directly establishes the scheduling dynamic-programming boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between exact aggregation and lower-bounding state relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If every fiber of \(\alpha_t\) satisfies equality of feasible actions and stage costs and has identical aggregated successors, with terminal costs constant on fibers, then \(V_t(s)=\bar V_t(\alpha_t(s))\) and hence \(\Delta=0\). If any of these equalities is replaced by an outer approximation that admits an action or transition unavailable from some represented state, the reduced model is only a relaxation: \(\bar V_0^*\le V_0^*\). Equality may still occur accidentally, but is no longer guaranteed. For example, merging two initial states whose only feasible actions have respective costs \(0\) and \(1\), while retaining both actions, gives relaxed value \(0\) for the second state and gap \(1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bellman-equivalent state classes preserve exactness. Enlarging a class's actions or transitions preserves only a lower bound and can create a positive gap.
knowledge_statements.title: Exactness-Relaxation Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exactness-versus-relaxation distinction is plausible, but the optimal values and gap are not tied to a specified initial state or initial-state distribution. The example is therefore not fully aligned with the scalar definition of Delta, and no source supports the stated boundary.

children.title: Scheduling Decomposition Regime Family
children.top_down_role: Temporal, resource, job-set, and planning-horizon decompositions.

children.title: Temporal Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Partitioning scheduling decisions across time segments.

assumptions_latex: Scheduling variables and constraints are assigned to consecutive time blocks \(I_1,\ldots,I_K\).
All constraints coupling adjacent or nonadjacent blocks are represented through interface variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A collection of block schedules is globally feasible exactly when every block is locally feasible and all shared interface values agree.

notation.meaning: Local feasible set for temporal block k.
Interface projection from block k toward block l.
Decision vector in temporal block k.

review_flags: locator supports decomposition generally rather than temporal scheduling specifically
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact feasibility representation for time-block decomposition.

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X_k\) contain precisely the assignments satisfying all scheduling constraints internal to time block \(I_k\). For every pair of blocks sharing boundary information, let \(B_{kl}x_k\) and \(B_{lk}x_l\) encode the same interface quantities, including unfinished-operation status, carried inventory, or resource state. The global feasible set has the decomposition
\[X=\left\{(x_1,\ldots,x_K):x_k\in X_k\ \text{for all }k,\ B_{kl}x_k=B_{lk}x_l\ \text{for every coupled pair }(k,l)\right\}.\]
Thus independent block solutions form a feasible global schedule if and only if all interface equalities hold; omitting an interface condition generally produces an outer relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Temporal decomposition splits the horizon into locally feasible blocks; their schedules combine exactly when all carried states and boundary decisions agree.
knowledge_statements.title: Temporal Decomposition

source_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

children.title: Resource Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Partitioning scheduling decisions by machines, crews, or capacity pools.

assumptions_latex: The scheduling model has a finite resource set \(R\).
Every cross-resource technological constraint is exposed through shared operation or interface variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Resource-subproblem solutions constitute a global schedule exactly when their shared operation decisions are mutually consistent and all global coupling constraints hold.

notation.meaning: Local decision vector for resource r.
Projection onto decisions shared by resources r and q.

review_flags: locator supports decomposition generally rather than resource scheduling specifically
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility representation obtained by partitioning scheduling constraints by resource.

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each \(r\in R\), let \(X_r\) impose the capacity, sequencing, setup, and calendar constraints local to resource \(r\). If resources \(r\) and \(q\) share an operation or technological decision, let \(P_{rq}x_r\) and \(P_{qr}x_q\) denote their local copies. With \(G(x_1,\ldots,x_{|R|})=0\) collecting remaining global constraints, the feasible schedules are
\[X=\left\{(x_r)_{r\in R}:x_r\in X_r,\ P_{rq}x_r=P_{qr}x_q\ \text{for all coupled }r,q,\ G((x_r)_{r\in R})=0\right\}.\]
Dropping the consistency or global constraints separates the resource subproblems but relaxes global feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Resource decomposition creates one constrained schedule per resource; consistency of shared operations and global technological constraints is necessary and sufficient for recombination.
knowledge_statements.title: Resource Decomposition

source_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

children.title: Job-Set Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Partitioning the scheduled workload into interacting job subsets.

knowledge_statements.title: Job-Set Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact recombination condition for a partition of the job set with cross-block precedence and time-indexed renewable-resource capacity constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(J=\dot\bigcup_{k=1}^K J_k\), and let \(X_k\) be the schedules satisfying all release, routing, precedence, and resource constraints involving only jobs in \(J_k\). For \(x_k\in X_k\), let \(u_{rk}(t;x_k)\) denote the usage of renewable resource \(r\) at time \(t\) by block schedule \(x_k\), and let \(C_r(t)\) be its available capacity. Write \(x=\bigcup_{k=1}^K x_k\). Then \(x\) is globally feasible if and only if every precedence constraint whose endpoints lie in different blocks is satisfied and, for every renewable resource \(r\) and relevant time \(t\), \[\sum_{k=1}^K u_{rk}(t;x_k)\le C_r(t).\] Consequently, independent feasibility of all \(x_k\) is insufficient whenever job blocks interact through precedence or shared-resource capacity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partitioning jobs yields locally feasible subproblems, but their union is feasible only when every cross-block precedence and all combined time-indexed renewable-resource capacity constraints are satisfied.
assumptions_latex: The finite job set \(J\) is partitioned into nonempty subsets \(J_1,\ldots,J_K\).
Each subproblem enforces all constraints internal to its assigned jobs.
Cross-block resource coupling is represented by time-indexed usage of renewable resources with capacities \(C_r(t)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The union of subproblem schedules is globally feasible exactly when every cross-block precedence and shared renewable-resource capacity constraint is satisfied.

notation.meaning: Locally feasible schedules for jobs in block k.
Usage of renewable resource r at time t by block schedule x_k.
Available capacity of renewable resource r at time t.

children.title: Rolling-Horizon Scheduling
children.top_down_role: Repeated optimization over a moving planning window.

assumptions_latex: Decision epochs satisfy \(0=\tau_0<\tau_1<\cdots\), with look-ahead length \(H_k>\tau_{k+1}-\tau_k\).
At epoch \(\tau_k\), current system state and previously committed decisions are fixed data.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each iteration returns an implementable schedule prefix; finite termination follows when every iteration commits at least one remaining operation and no new operations arrive.

notation.meaning: Look-ahead horizon length at epoch k.

review_flags: no supplied locator directly addresses rolling-horizon scheduling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic rolling-horizon construction with irreversible committed prefixes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(k=0\) and the set of committed decisions as empty. At epoch \(\tau_k\), update the scheduling data and solve the finite-window problem over \([\tau_k,\tau_k+H_k]\), subject to the observed state and all earlier commitments, obtaining \(x^k\). Commit and implement only the decisions of \(x^k\) whose execution lies in \([\tau_k,\tau_{k+1})\); discard the uncommitted suffix, set \(k\leftarrow k+1\), and repeat. Stop when all required operations are committed, or continue indefinitely under arrivals. Feasibility of each committed prefix is preserved provided every window model includes the inherited state and constraints linking that prefix to future work.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly optimize a look-ahead window, irrevocably execute its first segment, update the state, and continue until all operations are committed.
knowledge_statements.title: Rolling-Horizon Scheduling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm is a recognizable deterministic rolling-horizon scheme and fits the leaf, but no citation supports its commitment, inherited-state feasibility, or finite-termination conditions.

children.title: Decomposition Coordination
children.top_down_role: Interfaces, commitments, and consistency across scheduling subproblems.

assumptions_latex: The global minimization model is separable as \(\min\{\sum_{k=1}^K f_k(x_k):x_k\in X_k,\ \sum_{k=1}^K A_kx_k=b\}\).
Each subproblem minimum is attained for the multipliers considered.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The dual value is a valid lower bound, while primal feasibility requires a coordination step enforcing \(\sum_k A_kx_k=b\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lagrangian coordination of separable scheduling subproblems.

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(\lambda^0\), iteration \(n\) solves independently
\[x_k^n\in\arg\min_{x_k\in X_k}\{f_k(x_k)+(\lambda^n)^{\mathsf T}A_kx_k\},\qquad k=1,\ldots,K.\]
It computes \(r^n=\sum_kA_kx_k^n-b\) and updates \(\lambda^{n+1}=\lambda^n+\alpha_nr^n\) with \(\alpha_n>0\). The dual value
\[q(\lambda^n)=-(\lambda^n)^{\mathsf T}b+\sum_k\min_{x_k\in X_k}\{f_k(x_k)+(\lambda^n)^{\mathsf T}A_kx_k\}\]
is a lower bound on the global optimum. Stop by a prescribed iteration or residual rule; a primal schedule is certified feasible only after recombination or repair achieves \(r^n=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multipliers price coupling violations, subproblems solve independently, and residuals update the prices; dual values bound the optimum, but feasible schedules require consistent recombination.
knowledge_statements.title: Decomposition Coordination

source_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

children.title: Scheduling Construction-Improvement Heuristics
children.top_down_role: Schedule construction and neighborhood-based improvement families.

children.title: Dispatching Rules
children.top_down_role: Priority-based selection of the next activity or resource decision.

assumptions_latex: At each decision time \(t\), \(E(t)\) is the finite set of eligible unscheduled operations.
A deterministic priority index \(p_j(t)\) and tie-breaking order are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The rule selects an eligible operation of minimum priority index and advances time when no operation is eligible.

notation.meaning: Priority index of operation j at time t.

review_flags: no supplied locator directly defines scheduling dispatching rules
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Serial, nonpreemptive priority dispatch with deterministic ties.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Initialize time \(t\) and the partial schedule. While unscheduled operations remain, construct \(E(t)\) from operations whose predecessors are complete, release dates have passed, and required resources are available. If \(E(t)\ne\varnothing\), choose
\[j^*\in\arg\min_{j\in E(t)}p_j(t),\]
break ties by the prescribed order, assign \(j^*\) at its earliest feasible start, and update resource availability and eligibility. If \(E(t)=\varnothing\), advance \(t\) to the next release or completion event. Stop when all operations are assigned; output the resulting schedule. Feasibility follows only when every assignment explicitly respects all modeled precedence and resource constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dispatching rule repeatedly assigns the highest-priority eligible operation at its earliest feasible start, advancing to the next event when none is eligible.
knowledge_statements.title: Dispatching Rules

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The serial priority-dispatch algorithm is plausible and appropriately typed as an algorithm, but no source is supplied for this scheduling-specific definition or its feasibility qualification.

children.title: Constructive Scheduling Heuristics
children.top_down_role: Incremental construction of complete feasible schedules.

knowledge_statements.title: Constructive Scheduling Heuristics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic insertion-based constructive scheduling heuristic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(S_0=\varnothing\), \(U_0=J\), and \(k=0\). While \(U_k\ne\varnothing\), select an operation \(j_k\in U_k\) by the prescribed priority rule and compute \(P(j_k,S_k)\), the placements extending \(S_k\) without violating modeled constraints. If \(P(j_k,S_k)=\varnothing\), stop with construction failure or invoke a specified backtracking or repair rule. Otherwise choose \(p_k\in P(j_k,S_k)\), set \(S_{k+1}=S_k\cup\{(j_k,p_k)\}\), \(U_{k+1}=U_k\setminus\{j_k\}\), and increment \(k\). When \(U_k=\varnothing\), output \(S_k\), which is feasible by invariant preservation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Build a schedule one operation at a time using prescribed priorities and feasible placements; return the complete feasible schedule or a declared construction failure.
assumptions_latex: The scheduling instance has a finite operation set \(J\) and a decidable feasibility predicate for extending a partial schedule.
A deterministic candidate-selection rule and placement rule are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure either returns a complete feasible schedule or reports that its construction rule cannot extend the current partial schedule.

notation.meaning: Finite set of operations to be scheduled.
Feasible placements of operation j into the partial schedule.

source_refs.locator: 2.7 Primal Bounds: Greedy and Local Search p. 34

children.title: Scheduling Local Search
children.top_down_role: Neighborhood-based improvement of complete or partial schedules.

assumptions_latex: The feasible schedule set \(X\) is finite and nonempty.
An objective \(f:X\to\mathbb R\), neighborhood mapping \(N:X\rightrightarrows X\), and tie-breaking rule are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Strict-improvement local search terminates at a schedule \(x^*\) satisfying \(f(x^*)\le f(y)\) for every \(y\in N(x^*)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite strict-improvement local search for scheduling minimization.

source_refs.locator: 2.7 Primal Bounds: Greedy and Local Search p. 34

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose an initial schedule \(x^0\in X\) and set \(k=0\). At iteration \(k\), evaluate feasible neighbors in \(N(x^k)\). If there exists \(y\in N(x^k)\) with \(f(y)<f(x^k)\), select one according to the prescribed first-improvement or best-improvement rule, set \(x^{k+1}=y\), and increment \(k\). Otherwise stop and output \(x^*=x^k\). Because \(X\) is finite and every accepted move strictly decreases \(f\), no schedule can repeat and termination occurs after at most \(|X|-1\) accepted moves. The output is locally optimal relative to \(N\), not necessarily globally optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from a feasible schedule, repeatedly accept a strictly improving feasible neighbor; finiteness guarantees termination at a neighborhood-local optimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Scheduling Local Search

source_witnesses.locator: 2.7 Primal Bounds: Greedy and Local Search p. 34

children.title: Schedule Neighborhood Design
children.top_down_role: Move structures based on sequence, timing, assignment, or critical-path changes.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is the feasible schedule set.
\(M\) is a specified family of schedule transformations with decidable applicability and feasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A valid neighborhood contains exactly the feasible schedules reachable by one allowed move; its symmetry and connectivity depend on the move family.
review_flags: locator supports local search but may not detail schedule neighborhoods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Move-induced neighborhoods restricted to feasible schedules.

source_refs.locator: 2.7 Primal Bounds: Greedy and Local Search p. 34

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a feasible schedule \(x\in X\) and move family \(M\), the move-induced neighborhood is
\[N_M(x)=\{m(x)\in X:m\in M\text{ is applicable to }x\}.\]
Moves may alter operation order, machine assignment, start times, or a bounded block of decisions, but every neighbor must satisfy the defining feasibility constraints of \(X\), or be passed through an explicitly defined repair map before inclusion. The neighborhood is symmetric exactly when every feasible applied move has an inverse move in \(M\). It is connected exactly when, for every \(x,y\in X\), a finite sequence of moves from \(M\) transforms \(x\) into \(y\) through feasible intermediate schedules.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A schedule neighborhood is the set of feasible schedules reachable by one permitted move; inverse moves determine symmetry and move sequences determine connectivity.
knowledge_statements.title: Schedule Neighborhood Design
