children.title: Temporal Relation-Composition Calculus
children.top_down_role: Algebraic organization of temporal relations and their compositions.

children.title: Temporal Relation Algebras
children.top_down_role: Algebraic organization of qualitative temporal relations.

knowledge_statements.title: Temporal Relation Algebras
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite qualitative relation algebra induced by jointly exhaustive, pairwise disjoint temporal atoms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U\) be a set of temporal objects and let \(\mathcal A\) be a finite jointly exhaustive, pairwise disjoint partition of \(U\times U\) containing an identity atom and closed under converse. A qualitative temporal relation is a union of atoms, represented by an element of \(2^{\mathcal A}\). With union, intersection, complement relative to \(\mathcal A\), converse, identity, and semantic or weak composition, \(2^{\mathcal A}\) is the temporal relation-algebra calculus. If unions of atoms are closed under exact relational composition, this structure is a relation algebra; otherwise weak composition supplies the least representable atomic over-approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A temporal relation algebra represents qualitative relations as unions of disjoint temporal atoms equipped with Boolean operations, converse, identity, and composition.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A\) partitions \(U\times U\) and is finite.
\(\mathcal A\) contains identity and is closed under converse.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The qualitative relations form \(2^{\mathcal A}\) with Boolean operations, converse, identity, and exact or weak composition.

source_refs.locator: Communications of the ACM 26(11), Sections 2–4, pp. 832–843

source_witnesses.locator: Communications of the ACM 26(11), Sections 2–4, pp. 832–843

children.title: Temporal Relation Composition
children.top_down_role: Inference based on composing qualitative relations across linked temporal entities.

knowledge_statements.title: Temporal Relation Composition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic and weak composition of qualitative temporal relations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For binary relations \(R,S\subseteq U\times U\), their semantic composition is \[R\circ S=\{(x,z)\in U\times U:\exists y\in U,\ (x,y)\in R\ \text{and}\ (y,z)\in S\}.\] If representable relations are unions of atoms from \(\mathcal A\), their weak composition is \[R\mathbin{\circ_w}S=\bigcup\{a\in\mathcal A:a\cap(R\circ S)\ne\varnothing\}.\] Thus weak composition is the unique least union of atoms containing the exact semantic composition; it equals exact composition precisely when \(R\circ S\) is itself a union of atoms.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Composition eliminates an intermediate temporal object; weak composition returns the smallest representable union of atoms containing the exact result.
assumptions_latex: \(R,S\subseteq U\times U\).
\(\mathcal A\) is a finite partition of \(U\times U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R\circ S\subseteq R\mathbin{\circ_w}S\), with equality exactly when \(R\circ S\) is a union of atoms.

source_refs.locator: Communications of the ACM 26(11), Sections 2–4, pp. 832–843

source_witnesses.locator: Communications of the ACM 26(11), Sections 2–4, pp. 832–843

children.title: Composition Tables
children.top_down_role: Tabular organization of admissible composed temporal relations.

knowledge_statements.title: Composition Tables
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite tabular representation of atomic weak composition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal A=\{a_1,\ldots,a_m\}\) be the atoms of a qualitative temporal calculus. Its composition table is the map \(T:\mathcal A\times\mathcal A\to2^{\mathcal A}\) defined by \[T(a,b)=\{c\in\mathcal A:c\cap(a\circ b)\ne\varnothing\}.\] For arbitrary representable relations \(R,S\subseteq\mathcal A\), composition is recovered by \[R\mathbin{\circ_w}S=\bigcup_{a\in R,\,b\in S}T(a,b).\] Hence the \(m^2\) atomic entries determine every weak composition in the calculus; converse symmetry may make some entries derivable from others.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A composition table lists the possible output atoms for each ordered pair of input atoms and determines composition of all disjunctive relations.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A\) is a finite set of jointly exhaustive, pairwise disjoint atoms.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every weak composition is obtained by taking the union of the corresponding atomic table entries.

notation.meaning: set of atoms possible after composing atoms a and b

source_refs.locator: Communications of the ACM 26(11), temporal-relation transitivity table, pp. 832–843

source_witnesses.locator: Communications of the ACM 26(11), temporal-relation transitivity table, pp. 832–843

children.title: Composition Precision Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Regimes where composed relations are exact, weak, or ambiguous.

knowledge_statements.title: Composition Precision Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exactness boundary for atomically representable temporal composition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\gamma(R)=\bigcup_{a\in R}a\) interpret \(R\subseteq\mathcal A\). Weak composition satisfies \[\gamma(R)\circ\gamma(S)\subseteq\gamma(R\mathbin{\circ_w}S).\] Equality holds if and only if the exact composite \(\gamma(R)\circ\gamma(S)\) is a union of atoms of \(\mathcal A\). If some atom \(c\) intersects but is not contained in that composite, then weak composition includes all of \(c\), introducing unsupported pairs. Consequently, repeated table composition can lose information, and identities valid for exact relational composition, including associativity, are not guaranteed for a weak-composition calculus without additional algebraic closure conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weak composition is exact only when the semantic result is atomically representable; otherwise entire intersecting atoms introduce spurious temporal possibilities.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A\) partitions the temporal universe.
\(R,S\subseteq\mathcal A\) are representable relations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\gamma(R\mathbin{\circ_w}S)=\gamma(R)\circ\gamma(S)\) exactly when the semantic composite is a union of atoms.

notation.meaning: semantic interpretation of a set of atoms

review_flags: A source explicitly covering weak-composition exactness and possible nonassociativity is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exactness boundary is mathematically coherent, but the additional claim that weak composition may fail associativity requires an explicit authoritative source.

children.title: Qualitative Network Closure Calculus
children.top_down_role: Local-consistency and closure families for qualitative temporal networks.

children.title: Path Consistency
children.top_down_role: Local qualitative-temporal filtering over relation triples.

knowledge_statements.title: Path Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Three-variable consistency condition for qualitative constraint networks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(N=(V,(R_{ij}))\) be a binary qualitative temporal network over universe \(U\), with \(R_{ij}\subseteq U\times U\), \(R_{ii}\) equal to identity, and \(R_{ji}=R_{ij}^{\smile}\). The network is path-consistent if, for every \(i,j,k\in V\), \[R_{ij}\subseteq R_{ik}\circ R_{kj}.\] In an atomic calculus using weak composition, the operational predicate is \[R_{ij}\subseteq R_{ik}\mathbin{\circ_w}R_{kj}.\] Equivalently, every allowed assignment to \((i,j)\) can be extended through each third variable \(k\) when exact semantic composition is used.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A network is path-consistent when every allowed relation between two variables remains supportable through every third variable.
assumptions_latex: All network constraints are binary relations on a common temporal universe.
Converse constraints and identity self-relations are maintained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For all \(i,j,k\in V\), \(R_{ij}\subseteq R_{ik}\circ R_{kj}\), or its weak-composition analogue.

notation.meaning: allowed relation from variable i to variable j

source_refs.locator: Communications of the ACM 26(11), constraint-propagation procedure, Sections 3–4, pp. 832–843

source_witnesses.locator: Communications of the ACM 26(11), constraint-propagation procedure, Sections 3–4, pp. 832–843

children.title: Qualitative Network Closure
children.top_down_role: Network-wide refinement of qualitative temporal relations.

knowledge_statements.title: Qualitative Network Closure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-point closure under converse, intersection, and ternary composition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a finite network \(N=(V,(R_{ij}))\). Initialize missing off-diagonal constraints to the universal relation, set each \(R_{ii}\) to identity, and enforce \(R_{ji}=R_{ij}^{\smile}\). Repeatedly apply, for every \(i,j,k\in V\), \[R_{ij}\leftarrow R_{ij}\cap(R_{ik}\mathbin{\circ_w}R_{kj}),\qquad R_{ji}\leftarrow R_{ij}^{\smile},\] until no relation changes or some \(R_{ij}=\varnothing\). The output is the path-consistency closure. Because every update only removes atoms and the network is finite, termination occurs. An empty relation certifies inconsistency; a nonempty fixed point certifies path consistency but not generally global satisfiability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Qualitative closure repeatedly intersects each constraint with every compositional consequence until reaching a fixed point or deriving an empty relation.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) and the atom set are finite.
The weak-composition table and converse operation are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm terminates at a path-consistent fixed point or returns an empty relation certifying inconsistency.

notation.meaning: current qualitative constraint between i and j

source_refs.locator: Communications of the ACM 26(11), constraint-propagation algorithm, Sections 3–4, pp. 832–843

source_witnesses.locator: Communications of the ACM 26(11), constraint-propagation algorithm, Sections 3–4, pp. 832–843

children.title: Incremental Closure Maintenance
children.top_down_role: Closure maintenance after additions, removals, or refinements of temporal constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Incremental Closure Maintenance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Queue-based restoration of qualitative closure after constraint tightening.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a closed finite network and a tightened constraint \(R_{pq}\leftarrow R_{pq}\cap S\), set \(R_{qp}=R_{pq}^{\smile}\) and initialize a queue with the changed ordered pairs. While the queue is nonempty, remove \((i,j)\) and, for every \(k\in V\), compute \[R'_{ik}=R_{ik}\cap(R_{ij}\mathbin{\circ_w}R_{jk}),\qquad R'_{kj}=R_{kj}\cap(R_{ki}\mathbin{\circ_w}R_{ij}).\] Replace any strictly reduced relation, update its converse, and enqueue affected pairs. Stop with inconsistency if a relation becomes empty; otherwise output the new fixed point when the queue empties. Monotone deletion ensures termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After tightening one constraint, a queue propagates only affected compositions until closure is restored or an empty relation is found.
assumptions_latex: The initial finite network is path-consistency closed.
The update only removes allowed atoms.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure terminates with the closure of the tightened network or detects inconsistency through an empty relation.

notation.meaning: new relation restricting the updated pair

review_flags: A precise source for the stated incremental queue update scheme is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The queue scheme is plausible and fits the algorithm container, but its claim to compute the complete new fixed point depends on precise scheduling invariants and needs a supporting source.

children.title: Local-Global Consistency Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Regimes where local consistency does or does not establish global consistency.

knowledge_statements.title: Local-Global Consistency Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between path consistency and global temporal satisfiability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every qualitative network, global satisfiability implies path consistency, and failure of path consistency therefore proves inconsistency. The converse is valid only for calculi or relation fragments having the path-consistency extension property: every nonempty path-consistent network over the fragment admits a joint realization. Without that property, closure may terminate with every \(R_{ij}\ne\varnothing\) although no global assignment exists. Thus a nonempty closure is a complete satisfiability certificate only on a fragment for which path-consistency completeness has been established; on unrestricted disjunctive interval-algebra networks it is merely a necessary local-consistency test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Path consistency is always necessary, but it decides satisfiability only on fragments with a proven extension property; unrestricted disjunctive interval networks exceed this boundary.
assumptions_latex: The network uses binary qualitative temporal relations.
Closure employs sound semantic or weak composition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Global satisfiability implies path consistency, whereas the reverse implication requires a path-consistency-complete fragment.

notation.meaning: allowed qualitative relation for a variable pair

review_flags: A source giving an explicit path-consistent unsatisfiable temporal network or an exact incompleteness theorem is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure boundary is correctly framed, but the unrestricted interval-algebra incompleteness claim needs a cited theorem or explicit path-consistent unsatisfiable example.

children.title: Tractable Qualitative Fragments
children.top_down_role: Subalgebras and relation restrictions supporting complete efficient reasoning.

knowledge_statements.title: Tractable Qualitative Fragments
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relation restrictions on which closure gives a polynomial complete decision procedure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal Q\subseteq2^{\mathcal A}\) be a family of qualitative temporal relations containing identity and closed under converse, intersection, and weak composition. Call \(\mathcal Q\) a path-consistency-complete tractable fragment if every finite network whose constraints lie in \(\mathcal Q\) is satisfiable exactly when its path-consistency closure contains no empty relation. If atomic operations are table lookups, closure on \(n\) variables uses \(O(n^3)\) triple revisions, apart from the fixed cost of relation-set operations. Closure of \(\mathcal Q\) ensures that propagation never leaves the fragment, while completeness converts the local fixed point into a global satisfiability decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A tractable qualitative fragment is closed under propagation operations and makes nonempty path-consistency closure equivalent to global satisfiability.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A\) is a fixed finite atom set.
Relation operations have constant cost for the fixed calculus.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For networks over \(\mathcal Q\), satisfiability is equivalent to nonempty path-consistency closure and is decidable in \(O(n^3)\) revisions.

notation.meaning: restricted family of admissible qualitative relations

source_refs.source_title: Reasoning about Temporal Relations: A Maximal Tractable Subclass of Allen's Interval Algebra

children.title: Temporal Graph Representation Hierarchy
children.top_down_role: Graph-based temporal representations and equivalent closed or reduced forms.

children.title: Temporal Distance Graphs
children.top_down_role: Graph representations of metric temporal bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Temporal Distance Graphs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted directed-graph representation of a simple temporal network.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A simple temporal network on variables \(t_0,\ldots,t_n\in\mathbb R\) with constraints \(l_{ij}\le t_j-t_i\le u_{ij}\) is represented by a directed weighted graph \(G=(V,E,w)\), where \(V=\{0,\ldots,n\}\). Each finite upper bound contributes an arc \(i\to j\) of weight \(u_{ij}\), encoding \(t_j-t_i\le u_{ij}\), and each finite lower bound contributes an arc \(j\to i\) of weight \(-l_{ij}\). An assignment is feasible exactly when it is a potential satisfying \(t_v\le t_u+w(u,v)\) for every arc \((u,v)\in E\). The network is feasible exactly when \(G\) has no negative-weight directed cycle.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An STN becomes a weighted digraph whose arcs encode difference upper bounds; feasibility is equivalent to absence of a negative directed cycle.
assumptions_latex: All temporal constraints are finite or infinite interval bounds on pairwise differences.
Time variables range over \(\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The STN is feasible if and only if its distance graph contains no negative-weight directed cycle.

notation.meaning: upper bound encoded by the arc from u to v
lower and upper bounds on the temporal difference

children.title: Closed Temporal Networks
children.top_down_role: Temporal networks carrying implied tight pairwise bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Closed Temporal Networks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: All-pairs shortest-path closure of a feasible simple temporal network.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E,w)\) be the distance graph of a feasible simple temporal network, and let \(d(i,j)\) be the shortest-path distance from \(i\) to \(j\), with \(d(i,j)=+\infty\) when no path exists. The closed network contains, for every ordered pair, the tight implied constraint \(t_j-t_i\le d(i,j)\). It is characterized by \(d(i,i)=0\) and the triangle inequalities \(d(i,j)\le d(i,k)+d(k,j)\) for all \(i,j,k\). Closure preserves exactly the feasible schedules and exposes the tightest entailed upper bound for every temporal difference.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closed STN stores every tight all-pairs implied difference bound obtained from shortest-path distances while preserving exactly the original schedules.
assumptions_latex: The simple temporal network is feasible.
Shortest-path distances are computed in its distance graph.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The closed constraint from \(i\) to \(j\) is \(t_j-t_i\le d(i,j)\), the tightest entailed upper bound.

notation.meaning: shortest-path distance from i to j

children.title: Minimal Temporal Representations
children.top_down_role: Reduced temporal forms preserving relevant solution-space information.

knowledge_statements.title: Minimal Temporal Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inclusion-minimal, distance-equivalent representations of a consistent simple temporal network.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E,w)\) be a consistent distance graph encoding constraints \(x_j-x_i\le w_{ij}\), and let \(d_G(i,j)\) denote its shortest-path distance. A subgraph \(H=(V,F,w|_F)\), where \(F\subseteq E\), is an equivalent temporal representation when \(d_H(i,j)=d_G(i,j)\) for every ordered pair \((i,j)\). It is minimal when no proper subset \(F'\subsetneq F\) induces an equivalent representation. Thus every retained edge is necessary for preserving at least one finite implied temporal bound, although a minimal representation need not be unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A minimal temporal representation preserves every implied bound while making every retained constraint indispensable; different minimal representations may exist.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is finite and has no negative-weight directed cycle.
Only original weighted edges may be retained in \(H\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H\text{ is minimal}\iff H\text{ is distance-equivalent to }G\text{ and }H-e\text{ is not distance-equivalent to }G\text{ for every }e\in F.\)

notation.meaning: Shortest-path distance from timepoint i to timepoint j in G.
Retained edge set of the representation.

Relevant temporal-network complexity source is missing.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Storage and query consequences of closed versus sparse equivalent temporal graphs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a consistent temporal distance graph on \(n\) timepoints, its closure contains the tight finite bound \(d(i,j)\) for every reachable ordered pair and therefore permits an implied-bound query by one table lookup. An equivalent inclusion-minimal subgraph may omit an edge \((i,j)\), but then \(d(i,j)\) must be recovered by a shortest-path computation unless an auxiliary index is stored. Consequently closure favors constant-time bound access at up to quadratic edge storage, whereas edge minimality favors sparse storage but does not by itself preserve constant-time queries. Closing a sparse representation generally restores omitted redundant edges and destroys edge minimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Closure stores all tight pairwise bounds for direct queries; minimal representations remove redundant edges but may require path computation and lose minimality when closed.
knowledge_statements.title: Closure-Minimality Tradeoffs

children.title: Temporal Consistency Query Calculus
children.top_down_role: Consistency checking, feasible-time queries, and implied-bound analysis.

children.title: Temporal Consistency Checking
children.top_down_role: Detection of whether a temporal network admits feasible assignments.

knowledge_statements.title: Temporal Consistency Checking
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Negative-cycle consistency test for finite simple temporal networks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given constraints \(x_j-x_i\le w_{ij}\), construct the directed graph having edge \(i\to j\) of weight \(w_{ij}\). Add a super-source \(s\) with a zero-weight edge to every timepoint and run a negative-cycle-detecting shortest-path algorithm. If a negative cycle is found, output inconsistent and that cycle. Otherwise output consistent together with distances \(p_i=d(s,i)\). The assignment \(x_i=p_i\) satisfies every constraint because shortest-path optimality gives \(p_j\le p_i+w_{ij}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Encode every difference bound as an edge; the temporal network is consistent exactly when its distance graph has no negative cycle.
assumptions_latex: The network has finitely many real-valued timepoints and difference constraints.
All edge weights admit exact comparison and addition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{x:x_j-x_i\le w_{ij}\text{ for all }(i,j)\in E\}\ne\varnothing\iff G\text{ has no negative-weight directed cycle}.\)

notation.meaning: Shortest distance from the added super-source to timepoint i.

review_flags: No relevant authoritative source locator was supplied.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The negative-cycle algorithm and feasibility criterion fit temporal consistency checking and are internally consistent, but no authoritative source or inspectable locator is supplied.

children.title: Feasible-Time Queries
children.top_down_role: Queries concerning admissible execution times for temporal variables.

assumptions_latex: The simple temporal network is consistent.
The origin satisfies \(x_0=0\), and all-pairs tight distances are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{x_k:x\text{ is a feasible schedule and }x_0=0\}=[-d(k,0),d(0,k)].\)

notation.meaning: Tight upper bound on x_j minus x_i.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: projection formula for a consistent closed STN
No relevant temporal-reasoning source locator was supplied.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection of an STN feasible region onto one timepoint relative to a fixed origin.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a consistent closed temporal network have distinguished origin \(0\) fixed by \(x_0=0\), and let \(d(i,j)\) be the tight upper bound on \(x_j-x_i\). For any timepoint \(k\), the set of values attained by \(x_k\) over all feasible schedules is the closed interval \[I_k=[-d(k,0),\ d(0,k)].\] An endpoint is infinite when the corresponding directed distance is infinite. Hence a proposed time \(t\in\mathbb R\) is feasible for \(k\) exactly when \(-d(k,0)\le t\le d(0,k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relative to a fixed origin, a timepoint can assume exactly the values between its tight implied lower and upper bounds.
knowledge_statements.title: Feasible-Time Queries

children.title: Implied-Bound Queries
children.top_down_role: Queries concerning temporal bounds entailed by the network.

assumptions_latex: The temporal network is finite and consistent.
Timepoints are real-valued and constraints are non-strict difference bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup\{x_j-x_i:x\text{ feasible}\}=d(i,j)\) and \(\inf\{x_j-x_i:x\text{ feasible}\}=-d(j,i)\).

notation.meaning: Shortest-path distance from i to j.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard STN shortest-path bound semantics
No relevant authoritative source locator was supplied.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tight difference-bound queries answered by shortest-path distances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In a consistent temporal distance graph encoding \(x_j-x_i\le w_{ij}\), let \(d(i,j)\) be the shortest-path distance from \(i\) to \(j\). The tightest network-implied upper bound on \(x_j-x_i\) is \(d(i,j)\), with value \(+\infty\) when no directed path exists. The tightest implied lower bound is \(-d(j,i)\). Therefore the complete implied interval for the difference is \[-d(j,i)\le x_j-x_i\le d(i,j).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Shortest-path distances give the tightest implied upper and lower bounds on every pairwise time difference.
knowledge_statements.title: Implied-Bound Queries

children.title: Temporal Slack Queries
children.top_down_role: Queries concerning available timing flexibility within a feasible network.

knowledge_statements.title: Temporal Slack Queries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise and total slack derived from a feasible-time interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a consistent temporal network with origin \(x_0=0\), write \(L_k=-d(k,0)\) and \(U_k=d(0,k)\). The total temporal slack of timepoint \(k\) is \(S_k=U_k-L_k\). For a proposed feasible execution time \(t\in[L_k,U_k]\), its backward and forward slacks are \(S_k^-(t)=t-L_k\) and \(S_k^+(t)=U_k-t\), respectively; its symmetric robustness margin is \(S_k^{\min}(t)=\min\{S_k^-(t),S_k^+(t)\}\). Infinite endpoints induce the corresponding infinite slack.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Temporal slack measures the width of a feasible-time interval and the remaining margins before or after a proposed execution time.
assumptions_latex: The network is consistent and has a fixed zero origin.
The queried execution time lies in its feasible interval.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_k=d(0,k)+d(k,0)\) whenever both distances are finite.

notation.meaning: Tight lower and upper feasible times for k.
Two-sided robustness margin at time t.

review_flags: Terminology for temporal slack varies; a domain-specific source is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The formulas are internally consistent with the stated interval-based convention and the definition kind fits the leaf. However, “temporal slack” and the proposed symmetric robustness margin are convention-dependent, and no domain-specific source or locator establishes these exact definitions.

children.title: Dynamic Temporal Network Update Family
children.top_down_role: Temporal reasoning under constraint additions, removals, tightening, and relaxation.

children.title: Incremental Constraint Insertion
children.top_down_role: Temporal-network changes caused by newly introduced constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Incremental Constraint Insertion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact closure update after inserting one difference constraint into a consistent STN.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(d(i,j))\) be the distance closure of a consistent network. To insert \(x_b-x_a\le c\), first test \(d(b,a)+c<0\). If true, reject the insertion as inconsistent. Otherwise set, for every ordered pair \((i,j)\), \[d'(i,j)=\min\{d(i,j),\ d(i,a)+c+d(b,j)\}.\] Interpret arithmetic with infinite distances in the extended-real sense. The resulting matrix \(D'\) is the exact closure after insertion; the update uses \(O(n^2)\) time and preserves the old closure if the new constraint is redundant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A single inserted bound updates every pairwise distance through the new edge; a negative return path detects inconsistency.
assumptions_latex: The old network is consistent and its exact distance closure is stored.
Exactly one non-strict difference constraint is inserted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D'\text{ is consistent}\iff d(b,a)+c\ge0\), and then \(d'(i,j)=\min\{d(i,j),d(i,a)+c+d(b,j)\}.\)

notation.meaning: Inserted edge encoding the new upper bound.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: single-edge dynamic all-pairs shortest-path update
No relevant dynamic-STN source locator was supplied.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The single-edge insertion test, closure update, and quadratic running-time claim fit the algorithm leaf and are internally coherent. No dynamic-STN or dynamic shortest-path source with an inspectable locator is supplied.

children.title: Constraint Retraction
children.top_down_role: Temporal-network changes caused by removed constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint Retraction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact retraction from the primitive constraint graph, avoiding deletion from closure alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain both the primitive temporal graph \(G=(V,E,w)\) and its closure. To retract a primitive constraint edge \(e\), form \(G^-=(V,E\setminus\{e\},w)\) and recompute shortest-path distances \(d^-(i,j)\) in \(G^-\). Output \(G^-\) and its closure. Retraction cannot make a consistent network inconsistent, and every new tight bound is no smaller than its former value. Deleting only the corresponding closed edge is not exact because that edge may encode other paths or may support many closure entries.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Retract constraints from the primitive graph and recompute closure; consistency is preserved, but implied bounds may weaken globally.
assumptions_latex: The retracted edge is a primitive constraint, not merely a closure edge.
The original temporal network is consistent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d^-(i,j)\ge d(i,j)\) for all \((i,j)\), and the feasible set after retraction contains the original feasible set.

notation.meaning: Primitive graph after removing the selected constraint.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: monotonicity of difference constraints under deletion
No relevant dynamic temporal-network source locator was supplied.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The primitive-edge retraction procedure and monotonicity claims fit the algorithm leaf, but no authoritative dynamic temporal-network source or specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Bound Tightening
children.top_down_role: Maintenance under stricter temporal bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Bound Tightening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incremental closure update when an existing temporal upper bound is decreased.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the primitive constraint \(x_b-x_a\le c\) is replaced by the tighter bound \(x_b-x_a\le c'\), where \(c'<c\), and let \(D=(d(i,j))\) be the old consistent closure. Treat the replacement as insertion of edge \(a\to b\) with weight \(c'\). If \(d(b,a)+c'<0\), report inconsistency. Otherwise update every pair by \[d'(i,j)=\min\{d(i,j),\ d(i,a)+c'+d(b,j)\}.\] The feasible set can only shrink, and no implied upper bound increases.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tightening a bound is a single-edge insertion: it may cause inconsistency and can only decrease implied upper bounds.
assumptions_latex: The old network is consistent and its exact closure is available.
The replacement weight satisfies \(c'<c\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d'(i,j)\le d(i,j)\) for all \((i,j)\), provided \(d(b,a)+c'\ge0\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: bound tightening as incremental edge insertion
No relevant dynamic-STN source locator was supplied.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Treating a strict decrease of an existing bound as insertion of the tighter edge is coherent and fits the algorithm leaf. The exact update and inconsistency test still require an authoritative source with a specific locator.

children.title: Bound Relaxation
children.top_down_role: Maintenance under weakened temporal bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Bound Relaxation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact update when an existing primitive temporal upper bound is increased.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a primitive edge \(a	o b\) of weight \(c\) is replaced by \(c'>c\). Modify that edge in the primitive graph and recompute shortest-path distances from the modified graph, rather than changing only \(d(a,b)\) in the old closure. The resulting closure \(D'=(d'(i,j))\) satisfies \(d'(i,j)\ge d(i,j)\) for every ordered pair. Relaxation enlarges the feasible set and therefore preserves consistency, but it may weaken many bounds whose former shortest paths used the modified edge.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relaxing one primitive bound preserves consistency but may increase many implied bounds, so the closure must be repaired from the primitive graph.
assumptions_latex: The old primitive temporal graph and its consistent closure are available.
The replacement weight satisfies \(c'>c\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal F(D)\subseteq\mathcal F(D')\) and \(d'(i,j)\ge d(i,j)\) for all \((i,j)\).

notation.meaning: Feasible schedules represented by the old network.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: monotonicity under relaxation of difference constraints
No relevant dynamic shortest-path source locator was supplied.
statement_latex contains an invalid control character and requires correction before promotion

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The relaxation procedure, feasible-set inclusion, and distance monotonicity are internally coherent and fit the algorithm leaf. The supplied statement does not contain the alleged invalid control character, but it has no authoritative source or inspectable locator.

children.title: Online Consistency Maintenance
children.top_down_role: Continuously updated consistency information for changing networks.

knowledge_statements.title: Online Consistency Maintenance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transactional maintenance of an exact STN closure under an online update stream.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize with a consistent primitive graph \(G_0\) and exact closure \(D_0\). For each online update, apply the single-edge insertion formula to insertions or tightenings. Commit such an update only if its new-edge cycle test is nonnegative; otherwise return the detected inconsistency and retain the previous state. For retractions or relaxations, modify the primitive graph and recompute or dynamically repair every affected shortest-path distance before committing. After each committed update \(t\), expose \(D_t\) for consistency and bound queries.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maintain primitive constraints and exact closure transactionally, rejecting inconsistent tightenings and repairing distances after relaxations or deletions.
assumptions_latex: Updates are processed sequentially and atomically.
The maintained closure is exact before each update.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_t\) equals the all-pairs shortest-path closure of \(G_t\), and every committed \(G_t\) is consistent.

notation.meaning: Primitive temporal graph after committed update t.
Exact closure maintained after update t.

review_flags: No authoritative online temporal-network algorithm source was supplied.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The transactional invariant fits online consistency maintenance, but “dynamically repair every affected shortest-path distance” does not identify a concrete repair algorithm or its conditions. An authoritative source is needed to determine the intended online algorithm and validate the stated maintenance guarantee.

children.title: Dispatchable Temporal Networks
children.top_down_role: Execution-oriented forms supporting local online timing decisions.

knowledge_statements.title: Dispatchable Temporal Networks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational definition of an equivalent network supporting local, backtrack-free execution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(N	ext{}\) be a consistent simple temporal network. An equivalent temporal network \(H\) is dispatchable when execution can proceed without global search as follows: after any extendable partial schedule on executed set \(E\), an unexecuted timepoint may be assigned using only the current time and constraints of \(H\) incident to already executed timepoints, and every assignment admitted by the dispatch rule preserves extendability to a complete schedule satisfying \(N\). Equivalence requires that \(H\) and \(N\) have the same complete feasible schedules; dispatchability additionally requires sound, backtrack-free local decisions at every reachable execution state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dispatchable network preserves the original schedules while allowing sound online timing choices from local constraints without backtracking or global search.
assumptions_latex: All durations and execution times are deterministic.
The original simple temporal network is consistent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal F(H)=\mathcal F(N)\), and each locally admitted execution step maps an extendable partial schedule to another extendable partial schedule.

notation.meaning: Complete feasible schedules of network N.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: operational characterization of deterministic STN dispatchability
Dispatchability definitions vary by execution semantics; an exact authoritative source is required.
statement_latex contains an invalid control character and requires correction before promotion

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind and execution-oriented scope fit the topic, and the displayed LaTeX contains no actual invalid control character. However, the local dispatch rule, reachable-state quantification, and requirement that every admitted assignment preserve extendability depend on the precise dispatch semantics. No authoritative source or locator is supplied to validate this formulation.

children.title: Temporal Decoupling
children.top_down_role: Separation into independently executable or organizationally partitioned subnetworks.

knowledge_statements.title: Temporal Decoupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong decoupling of a simple temporal network into independently schedulable blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an STN have timepoints \(V\), feasible schedules \(F\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{V}\), and a partition \(V=V_1\mathbin{\dot\cup}\cdots\mathbin{\dot\cup}V_m\). A temporal decoupling is a family of local constraint sets \(D_k\) on \(V_k\) such that each local feasible set \(F_k\) is nonempty and \[\prod_{k=1}^{m}F_k\subseteq F.\] Thus every independently selected tuple of local schedules combines into a globally feasible schedule. A reference timepoint may be copied into every block and fixed identically without violating disjointness of the decision coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A temporal decoupling gives each block local constraints so that every combination of independently chosen local schedules satisfies the original temporal network.
assumptions_latex: \(F\neq\varnothing\).
All blocks use the same fixed value for any copied reference timepoint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\prod_{k=1}^{m}F_k\subseteq F\).

notation.meaning: Globally feasible schedules of the original STN.
Schedules satisfying the local constraints for block k.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the leaf and states the strong independent-combination property precisely, but no source supports this particular notion of temporal decoupling or the copied-reference-timepoint convention.

children.title: General Disjunctive Temporal Problems
children.top_down_role: Unrestricted temporal disjunctions and their combinatorial boundary.

knowledge_statements.title: General Disjunctive Temporal Problems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite DTPs with unrestricted finite disjunctions of temporal difference bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A general disjunctive temporal problem consists of real-valued timepoints \(t_1,\ldots,t_n\) and constraints \[C_r=\bigvee_{q=1}^{k_r}\bigl(\ell_{rq}\le t_{j_{rq}}-t_{i_{rq}}\le u_{rq}\bigr),\qquad r=1,\ldots,m,\] where \(k_r\ge1\), endpoints may be infinite, and no common-variable or common-endpoint pattern is required among disjuncts. A schedule is feasible precisely when it satisfies at least one interval disjunct in every \(C_r\). Consistency asks whether such a schedule exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A general DTP asks for real event times satisfying one alternative interval-difference bound from every unrestricted finite disjunction.
assumptions_latex: \(n,m<\infty\).
\(\ell_{rq}\le u_{rq}\) for every finite interval.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists t\in\mathbb{R}^n\;\forall r\;\exists q\le k_r:\ell_{rq}\le t_{j_{rq}}-t_{i_{rq}}\le u_{rq}\).

notation.meaning: Number of alternatives in constraint r.

children.title: Restricted Disjunctive Temporal Problems

knowledge_statements.title: Restricted Disjunctive Temporal Problems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restriction is expressed by an explicit admissible family of temporal disjunctions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a family \(\mathcal R\) of admissible finite disjunctions of interval difference constraints. An \(\mathcal R\)-restricted disjunctive temporal problem is a general DTP in which every constraint \(C_r\) belongs to \(\mathcal R\). The family may restrict disjunction arity, permitted endpoint patterns, shared timepoints, interval geometry, or an associated graph parameter. Any tractability assertion must name \(\mathcal R\) and its encoding; restriction alone does not imply polynomial-time consistency.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A restricted DTP permits only disjunctions from a specified family; the restriction and encoding must be stated before tractability can be claimed.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal R\) is fixed independently of the particular instance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C_r\in\mathcal R\) for every \(r=1,\ldots,m\).

children.title: Temporal Disjunction Search-Propagation Interface
children.top_down_role: Search families combining temporal consistency with disjunct selection.

children.title: Disjunct Selection Search
children.top_down_role: Search organizations centered on selecting temporal alternatives.

knowledge_statements.title: Disjunct Selection Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complete depth-first search over one selected alternative per temporal disjunction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a DTP \(C_1,\ldots,C_m\). Initialize an empty partial selection \(S\). At a search node, propagate the STN formed by the bounds selected in \(S\); prune if it contains a negative cycle. If all constraints are selected, output the resulting feasible STN and a schedule. Otherwise choose an unassigned \(C_r\), create one child \(S\cup\{(r,q)\}\) for each disjunct \(q\), and recurse. Output infeasible only after every child has been pruned. The procedure is complete because every total disjunct selection occurs on some root-to-leaf path.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Branch on one alternative of an unresolved temporal disjunction, reject inconsistent partial STNs, and return infeasible only when every branch fails.
assumptions_latex: Each \(C_r\) has finitely many disjuncts.
The STN consistency test is sound and complete.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is either a feasible schedule or a complete exhaustion certificate for all \(\prod_r k_r\) selections.

notation.meaning: Selection of alternative q from constraint r.

source_refs.locator: 2.2.1 Outline of the general branch-and-bound method p. 15

source_witnesses.locator: 2.2.1 Outline of the general branch-and-bound method p. 15

children.title: Temporal Consistency Propagation
children.top_down_role: Temporal filtering performed within disjunctive reasoning.

knowledge_statements.title: Temporal Consistency Propagation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: STN closure is applied after each partial selection of temporal alternatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given selected difference bounds \(t_j-t_i\le b_{ij}\), construct a weighted graph with arc \(i\to j\) of weight \(b_{ij}\). Initialize \(d_{ij}=b_{ij}\), \(d_{ii}=0\), and missing entries to \(+\infty\); repeatedly apply \(d_{ij}\leftarrow\min\{d_{ij},d_{ik}+d_{kj}\}\). If some \(d_{ii}<0\), report inconsistency and prune the search node. Otherwise replace each bound by the implied tight bound \(t_j-t_i\le d_{ij}\), remove disjuncts contradicted by the closure, and continue search or output the closed consistent STN.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Close the selected STN by shortest paths, prune negative cycles, and delete unresolved alternatives contradicted by the resulting tight bounds.
assumptions_latex: Selected alternatives are representable as finite systems of difference bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_{ii}<0\) certifies inconsistency; otherwise \(d_{ij}\) gives the tight implied upper bounds.

notation.meaning: Current shortest-path upper bound on the difference from i to j.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Shortest-path closure and negative-cycle detection are standard, but the record gives no source and does not formalize the test by which closure contradicts and deletes an unresolved interval disjunct.

children.title: Conflict-Guided Branching
children.top_down_role: Branching organizations informed by detected temporal conflicts.

knowledge_statements.title: Conflict-Guided Branching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Negative-cycle explanations guide backtracking and subsequent disjunct choices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain a partial disjunct selection \(S\). When propagation finds a negative cycle, extract the selected literals \(K\subseteq S\) whose bounds label that cycle and record the nogood \(\neg\bigwedge_{a\in K}a\). Backtrack to the most recent decision in \(K\), delete its current alternative, and propagate the nogood. At a consistent node, select an unresolved disjunction whose alternatives occur most often in recorded nogoods, branch on its remaining alternatives, and repeat. A nogood may prune a node only when all its literals are selected there.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Explain each negative cycle by its selected alternatives, record that combination as a nogood, and prioritize disjunctions implicated in conflicts.
assumptions_latex: Every extracted conflict \(K\) labels an actual negative cycle.
Recorded nogoods persist throughout the search.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No feasible total selection extends \(K\), so every node containing \(K\) is soundly pruned.

notation.meaning: Conflict set of selected disjunct literals.

source_refs.locator: 2.2.1 Outline of the general branch-and-bound method p. 15

source_witnesses.locator: 2.2.1 Outline of the general branch-and-bound method p. 15

children.title: Search-Pruning Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Interfaces between temporal inference and branch elimination.

knowledge_statements.title: Search-Pruning Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Soundness and completeness contract between disjunctive search and temporal propagation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\) be a partial disjunct selection and let \(P(S)\) return consistent, inconsistent, or unknown, together with optional domain deletions. A valid search-pruning interface satisfies: inconsistent implies that no total selection extending \(S\) has a feasible schedule; every deleted alternative has no feasible extension with \(S\); and consistent is terminal only when \(S\) is total and the selected STN is feasible. If branching eventually enumerates every undeleted alternative, these conditions make the combined search sound and complete.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Propagation may prune only impossible extensions, and search must eventually branch over every surviving alternative; together these rules preserve soundness and completeness.
assumptions_latex: Every DTP constraint has finitely many alternatives.
Branching is exhaustive over alternatives not soundly deleted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The combined procedure returns feasible exactly when the input DTP has a feasible schedule.

notation.meaning: Propagation result for partial selection S.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the search-pruning interface leaf and gives plausible soundness and exhaustiveness requirements, but its exact soundness-and-completeness contract has no cited source.

children.title: Structural Tractability Regime Family

children.title: Interaction Graph Width
children.top_down_role: Difficulty classifications based on interaction-graph structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Interaction Graph Width
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal graph width of the disjunct-choice constraint representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite constraint representation with choice variables \(Y_1,\ldots,Y_m\), its interaction graph \(G_I\) has vertex set \(\{Y_1,\ldots,Y_m\}\) and an edge \(Y_rY_s\) whenever some represented feasibility constraint depends jointly on both variables. A tree decomposition is a tree of bags covering every vertex and edge and satisfying connected occurrence of each vertex. The interaction graph width is \[\operatorname{tw}(G_I)=\min_{\mathcal T}\left(\max_{B\in\mathcal T}|B|-1\right).\] The chosen constraint representation is part of the definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Interaction width is the treewidth of the primal graph connecting disjunct-choice variables that participate jointly in a represented feasibility constraint.
assumptions_latex: The choice-variable constraint representation is finite and explicitly fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{width}=\operatorname{tw}(G_I)\).

notation.meaning: Interaction or primal graph of choice variables.
A tree decomposition of the interaction graph.

children.title: Incidence Graph Width
children.top_down_role: Difficulty classifications based on constraint-incidence structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Incidence Graph Width
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Treewidth of the bipartite variable-constraint incidence graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite temporal constraint representation with variable set \(X\) and constraint set \(\mathcal C\), the incidence graph \(G_{\mathrm{inc}}\) is bipartite with vertices \(X\mathbin{\dot\cup}\mathcal C\) and edge \(xC\) exactly when the expression defining \(C\) contains \(x\). Its incidence graph width is \[\operatorname{itw}(X,\mathcal C)=\operatorname{tw}(G_{\mathrm{inc}})=\min_{\mathcal T}\left(\max_{B\in\mathcal T}|B|-1\right).\] For a DTP, each complete disjunction is one constraint vertex unless another encoding is explicitly declared.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Incidence width is the treewidth of the bipartite graph joining each temporal variable to every complete disjunctive constraint containing it.
assumptions_latex: The temporal variables and represented constraints are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{itw}(X,\mathcal C)=\operatorname{tw}(G_{\mathrm{inc}})\).

children.title: Disjunction Arity Restrictions
children.top_down_role: Complexity regimes distinguished by the size of temporal alternatives.

knowledge_statements.title: Disjunction Arity Restrictions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform bound on the number of temporal alternatives per constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a DTP \(\mathcal D=\{C_1,\ldots,C_m\}\), write \(C_r=\bigvee_{q=1}^{k_r}A_{rq}\), where each \(A_{rq}\) is an interval difference constraint. The instance has disjunction arity at most \(a\) precisely when \[\max_{1\le r\le m}k_r\le a.\] A class has bounded arity when one constant \(a\), independent of input size, bounds every member. This condition limits branching factor but, by itself, does not assert polynomial-time consistency.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Disjunction arity is bounded when a fixed constant limits the number of alternatives in every temporal constraint across the whole instance class.
assumptions_latex: \(a\in\mathbb N\) is independent of the encoded instance size.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(k_r\le a\) for every \(r=1,\ldots,m\).

notation.meaning: Number of alternatives in constraint r.

children.title: Tractable Structural Regimes
children.top_down_role: Structural subclasses supporting efficient temporal reasoning.

knowledge_statements.title: Tractable Structural Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tree-decomposition dynamic programming for an exact finite-domain constraint encoding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose DTP consistency is represented exactly by a finite CSP with \(N\) choice variables, domain size at most \(d\), and primal interaction graph of treewidth at most \(w\), and suppose every local relation can be tested in polynomial time. Given a width-\(w\) tree decomposition, dynamic programming stores feasible assignments on each bag and combines compatible child tables. It decides consistency using \(O(Nd^{w+1})\) table entries, up to polynomial-time local-relation and decomposition overhead. Hence the represented class is polynomial-time decidable for fixed \(d\) and \(w\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact bounded-domain encoding with bounded interaction treewidth is decidable by tree-decomposition dynamic programming in polynomial time.
assumptions_latex: The CSP encoding is feasibility-equivalent to the DTP.
\(d\) and \(w\) are fixed constants.
A width-\(w\) decomposition is supplied or found in polynomial time.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The number of dynamic-programming table entries is \(O(Nd^{w+1})\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind fits the tractability leaf, but the exact CSP encoding, relation placement, decomposition normalization, and resulting O(Nd^{w+1}) table bound require an authoritative structural-CSP source.

children.title: Hardness Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Transitions from restricted tractability to computational hardness.

knowledge_statements.title: Hardness Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unrestricted finite temporal disjunctions cross the NP-completeness boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consistency of general DTPs with rational interval endpoints is NP-complete. NP-hardness already holds when a reference timepoint \(z\) is fixed, every variable timepoint \(x_i\) is restricted by \((x_i-z=0)\vee(x_i-z=1)\), and each remaining constraint is a three-way disjunction of equalities encoding the literals of one 3-CNF clause. The constructed DTP is feasible exactly when the formula is satisfiable. Membership in NP follows by selecting one disjunct per constraint and checking the resulting system of difference constraints in polynomial time.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Allowing unrestricted temporal disjunctions makes consistency NP-complete; binary-valued timepoints and three-way clause disjunctions already encode 3-SAT.
assumptions_latex: All interval endpoints are rational and binary encoded.
Feasibility is interpreted over real-valued timepoints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathrm{DTP\text{-}CONSISTENCY}\) is NP-complete under polynomial-time many-one reductions.

notation.meaning: Binary-valued timepoint representing Boolean variable i.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary claim and sketched 3-SAT encoding are plausible and appropriately classified, but the exact restricted NP-hardness construction and NP-membership claim have no cited source.

children.title: Simple Temporal Networks with Uncertainty
children.top_down_role: Temporal networks separating controllable time points from contingent durations.

knowledge_statements.title: Simple Temporal Networks with Uncertainty
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard finite STNU with requirement constraints and bounded contingent links.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A simple temporal network with uncertainty is a tuple \(\mathcal N=(V,V_c,R,L)\), where \(V\) is a finite set of time points, \(V_c\subseteq V\) are executable time points, and \(R\) contains requirement constraints \(l_{ij}\le t_j-t_i\le u_{ij}\). Each contingent link \((A,\ell,u,C)\in L\) has executable activation \(A\), uncontrollable endpoint \(C\), and duration chosen by nature in \([\ell,u]\), with \(0<\ell\le u<\infty\). A scenario selects one duration for every contingent link; an execution is viable when all induced contingent equalities and all requirement constraints hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An STNU augments difference constraints with bounded durations whose endpoints are controlled by nature after executable activation points occur.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) and \(L\) are finite.
Each contingent endpoint belongs to exactly one contingent link.
Contingent durations satisfy \(0<\ell\le u<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[t_C-t_A\in[\ell,u]\quad\text{for every }(A,\ell,u,C)\in L,\qquad l_{ij}\le t_j-t_i\le u_{ij}\quad\text{for every requirement constraint}.\]

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the STNU container, but no evidence is cited and the relationship between executable points, contingent endpoints, and all of V is not fully specified. A formal STNU definition is required.

children.title: Controllability Families
children.top_down_role: Execution-policy regimes distinguished by commitment timing and information availability.

children.title: Strong Controllability
children.top_down_role: Precommitted execution regimes without adaptation to contingent observations.

knowledge_statements.title: Strong Controllability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong controllability under a single precommitted schedule for executable time points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Omega\) be the set of scenarios of an STNU, and let \(t^	heta\) denote the complete schedule induced by executable-time assignment \(x\) and scenario \(\theta\). The STNU is strongly controllable if there exists one assignment \(x:V_c\to\mathbb R\), chosen before any contingent duration is observed, such that every scenario produces a viable schedule. Thus the same executable times must satisfy all requirement constraints for every admissible realization of the contingent links.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong controllability means one fixed advance schedule works for every admissible realization of all contingent durations.
assumptions_latex: \(\Omega\) contains every admissible assignment of contingent-link durations.
The assignment \(x\) is independent of the realized scenario.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\exists x:V_c\to\mathbb R\;\forall\theta\in\Omega:\quad t^\theta(x)\text{ is viable}.\]

notation.meaning: Complete schedule induced under scenario theta.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The quantifier order correctly expresses a single precommitted schedule, but the record has no cited source for the formal strong-controllability semantics.

children.title: Dynamic Controllability
children.top_down_role: Nonanticipative adaptive execution regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Dynamic Controllability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dynamic controllability via a viable nonanticipative execution strategy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An execution strategy \(\sigma\) maps each scenario \(\theta\in\Omega\) to executable times \(\sigma(\theta):V_c\to\mathbb R\). It is nonanticipative if, whenever two scenarios have identical observations strictly before the execution time assigned to an executable point \(X\), they assign the same time to \(X\). An STNU is dynamically controllable if a nonanticipative strategy exists whose induced complete schedule is viable in every scenario.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dynamic controllability permits adaptation to observed contingent outcomes but forbids decisions based on outcomes not yet observed.
assumptions_latex: Contingent endpoints reveal their realized durations when they occur.
Strategies use only observations available before the relevant execution decision.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\exists\sigma\;\bigl(\sigma\text{ is nonanticipative}\bigr)\;\forall\theta\in\Omega:\quad t^\theta(\sigma(\theta))\text{ is viable}.\]

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind and adaptive interpretation fit the container, but the history-equivalence condition is informal and ambiguous when the two scenarios assign different execution times. A source-backed formal definition is required.

children.title: Weak Controllability
children.top_down_role: Scenario-dependent feasibility regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Weak Controllability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak controllability with a scenario-specific feasible executable schedule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Omega\) be the scenario set of an STNU. The network is weakly controllable if, for every scenario \(\theta\in\Omega\), there exists an assignment \(x_\theta:V_c\to\mathbb R\) such that the complete schedule induced by \(x_\theta\) and \(\theta\) is viable. The assignment may depend on the entire scenario, including contingent outcomes that would not yet be known online; weak controllability therefore asserts scenario-wise feasibility, not implementability by a nonanticipative policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weak controllability requires a feasible executable schedule for each scenario, even if that schedule uses complete foreknowledge of the scenario.
assumptions_latex: \(\Omega\) contains every admissible contingent-duration realization.
Scenario-specific assignments may use complete scenario information.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\forall\theta\in\Omega\;\exists x_\theta:V_c\to\mathbb R:\quad t^\theta(x_\theta)\text{ is viable}.\]

notation.meaning: Executable schedule selected for scenario theta.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The scenario-first quantifier order correctly captures weak controllability, but no authoritative source is supplied.

children.title: Conditional Temporal Networks with Uncertainty
children.top_down_role: Temporal networks combining observation-dependent conditions with contingent durations.

knowledge_statements.title: Conditional Temporal Networks with Uncertainty
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite CTNU combining propositional labels, observations, and bounded contingent durations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A conditional temporal network with uncertainty consists of an STNU structure together with a finite proposition set \(P\), observation time points \(O_p\) for \(p\in P\), and conjunction labels on time points and constraints. A truth scenario \(s:P\to\{0,1\}\) activates exactly the labeled objects whose labels are satisfied by \(s\); a duration scenario selects every active contingent duration. A valid execution schedules active executable points, observes \(p\) only when \(O_p\) executes, and satisfies every active requirement and contingent constraint without using unobserved truth values or future durations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A CTNU combines labeled conditional constraints and observation events with bounded uncertain durations, permitting only observation-respecting execution decisions.
assumptions_latex: \(P\), the time-point set, and the constraint set are finite.
Each proposition has a designated observation time point.
Labels are conjunctions of proposition literals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathcal N_{s,\theta}=\{\text{time points and constraints whose labels hold under }s\}\quad\text{must admit an observation-respecting viable execution for the chosen controllability regime}.\]

notation.meaning: Observation time point for proposition p.
Active temporal scenario under truth and duration realizations.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record broadly matches CTNUs, but its conclusion adds existence of an observation-respecting viable execution, which is a controllability property rather than part of the network definition. Formal label, scenario-projection, and controllability semantics need a CTNU source.

children.title: Distributional Duration Models
children.top_down_role: Temporal models assigning probability distributions to uncertain durations.

knowledge_statements.title: Distributional Duration Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint probability models for exogenous temporal durations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L=\{1,\ldots,m\}\) index contingent links and let \(D=(D_1,\ldots,D_m)\) be their random durations. A distributional duration model is a probability space \((\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P)\) together with a measurable map \(D:\Omega\to\mathcal D\subseteq\mathbb R_+^m\). Its joint law \(Q=\mathbb P\circ D^{-1}\) specifies both marginal duration distributions and dependence across links. Independence may be imposed only by the additional factorization \(Q=\bigotimes_{i=1}^m Q_i\); it is not inherent in the model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A distributional duration model assigns a joint probability law to nonnegative contingent durations, including any dependence among them.
assumptions_latex: The duration vector \(D\) is measurable.
All modeled durations are nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[Q(B)=\mathbb P\{\omega\in\Omega:D(\omega)\in B\},\qquad B\in\mathcal B(\mathcal D).\]

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The probability-space representation is mathematically coherent and fits the leaf, but no source connects this generic joint-law construction to contingent temporal durations.

children.title: Chance-Constrained Temporal Networks
children.top_down_role: Temporal feasibility organized by probabilistic satisfaction criteria.

knowledge_statements.title: Chance-Constrained Temporal Networks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint chance feasibility for temporal constraints under random durations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\) be the random contingent-duration vector, let \(\pi\) be an admissible execution policy, and let \(g_k(\pi,D)\le0\), for \(k=1,\ldots,q\), encode all selected temporal requirements after execution. A joint chance-constrained temporal network at risk tolerance \(\varepsilon\in[0,1]\) requires \(\pi\) to respect the prescribed information structure and to make all encoded requirements hold simultaneously with probability at least \(1-\varepsilon\). Individual chance constraints are distinct and do not generally imply this joint guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A policy is chance-feasible when all designated temporal requirements hold jointly with probability at least one minus the risk tolerance.
assumptions_latex: The duration vector \(D\) has a specified probability law.
Each violation function \(g_k(\pi,D)\) is measurable.
\(\varepsilon\in[0,1]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathbb P\!\left(\bigcap_{k=1}^{q}\{g_k(\pi,D)\le0\}\right)\ge1-\varepsilon.\]

children.title: Risk-Sensitive Dispatch
children.top_down_role: Dispatch policies evaluated through risk-sensitive execution goals.

knowledge_statements.title: Risk-Sensitive Dispatch
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Receding-horizon dispatch minimizing conditional risk while respecting temporal feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a temporal network, duration law, filtration \((\mathcal F_t)\), admissible risk functional \(\rho_t\), and stopping time \(T\). Initialize the executed set and observation history at time zero. At each decision time \(t<T\), form the policies consistent with completed events, observations, and hard constraints; select a next executable event and time minimizing \(\rho_t(Z^\pi\mid\mathcal F_t)\), where \(Z^\pi\) is future temporal loss; execute the selection and update \(\mathcal F_t\). Stop when all required events execute or infeasibility is certified, and output the realized schedule and risk evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Risk-sensitive dispatch repeatedly chooses a history-feasible next action minimizing conditional risk, then updates after new temporal observations.
assumptions_latex: Every dispatch decision is measurable with respect to the current history \(\mathcal F_t\).
The conditional risk minimization has an optimizer or a specified tie-breaking approximation.
Hard temporal constraints remain mandatory.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\pi_t\in\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{\pi\in\Pi(\mathcal F_t)}\rho_t\!\left(Z^\pi\mid\mathcal F_t\right),\quad\text{followed by history update until completion or certified infeasibility}.\]

notation.meaning: Information available at dispatch time t.
Future temporal loss under policy pi.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is an appropriate content kind, but the proposed procedure is a generic receding-horizon template. Its admissible policy class, decision epochs, risk functional, feasibility preservation, and claimed infeasibility certification require a source-backed specification.

children.title: Tail-Risk Temporal Criteria
children.top_down_role: Temporal objectives emphasizing adverse timing outcomes.

knowledge_statements.title: Tail-Risk Temporal Criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value-at-Risk and Conditional Value-at-Risk criteria for temporal loss.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z\in L^1\) be a temporal loss, such as deadline overrun or total weighted violation, and let \(\alpha\in(0,1)\). Its value-at-risk is the lower \(\alpha\)-quantile \(\operatorname{VaR}_\alpha(Z)=\inf\{z:\mathbb P(Z\le z)\ge\alpha\}\). Its conditional value-at-risk admits the optimization representation \(\operatorname{CVaR}_\alpha(Z)=\inf_{\eta\in\mathbb R}\{\eta+(1-\alpha)^{-1}\mathbb E[(Z-\eta)_+]\}\). A tail-risk temporal criterion minimizes this quantity over admissible schedules or policies.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tail-risk criteria evaluate large temporal losses using a loss quantile or the optimized mean excess beyond a threshold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\min_{\pi\in\Pi}\operatorname{CVaR}_\alpha(Z^\pi)=\min_{\pi\in\Pi,\,\eta\in\mathbb R}\left\{\eta+\frac{1}{1-\alpha}\mathbb E[(Z^\pi-\eta)_+]\right\}.\]

notation.meaning: Positive part, max of x and zero.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The VaR and CVaR formulas are standard, but no source is cited. The conclusion also uses minima over policies and thresholds without assumptions ensuring attainment; an infimum formulation or attainment hypotheses are required.

children.title: Temporal Preference-Flexibility Regime Family
children.top_down_role: Temporal models distinguishing hard feasibility from preferred timing, retained slack, and execution quality.

children.title: Graded Temporal Preference Models
children.top_down_role: Temporal networks with graded or prioritized timing preferences.

children.title: Soft Temporal Constraints
children.top_down_role: Timing restrictions whose violation may be tolerated at a cost.

knowledge_statements.title: Soft Temporal Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Temporal constraints whose violations incur penalties rather than infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For time variables \(t=(t_v)_{v\in V}\), a soft temporal constraint is a difference requirement \(l_k\le t_{j_k}-t_{i_k}\le u_k\) paired with a nonnegative penalty function \(p_k:\mathbb R_+\to\mathbb R_+\) satisfying \(p_k(0)=0\). Its violation magnitude is the distance of \(t_{j_k}-t_{i_k}\) from \([l_k,u_k]\). Unlike a hard constraint, violation remains admissible and contributes \(p_k(v_k(t))\) to an objective or bounded penalty budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A soft temporal constraint may be violated, with the amount of interval violation converted into a nonnegative optimization penalty.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) is finite.
Each penalty satisfies \(p_k(0)=0\) and \(p_k(r)\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[v_k(t)=\max\{l_k-(t_{j_k}-t_{i_k}),\,0,\,(t_{j_k}-t_{i_k})-u_k\},\qquad \min_t\sum_k p_k(v_k(t)).\]

notation.meaning: Violation magnitude of soft temporal constraint k.

children.title: Preferred Temporal Constraints
children.top_down_role: Timing choices distinguished by stated preference.

knowledge_statements.title: Preferred Temporal Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Temporal difference constraints equipped with graded satisfaction functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A preferred temporal constraint on time points \(i,j\) is a pair \((I_k,s_k)\), where \(I_k\subseteq\mathbb R\) is the admissible domain for the difference \(d_k=t_j-t_i\) and \(s_k:I_k\to S\) assigns a preference value in a totally ordered scale \((S,\preceq)\). A schedule is feasible when every difference lies in its admissible domain; among feasible schedules, larger satisfaction values are preferred according to a specified aggregation operator or ordering.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A preferred temporal constraint assigns graded desirability to each admissible time difference, separating feasibility from preference quality.
assumptions_latex: The preference scale \((S,\preceq)\) is totally ordered.
Each satisfaction function \(s_k\) is defined on its entire admissible domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[d_k=t_j-t_i\in I_k,\qquad \operatorname{pref}_k(t)=s_k(d_k),\qquad t\succcurlyeq t'\text{ according to the declared aggregation of }(s_k(d_k))_k.\]

notation.meaning: Admissible interval or domain for a temporal difference.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The local satisfaction-function model fits the topic, but no source is supplied and the global comparison is deferred to an unspecified aggregation operator whose required properties are not stated.

children.title: Priority-Based Preference Models
children.top_down_role: Temporal preferences organized through priority levels.

knowledge_statements.title: Priority-Based Preference Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lexicographic temporal preferences partitioned into ordered priority levels.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let temporal preference criteria be partitioned into priority levels \(C_1,\ldots,C_r\), with level one most important. For a feasible schedule \(t\), define the level score \(F_h(t)=\sum_{k\in C_h}w_k c_k(t)\), where lower values are preferred and \(w_k>0\). The priority model orders schedules lexicographically: \(t\prec_{\mathrm{lex}}t'\) precisely when, at the first level \(h\) where their scores differ, \(F_h(t)<F_h(t')\). Lower-priority improvement can never compensate for higher-priority deterioration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Priority-based models compare schedules at the highest priority where they differ, ignoring compensation from all lower levels.
assumptions_latex: The number of priority levels and criteria is finite.
All within-level weights satisfy \(w_k>0\).
Schedules compared satisfy the hard temporal constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[t\prec_{\mathrm{lex}}t'\iff \exists h:\ \bigl(\forall q<h,\ F_q(t)=F_q(t')\bigr)\ \land\ F_h(t)<F_h(t').\]

notation.meaning: Criteria assigned to priority level h.
Aggregate cost at priority level h.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation correctly describes finite lexicographic priority ordering, but no temporal-preference source is cited and the criterion functions c_k are not explicitly defined or characterized.

children.title: Graded Temporal Costs
children.top_down_role: Temporal quality represented through graded penalties or utilities.

assumptions_latex: A temporal network has variables \(t=(t_1,\ldots,t_n)\in\mathbb R^n\) and feasible set \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\).
Each indexed temporal requirement \(k\in K\) has a cost function \(c_k:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R_{\ge 0}\cup\{+\infty\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The graded temporal cost of schedule \(t\) is \(C(t)\), with smaller finite values representing more preferred feasible schedules.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: additive and monotone aggregations are standard formulations of graded temporal penalties
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive graded costs for deterministic temporal networks; hard infeasibility may be represented by infinite cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each \(t\in\mathbb R^n\), define \(d_k(t)=t_{j_k}-t_{i_k}\). Given nonnegative weights \(w_k\), the additive graded temporal cost is \[C(t)=\begin{cases}\displaystyle\sum_{k\in K}w_kc_k(d_k(t)),&t\in F,\\+\infty,&t\notin F.\end{cases}\] More generally, \(C(t)=A((c_k(d_k(t)))_{k\in K})\) for an aggregation map \(A\) that is nondecreasing in every coordinate. A schedule \(t^\star\) is cost-optimal when \(C(t^\star)=\inf_{t\in\mathbb R^n}C(t)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A graded temporal cost aggregates the penalties assigned to realized time differences, while infeasible schedules receive infinite cost; an optimal schedule minimizes this aggregate.
knowledge_statements.title: Graded Temporal Costs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the Graded Temporal Costs leaf and its notation is internally consistent, but the additive and general monotone aggregation formulations have no cited temporal-preference source or inspectable locator. Standard-field rationale alone does not resolve whether this is the intended domain-specific model.

children.title: Temporal Execution Resilience Measures
children.top_down_role: Structural measures of slack, controllability margin, and execution resilience.

children.title: Temporal Slack Measures
children.top_down_role: Measures of timing latitude within feasible schedules.

assumptions_latex: The temporal network has variables \(t=(t_1,\ldots,t_n)\in\mathbb R^n\) and a nonempty feasible schedule set \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\).
The nonempty finite set \(K\) indexes constraints \(\ell_k\le t_{j_k}-t_{i_k}\le u_k\), where \(i_k,j_k\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\) and \(\ell_k\le u_k\).
A feasible schedule \(t\in F\) is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The quantities \(s_k(t)\), \(s_{\min}(t)\), and \(s_{\Sigma}(t)\) respectively measure local, worst-case, and aggregate temporal slack.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: residuals of temporal difference inequalities are standard schedule-slack measures
