knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-based slack for a finite nonempty family of bounded difference constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each \(k\in K\), define the two-sided temporal slack at \(t\) by \[s_k(t)=\min\{t_{j_k}-t_{i_k}-\ell_k,\;u_k-(t_{j_k}-t_{i_k})\}.\] For a feasible schedule, \(s_k(t)\ge 0\). Define the bottleneck and aggregate slack by \[s_{\min}(t)=\min_{k\in K}s_k(t),\qquad s_{\Sigma}(t)=\sum_{k\in K}s_k(t).\] For a one-sided constraint, use its single finite-bound residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The slack of a bounded temporal constraint is the distance from its realized time difference to the nearer bound. The minimum and sum over a finite nonempty constraint family give bottleneck and aggregate slack.
knowledge_statements.title: Temporal Slack Measures

children.title: Flexibility-Volume Measures
children.top_down_role: Geometric measures of the size of feasible temporal regions.

assumptions_latex: Let \(n\ge2\), let \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty feasible schedule set, and suppose \(F+a\mathbf 1=F\) for every \(a\in\mathbb R\).
Fix a reference index \(r\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\) and define \(F_0=F\cap\{t\in\mathbb R^n:t_r=0\}\).
The anchored set \(F_0\) is measurable and bounded in the affine space \(\{t:t_r=0\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The measure \(V(F)=\lambda_{n-1}(F_0)\) quantifies anchored geometric temporal flexibility, and \(\bar V(F;B)\) is a dimensionless normalization relative to \(B\).

notation.meaning: Lebesgue measure on the anchored affine space.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: feasible-region volume is a standard geometric flexibility functional after removing temporal translation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric flexibility of a translation-invariant schedule set after fixing one reference time.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Regard \(F_0\) as a measurable subset of the \((n-1)\)-dimensional affine space \(\{t:t_r=0\}\). Define its flexibility volume by \[V(F)=\lambda_{n-1}(F_0).\] If a measurable reference region \(B\) in that affine space satisfies \(F_0\subseteq B\) and \(0<\lambda_{n-1}(B)<\infty\), define \[\bar V(F;B)=\frac{\lambda_{n-1}(F_0)}{\lambda_{n-1}(B)}\in[0,1].\] In particular, \(V(F)=0\) whenever \(F_0\) has affine dimension less than \(n-1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Flexibility volume is the Lebesgue measure of the feasible schedule region after temporal translation invariance is removed by fixing one reference time. It may be normalized by the finite positive volume of a containing reference region.
knowledge_statements.title: Flexibility-Volume Measures

children.title: Controllability Margins
children.top_down_role: Margins quantifying proximity to controllability loss.

assumptions_latex: A temporal execution model is parameterized by uncertainty \(u\in U(\rho)\), where \(U(\rho_1)\subseteq U(\rho_2)\) whenever \(\rho_1\le\rho_2\).
\(\Pi\) is the admitted class of nonanticipative execution policies.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The margin \(\rho^\star\) is the largest uncertainty radius for which some admitted policy guarantees satisfaction of every temporal constraint.

notation.meaning: Constraint-satisfaction predicate under policy \(\pi\) and uncertainty \(u\).

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: robust feasibility radius is a standard margin construction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Robust policy-based margin for a nested family of temporal uncertainty sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the controllability margin by \[\rho^\star=\sup\left\{\rho\ge0:\exists\pi\in\Pi\ \forall u\in U(\rho),\ \operatorname{Feas}(\pi,u)\right\}.\] Here nonanticipativity requires each execution decision of \(\pi\) to depend only on uncertainty outcomes observed before that decision. If the set is empty, set \(\rho^\star=0\); if it is unbounded, set \(\rho^\star=+\infty\). Nestedness makes controllability monotone in \(\rho\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A controllability margin is the largest uncertainty radius under which a nonanticipative execution policy can guarantee all temporal constraints.
knowledge_statements.title: Controllability Margins

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The robust-radius definition is coherent and fits Controllability Margins, but it is a generic robust-control construction rather than a sourced temporal-network definition. A temporal controllability reference must establish the uncertainty family, admitted policy class, and intended margin interpretation.

children.title: Execution Resilience Metrics
children.top_down_role: Metrics for tolerance to execution-time disturbances.

assumptions_latex: Uncertainty realizations \(u\) are distributed according to a probability law \(P\).
A fixed execution policy \(\pi\) produces a measurable execution trace \(T(\pi,u)\).

The execution loss is measurable and satisfies \(0
e L_{\max}<\infty\) and \(0\le L(T(\pi,u))\le L_{\max}\) for every relevant \(u\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The pair \((R_{\rm feas}(\pi),R_{\rm loss}(\pi))\) records feasibility probability and normalized expected-loss resilience under temporal uncertainty.

notation.meaning: Indicator that the execution trace satisfies all hard temporal constraints.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: probability of success and expected loss are standard stochastic resilience summaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Probabilistic resilience of a fixed temporal execution policy under a specified uncertainty distribution and a positive loss scale.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I_{\rm feas}(\pi,u)=1\) exactly when \(T(\pi,u)\) satisfies every hard temporal constraint, and let it equal \(0\) otherwise. Define \[R_{\rm feas}(\pi)=\mathbb E_P[I_{\rm feas}(\pi,u)]=P\{u:T(\pi,u)\text{ is feasible}\},\] \[R_{\rm loss}(\pi)=1-\frac{\mathbb E_P[L(T(\pi,u))]}{L_{\max}}.\] Both metrics lie in \([0,1]\), with larger values indicating greater execution resilience.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Execution resilience is summarized by the probability that the policy satisfies all hard temporal constraints and by one minus its expected loss normalized by a strictly positive loss bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Execution Resilience Metrics

children.title: Preference-Aware Temporal Dispatch
children.top_down_role: Execution policies balancing feasibility, preference satisfaction, and retained flexibility.

assumptions_latex: At each decision epoch, the observed partial execution induces a nonempty set \(A(h)\) of immediately feasible actions.
Each \(a\in A(h)\) has predicted preference loss \(p(a\mid h)\) and retained-flexibility score \(f(a\mid h)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure outputs a history-dependent execution trace that preserves immediate feasibility and greedily balances preference loss against retained flexibility.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: receding-horizon feasible action selection with a scalarized objective is a standard dispatch construction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Online scalarized dispatch over actions that are currently certified feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input the temporal network, preference model, flexibility score, and \(\lambda\ge0\); initialize \(h\) to the empty history. At each decision epoch compute \(A(h)\). If \(A(h)=\varnothing\), return failure and \(h\). Otherwise select \[a^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{a\in A(h)}\bigl(p(a\mid h)-\lambda f(a\mid h)\bigr),\] execute \(a^\star\), observe its outcome, and append both to \(h\). Stop when every required event has executed, and output \(h\). Ties are resolved by a fixed deterministic rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each execution step, choose an immediately feasible action minimizing predicted preference loss minus a weighted retained-flexibility score, then update after observing the outcome.
knowledge_statements.title: Preference-Aware Temporal Dispatch

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind algorithm fits the dispatch topic, and the procedure only claims immediate feasibility rather than guaranteed completion. However, the scalarized greedy rule is an unsourced construction; no evidence establishes that its action set, preference predictor, or flexibility score corresponds to a recognized preference-aware temporal dispatch method.

children.title: Temporal Conflict Diagnosis-Repair System
children.top_down_role: Failure detection, conflict localization, relaxation, and restoration for temporal networks.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Simple Temporal Networks: A Practical Foundation for Temporal Representation and Reasoning
top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Restoring Consistency
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Simple Temporal Networks: A Practical Foundation for Temporal Representation and Reasoning

children.title: Temporal Conflict Certificates
children.top_down_role: Graph and constraint artifacts identifying inconsistent temporal dependencies.

assumptions_latex: A simple temporal network contains finitely many difference constraints \(t_j-t_i\le b_{ij}\) with rational bounds.
Its distance graph \(G=(V,E,w)\) has an arc \(i\to j\) of weight \(b_{ij}\) for every such constraint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A directed cycle with negative total weight is a polynomially checkable certificate that the temporal network is inconsistent.

notation.meaning: Distance graph of the temporal network.
Directed cycle in the distance graph.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: negative-cycle infeasibility certificates for systems of difference constraints are classical
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Negative-cycle certificate for inconsistency of a finite simple temporal network with rational bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A temporal conflict certificate is a directed cycle \(C=(v_0,v_1,\ldots,v_m=v_0)\) in \(G\) satisfying \[w(C)=\sum_{r=0}^{m-1}w(v_r,v_{r+1})<0.\] Such a certificate establishes that the represented temporal network is inconsistent. It can be verified by checking the listed arcs and summing their rational weights, in time polynomial in the certificate length and the weight encoding size.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A negative directed cycle in the distance graph is a polynomially checkable certificate that a simple temporal network is inconsistent.
knowledge_statements.title: Temporal Conflict Certificates

children.title: Minimal Temporal Conflicts
children.top_down_role: Irreducible inconsistent temporal subnetworks and related explanation families.

assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a finite family of temporal constraints.
For \(S\subseteq K\), \(F(S)\) denotes the set of schedules satisfying every constraint in \(S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A set \(M\subseteq K\) is a minimal temporal conflict exactly when it is infeasible but every proper subset is feasible.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: inclusion-minimal infeasible subsets are the standard irreducible-conflict notion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inclusion-minimal infeasible subsets, distinct from minimum-cardinality conflicts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A subset \(M\subseteq K\) is a minimal temporal conflict if \[F(M)=\varnothing\quad\text{and}\quad F(M\setminus\{k\})\ne\varnothing\ \text{ for every }k\in M.\] Equivalently, \(F(M)=\varnothing\) and \(F(S)\ne\varnothing\) for every proper subset \(S\subsetneq M\). Minimality is by set inclusion; it does not assert that \(M\) has minimum cardinality among all infeasible subsets of \(K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A minimal temporal conflict is an infeasible constraint subset that becomes feasible whenever any one of its constraints is removed.
knowledge_statements.title: Minimal Temporal Conflicts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition correctly distinguishes inclusion-minimal infeasibility from minimum cardinality and fits the Minimal Temporal Conflicts leaf. It nevertheless has no temporal-conflict citation or inspectable locator, so its domain-specific terminology remains unsupported.

children.title: Temporal Constraint Repair Calculus
children.top_down_role: Constraint removal, bound relaxation, preference-aware restoration, and minimal-change repair.

children.title: Constraint Removal Repair
children.top_down_role: Restoration through removal of selected temporal constraints.

assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a finite inconsistent temporal constraint family.
Each constraint \(k\in K\) has a nonnegative removal cost \(c_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm returns a minimum-cost set \(R^\star\) whose removal restores consistency.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: weighted constraint deletion is a standard consistency-restoration formulation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact weighted deletion repair for a finite temporal constraint family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input \(K\) and costs \((c_k)_{k\in K}\). Solve \[R^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{R\subseteq K}\left\{\sum_{k\in R}c_k:F(K\setminus R)\ne\varnothing\right\}.\] Initialize the incumbent with \(R=K\); enumerate candidate removal sets by nondecreasing cost, or solve the equivalent binary optimization model with variables \(z_k=1\) for removed constraints. Stop when optimality is certified, and output \(R^\star\) together with any schedule \(t^\star\in F(K\setminus R^\star)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Remove a minimum-cost subset of temporal constraints so that the remaining family admits a schedule, and return both the removed set and a feasible schedule.
knowledge_statements.title: Constraint Removal Repair

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The minimum-cost deletion formulation fits Constraint Removal Repair, but the record supplies no temporal-repair source. Its references to enumeration and an equivalent binary model also do not specify a complete optimization encoding or a concrete optimality certificate, so evidence is needed before treating it as a supported algorithm.

children.title: Bound-Relaxation Repair
children.top_down_role: Restoration through weakening selected temporal bounds.

assumptions_latex: Constraint \(k\in K\) has original bounds \(\ell_k\le t_{j_k}-t_{i_k}\le u_k\).
Relaxation penalties \(c_k^-,c_k^+\) are nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm returns feasible relaxed bounds minimizing the prescribed weighted total enlargement.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: minimum weighted bound enlargement is a standard elastic-constraint repair model
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuous bound enlargement with weighted linear repair cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input the bounds and penalties; initialize \(\delta_k^-=\delta_k^+=0\). Solve \[\min_{t,\delta^-,\delta^+}\sum_{k\in K}(c_k^-\delta_k^-+c_k^+\delta_k^+)\] subject to \[\ell_k-\delta_k^-\le t_{j_k}-t_{i_k}\le u_k+\delta_k^+,\qquad \delta_k^-,\delta_k^+\ge0\quad(k\in K).\] Stop when an optimal solution is certified. Output \(t^\star\) and repaired bounds \((\ell_k-\delta_k^{-*},u_k+\delta_k^{+*})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Enlarge lower and upper temporal bounds by nonnegative amounts, minimizing weighted total enlargement while requiring the repaired network to admit a schedule.
knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Relaxation Repair

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The weighted bound-enlargement optimization model is coherent and appropriately placed under Bound-Relaxation Repair. No cited source with a specific locator supports its status as a temporal repair algorithm, however, and the local inventory is unrelated to temporal networks.

children.title: Preference-Aware Restoration
children.top_down_role: Restoration guided by temporal preference information.

assumptions_latex: \(H\) is the family of hard temporal constraints and may be repaired only through an admitted repair variable \(r\in\mathcal R\).
\(P(t)\) is the aggregate preference cost of schedule \(t\), and \(D(r)\) is repair cost.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm restores hard feasibility while selecting, among admitted repairs, a schedule-repair pair balancing repair magnitude and temporal preference.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: scalarized restoration combines feasibility repair with preference optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalarized joint optimization of admitted repair and residual temporal preference cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input \(H\), \(\mathcal R\), costs \(D\) and \(P\), and weight \(\lambda\ge0\). Solve \[(r^\star,t^\star)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{r\in\mathcal R,\ t\in F_H(r)}\bigl(D(r)+\lambda P(t)\bigr).\] Initialize with any pair having \(t\in F_H(r)\); if none exists, return failure. Stop when optimality is certified and output \((r^\star,t^\star)\). For \(\lambda=0\), the rule minimizes repair cost only; positive \(\lambda\) distinguishes repairs by retained preference quality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose an admitted repair and a feasible schedule jointly, minimizing repair cost plus a weighted residual preference cost.
knowledge_statements.title: Preference-Aware Restoration

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The scalarized formulation matches the Preference-Aware Restoration leaf, but feasibility of one pair does not ensure that the displayed argmin is attained, and no concrete solution or certification method is specified. A source is required to determine the intended repair space, existence conditions, and recognized algorithmic formulation.

children.title: Minimal-Change Temporal Repair
children.top_down_role: Repairs organized by limited deviation from the original network.

assumptions_latex: \(x^0\) encodes the original temporal network and \(\mathcal X_{m feas}\) contains all admitted consistent repaired encodings.
\(d:\mathcal X\times\mathcal X\to\mathbb R_{\ge0}\) is a specified change measure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm returns an admitted consistent temporal network at minimum distance from the original encoding.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: nearest feasible model under a prescribed distance is the standard minimal-change repair formulation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nearest consistent admitted encoding under an explicitly chosen change metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input \(x^0\), \(\mathcal X_{m feas}\), and \(d\). Solve \[x^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathcal X_{m feas}}d(x,x^0).\] Initialize with any \(x\in\mathcal X_{m feas}\); if no such encoding exists, return failure. Stop when a lower bound equals the incumbent value, and output \(x^\star\) with a feasible schedule for its encoded network. The metric must be fixed before optimization; examples include weighted deletion count and weighted \(\ell_1\) bound displacement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A minimal-change repair is the consistent admitted network closest to the original under a predetermined distance, with distance choice defining what counts as change.
knowledge_statements.title: Minimal-Change Temporal Repair

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The nearest-feasible formulation is relevant to Minimal-Change Temporal Repair, but the assumptions call d only a nonnegative change measure while the statement later calls it a metric, and nonempty feasibility alone does not ensure an argmin exists. Source evidence is needed to fix the admissible encoding space, distance assumptions, attainment conditions, and algorithmic certification method.

children.title: Temporal Execution Failure Boundary
children.top_down_role: Loss of feasibility or controllability during execution and the boundary between local recovery and replanning.

children.title: Dispatch Failure
children.top_down_role: Failures arising from dispatchability limitations.

assumptions_latex: The residual temporal network is finite and all executed timepoints have fixed observed times.
Dispatch decisions may assign only times consistent with the current execution history.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Dispatch failure occurs exactly when \(D(h)=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: admissible next dispatch decisions after the history
set of complete feasible temporal extensions

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: operational boundary formalized using standard temporal-network dispatch semantics
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational failure of an online dispatcher, distinct from infeasibility of every residual schedule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(h\) fix the occurrence times of all executed timepoints and let \(F(h)\) be the complete schedules extending \(h\) that satisfy every active temporal constraint. Let \(D(h)\) contain the enabled next-event and execution-time choices admitted by the dispatcher and preserving at least one member of \(F(h)\). A dispatch failure occurs at \(h\) when \(D(h)=\varnothing\). If \(F(h)\neq\varnothing\), the failure is algorithmic or policy-relative; if \(F(h)=\varnothing\), it is induced by execution feasibility loss.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dispatch fails when the dispatcher has no admissible next action preserving a feasible temporal extension; the cause may be policy weakness or actual infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.title: Dispatch Failure

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind and policy-relative distinction fit the leaf, and the mathematical statement is internally coherent. However, no inspectable source is supplied for the dispatcher semantics or the claimed boundary, so source support is required before candidate review.

children.title: Execution Feasibility Loss
children.top_down_role: Loss of temporal feasibility during execution.

assumptions_latex: The temporal network and execution history are finite.
Executed timepoints cannot be reassigned.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Execution feasibility is lost exactly when \(F(h)=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: complete schedules extending the history and satisfying all active constraints

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: residual feasibility is the standard extension predicate for temporal constraint networks
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual deterministic feasibility after fixing an observed execution prefix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an execution history \(h\), define \(F(h)\) as the set of assignments to all unexecuted timepoints that, together with the fixed observations in \(h\), satisfy every active temporal constraint. Execution feasibility is lost at \(h\) precisely when \(F(h)=\varnothing\). Equivalently, the temporal constraints augmented by equalities fixing every executed timepoint to its observed time are inconsistent. This condition is independent of whether a particular dispatch procedure detects the inconsistency.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Execution feasibility is lost when the fixed execution history has no complete schedule satisfying all remaining temporal constraints.
knowledge_statements.title: Execution Feasibility Loss

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The residual-feasibility condition precisely matches the leaf and is stated consistently in plain text and LaTeX. No source with a specific locator is provided, so the temporal-network formulation remains unsupported.

children.title: Controllability Loss
children.top_down_role: Execution states where required controllability no longer holds.

assumptions_latex: Uncontrollable durations range over their declared uncertainty sets.
Execution strategies are nonanticipative: decisions depend only on observations available at the decision time.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Controllability is lost after \(h\) exactly when \(\Sigma(h)=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: admissible future uncertainty realizations consistent with the history
feasible nonanticipative execution strategies after the history

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: dynamic controllability is expressed by existence of a nonanticipative strategy robust to all admissible realizations
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dynamic controllability of a residual temporal network with uncertainty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given history \(h\), let \(\Omega(h)\) be the uncertainty realizations still consistent with observations. Let \(\Sigma(h)\) contain the nonanticipative strategies whose induced schedule satisfies every temporal constraint for every \(\omega\in\Omega(h)\). Controllability is lost after \(h\) when \(\Sigma(h)=\varnothing\), equivalently when every nonanticipative strategy fails for at least one admissible realization: \(\forall \sigma\,\exists\omega\in\Omega(h)\) such that the schedule induced by \(\sigma\) and \(\omega\) violates an active constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Controllability is lost when no observation-respecting execution strategy can satisfy the temporal constraints for every still-possible uncertainty realization.
knowledge_statements.title: Controllability Loss

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind is appropriate for loss of residual dynamic controllability. An authoritative STNU source is absent, and the final quantified formulation should explicitly restrict sigma to the admissible nonanticipative strategies rather than quantify over an unstated universe.

children.title: Local Temporal Recovery
children.top_down_role: Recovery confined to the affected temporal neighborhood.

assumptions_latex: The execution history and a designated frozen set must remain unchanged.
A finite neighborhood of repairable constraints or unexecuted timepoints is supplied.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm returns a feasible local repair or reports that none exists in \(\mathcal R(h,L)\).

notation.meaning: candidate repairs confined to the neighborhood

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: bounded-neighborhood repair is a standard constraint-based recovery pattern
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Repair confined to an explicitly supplied temporal neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a temporal network, execution history \(h\), and repair neighborhood \(L\). Construct \(\mathcal R(h,L)\) from permitted relaxations, retimings, or precedence changes whose support lies in \(L\), while fixing executed times and all protected decisions. Test candidates in nondecreasing repair cost. Return the first \(r\in\mathcal R(h,L)\) for which the repaired residual network has a feasible extension, together with such an extension. Stop with local-recovery failure when every candidate has been excluded or the repair subproblem is proved infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Search the permitted local modifications by repair cost, returning a feasible repaired schedule while preserving executed and protected decisions, or report local failure.
knowledge_statements.title: Local Temporal Recovery

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: An algorithm is an appropriate role for local temporal recovery, but no source supports the proposed repair procedure. A finite neighborhood does not by itself make the repair family finite or enumerable, so the claimed exhaustive failure report and first-by-cost return require additional assumptions or a sourced optimization procedure.

children.title: Replanning Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Conditions separating local recovery from broader replanning.

assumptions_latex: Executed timepoints and protected plan decisions are immutable.
The admissible local repair family is explicitly specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Replanning is necessary relative to \(\mathcal R_L\) exactly when \(\{r\in\mathcal R_L:F_r(h)\neq\varnothing\}=\varnothing\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: replanning boundary is defined relative to exhaustion of the declared local repair space
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between bounded temporal repair and changes to higher-level plan decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal R_L\) be the complete family of permitted local temporal repairs preserving the execution history \(h\) and every protected plan decision. For each \(r\in\mathcal R_L\), let \(F_r(h)\) be the feasible extensions of the repaired residual network. The replanning boundary is crossed when \(F_r(h)=\varnothing\) for every \(r\in\mathcal R_L\). Any successful recovery must then alter a decision outside the local repair scope, enlarge that scope, revise a requirement, or terminate the plan.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replanning becomes necessary when every allowed local temporal repair lacks a feasible extension, so recovery must alter decisions outside the protected repair scope.
knowledge_statements.title: Replanning Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The relative failure boundary is coherent and correctly distinguishes exhaustion of a declared local repair family from global impossibility. No inspectable plan-repair source is supplied for this formalization.

children.title: Configuration Problems
children.top_down_role: Knowledge-based selection, composition, validation, optimization, interaction, and evolution of product or system variants.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Knowledge-Based Configuration: From Research to Business Cases
top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Basics; Advanced Topics; Configuration Environments
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Knowledge-Based Configuration: From Research to Business Cases

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Variant Tables; Feature Models; Rule-Based Systems; Logic; Constraint Programming

children.title: Configuration Task Families
children.top_down_role: Distinct construction and lifecycle tasks performed over configuration knowledge.

children.title: Initial Configuration
children.top_down_role: Construction of a complete valid configuration from requirements and domain knowledge.

assumptions_latex: The variable set and every variable domain are finite.
Domain constraints and requirements are jointly represented by a predicate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An initial configuration is any \(x\in\prod_{i\in I}D_i\) satisfying \(C(x)\land R(x)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: finite-domain CSP solution semantics provide the standard mathematical model of initial configuration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-domain construction of a complete configuration from requirements and domain constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An initial configuration instance consists of finite variables \((x_i)_{i\in I}\), finite domains \((D_i)_{i\in I}\), a domain-knowledge predicate \(C\), and a requirements predicate \(R\). A complete valid initial configuration is an assignment \(x\in\prod_{i\in I}D_i\) such that \(C(x)\land R(x)\) holds. The construction task returns one such assignment, or establishes that the feasible configuration set \(\{x:C(x)\land R(x)\}\) is empty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Initial configuration assigns every finite-domain variable so that all domain constraints and stated requirements hold, or determines that no such assignment exists.
knowledge_statements.title: Initial Configuration

children.title: Configuration Completion Regime Family
children.top_down_role: Extension of partial decisions while preserving valid completions.

children.title: Partial Configuration Completion
children.top_down_role: Extension of partial selections into valid configurations.

assumptions_latex: The configuration variables have finite domains.
The given partial assignment is internally consistent but need not be completable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A successful output \(x\) satisfies \(p\subseteq x\) and \(C(x)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: completion is standard finite-domain CSP search under fixed assignments
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Completion of a fixed partial assignment without revising its selected values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a finite configuration model \(C\) and partial assignment \(p\). Fix every assignment in \(p\), propagate the resulting domain restrictions, and search over the remaining variables \(U\). Return a total assignment \(x\) when \(p\subseteq x\) and \(C(x)\) hold. If propagation derives an empty domain or exhaustive search excludes every remaining assignment, return failure; this failure means that no valid complete configuration extends \(p\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fix the user's partial choices, propagate constraints, and search the remaining domains for a valid total extension; report failure only when no extension exists.
knowledge_statements.title: Partial Configuration Completion

children.title: Proactive Autocompletion
children.top_down_role: System-initiated completion support during configuration.

assumptions_latex: The configuration model has finite domains.
An extension-preserving acceptance policy and a deterministic tie-breaking rule are supplied.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each committed state \(p_{k+1}\) satisfies \(\operatorname{Ext}(p_{k+1})\neq\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: valid complete extensions of a partial assignment

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: autocompletion formalized as scored CSP completion with an extendability invariant
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Automatic incremental completion while preserving at least one valid total extension.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a configuration model, a partial assignment \(p_0\), and score \(s(i,v\mid p_k)\). At iteration \(k\), propagate constraints, enumerate unassigned pairs \((i,v)\), and discard every pair for which \(\operatorname{Ext}(p_k\cup\{x_i=v\})=\varnothing\). Select the highest-scoring retained pair, set \(p_{k+1}=p_k\cup\{x_i=v\}\), and repeat until the acceptance policy stops or the assignment is total. Output the final partial or complete configuration; report failure if \(\operatorname{Ext}(p_0)=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly add the highest-scoring inferred choice that still permits a valid completion, stopping under the acceptance policy or when the configuration is complete.
knowledge_statements.title: Proactive Autocompletion

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithmic kind fits proactive autocompletion, and the extendability filter establishes the stated invariant. No inspectable source supports this particular scored, incremental recommendation procedure or its acceptance-policy formulation.

children.title: Completion-Preserving Recommendations
children.top_down_role: Suggestions restricted to choices retaining valid completions.

assumptions_latex: The current partial assignment has at least one valid completion.
Each recommendation assigns one currently unassigned variable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A recommendation \((i,v)\) is completion-preserving exactly when \(\operatorname{Ext}(p\cup\{x_i=v\})\neq\varnothing\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: recommendation safety is expressed by the standard CSP extendability predicate
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safety condition for recommending a single additional configuration choice.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p\) be a partial configuration with \(\operatorname{Ext}(p)\neq\varnothing\). A recommendation \((i,v)\), where \(x_i\) is unassigned in \(p\) and \(v\in D_i\), is completion-preserving if and only if \(\operatorname{Ext}(p\cup\{x_i=v\})\neq\varnothing\). Thus accepting the recommendation cannot by itself eliminate all valid completions. A displayed recommendation set is universally completion-preserving when this condition holds separately for every displayed pair; it need not imply that all displayed pairs are jointly compatible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A recommended value is completion-preserving when adding it to the current choices leaves at least one valid total configuration; individually safe recommendations may conflict jointly.
knowledge_statements.title: Completion-Preserving Recommendations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition precisely captures individual completion preservation and correctly warns that individually safe recommendations need not be jointly compatible. The record has no cited source with a specific locator.

children.title: Completion Failure Detection
children.top_down_role: Recognition of partial configurations lacking valid extensions.

assumptions_latex: The configuration model is a finite constraint system.
The partial assignment is encoded as a set of unary constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A subset-minimal unsatisfiable core \(K\) certifies \(\operatorname{Ext}(p)=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: model constraints together with assignments from the partial configuration

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: unsatisfiable cores are standard finite-CSP certificates of nonextendability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unsatisfiable-core certificate for nonextendability of a partial configuration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Form \(\mathcal C_p\) by adjoining the unary constraints induced by partial assignment \(p\) to the configuration model. Completion failure holds exactly when \(\mathcal C_p\) is unsatisfiable, equivalently when \(\operatorname{Ext}(p)=\varnothing\). A verifiable failure certificate is a subset \(K\subseteq\mathcal C_p\) whose conjunction is unsatisfiable. When every proper subset of \(K\) is satisfiable, \(K\) is subset-minimal and isolates an irreducible conflict, although it need not have minimum cardinality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Completion fails when the partial choices and model constraints are unsatisfiable; an unsatisfiable core certifies failure and a subset-minimal core isolates an irreducible conflict.
knowledge_statements.title: Completion Failure Detection

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The unsatisfiability condition and distinction between subset-minimal and minimum-cardinality cores are mathematically precise, and a certificate is a defensible role for this detection leaf. The cited general constraint-programming section does not specifically establish unsatisfiable-core certificates or minimal-core terminology, so a targeted source is required.

children.title: Configuration Transformation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Transformation of an existing configuration under changed requirements, components, or knowledge.

children.title: Requirement-Driven Reconfiguration
children.top_down_role: Configuration changes prompted by revised requirements.

assumptions_latex: The old configuration is complete and valid under the previous requirements.
The revised model has finite domains and a nonnegative change-cost function.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output belongs to \(\arg\min\{d(x,x^0):C'(x)\land R'(x)\}\), or infeasibility is reported.

notation.meaning: cost of changing the existing configuration

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: reconfiguration is modeled as constrained optimization relative to an incumbent assignment
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimal configuration revision induced by changed requirements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input an existing configuration \(x^0\), revised predicates \(C'\) and \(R'\), and change cost \(d\). Form the feasible revised set \(X'=\{x:C'(x)\land R'(x)\}\). If \(X'=\varnothing\), report that the new requirements are incompatible with the domain model. Otherwise solve \(\min_{x\in X'}d(x,x^0)\), using the declared tie-breaking rule when several minimizers exist, and return an optimizer together with the variables whose values differ from \(x^0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Find a configuration satisfying the revised requirements while minimizing declared change cost from the old configuration, or report that the revised model is infeasible.
knowledge_statements.title: Requirement-Driven Reconfiguration

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-domain optimization algorithm matches requirement-driven reconfiguration and has sufficient assumptions for an optimizer whenever the revised feasible set is nonempty. No authoritative reconfiguration source with an inspectable locator is supplied.

children.title: Component Upgrade
children.top_down_role: Replacement or advancement of components in existing products.

assumptions_latex: A complete incumbent configuration and a designated component replacement are given.
Compatibility and requirement predicates include all mandatory consequences of the replacement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A valid upgrade is any \(x\in X_u\); an optimal upgrade minimizes \(d(x,x^0)\) over \(X_u\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: component upgrade is a reconfiguration problem with a forced replacement constraint
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reconfiguration with a mandatory component replacement and propagated compatibility constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x^0\) be the incumbent configuration and let the upgrade require \(x_j=u\) for designated component variable \(x_j\). With current compatibility predicate \(C_u\) and requirements predicate \(R_u\), define \(X_u=\{x:x_j=u,\ C_u(x),\ R_u(x)\}\). A component upgrade is any \(x\in X_u\). If change cost matters, a minimal-change upgrade is an optimizer of \(\min_{x\in X_u}d(x,x^0)\). If \(X_u=\varnothing\), the requested component has no compatible valid upgrade under the current model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A component upgrade forces the designated replacement and adjusts other choices until compatibility and requirements hold, optionally minimizing changes from the incumbent configuration.
knowledge_statements.title: Component Upgrade

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition correctly specializes reconfiguration by imposing a mandatory component value and propagating compatibility and requirement constraints. The optional minimal-change variant is clearly separated, but no inspectable configuration-upgrade source is provided.

children.title: Legacy Constraint Migration
children.top_down_role: Transfer of existing configuration commitments to revised knowledge.

assumptions_latex: The legacy and target models have finite variable sets and decidable constraints.
A partial correspondence \(\mu\) maps legacy assignments to target assignments.
The preservation predicate \(P(x,y)\) specifies the required migration semantics.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output \(y^*\) is target-valid and preserves the legacy assignment: \(y^*\models C_T\land P(x,y^*)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: finite constraint migration is naturally formalized as target satisfaction plus an explicit preservation predicate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-domain semantic migration with an explicit preservation relation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a legacy solution \(x\models C_L\), construct target variables from \(\mu(x)\), leave unmapped target variables free, and solve \[C_T(y)\land P(x,y).\] If this formula is satisfiable, return any satisfying assignment \(y^*\); otherwise return migration failure. The predicate \(P\) must explicitly encode every legacy decision required to survive migration, including mapped values and any designated invariant relations. Thus success is not merely satisfiability of the target model: it requires both target validity and semantic preservation. The procedure terminates because the target domains are finite and its constraint solver is assumed complete.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Translate a valid legacy assignment, complete its unmapped decisions, and return a target-valid configuration satisfying every explicitly declared preservation requirement.
knowledge_statements.title: Legacy Constraint Migration

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the migration leaf, but no inspectable source supports this particular preservation-based procedure. The partial correspondence does not itself specify how target variables are constructed, and the required relationship between the construction from mu and the independently declared predicate P remains source-dependent.

children.title: Minimal-Change Upgrade
children.top_down_role: Upgrades organized by limited departure from an installed configuration.

assumptions_latex: The configuration domain \(D=\prod_{i=1}^n D_i\) is finite.
The upgraded constraints \(C'\) are decidable.
Each change cost \(w_i\) is nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every optimizer \(y^*\) satisfies \(C'(y^*)\) and has minimum weighted change from \(x^0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted Hamming-distance formulation for finite configuration upgrades.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an existing configuration \(x^0\in D\), upgraded feasibility predicate \(C':D\to\{0,1\}\), and weights \(w_i\ge 0\), define the weighted change distance by \[d_w(y,x^0)=\sum_{i=1}^n w_i\mathbf{1}[y_i\ne x_i^0].\] A minimal-change upgrade is any configuration \[y^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in D}\{d_w(y,x^0):C'(y)=1\}.\] If the feasible set is empty, no upgrade exists. Zero-weight coordinates may change without affecting optimality; uniqueness therefore requires either a unique minimizer or an explicit tie-breaking rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A minimal-change upgrade is an upgraded valid configuration minimizing the weighted number of component values changed from the existing configuration.
knowledge_statements.title: Minimal-Change Upgrade

children.title: Configuration Validity Certificate System
children.top_down_role: Checking candidate products against structural, compatibility, and requirement constraints.

children.title: Structural Validation
children.top_down_role: Checks of candidate structure against configuration rules.

assumptions_latex: The configuration is represented by finitely many selected component instances.
The containment relation is required to form a rooted tree or rooted forest.
Every component type has declared parent and child-cardinality rules.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A passing certificate establishes that the configuration has the required containment shape and satisfies every local structural cardinality.

notation.meaning: Selected component instances and containment edges.
Allowed parent types for type t.
Permitted number of children of type u under type t.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: structural validity can be checked by graph shape, typing, and local cardinality predicates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate for tree-structured component containment and local multiplicities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A structural-validity certificate for a selected containment graph \((V,E)\) consists of a designated root set, a parent pointer for every nonroot vertex, component-type labels, and child counts. Verification accepts exactly when \((V,E)\) is acyclic, every nonroot vertex has one parent, every edge \((p,v)\in E\) satisfies \(\operatorname{type}(p)\in A_{\operatorname{type}(v)}\), and every vertex \(p\) of type \(t\) has between \(\ell_{tu}\) and \(u_{tu}\) children of each relevant type \(u\). These checks certify structural validity independently of nonstructural compatibility and user requirements.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Parent pointers, types, and child counts certify that selected components form the required hierarchy and obey every declared local multiplicity rule.
knowledge_statements.title: Structural Validation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Certificate is appropriate within the Configuration Validity Certificate System, and the stated checks are internally coherent for rooted-tree or rooted-forest containment. No inspectable source supports this particular certificate format or its claimed structural scope.

children.title: Compatibility Conformance
children.top_down_role: Checks of selected elements against coexistence restrictions.

assumptions_latex: The selected configuration is \(S\subseteq U\) for a finite component universe \(U\).
Compatibility is specified by required pairs \(R\) and forbidden pairs \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The configuration conforms exactly when all required companions are selected and no forbidden pair is jointly selected.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: requires and excludes relations have a direct finite-set conformance predicate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pairwise requires-and-excludes compatibility semantics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Compatibility conformance holds for \(S\) precisely when \[\bigl(\forall(a,b)\in R,\ a\in S\Rightarrow b\in S\bigr)\ \land\ \bigl(\forall\{a,b\}\in F,\ \neg(a\in S\land b\in S)\bigr).\] Equivalently, every selected component brings all of its required companions into the configuration, while no declared incompatible pair is selected together. For compatibility rules of arity greater than two, the same definition extends by conjoining their declared predicates; pairwise conformance alone does not certify those higher-arity rules.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A configuration conforms when every selected component has its required companions and no forbidden pair is selected together.
knowledge_statements.title: Compatibility Conformance

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Condition is the correct role for pairwise compatibility conformance, and the requires/excludes predicate is precise. The record has no citation supporting these semantics or the proposed extension to higher-arity compatibility rules.

children.title: Requirement Satisfaction Checks
children.top_down_role: Checks of candidate products against stated requirements.

assumptions_latex: The configuration domain \(D\) and requirement index set \(J\) are finite.
Each requirement is represented by a decidable predicate \(r_j:D\to\{0,1\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Acceptance certifies \(x\models\bigwedge_{j\in J}r_j\); rejection identifies at least one violated requirement.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct evaluation of finite, decidable configuration requirements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a candidate configuration \(x\in D\), evaluate every requirement predicate and form \[V(x)=\{j\in J:r_j(x)=0\}.\] The requirement-satisfaction check accepts if and only if \(V(x)=\varnothing\). An acceptance certificate is the vector \((r_j(x))_{j\in J}=\mathbf{1}\), whose entries can be recomputed independently. On rejection, the set \(V(x)\), together with the values used to evaluate its predicates, identifies the violated requirements. This check certifies only the declared predicates; omitted or incorrectly encoded requirements remain outside its guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Evaluate every declared requirement on the candidate; accept only when all hold, otherwise return the indices of violated requirements.
knowledge_statements.title: Requirement Satisfaction Checks

children.title: Invalid-Product Certificates
children.top_down_role: Evidence identifying why a candidate configuration is unacceptable.

assumptions_latex: The validity model is a finite conjunction \(C=\bigwedge_{i\in I}c_i\).
The candidate assignment \(x\) gives every variable needed to evaluate each \(c_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any returned pair \((K,x|_{\operatorname{vars}(K)})\) with \(K\ne\varnothing\) certifies \(x\not\models C\).

notation.meaning: Indices of constraints falsified by x.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Locally checkable invalidity witness for a fully assigned product.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a fully assigned product \(x\), define \[K=\{i\in I:c_i(x)=0\}.\] An invalid-product certificate is a nonempty set \(K\), the restriction of \(x\) to variables occurring in \((c_i)_{i\in K}\), and enough evaluation data to recompute each falsified predicate. A verifier accepts the certificate exactly when \(K\ne\varnothing\) and \(c_i(x)=0\) for every \(i\in K\). Since \(C\) is conjunctive, one verified member of \(K\) already proves \(x\not\models C\); additional members provide diagnostic information rather than stronger logical invalidity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A falsified declared constraint, accompanied by the relevant assigned values, is a directly checkable certificate that the product is invalid.
knowledge_statements.title: Invalid-Product Certificates

children.title: Configuration-Space Exploration Family
children.top_down_role: Generation and quantitative exploration of valid variants.

children.title: Valid Configuration Enumeration
children.top_down_role: Systematic generation of valid configuration variants.

assumptions_latex: The variables \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\) have finite ordered domains.
Constraint propagation is sound.
The search explores every surviving value branch.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output list contains every solution of \(C\) exactly once and contains no invalid assignment.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complete depth-first enumeration over finite-domain configurations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(L=\varnothing\) and propagate \(C\). If propagation detects inconsistency, return from the current search branch. If all variables are assigned, append the assignment to \(L\). Otherwise choose an unassigned variable \(x_i\), and, in its fixed domain order, recursively impose \(x_i=a\) for every surviving value \(a\), propagating after each choice. Stop when all branches have been exhausted and output \(L\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exhaustively branch over finite variable domains, prune only proven inconsistencies, and output each complete constraint-satisfying configuration exactly once.
knowledge_statements.title: Valid Configuration Enumeration

children.title: Exact Variant Counting
children.top_down_role: Exact cardinality analysis of valid configuration spaces.

assumptions_latex: The configuration domain \(D=\prod_{i=1}^n D_i\) is finite.
Validity is represented by a decidable predicate \(C:D\to\{0,1\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The exact variant count equals both \(|\{x\in D:C(x)=1\}|\) and the displayed indicator sum.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite model-counting representation of product-line variability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The exact number of valid variants is \[N_C=|\{x\in D:C(x)=1\}|=\sum_{x\in D}\mathbf{1}[C(x)=1].\] For Boolean configuration variables, this is the model count of the validity formula. The value counts distinct complete assignments under the chosen variable representation; if multiple assignments encode the same physical product, a canonical encoding or an explicit equivalence quotient is required before the count can be interpreted as the number of distinct products.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact variant counting is finite model counting: sum one indicator for every complete assignment satisfying the configuration constraints.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Variant Counting

children.title: Representative Configuration Sampling
children.top_down_role: Selection of representative valid configurations.

assumptions_latex: The valid configuration set \(V\) is finite and nonempty.
A probability mass function \(\pi:V\to[0,1]\) with \(\sum_{x\in V}\pi(x)=1\) is specified.
A complete sampler for \(\pi\) is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output sample has joint law \(\pi^{\otimes m}\), so its empirical frequencies estimate expectations under the declared target distribution.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distribution-relative representative sampling, not an intrinsic notion.

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(m\ge 1\), independently draw \(X_1,
\ldots,X_m\) from \(\pi\) and output the ordered sample \((X_1,
\ldots,X_m)\). Every draw lies in \(V\), and for each \((x_1,
\ldots,x_m)\in V^m\), \[\Pr[X_1=x_1,
\ldots,X_m=x_m]=\prod_{k=1}^m\pi(x_k).\] Representativeness is therefore relative to \(\pi\): uniform sampling represents variants equally, while a usage-weighted \(\pi\) represents operational prevalence. Without a declared target distribution, the term representative has no mathematically determined meaning.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Draw valid configurations from an explicit target distribution; representativeness means matching that distribution, not merely producing diverse valid products.
knowledge_statements.title: Representative Configuration Sampling

source_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

children.title: Coverage-Oriented Sampling
children.top_down_role: Sampling organized to cover configuration-space characteristics.

assumptions_latex: The valid configuration set \(V\) and obligation set \(T\) are finite.
Each configuration \(x\in V\) covers a known subset \(A(x)\subseteq T\).
The sample budget is \(k\ge 0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm returns at most \(k\) valid configurations and stops earlier only when no remaining configuration adds coverage.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: greedy maximum-marginal-coverage selection is a standard finite coverage heuristic
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Greedy budgeted sampling for declared finite coverage obligations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(S=\varnothing\) and \(U=\varnothing\). While \(|S|<k\), choose \[x^*\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in V\setminus S}|A(x)\setminus U|,\] using a fixed tie-breaking order. If \(A(x^*)\setminus U=\varnothing\), stop; otherwise set \(S\leftarrow S\cup\{x^*\}\) and \(U\leftarrow U\cup A(x^*)\). Output \(S\), its covered set \(U\), and uncovered obligations \(T\setminus U\). Every selected item is valid by membership in \(V\), and each iteration maximizes immediate additional coverage among remaining configurations; no global optimality is asserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly select the valid configuration covering the most currently uncovered obligations, stopping at the budget or when no coverage can improve.
knowledge_statements.title: Coverage-Oriented Sampling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is the correct role, and the statement accurately limits the greedy method to maximum immediate marginal coverage without asserting global optimality. No inspectable source supports the configuration-sampling application or this precise greedy procedure.

children.title: Configuration Knowledge Representations
children.top_down_role: Alternative encodings of product structure, choices, compatibility, attributes, and construction knowledge.

children.title: Feature Models
children.top_down_role: Hierarchical variability models with groups, cross-tree relations, cardinalities, attributes, and context.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Automated Analysis of Feature Models 20 Years Later
top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Feature-model representations and automated analyses
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Automated Analysis of Feature Models 20 Years Later

children.title: Basic Feature Models
children.top_down_role: Tree-organized feature choices and cross-tree constraints.

assumptions_latex: The feature set \(F\) is finite and organized as a rooted tree.
Each nonroot feature has one parent and a relation type.
Cross-tree constraints form a finite propositional formula \(\Phi\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A product is valid exactly when its Boolean selection satisfies the root, tree-relation, and cross-tree formulas.

notation.meaning: Boolean selection variable for feature f.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Boolean feature models use rooted tree relations conjoined with propositional cross-tree constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boolean rooted-tree feature model with propositional cross-tree constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A basic feature model consists of a finite rooted feature tree and a propositional cross-tree formula \(\Phi\). A product is a vector \(z\in\{0,1\}^{F}\) satisfying the root equation \(z_r=1\). For every child \(c\) with parent \(p\), selection implies \(z_c\le z_p\); a mandatory child additionally satisfies \(z_c=z_p\), while an optional child has no converse implication. An exclusive-or group \(G\) under \(p\) satisfies \(\sum_{g\in G}z_g=z_p\), and an inclusive-or group satisfies \(z_p\le\sum_{g\in G}z_g\le |G|z_p\). Validity also requires \(\Phi(z)=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A basic feature model combines rooted mandatory, optional, and grouped feature choices with propositional cross-tree constraints; valid products satisfy all of them.
knowledge_statements.title: Basic Feature Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Definition is the correct role, and the Boolean formulas consistently encode rooted mandatory, optional, XOR, OR, and cross-tree constraints. The record nevertheless lacks the required authoritative feature-model citation and locator.

children.title: Quantitative Feature Model Family
children.top_down_role: Feature models extended with multiplicities, attributes, and quantitative relations.

children.title: Cardinality-Based Feature Models
children.top_down_role: Feature models supporting multiplicities for features or groups.

assumptions_latex: The feature tree and every child group are finite.
Each feature has a nonnegative integer multiplicity variable.
Every group has declared lower and upper cardinalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An assignment is valid exactly when all parent-activation, feature-multiplicity, group-cardinality, and cross-tree constraints hold.

notation.meaning: Allowed multiplicity interval for feature f.
Children in a cardinality group under parent p.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: cardinality-based feature models extend Boolean selections with bounded multiplicities and bounded group selections
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Integer multiplicities and group cardinalities extending a rooted feature model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A cardinality-based feature model assigns each feature \(f\) an integer multiplicity \(m_f\ge 0\) and an allowed interval \([\ell_f,u_f]\). For a nonroot feature \(f\) with parent \(p\), validity requires \[m_p=0\Rightarrow m_f=0,\qquad m_p>0\Rightarrow \ell_f\le m_f\le u_f.\] For a child group \(G_p\) with group bounds \([L_p,U_p]\), define activation indicators \(z_g=\mathbf{1}[m_g>0]\) and require \[m_p>0\Rightarrow L_p\le\sum_{g\in G_p}z_g\le U_p.\] Root multiplicity, any per-parent scaling convention, and all quantitative cross-tree constraints must also be declared explicitly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cardinality-based feature models replace Boolean presence with bounded feature multiplicities and constrain how many children in each group may be active.
knowledge_statements.title: Cardinality-Based Feature Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Definition fits the leaf, but cardinality-based feature-model semantics depend on whether multiplicities are global or per parent instance. The statement leaves root multiplicity and per-parent scaling as conventions to be declared, so it does not yet determine one complete validity semantics. An authoritative source is required to select and state the intended variant.

children.title: Attributed Feature Models
children.top_down_role: Feature models enriched with quantitative or symbolic attributes.

assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a finite feature set with Boolean selection variables \(x_f\in\{0,1\}\).
Each attribute \(a\in A_f\) has domain \(D_a\), value variable \(v_a\), and a designated inactive value \(\bot_a\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Conf}(M)=\{(x,v):\Phi_F(x)\land\Phi_A(x,v)\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-domain constraint semantics for Boolean features carrying typed quantitative attributes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An attributed feature model is a tuple \(M=(F,A,D,\Phi_F,\Phi_A)\), where \(A=\bigcup_{f\in F}A_f\), \(D=(D_a)_{a\in A}\), \(\Phi_F\) constrains feature selections, and \(\Phi_A\) constrains selections and attribute values. A configuration is \((x,v)\) satisfying \(\Phi_F(x)\land\Phi_A(x,v)\), with \(v_a\in D_a\cup\{\bot_a\}\) and \(x_f=0\Rightarrow v_a=\bot_a\) for every \(a\in A_f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An attributed feature model combines Boolean feature choices with typed attribute values, structural constraints, quantitative constraints, and explicit inactive values for attributes of unselected features.
knowledge_statements.title: Attributed Feature Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No citation supports this particular tuple semantics, the designated inactive values, or the biconditional-style activation convention. These choices vary among attributed feature-model formalisms, so the mathematical version cannot be validated from the supplied general optimization sources.

children.title: Multiplicity–Attribute Coupling
children.top_down_role: Interactions between feature multiplicities and attribute restrictions.

assumptions_latex: \(F\) is finite, and each feature multiplicity variable satisfies \(m_f\in\{0,dots,U_f\}\).
Every attribute associated with \(f\) has a finite or numeric domain containing an inactive value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m_f=0\) deactivates the attributes of \(f\), while \(m_f>0\) permits only attribute tuples admitted for that multiplicity.

notation.meaning: Number of instantiated copies of feature f
Attribute tuple attached to feature f
Admissible attribute tuples at multiplicity k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relational coupling between feature copy counts and aggregate or per-feature attribute values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A multiplicity–attribute coupling for feature \(f\) is a family \((R_{f,k})_{k=0}^{U_f}\) of admissibility relations. Feasibility requires \(v_f\in R_{f,m_f}\). The inactive relation is \(R_{f,0}=\{\bot_f\}\); hence \(m_f=0\Leftrightarrow v_f=\bot_f\). For additive attributes with per-copy value \(q_f\), a standard coupling additionally imposes \(v_f=m_fq_f\), with any stated bounds on \(q_f\) enforced whenever \(m_f>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiplicity–attribute coupling makes admissible attribute values depend on the number of feature copies, deactivating attributes at zero copies and optionally aggregating per-copy quantities.
knowledge_statements.title: Multiplicity–Attribute Coupling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports the proposed family-of-relations semantics or the claim that the additive equation is standard. The relationship between aggregate and per-copy attributes is formalism-dependent. In addition, the assumption uses the malformed domain notation \(\{0,dots,U_f\}\), which should be corrected after the intended semantics are sourced.

children.title: Quantitative Cross-Tree Relations
children.top_down_role: Cross-tree restrictions involving feature attributes or multiplicities.

assumptions_latex: \(x\in\{0,1\}^{F}\) is a feature-selection vector.
\(v\in D=\prod_{a\in A}D_a\) is an attribute vector over specified finite or numeric domains.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x,v)\) satisfies the relation exactly when \(g(x,v)\bowtie b\).

notation.meaning: Quantitative expression spanning distinct feature-tree regions

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraint semantics for quantitative dependencies between features outside one parent–child group.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A quantitative cross-tree relation is a constraint \(g(x,v)\bowtie b\) whose support contains variables associated with at least two features that do not belong to one immediate feature group. The expression \(g\) may be Boolean-guarded; for example, \(x_p=1\Rightarrow \sum_{a\in S}c_av_a\leq b\). A configuration is valid only if every such relation evaluates true together with the underlying feature-tree and attribute-domain constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quantitative cross-tree relation constrains selections or attributes from separate feature-tree regions, including guarded budgets, capacities, balances, and threshold dependencies.
knowledge_statements.title: Quantitative Cross-Tree Relations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record gives a plausible constraint pattern, but no feature-model source supports its definition of cross-tree scope or its unrestricted expression language. The criterion involving features outside one immediate group may not coincide with the established meaning of a quantitative cross-tree relation.

children.title: Cross-Context Product-Line Feature Model Family
children.top_down_role: Variability models spanning contexts or interacting product lines.

children.title: Contextual Feature Models
children.top_down_role: Feature models whose valid choices depend on external context.

assumptions_latex: \(F\) and the context-variable set \(C\) are finite.
\(x\in\{0,1\}^{F}\), and each context variable \(c\in C\) ranges over a specified domain \(D_c\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Conf}(M,\gamma)=\{x:\Phi_F(x)\land\Phi_C(x,\gamma)\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Static finite-domain semantics in which an external context valuation restricts product configurations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A contextual feature model is a tuple \(M=(F,C,D,\Phi_F,\Phi_C)\). Here \(\Phi_F(x)\) is the context-independent feature theory and \(\Phi_C(x,gamma)\) contains context-sensitive constraints. For a fixed context valuation \(\gamma\), a product configuration is any \(x\in\{0,1\}^{F}\) satisfying \(\Phi_F(x)\land\Phi_C(x,gamma)\). Context variables are parameters of configuration validity, not selected product features, unless explicitly identified as such.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A contextual feature model parameterizes valid feature selections by an external context valuation while retaining a context-independent core feature theory.
knowledge_statements.title: Contextual Feature Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No citation establishes this static parameterized semantics for contextual feature models. Context formalisms differ on context-feature status, adaptation, and validity semantics. The statement also writes \(\Phi_C(x,gamma)\) where the introduced valuation is \(\gamma\).

children.title: Multi-Product-Line Feature Models
children.top_down_role: Variability representations spanning multiple product lines.

assumptions_latex: There are finitely many product lines indexed by \(L=\{1,dots,m\}\).
Each line \(i\) has finite feature set \(F_i\) and local constraint theory \(\Phi_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Conf}(M)=\{x:\bigwedge_{i\in L}\Phi_i(x|_{F_i})\land\Psi(x)\}\).

notation.meaning: Feature-selection vector on the union of line features

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint constraint semantics for several product lines with local theories and explicit inter-line dependencies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A multi-product-line feature model is a tuple \(M=((F_i,Phi_i)_{i\in L},Psi)\), where each \(\Phi_i\) constrains the restriction \(x|_{F_i}\), and \(\Psi\) constrains variables from two or more lines. Shared features are represented by identical variables only when common identity is declared; otherwise line-qualified variables are distinct. A joint configuration \(x\in\{0,1\}^{\cup_iF_i}\) is valid precisely when every local theory and \(\Psi\) are satisfied.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multi-product-line feature model combines local feature theories with explicit cross-line constraints and a declared policy for identifying shared features.
knowledge_statements.title: Multi-Product-Line Feature Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No product-line source supports the proposed joint tuple, cross-line theory, or shared-feature identity policy. The statement also uses \(Phi_i\) and \(Psi\) as ordinary letter products instead of the introduced symbols \(\Phi_i\) and \(\Psi\), and the assumption contains malformed \(\{1,dots,m\}\) notation.

children.title: Cross-Line Variability
children.top_down_role: Variability relationships connecting separate product lines.

assumptions_latex: \(L\) is a finite set of product lines with line-qualified Boolean feature variables.
Each local theory \(\Phi_i\) is defined on the variables of line \(i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A joint selection is cross-line valid exactly when it satisfies \(\bigwedge_{i\in L}\Phi_i\land\Psi\).

notation.meaning: Selection of feature f in product line i
Local feature theory for line i

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraint-level characterization of variability dependencies whose scopes cross product-line boundaries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Cross-line variability is represented by a theory \(\Psi\) containing constraints whose support intersects the variable sets of at least two distinct lines. Typical predicates include cross-line implication \(x_{i,f}\leq x_{j,g}\), exclusion \(x_{i,f}+x_{j,g}\leq1\), and synchronization \(x_{i,f}=x_{j,g}\). These constraints supplement rather than replace local theories: feasibility requires \(\bigwedge_{i\in L}\Phi_i(x_i)\land\Psi((x_i)_{i\in L})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cross-line variability consists of constraints spanning multiple product lines, such as implication, exclusion, or synchronized selection, imposed alongside every line's local theory.
knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Line Variability

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The examples are mathematically coherent for Boolean line-qualified variables, but no domain-specific citation establishes that this constraint-support definition is the intended meaning of cross-line variability. The supplied optimization sources do not support the product-line terminology or taxonomy.

children.title: Context-Dependent Feature Availability
children.top_down_role: Feature availability conditioned by deployment or usage context.

assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a finite feature set and \(\Gamma\) is the set of admissible context valuations.
Feature selections are represented by \(x_f\in\{0,1\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_f\leq a_f(gamma)\) for every \(f\in F\) characterizes context-dependent availability.

notation.meaning: Availability indicator for feature f in context gamma

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise availability semantics for a fixed context; temporal context transitions are excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each feature \(f\), let \(a_f:\Gamma\to\{0,1\}\) be its availability predicate. Under context \(\gamma\in\Gamma\), admissibility requires \(x_f\leq a_f(gamma)\): an unavailable feature cannot be selected, while availability alone does not force selection. If \(f\) is mandatory under selected parent \(p\), the combined condition is \(x_f=x_p a_f(gamma)\); consequently, contexts making a required feature unavailable may render the model infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feature may be selected only when its context predicate is true; availability permits selection but does not generally require it.
knowledge_statements.title: Context-Dependent Feature Availability

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The inequality \(x_f\leq a_f(\gamma)\) is a plausible availability condition, but no source supports it as the selected formalism. The stronger mandatory-child equation depends on feature-tree semantics that are not stated or cited. The statement repeatedly uses \(a_f(gamma)\) instead of the introduced \(a_f(\gamma)\).

children.title: Component Interface Assembly Models
children.top_down_role: Object-centered structures with parts, interfaces, cardinalities, and connections.

children.title: Component Models
children.top_down_role: Object-centered representations of configurable parts.

assumptions_latex: \(T\) is a finite set of component types and \(I\) a finite set of candidate component instances.
Every instance \(i\in I\) has a declared type \(\tau(i)\in T\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A component configuration is any \((y,theta)\) satisfying activation, typing, parameter-domain, and component constraints.

notation.meaning: Activation indicator for component instance i

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-instance constraint model for typed components, activation decisions, and local parameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A component model is a tuple \(M=(T,I,tau,D,Phi)\), where \(D_i\) is the parameter domain of candidate instance \(i\) and \(\Phi\) is a constraint theory. A component configuration assigns \(y_i\in\{0,1\}\) and \(\theta_i\in D_i\cup\{\bot_i\}\) such that \(y_i=0\Leftrightarrow\theta_i=\bot_i\), all type-specific constraints hold for active instances, and \(\Phi(y,theta)\) is true.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A component model represents typed candidate instances, activation choices, local parameter values, and constraints determining valid active assemblies.
knowledge_statements.title: Component Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No component-configuration source supports this finite candidate-instance tuple, inactive parameter value, or activation biconditional. The tuple uses \(tau\) and \(Phi\), while the assumptions and remainder introduce \(\tau\) and \(\Phi\). General mathematical-programming references are insufficient for this domain definition.

children.title: Port Interface Models
children.top_down_role: Representations of component interfaces and attachment points.

assumptions_latex: Each candidate component instance has a finite set of declared ports.
Every port has a direction, an interface type, and lower and upper connection bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An interface assignment is valid when every active port respects activation, direction, type compatibility, and its declared connection bounds.

notation.meaning: Set of ports belonging to component instance i

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Typed directed ports with activation and connection-degree requirements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A port interface model associates each port \(p\in P_i\) with direction \(d(p)\in\{\mathrm{provided},mathrm{required}\}\), type \(\sigma(p)\), and bounds \(0\leq\ell_p\leq u_p\). If \(z_p\) indicates port activation and \(y_i\) component activation, then \(z_p\leq y_i\). Connections incident to \(p\) must have compatible opposite endpoints, and an active port satisfies \(\ell_pz_p\leq\deg(p)\leq u_pz_p\).
