knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A port interface model assigns each component port a direction, type, activation state, compatibility rule, and permissible number of incident connections.
knowledge_statements.title: Port Interface Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No citation supports the chosen provided/required-port formalism, compatibility relation, activation semantics, or conditional degree bounds. The statement also contains malformed intended notation: \(mathrm{required}\) lacks the command prefix, and the notation entry uses \((ell_p,u_p)\) instead of \((\ell_p,u_p)\).

children.title: Connection Models
children.top_down_role: Representations of allowable links between configured objects.

assumptions_latex: \(P\) is a finite set of ports partitioned into provided and required ports.
\(K\subseteq P\times P\) contains only directionally and type-compatible endpoint pairs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A feasible connection set is \(E=\{(p,q)\in K:e_{pq}=1\}\) satisfying endpoint activation and all assembly constraints.

notation.meaning: Set of compatible candidate endpoint pairs
Indicator that ports p and q are connected

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary compatible-port connection model; higher-arity connectors require an explicit extension.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A connection model specifies binary variables \(e_{pq}\) for \((p,q)\in K\). Endpoint activation is enforced by \(e_{pq}\leq z_p\) and \(e_{pq}\leq z_q\). Pairs outside \(K\) are forbidden. The selected connections form \(E=\{(p,q)\in K:e_{pq}=1\}\), and feasibility additionally requires all declared port-degree, component-coexistence, and global assembly constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A connection model selects compatible pairs of active ports and combines endpoint activation with local degree and global assembly constraints.
knowledge_statements.title: Connection Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The binary edge-selection formulation is internally plausible, but no domain-specific source establishes it as a connection model or supports the asserted scope of the additional assembly constraints. Connector direction, multiplicity, and higher-arity semantics remain source-dependent.

children.title: Connection Cardinalities
children.top_down_role: Multiplicity restrictions governing component connections.

assumptions_latex: \(K\) is the finite set of candidate port connections with binary variables \(e_{pq}\).
Each port \(p\) has activation variable \(z_p\) and bounds \(0\leq\ell_p\leq u_p\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\ell_pz_p\leq\sum_{q:(p,q)\in K\text{ or }(q,p)\in K}e_{pq}\leq u_pz_p\) for every port \(p\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional lower and upper degree bounds for binary port connections.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(\deg_E(p)=\sum_{q:(p,q)\in K}e_{pq}+\sum_{q:(q,p)\in K}e_{qp}\). The connection-cardinality condition is \(\ell_pz_p\leq\deg_E(p)\leq u_pz_p\) for every \(p\). Thus an inactive port has degree zero, while an active port has between \(\ell_p\) and \(u_p\) selected incident connections. Exact-one connectivity is the special case \(\ell_p=u_p=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Connection cardinalities impose conditional lower and upper bounds on each port's selected degree, forcing zero connections when the port is inactive.
knowledge_statements.title: Connection Cardinalities

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No cited source supports these conditional connection-cardinality semantics. Moreover, the conclusion sums \(e_{pq}\) even when the candidate pair is \((q,p)\); it should use consistent oriented indexing, as the statement's second sum does. The exact-one special case also applies only to active ports under this formulation.

children.title: Topological Assembly Structure
children.top_down_role: Network structure induced by configured components and connections.

assumptions_latex: \(I\) is a finite set of candidate component instances with activation variables \(y_i\).
Selected compatible port connections induce component-level edges.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The topology of an assembly is the active induced graph \(G_y=(V_y,E_y)\), optionally restricted by explicit graph predicates.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Graph representation of the selected component assembly, independent of a particular connectivity encoding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given component activations and selected port connections, define \(V_y=\{i\in I:y_i=1\}\) and \(E_y=\{\{i,j\}:i,j\in V_y\text{ and some selected connection joins a port of }i\text{ to a port of }j\}\). The topological assembly structure is \(G_y=(V_y,E_y)\). Required properties such as connectedness, acyclicity, prescribed roots, bounded degree, or forbidden subgraphs are imposed as explicit predicates on \(G_y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The selected components and their realized connections induce an assembly graph on which connectivity, acyclicity, rooting, degree, or forbidden-pattern constraints can be imposed.
knowledge_statements.title: Topological Assembly Structure

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No component-assembly source supports this graph representation or the listed topology predicates. Defining \(E_y\) as a set of unordered component pairs collapses multiple realized port connections and discards direction, so a source is needed to determine whether a simple undirected graph, directed graph, or multigraph is intended.

children.title: Constraint-Based Configuration Models
children.top_down_role: Finite-domain, Boolean, arithmetic, and global-constraint models of configuration choices.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Based Configuration Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-domain constraint model for selecting and parameterizing components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A constraint-based configuration model is a tuple \(M=(X,D,C)\), where \(X=\{x_1,\ldots,x_n\}\) is a finite set of decision variables, \(D(x_i)\) is a finite domain for each variable, and \(C\) is a finite set of Boolean, arithmetic, or global constraints over \(X\). A configuration is an assignment \(a\in\prod_{i=1}^n D(x_i)\). It is valid precisely when \(c(a)=\mathsf{true}\) for every \(c\in C\). Boolean variables may encode component presence, while non-Boolean variables encode types, quantities, capacities, or interface parameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A configuration model assigns finite-domain variables representing choices and parameters; a configuration is valid exactly when it satisfies every Boolean, arithmetic, and global constraint.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and every \(D(x_i)\) are finite.
Every \(c\in C\) has a defined truth value on each complete assignment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Sol}(M)=\{a\in\prod_{i=1}^nD(x_i):\forall c\in C,\ c(a)=\mathsf{true}\}\).

notation.meaning: Variables, domain map, and constraint set.

review_flags: configuration-specific formulation should be checked against a dedicated configuration reference

children.title: Declarative Configuration Logic Family
children.top_down_role: Declarative logical and rule-based representations of configuration knowledge.

children.title: Logic-Based Configuration
children.top_down_role: Configuration knowledge expressed through logical constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Logic-Based Configuration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Model-theoretic configuration using formulas over component and attribute symbols.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A logic-based configuration model is a pair \(M=(\Sigma,T)\), where \(\Sigma\) is a finite signature containing symbols for component selections, types, relations, and attributes, and \(T\) is a finite theory over \(\Sigma\). A configuration is a finite \(\Sigma\)-structure \(I\) whose domain and symbol interpretations describe the selected components and their relationships. The configuration is valid exactly when \(I\models T\). If only some symbols are externally observable, the delivered configuration is the reduct \(I|_{\Sigma_o}\) to a designated output signature \(\Sigma_o\subseteq\Sigma\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A configuration is represented by a finite logical structure and is valid exactly when that structure is a model of the configuration theory.
assumptions_latex: \(\Sigma\) and \(T\) are finite.
Candidate configurations are finite \(\Sigma\)-structures.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Conf}(M)=\{I:I\text{ is a finite }\Sigma\text{-structure and }I\models T\}\).

notation.meaning: Structure I satisfies every formula of T.

review_flags: dedicated source for model-theoretic configuration semantics required

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The model-theoretic definition is plausible and fits the leaf, but no source fixes the intended logic, structure semantics, or output-reduct convention.

children.title: Rule-Based Configuration
children.top_down_role: Configuration knowledge expressed through declarative rules.

knowledge_statements.title: Rule-Based Configuration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Forward-chaining configuration over monotone production rules.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given initial facts \(F_0\), rules \(R=\{B_r\rightarrow H_r:r\in R\}\), and integrity constraints \(K\), initialize \(F:=F_0\). Repeatedly choose any rule satisfying \(B_r\subseteq F\) and set \(F:=F\cup H_r\); stop when no rule adds a fact. Reject if some \(k\in K\) is false in the closure \(F^*\); otherwise output the component and attribute facts in \(F^*\). When all rule heads are positive and the fact vocabulary is finite, this process terminates and its closure is independent of rule-firing order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Forward chaining repeatedly applies enabled positive rules. The resulting finite closure is accepted when it satisfies every integrity constraint.
assumptions_latex: The ground fact vocabulary is finite.
Every rule has a positive head and adds facts without retracting them.
Integrity constraints are evaluated after closure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F^*=\operatorname{lfp}(F\mapsto F\cup\bigcup_{r:B_r\subseteq F}H_r)\), and the output is valid iff \(F^*\models K\).

notation.meaning: Initial facts and their rule closure.

review_flags: source for production-rule configuration and confluence conditions required

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits rule-based configuration, but the production-rule semantics and rule-order independence claim require an authoritative source. The self-indexed notation for R should also be clarified when sourced.

children.title: Answer-Set Configuration
children.top_down_role: Configuration knowledge represented for answer-set semantics.

knowledge_statements.title: Answer-Set Configuration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stable-model encoding of finite configuration choices and requirements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) be a finite ground normal logic program whose atoms encode component selections, attribute values, and assembly relations. An interpretation \(A\) represents an admissible configuration exactly when \(A\) is a stable model of \(P\): form the Gelfond--Lifschitz reduct \(P^A\) by deleting every rule having a negative body atom in \(A\), then deleting remaining negative literals; require \(A\) to be the least model of the positive program \(P^A\). The reported configuration is the projection \(A\cap O\) onto designated output atoms \(O\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Answer-set configuration represents valid products as stable models of a finite program, projected onto atoms describing delivered components and attributes.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is a finite ground normal logic program.
\(O\) is a designated set of output atoms.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Conf}(P,O)=\{A\cap O:A=\operatorname{LM}(P^A)\}\).

notation.meaning: Gelfond--Lifschitz reduct of P relative to A.
Least model of a positive program.

review_flags: configuration projection convention requires domain-specific support

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation correctly resembles stable-model semantics for finite ground normal programs, but neither that semantics nor the configuration projection convention is cited.

children.title: Hybrid Declarative Encodings
children.top_down_role: Configuration encodings combining multiple declarative formalisms.

knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Declarative Encodings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint logical and finite-domain encoding linked by shared variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A hybrid declarative configuration encoding is a tuple \(H=(P,X,D,C,L)\), where \(P\) is a finite ground logic program, \((X,D,C)\) is a finite-domain constraint model, and \(L\) is a set of linking conditions between program atoms and variable predicates. A solution is a pair \((A,a)\) such that \(A\) is a stable model of \(P\), \(a\in\prod_{x\in X}D(x)\) satisfies every constraint in \(C\), and every equivalence or implication in \(L\) holds under \((A,a)\). Its configuration is the prescribed projection of \((A,a)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hybrid encoding combines a stable model with a finite-domain assignment and requires both subsystems plus all linking conditions to hold.
assumptions_latex: \(P\), \(X\), every \(D(x)\), \(C\), and \(L\) are finite.
Stable-model and constraint satisfaction semantics are fixed independently.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Sol}(H)=\{(A,a):A\in\operatorname{SM}(P),\ a\models C,\ (A,a)\models L\}\).
review_flags: source fixing the intended linking semantics required

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record fits the hybrid-encoding leaf, but different hybrid formalisms assign materially different meanings to linking conditions and joint solutions; a source must fix the intended semantics.

children.title: Generative Configuration Grammar Family
children.top_down_role: Configuration models constructing valid assemblies through generative structures.

children.title: Generative Configuration Models
children.top_down_role: Models that characterize products through constructive generation.

knowledge_statements.title: Generative Configuration Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Configurations generated by finite sequences of admissible construction operations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A generative configuration model is a tuple \(G=(S,s_0,\mathcal{O},F)\), where \(S\) is a set of partial assemblies, \(s_0\in S\) is an initial assembly, each operation \(o\in\mathcal{O}\) is a partial map \(o:S\rightharpoonup S\), and \(F\subseteq S\) is the set of accepting assemblies. A configuration \(s\) is generated when there exist \(k\geq 0\) and operations \(o_1,\ldots,o_k\) such that every application is defined, \(s=o_k(\cdots o_1(s_0)\cdots)\), and \(s\in F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A generative model defines valid configurations as accepting assemblies reachable from an initial assembly through admissible construction operations.
assumptions_latex: Every operation has a specified applicability domain and state transformation.
Acceptance membership in \(F\) is defined for reachable assemblies.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Conf}(G)=F\cap\operatorname{Reach}_{\mathcal O}(s_0)\).

notation.meaning: Assembly state space and initial assembly.

review_flags: dedicated source for generative configuration semantics required

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The transition-system-style definition is plausible, but no configuration source supports this chosen abstraction. The k=0 case also needs an explicit empty-composition convention.

children.title: Grammar-Based Configuration Models
children.top_down_role: Configuration structures represented through formal grammars.

knowledge_statements.title: Grammar-Based Configuration Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Typed assemblies defined as terminal objects derivable from a grammar.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A grammar-based configuration model is a tuple \(G=(N,T,P,S,A)\), where \(N\) and \(T\) are finite sets of nonterminal and terminal component symbols, \(P\) is a finite set of structure-rewriting productions, \(S\in N\) is the start symbol, and \(A\) is an acceptance predicate on terminal assemblies. A configuration is a terminal assembly \(w\) for which \(S\Rightarrow_P^* w\) and \(A(w)=\mathsf{true}\). Productions may simultaneously introduce components and typed attachment relations, so derivability concerns assembly structure rather than only symbol strings.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A grammar-based model accepts terminal assemblies derivable from a start symbol and satisfying an explicit acceptance predicate.
assumptions_latex: \(N\), \(T\), and \(P\) are finite.
The rewrite relation preserves well-formed typed attachments.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Conf}(G)=\{w:S\Rightarrow_P^*w,\ w\text{ is terminal},\ A(w)=\mathsf{true}\}\).
review_flags: grammar formalism for structured assemblies must be fixed by a source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits grammar-based configuration, but structure-rewriting productions, terminal assemblies, typed attachments, and the acceptance predicate depend on a grammar formalism that no source identifies.

children.title: Derivation-Controlled Assemblies
children.top_down_role: Assemblies constrained by admissible derivation structures.

knowledge_statements.title: Derivation-Controlled Assemblies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Assembly derivations restricted by guards and a control language.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G\) have productions \(P\), let each production \(p\) have a guard \(g_p\) on the current partial assembly, and let \(L\subseteq P^*\) be a control language. A terminal assembly \(w\) is derivation-controlled admissible when there exist states \(s_0,\ldots,s_k=w\) and productions \(p_1\cdots p_k\in L\) such that, for every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,k\}\), the guard \(g_{p_i}(s_{i-1})\) is true and \(s_{i-1}\Rightarrow_{p_i}s_i\). Thus admissibility depends on both the final assembly and the permitted derivation history.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An assembly is admissible when a control language permits its production sequence and every production guard holds when that production is applied.
assumptions_latex: Each production guard is defined on every state where its production may be considered.
\(L\subseteq P^*\) specifies permitted production sequences.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(w\in\operatorname{Adm}(G,L)\iff\exists p_1\cdots p_k\in L\ \exists s_0\Rightarrow_{p_1}\cdots\Rightarrow_{p_k}w\ \forall i,\ g_{p_i}(s_{i-1})\).

notation.meaning: Partial assembly after i production steps.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition matches the leaf, but its guarded-production and control-language semantics require a controlled-grammar or graph-transformation source. The initial state must also be tied explicitly to G.

children.title: Generative Validity Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits separating generated structures from valid configurations.

knowledge_statements.title: Generative Validity Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Derivability alone does not ensure semantic configuration validity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G\) be a generative model and let \(V\) be the independently specified semantic validity predicate for completed assemblies. Generation is sound exactly when \(\operatorname{Conf}(G)\subseteq\{s:V(s)\}\), and complete exactly when \(\{s:V(s)\}\subseteq\operatorname{Conf}(G)\). If either inclusion fails, generation and semantic validity diverge: a generated \(s\) with \(\neg V(s)\) witnesses unsoundness, while a valid \(s\) not generated by \(G\) witnesses incompleteness. Consequently, restricting productions can restore soundness while destroying completeness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A generator exactly captures validity only when it generates every semantically valid assembly and no invalid assembly; either failed inclusion gives a concrete witness.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) is defined independently of derivability.
Generated and semantically valid objects share the same assembly universe.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Conf}(G)=\{s:V(s)\}\iff G\text{ is sound and complete for }V\).
review_flags: source connecting generative configuration with soundness and completeness required

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The two inclusions and witness descriptions are mathematically coherent and the failure-boundary kind is appropriate, but no source supports applying this soundness/completeness framing to generative configuration models.

children.title: Guided Selection Representation Pair
children.top_down_role: Tabular and decision-oriented structures supporting guided selection.

children.title: Variant Tables
children.top_down_role: Tabular representations of alternatives and admissible combinations.

knowledge_statements.title: Variant Tables
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extensional tabular representation of permitted combinations of option values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For finite attributes \(X=\{x_1,\ldots,x_n\}\) with domains \(D_i\), a variant table is a finite relation \(T\subseteq D_1\times\cdots\times D_n\). Each row \(t=(t_1,\ldots,t_n)\in T\) represents one permitted complete variant. For a partial customer selection \(q:J\to\bigcup_iD_i\), where \(J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) and \(q(i)\in D_i\), the compatible variants are precisely the rows agreeing with every specified value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A variant table lists permitted complete option combinations; filtering by a partial selection retains exactly the rows agreeing with all supplied values.
assumptions_latex: The attribute set and all domains are finite.
Every table row assigns exactly one value to every attribute.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_q=\{t\in T:\forall i\in J,\ t_i=q(i)\}\).
review_flags: authoritative source for variant-table configuration semantics required

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-relation representation and filtering formula are precise and fit the leaf, but an authoritative source for variant-table configuration semantics is absent.

children.title: Decision Models
children.top_down_role: Decision-oriented representations of configurable choices.

knowledge_statements.title: Decision Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite decision variables, feasibility conditions, and optional preference ordering.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A configuration decision model is a tuple \(M=(X,D,C,\preceq)\), where \(X\) is a finite set of decision variables, \(D(x)\) is the domain of variable \(x\), \(C\) is a set of feasibility conditions, and \(\preceq\) is an optional preorder on feasible assignments. A feasible decision is an assignment \(a\in\prod_{x\in X}D(x)\) satisfying every condition in \(C\). If preferences are present, an accepted decision may be required to be nondominated: no feasible \(b\) satisfies \(a\prec b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A decision model specifies configuration variables, their domains, feasibility conditions, and optionally preferences used to select nondominated feasible assignments.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and every \(D(x)\) are finite.
\(\preceq\), when present, is a preorder on feasible assignments.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Feas}(M)=\{a\in\prod_{x\in X}D(x):a\models C\}\).

notation.meaning: Decision variables, domains, and feasibility conditions.

source_refs.locator: 2.3 Decision support and expert systems p. 16

review_flags: configuration-specific decision-model formulation should be checked

source_witnesses.locator: 2.3 Decision support and expert systems p. 16

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited decision-support section is too general to establish this configuration-specific tuple and nondominance convention. The orientation of the preorder and the induced strict relation must be defined before the optimality claim is reliable.

children.title: Table-to-Decision Mappings
children.top_down_role: Correspondences between tabular alternatives and decision structures.

knowledge_statements.title: Table-to-Decision Mappings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extensional variant tables translated into equivalent finite-domain feasibility constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\subseteq D_1\times\cdots\times D_n\) be a variant table. Introduce decision variables \(x_i\in D_i\) and, for each row \(r\in T\), a Boolean selector \(y_r\). The table is represented exactly by the constraints \(\sum_{r\in T}y_r=1\) and \(y_r=1\Rightarrow x_i=r_i\) for every \(r\in T\) and every \(i\). Projection onto \((x_1,\ldots,x_n)\) yields precisely \(T\); hence table filtering and feasibility under fixed customer selections return the same complete variants.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One-hot row selectors convert a variant table into a decision model whose feasible assignments project exactly to the listed rows.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) and every \(D_i\) are finite.
Each selector satisfies \(y_r\in\{0,1\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_{x}\{(x,y):\sum_{r\in T}y_r=1,\ y_r=1\Rightarrow x_i=r_i\}=T\).

notation.meaning: Boolean selector for table row r.

review_flags: source for extensional-table encoding equivalence required

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The one-hot encoding is mathematically plausible and fits the mapping leaf, including the empty-table case, but the claimed exact projection and configuration interpretation have no cited source.

children.title: Guided Selection Views
children.top_down_role: User-facing views derived from variant or decision representations.

assumptions_latex: The configuration variables have finite domains, and the constraint set \(F\) is fixed.
The current interaction state is a consistent partial assignment \(a\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V_i(a)\) contains exactly the values for decision \(i\) that preserve extendability to a complete feasible configuration.

notation.meaning: Set of complete assignments satisfying all configuration constraints
Guided view of admissible values for decision \(i\)

review_flags: guided-view terminology not explicitly confirmed by locator
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extensional guided view defined by feasible completion, not merely local consistency.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D_i\) be the finite domain of decision \(i\), let \(F\) be the configuration constraints, and let \(a\) be a consistent partial assignment. The guided selection view for an unassigned decision \(i\) is
\[
V_i(a)=\{v\in D_i:\exists s\in\mathcal S(F)\text{ such that }s\supseteq a\text{ and }s_i=v\}.
\]
Thus a displayed value is selectable precisely when the augmented partial assignment \(a\cup\{i\mapsto v\}\) has at least one complete feasible extension.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A guided view shows exactly those values for an unassigned decision that can still be extended to a complete feasible configuration.
knowledge_statements.title: Guided Selection Views

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation is mathematically coherent and matches the leaf, but the cited general constraint-programming section does not specifically support the guided-selection terminology or the exact feasible-completion view. A configuration or interactive-configuration source with a section/page locator is required.

children.title: Configuration Constraint Families
children.top_down_role: Domain-level relations shaping valid assemblies and viable user choices.

children.title: Structural Multiplicity Constraint Family
children.top_down_role: Part-whole, multiplicity, containment, and grouped-choice restrictions.

children.title: Structural Constraints
children.top_down_role: Restrictions governing part-whole configuration structure.

assumptions_latex: The component-type set \(T\) and potential-instance set \(I\) are finite.
Each potential instance has a fixed type and each admissible structural arc has fixed endpoint types.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A configuration is structurally feasible exactly when its selected instances and active structural arcs satisfy the schema and all prescribed incidence bounds.

notation.meaning: Selection indicator for potential component instance \(i\)
Indicator that admissible structural arc \(e\) is active

review_flags: configuration-specific structural formulation not explicitly confirmed by locator
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite typed-instance formulation of structural feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(I\) be potential component instances, \(E\subseteq I\times I\) admissible structural arcs, and \(x_i,y_e\) their selection indicators. Given allowed type pairs \(R\subseteq T\times T\) and incidence bounds \(\ell_{it},u_{it}\), structural constraints require
\[
y_{(i,j)}\le x_i,\quad y_{(i,j)}\le x_j,\quad y_{(i,j)}=0\text{ if }(\tau(i),\tau(j))\notin R,
\]
and
\[
\ell_{it}x_i\le\sum_{j:\tau(j)=t}y_{(i,j)}\le u_{it}x_i
\]
for every \(i\in I\) and \(t\in T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Structural constraints require selected components and their active structural relations to conform to a typed schema and prescribed incidence multiplicities.
knowledge_statements.title: Structural Constraints

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite typed-arc formulation is plausible, but the cited general constraint-programming section does not establish this particular structural schema, its incidence model, or the asserted exact characterization of structural feasibility. The selected content kind should also be reconsidered as a condition once the intended formulation is sourced.

children.title: Cardinality Constraints
children.top_down_role: Restrictions governing allowable component or feature multiplicities.

assumptions_latex: The candidate set \(S\) is finite.
Every selection variable satisfies \(x_i\in\{0,1\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The feasible selections are exactly those satisfying \(L\le\sum_{i\in S}x_i\le U\).

notation.meaning: Finite set whose selected members are counted

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary-selection cardinality constraint with fixed integral bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a finite candidate set \(S\), binary selection variables \(x_i\), and integers \(0\le L\le U\le |S|\), the cardinality constraint is
\[
L\le\sum_{i\in S}x_i\le U.
\]
The special cases \(L=U=k\), \(L=0\), and \(U=|S|\) express exactly \(k\), at most \(U\), and at least \(L\) selected members, respectively. If activation is controlled by a binary parent variable \(p\), the conditional form is \(Lp\le\sum_{i\in S}x_i\le Up\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cardinality constraint places lower and upper bounds on how many members of a finite candidate set may be selected.
knowledge_statements.title: Cardinality Constraints

children.title: Group Constraints
children.top_down_role: Restrictions governing selections within grouped alternatives.

assumptions_latex: The child group \(G\) is finite and has a binary parent-selection variable \(p\).
Every child-selection variable satisfies \(x_i\in\{0,1\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: When \(p=0\) no child is selected; when \(p=1\), between \(L\) and \(U\) children are selected.

notation.meaning: Finite group of alternative child components

review_flags: group-activation interpretation not explicitly confirmed by locator
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parent-activated lower-upper group constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G\) be a finite group of child alternatives, let \(p\in\{0,1\}\) indicate selection of their parent, and let \(x_i\in\{0,1\}\) indicate selection of child \(i\). For integers \(0\le L\le U\le |G|\), the group constraint is
\[
Lp\le\sum_{i\in G}x_i\le Up.
\]
Consequently an unselected parent forces every child unselected, while a selected parent permits the specified multiplicity. The cases \(L=U=1\) and \(L=1,U=|G|\) give exclusive-choice and inclusive-choice groups.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A group constraint activates child choices with their parent and bounds the number of selected children, including exclusive-choice and inclusive-choice groups.
knowledge_statements.title: Group Constraints

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The parent-activated formula is mathematically correct, but the cited generalized-upper-bounding locator does not clearly support the lower-bound activation, parent-child interpretation, or exclusive/inclusive group terminology. A configuration-modeling source is needed.

children.title: Containment Restrictions
children.top_down_role: Restrictions governing admissible nesting or ownership.

assumptions_latex: The potential containment arcs form a finite set \(A\subseteq I\times I\).
Each selected child must have exactly one active immediate container.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Active containment arcs have selected endpoints, and each selected non-root instance has exactly one permitted selected container.

notation.meaning: Indicator that parent \(p\) immediately contains child \(c\)

review_flags: containment-specific formulation not explicitly confirmed by locator
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Immediate containment with unique parenthood for selected non-root components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(I\) be potential instances, \(R\subseteq I\) designated roots, and \(A\subseteq I\times I\) the permitted parent-child arcs. With selection indicators \(x_i\) and containment indicators \(z_{pc}\), immediate containment restrictions are
\[
z_{pc}\le x_p,
\qquad z_{pc}\le x_c
\quad ((p,c)\in A),
\]
and
\[
\sum_{p:(p,c)\in A}z_{pc}=x_c
\quad(c\in I\setminus R).
\]
Variables for pairs outside \(A\) are fixed to zero. Acyclicity, when required, is an additional topology constraint rather than part of immediate containment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Containment restrictions allow only permitted parent-child pairs, require both endpoints to be selected, and assign each selected non-root component one immediate container.
knowledge_statements.title: Containment Restrictions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The immediate-containment formulation is internally consistent, but the generic defining-constraints locator does not support the configuration-specific permitted-arc and unique-parent model. A source explicitly treating containment or hierarchical configuration constraints is required.

children.title: Selection Relation Constraint Family
children.top_down_role: Relations governing coexistence, incompatibility, implication, and conditional selection.

children.title: Compatibility Constraints
children.top_down_role: Restrictions governing which selections may coexist.

assumptions_latex: The selectable item set \(I\) is finite.
The symmetric relation \(C\subseteq I\times I\) lists compatible distinct pairs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every pair of selected distinct items belongs to the compatibility relation \(C\).
review_flags: compatibility-specific interpretation not explicitly confirmed by locator
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pairwise compatibility of selected items in a finite configuration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(I\) be selectable items, let \(x_i\in\{0,1\}\), and let \(C\subseteq I\times I\) be a symmetric compatibility relation on distinct items. A selection is pairwise compatible when
\[
x_i=x_j=1\Longrightarrow(i,j)\in C
\quad\text{for all distinct }i,j\in I.
\]
Equivalently, if \(F=\{\{i,j\}:i\ne j,\ (i,j)\notin C\}\), the binary linear formulation is
\[
x_i+x_j\le1\quad\text{for every }\{i,j\}\in F.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compatibility constraints require every pair of simultaneously selected items to be an allowed pair; each incompatible pair yields an at-most-one inequality.
knowledge_statements.title: Compatibility Constraints

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The pairwise compatibility formulation and its forbidden-pair linearization are correct, but the cited general constraint-programming section does not specifically support this interpretation. A locator addressing compatibility or conflict constraints is required.

children.title: Exclusion Constraints
children.top_down_role: Restrictions prohibiting specified combinations.

assumptions_latex: The item set \(I\) and exclusion family \(\mathcal E\subseteq 2^I\) are finite.
Every item-selection variable satisfies \(x_i\in\{0,1\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No exclusion set \(E\in\mathcal E\) is fully selected.

notation.meaning: Family of forbidden jointly selected subsets

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite forbidden-set formulation, including pairwise mutual exclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(I\) be selectable items and let \(\mathcal E\subseteq 2^I\) be a family of forbidden jointly selected sets, with \(|E|\ge2\) for every \(E\in\mathcal E\). Binary selection variables satisfy the exclusion constraints when
\[
\sum_{i\in E}x_i\le |E|-1
\quad\text{for every }E\in\mathcal E.
\]
Hence at least one member of each forbidden set is absent. For a forbidden pair \(E=\{i,j\}\), this reduces to \(x_i+x_j\le1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exclusion constraint forbids simultaneous selection of every member of a specified set; pairwise exclusion is the familiar at-most-one inequality.
knowledge_statements.title: Exclusion Constraints

children.title: Dependency Constraints
children.top_down_role: Restrictions requiring related configuration selections.

assumptions_latex: The selectable item set \(I\) is finite.
Each directed arc \((i,j)\in D\) means that selecting \(i\) requires selecting \(j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every selected antecedent item has all items on which it directly depends selected.
review_flags: dependency-specific interpretation not explicitly confirmed by locator
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive binary requires relation between selectable items.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(I\) be selectable items, let \(x_i\in\{0,1\}\), and let \(D\subseteq I\times I\) be a directed dependency relation, where \((i,j)\in D\) means that \(i\) requires \(j\). The dependency constraints are
\[
x_i\le x_j\quad\text{for every }(i,j)\in D.
\]
Equivalently, each arc enforces the implication \(x_i=1\Longrightarrow x_j=1\). Dependencies along a directed path hold by transitivity of these inequalities, although the transitive arcs need not be included explicitly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dependency constraint states that selecting one item requires selecting another, represented for binary variables by an implication or ordering inequality.
knowledge_statements.title: Dependency Constraints

children.title: Conditional Selection Relations
children.top_down_role: Selection relationships activated by other configuration choices.

assumptions_latex: All variables have finite domains.
The antecedent \(\phi\) and consequent \(\psi\) are predicates on the same configuration assignment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The relation is satisfied exactly when \(\phi\) is false or \(\psi\) is true.

notation.meaning: Binary truth indicator for the trigger

review_flags: conditional-selection terminology not explicitly confirmed by locator
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-domain implication with a selection relation as consequent.

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a configuration assignment \(s\), a conditional selection relation with antecedent \(\phi\) and consequent \(\psi\) is the constraint
\[
\phi(s)\Longrightarrow\psi(s),
\]
equivalently \(\neg\phi(s)\lor\psi(s)\). If \(b_\phi\in\{0,1\}\) is constrained to equal the truth value of \(\phi\), and \(\psi\) is the dependency \(x_i\le x_j\), its activated linear form is
\[
x_i-x_j\le1-b_\phi.
\]
Thus the selection relation is enforced exactly when the trigger is true.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A conditional selection relation enforces a compatibility, exclusion, or dependency predicate only when its trigger predicate is true.
knowledge_statements.title: Conditional Selection Relations

source_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The logical implication and activated binary inequality are mathematically correct, but neither cited locator specifically supports the stated conditional-selection relation or the required exact reification of the trigger predicate. A source on reified or conditional configuration constraints is required.

children.title: Assembly Connectivity Constraint Family
children.top_down_role: Interface matching, connectivity, placement, and network-structure restrictions.

children.title: Connection Constraints
children.top_down_role: Restrictions governing admissible links between configured elements.

assumptions_latex: The potential component set \(I\) and potential connection set \(E\) are finite.
Each potential connection has two fixed distinct endpoints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every active connection joins selected endpoints, and every selected component meets its prescribed connection-degree bounds.
review_flags: assembly-connection formulation not explicitly confirmed by locator
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Endpoint activation and degree bounds for finite undirected assembly graphs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(I\) be a finite set of potential components, let \(E\subseteq\{\{i,j\}:i,j\in I,\ i\ne j\}\) be a finite set of potential undirected connections, and let \(x_i,y_e\in\{0,1\}\). For every \(e=\{i,j\}\in E\), endpoint activation requires
\[
y_e\le x_i,
\qquad y_e\le x_j.
\]
For each \(i\in I\), define \(\delta(i)=\{e\in E:i\in e\}\). Given integer degree bounds \(0\le d_i^-\le d_i^+\), connection multiplicity requires
\[
d_i^-x_i\le\sum_{e\in\delta(i)}y_e\le d_i^+x_i
\quad(i\in I).
\]
These constraints govern local connections; global connectedness or acyclicity is imposed separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Connection constraints activate edges only between selected components and enforce lower and upper bounds on each selected component's incident connections.
knowledge_statements.title: Connection Constraints

children.title: Topology Constraints
children.top_down_role: Restrictions governing global network or assembly structure.

assumptions_latex: The selected vertex set is nonempty.
The active assembly graph is finite and undirected.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected assembly has the prescribed topology exactly when its active graph belongs to the designated graph family \(\mathcal T\).

notation.meaning: Graph induced by selected vertices and active edges
Prescribed family of admissible finite graphs

review_flags: specific intended topology class is not supplied by the node path
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Graph-family formulation; connected-tree constraints are given as a standard specialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For component indicators \(x\) and connection indicators \(y\), define the active graph
\[
G(x,y)=\bigl(V_x,E_y\bigr),
\quad V_x=\{i:x_i=1\},
\quad E_y=\{e:y_e=1\}.
\]
Given a prescribed family \(\mathcal T\) of finite graphs, the topology constraint is \(G(x,y)\in\mathcal T\). In the common connected-tree specialization, this means that every pair of vertices in \(V_x\) is joined by an active path and
\[
|E_y|=|V_x|-1.
\]
For a finite undirected graph, these two conditions are equivalent to being a tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A topology constraint requires the graph of selected components and active connections to belong to a prescribed class, such as connected trees.
knowledge_statements.title: Topology Constraints

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The graph-family definition and connected-tree specialization are mathematically correct, but the cited general constraint-programming section does not support the topology formulation or identify the intended admissible graph family. A graph-constrained configuration source is required.

children.title: Layout Constraints
children.top_down_role: Restrictions governing spatial placement of configured elements.

assumptions_latex: Each selected component \(i\) is represented by a compact footprint \(B_i\subseteq\mathbb R^d\).
Allowed placements are rigid transformations chosen from prescribed domains \(P_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every selected footprint lies within the assembly region, and interiors of distinct selected footprints are disjoint.
review_flags: geometric layout formulation not explicitly confirmed by locator
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rigid-placement containment and nonoverlap in Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(R\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) be the permitted assembly region. Component \(i\) has compact footprint \(B_i\subseteq\mathbb R^d\), selection indicator \(x_i\), and placement \(q_i\in P_i\), where \(q_i\) is an allowed rigid transformation. Basic layout constraints require
\[
x_i=1\Longrightarrow q_i(B_i)\subseteq R
\]
and, for all distinct \(i,j\),
\[
x_i=x_j=1\Longrightarrow
\operatorname{int}(q_i(B_i))\cap\operatorname{int}(q_j(B_j))=\varnothing.
\]
Additional adjacency or clearance requirements may further restrict the pair \((q_i,q_j)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Layout constraints place each selected component inside the allowed region and prevent interiors of distinct selected component footprints from overlapping.
knowledge_statements.title: Layout Constraints

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The containment and interior-nonoverlap conditions are plausible layout constraints, but the cited general constraint-programming section does not support this geometric model. The record also does not explicitly declare the component index set or the binary domain of each selection indicator. A sourced formulation is needed before choosing the precise corrected version.

children.title: Interface-Matching Restrictions
children.top_down_role: Restrictions governing compatible ports or attachment points.

knowledge_statements.title: Interface-Matching Restrictions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary compatibility formulation for undirected pairwise assembly interfaces with port-incidence limits.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E\subseteq\{\{p,q\}:p,q\in P,\ p\neq q\}\) be the candidate connections and let \(K\subseteq E\) contain the compatible connections. For every \(e\in E\), impose \(y_e=0\) when \(e\notin K\). For every \(p\in P\), also impose \[\sum_{e\in E:p\in e}y_e\leq d_p.\] Thus every selected connection is compatible and every port respects its prescribed incidence bound. Single-use ports have \(d_p=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A connection may be selected only between compatible interfaces, and the number of selected connections incident to each port cannot exceed that port's prescribed limit.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is a finite set of ports, \(E\subseteq\{\{p,q\}:p,q\in P,\ p\neq q\}\) is the set of candidate undirected connections, and \(K\subseteq E\) is the compatibility set.
For every \(e\in E\), \(y_e\in\{0,1\}\) indicates whether connection \(e\) is selected, and every \(p\in P\) has an incidence bound \(d_p\in\mathbb{Z}_{+}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y_e=0\) for every \(e\in E\setminus K\), and \(\sum_{e\in E:p\in e}y_e\leq d_p\) for every \(p\in P\).

notation.meaning: set of candidate undirected port connections
binary selection variable for candidate connection e
maximum permitted number of selected connections incident to port p

source_refs.source_title: Theory of Linear and Integer Programming

source_witnesses.source_title: Theory of Linear and Integer Programming

children.title: Resource Feasibility Constraint Family
children.top_down_role: Power, space, weight, performance, budget, and shared-capacity restrictions.

children.title: Resource Constraints
children.top_down_role: Restrictions on consumable or reusable configuration resources.

assumptions_latex: \(I\) and \(R\) are finite sets of selectable components and resource types.
\(x_i\in\mathbb{Z}_{+}\) is the selected multiplicity of component \(i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The configuration is resource-feasible exactly when \(L_r\leq \sum_{i\in I}a_{ri}x_i\leq U_r\) for every \(r\in R\).

notation.meaning: net contribution of one unit of component i to resource r
permitted lower and upper totals for resource r

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive multi-resource feasibility model allowing both required and limited resources.

source_refs.locator: 1.2.1 Resource allocation in production planning p. 4

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a_{ri}\in\mathbb{R}\) denote the net amount of resource \(r\) supplied by one unit of component \(i\), with negative values representing consumption. Given bounds \(L_r,U_r\in\mathbb{R}\cup\{-\infty,+\infty\}\) satisfying \(L_r\leq U_r\), the resource constraints are \[L_r\leq \sum_{i\in I}a_{ri}x_i\leq U_r\qquad(r\in R).\] A configuration is resource-feasible if and only if all these inequalities hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For every resource, the total amount supplied minus consumed by selected components must lie within its permitted interval.
knowledge_statements.title: Resource Constraints

source_witnesses.locator: 1.2.1 Resource allocation in production planning p. 4

children.title: Capacity Constraints
children.top_down_role: Limits on shared or component-specific capacities.

assumptions_latex: \(I\) and \(R\) are finite sets of component types and capacity pools.
\(x_i\in\mathbb{Z}_{+}\), \(a_{ri}\geq0\), and \(C_r\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Capacity feasibility is characterized by \(\sum_{i\in I}a_{ri}x_i\leq C_r\) for all \(r\in R\).

notation.meaning: capacity consumed by one unit of component i from pool r
available amount of capacity pool r

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic additive upper-capacity constraints for finite configuration choices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each capacity pool \(r\in R\), selecting \(x_i\) units of component type \(i\) consumes \(a_{ri}x_i\) units. The configuration satisfies its capacity constraints precisely when \[\sum_{i\in I}a_{ri}x_i\leq C_r\qquad(r\in R).\] If a capacity is available only when an enabling decision \(z_r\in\{0,1\}\) is selected, replace the right side by \(C_rz_r\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The aggregate demand placed on each capacity pool cannot exceed the capacity made available by the configuration.
knowledge_statements.title: Capacity Constraints

children.title: Performance Constraints
children.top_down_role: Restrictions on required configuration performance.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is the set of structurally admissible configurations.
Each performance response \(g_k:X\to\mathbb{R}\) and required threshold \(b_k\in\mathbb{R}\) are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The performance-feasible set is \(X_{\mathrm{perf}}=\{x\in X:g_k(x)\geq b_k\ \text{for every }k\in K\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Threshold formulation for deterministic configuration-performance requirements; upper limits can be represented by sign reversal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\) be a finite set of performance criteria. A configuration \(x\in X\) is performance-feasible when \[g_k(x)\geq b_k\qquad(k\in K).\] An upper-limit requirement \(h_k(x)\leq u_k\) has the same form after setting \(g_k=-h_k\) and \(b_k=-u_k\). These constraints may be nonlinear because a response can depend jointly on several selected components and their connections.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every modeled performance response of a structurally admissible configuration must meet its specified lower or upper threshold.
knowledge_statements.title: Performance Constraints

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The threshold formulation is coherent and fits the leaf, but no source is supplied for the performance-feasibility model or its nonlinear-response scope.

children.title: Budget Feasibility
children.top_down_role: Acceptability under cost, power, weight, space, or similar budgets.

assumptions_latex: \(I\) is a finite set of selectable items and \(x_i\in\mathbb{Z}_{+}\).
Each unit cost \(c_i\geq0\), fixed charge \(f_i\geq0\), and total budget \(B\geq0\) are given.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Budget feasibility is equivalent to \(\sum_{i\in I}(c_ix_i+f_iz_i)\leq B\) together with valid activation links.

notation.meaning: multiplicity and activation variables for item i
unit and fixed costs for item i

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single-period deterministic acquisition budget with optional fixed charges.

source_refs.locator: 1.2.1 Resource allocation in production planning p. 4

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z_i\in\{0,1\}\) indicate whether item type \(i\) is activated, and let \(M_i\in\mathbb{Z}_{+}\) be a valid multiplicity bound. Impose \(0\leq x_i\leq M_iz_i\) and \[\sum_{i\in I}\bigl(c_ix_i+f_iz_i\bigr)\leq B.\] The first inequalities charge \(f_i\) whenever a positive multiplicity is selected; the displayed inequality then characterizes feasibility with respect to the stated budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The sum of unit acquisition costs and any activated fixed charges must not exceed the available budget.
knowledge_statements.title: Budget Feasibility

children.title: Contextual Compliance Constraint Family
children.top_down_role: User, environmental, deployment, and regulatory conditions restricting acceptable variants.

children.title: Requirement Constraints
children.top_down_role: Restrictions derived from user or stakeholder requirements.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is the configuration domain and \(R\) is a finite set of mandatory requirements.
Each requirement \(r\in R\) has an applicability predicate \(a_r:X\to\{0,1\}\) and satisfaction predicate \(s_r:X\to\{0,1\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The requirement-feasible set is \(\{x\in X:a_r(x)\leq s_r(x)\ \text{for all }r\in R\}\).

notation.meaning: indicator that configuration x satisfies requirement r

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical encoding of mandatory conditional requirements over complete configurations.

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each \(r\in R\), enforce the implication \[a_r(x)=1\ \Longrightarrow\ s_r(x)=1.\] Because both predicates are binary, this is equivalently \(a_r(x)\leq s_r(x)\). Unconditional requirements use \(a_r(x)=1\). A configuration is requirement-feasible if and only if every applicable mandatory requirement is satisfied; requirements that are not applicable impose no restriction through this family.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each mandatory requirement must hold whenever its applicability condition is true; inapplicable requirements impose no restriction.
knowledge_statements.title: Requirement Constraints

source_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

children.title: Context Constraints
children.top_down_role: Restrictions activated by environmental or usage context.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is the configuration domain and \(C\) is a set of admissible contexts.
For each \(c\in C\), \(F(c)\subseteq X\) is the set of configurations permitted in context \(c\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A configuration-context pair is feasible exactly when \(x\in F(c)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Context-indexed feasibility correspondence for environmental or operational conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The context constraint is the membership predicate \[(x,c)\in\operatorname{graph}(F)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x\in F(c),\] where \(\operatorname{graph}(F)=\{(x,c)\in X\times C:x\in F(c)\}\). If \(F(c)\) is described by indexed inequalities \(g_j(x,c)\leq0\) for \(j\in J\), then contextual feasibility is equivalent to satisfying every such inequality at the realized context \(c\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A configuration is context-feasible when it belongs to the feasible set associated with the realized environmental or operational context.
knowledge_statements.title: Context Constraints

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The context-indexed feasible-set representation is internally valid, but no inspectable source supports this configuration-context formalization or its inequality representation.

children.title: Regulatory Constraints
children.top_down_role: Restrictions derived from applicable regulations or standards.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is the configuration domain and \(Q\) is a finite set of binding regulatory clauses.
Each clause \(q\in Q\) has applicability predicate \(a_q:X\to\{0,1\}\) and compliance predicate \(c_q:X\to\{0,1\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Regulatory compliance holds exactly when \(a_q(x)\leq c_q(x)\) for every \(q\in Q\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conjunctive compliance model for externally supplied, correctly encoded regulatory clauses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a complete configuration \(x\in X\), impose \[a_q(x)=1\ \Longrightarrow\ c_q(x)=1\qquad(q\in Q),\] equivalently \(a_q(x)\leq c_q(x)\). Hence \(x\) is compliant precisely when every binding clause applicable to \(x\) is satisfied. This mathematical condition certifies compliance only with the encoded clause set \(Q\); completeness and legal validity of that encoding are external assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every encoded regulatory clause that applies to a configuration must be satisfied; the model does not establish that the encoded clauses are legally complete.
knowledge_statements.title: Regulatory Constraints

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conditional-clause encoding is mathematically coherent and appropriately limits its claim to the encoded clauses, but no regulatory or formal-compliance source is provided.

children.title: Deployment Conditions
children.top_down_role: Operational conditions limiting acceptable configuration variants.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is the configuration domain and \(D\) is the set of deployment scenarios.
For each \(d\in D\), \(F_d\subseteq X\) denotes configurations operable under scenario \(d\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Robust deployability over \(D_0\subseteq D\) is equivalent to \(x\in\bigcap_{d\in D_0}F_d\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scenario-indexed robust deployability, excluding recourse or post-deployment reconfiguration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D_0\subseteq D\) be the scenarios against which deployment must be guaranteed. A fixed configuration \(x\in X\) satisfies the deployment conditions when \[x\in F_d\qquad\text{for every }d\in D_0,\] or equivalently \(x\in\bigcap_{d\in D_0}F_d\). For a single known deployment scenario \(d_0\), this reduces to \(x\in F_{d_0}\). The formulation assumes no scenario-dependent reconfiguration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed configuration is deployable when it remains operable in every deployment scenario for which feasibility is required.
knowledge_statements.title: Deployment Conditions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The intersection formulation consistently describes fixed-configuration robust deployability without recourse, but no source supports the deployment-scenario interpretation.
