children.title: Propagation-Search Configuration Calculus
children.top_down_role: Constraint-driven search with filtering and reversible choices.

children.title: Constraint Propagation
children.top_down_role: Filtering configuration choices through constraint consequences.

assumptions_latex: \(V\) is a finite variable set with finite current domains \(D_v\), and \(\mathcal{C}\) is a finite constraint set.
Each propagator is contracting and removes only values lacking support in its associated constraint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Propagation returns a sound common fixed point of the propagators, or detects failure when some domain becomes empty.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-domain work-list propagation to a local-consistency fixed point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize a work list \(W:=\mathcal{C}\). While \(W\neq\varnothing\), remove some \(C\in W\), replace the domain tuple \(D\) by \(P_C(D)\), and reinsert constraints whose propagators depend on any changed domain. Stop with failure if \(D_v=\varnothing\) for some \(v\in V\); otherwise stop when \(W=\varnothing\) and output \(D\). Finiteness and contraction imply termination, while support-preserving deletions retain every solution contained in the initial domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly apply sound domain-reduction operators until none changes a domain, reporting failure if any variable loses all values.
knowledge_statements.title: Constraint Propagation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-domain work-list algorithm and its termination and soundness claims require a constraint-programming source specifying the propagator and scheduling assumptions.

children.title: Backtracking Search
children.top_down_role: Exploration of reversible configuration choices.

assumptions_latex: \(V\) is finite, every domain \(D_v\) is finite, and feasibility is determined by constraints \(\mathcal{C}\).
Propagation is sound and reports failure whenever its current domain state is inconsistent by the enforced local test.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure returns a feasible complete assignment if one exists, and otherwise exhausts the finite search tree and reports infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Depth-first complete search over finite domains with sound propagation at every node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Propagate the current domains. If failure occurs, return to the most recent choice with an unexplored alternative. If every domain is singleton, output the induced assignment after checking \(\mathcal{C}\). Otherwise choose \(v\in V\) with \(|D_v|>1\), partition \(D_v\) into nonempty proper subsets \(S_1,\ldots,S_m\), and recursively search each state obtained by replacing \(D_v\) with \(S_j\). Report infeasibility only after all alternatives are exhausted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Propagate, branch on a non-singleton domain, and restore earlier states after failed branches until finding a solution or exhausting all alternatives.
knowledge_statements.title: Backtracking Search

children.title: Propagation–Search Coupling
children.top_down_role: Coordination between constraint filtering and search decisions.

assumptions_latex: The constraint problem has finitely many variables with finite domains.
Propagation is sound, and every branching step partitions the selected current domain into nonempty proper subsets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Interleaving propagation after every branch preserves completeness and can prune a branch only when that branch contains no feasible assignment.

notation.meaning: domain state at a search node
children produced by a domain partition

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sound propagation embedded at every node of a complete finite-domain search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a search node with domain state \(D\), first compute \(P(D)\). If propagation fails, prune the node. If \(P(D)\) is complete, verify and return its assignment. Otherwise branch into states \(D^{(1)},\ldots,D^{(m)}\) whose solution sets partition the solution set represented by \(P(D)\), and propagate each child before further branching. Sound propagation preserves all feasible assignments, while exhaustive partitioning ensures that coupling propagation with search does not destroy completeness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Propagation filters every search node before branching; sound filtering and exhaustive domain partitions preserve all solutions while detecting failed branches early.
knowledge_statements.title: Propagation–Search Coupling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The coupling principle is mathematically plausible under sound propagation and exhaustive solution-set partitions, but no source is supplied for its preservation and completeness claims.

children.title: Reversible Choice Management
children.top_down_role: Organization of configuration decisions that may be withdrawn.

knowledge_statements.title: Reversible Choice Management
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Trail-based restoration for finite-domain configuration search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given variables \(X\) with current domains \(D\), maintain a stack \(T\) of decision markers and records \((x,D_{\mathrm{old}}(x))\). Before changing \(D(x)\), append its old domain unless already recorded after the latest marker. To branch on \(x\in S\), push a marker, impose \(D(x)\leftarrow D(x)\cap S\), and propagate constraints. If propagation derives \(D(y)=\varnothing\), pop records to the marker and restore every recorded domain; then explore the complementary choice. Output a configuration when every domain is singleton and all constraints hold, or failure after all branches are exhausted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Record domain changes after each decision, restore them on conflict, and explore alternatives until a valid complete configuration is found or every branch fails.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and every initial domain \(D_0(x)\) are finite.
Propagation removes values but never adds values within a branch.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D\) is restored exactly to its state immediately before the reversed decision.

notation.meaning: current domain of configuration variable x
trail of reversible domain changes and decision markers

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm content and content_kind fit the reversible-choice leaf, but no citation or inspectable locator supports the trailing invariant, exact restoration claim, or search behavior.

children.title: Logical Solver Encoding Family
children.top_down_role: Compilation of configuration knowledge into logical solver interfaces.

children.title: SAT-Based Configuration
children.top_down_role: Configuration reasoning through propositional satisfiability encodings.

knowledge_statements.title: SAT-Based Configuration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Propositional encoding of finite configuration choices and constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) be a finite configuration model and let \(B\) contain Boolean variables representing selections and auxiliary encoding states. A SAT encoding is a CNF formula \(F_P\) together with a projection \(\pi:\{0,1\}^{B}\to\mathcal C\). It is sound and complete when \(F_P(b)=1\) implies \(\pi(b)\in\operatorname{Valid}(P)\), and every \(c\in\operatorname{Valid}(P)\) has some \(b\) satisfying \(F_P(b)=1\) and \(\pi(b)=c\). Thus configuration existence is equivalent to satisfiability of \(F_P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A SAT encoding is correct when projected satisfying assignments are exactly the valid configurations, including every valid configuration and no invalid one.
assumptions_latex: The configuration choices and their finite domains admit Boolean encoding.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Valid}(P)\neq\varnothing\iff F_P\text{ is satisfiable}.\)

notation.meaning: CNF encoding of configuration model P
projection from Boolean assignments to configurations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The sound-and-complete projected CNF representation fits SAT-based configuration, but the record supplies no source establishing this configuration-encoding correspondence.

children.title: SMT-Based Configuration
children.top_down_role: Configuration reasoning through satisfiability-modulo-theories encodings.

knowledge_statements.title: SMT-Based Configuration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Many-sorted theory encoding of configuration choices and attributes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) have finite selection variables and typed attributes over theory domains such as integers, reals, arrays, or uninterpreted sorts. An SMT encoding consists of a quantifier-free theory formula \(\Phi_P\) and a projection \(\pi\) from theory models to configurations. Correctness requires \(M\models\Phi_P\Rightarrow\pi(M)\in\operatorname{Valid}(P)\) and, for every \(c\in\operatorname{Valid}(P)\), a theory model \(M\models\Phi_P\) with \(\pi(M)=c\). Configuration existence is then equivalent to theory satisfiability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An SMT encoding preserves typed attributes directly and is correct when its theory models project exactly onto all valid configurations.
assumptions_latex: All configuration constraints are expressible in the selected background theories.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Valid}(P)\neq\varnothing\iff \Phi_P\text{ is satisfiable modulo the selected theories}.\)

notation.meaning: SMT formula encoding configuration model P
projection from theory models to configurations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation and satisfiability equivalence fit SMT-based configuration, but no authoritative SMT configuration source and specific locator are supplied.

children.title: Answer-Set Configuration
children.top_down_role: Configuration reasoning through answer-set solver interfaces.

knowledge_statements.title: Answer-Set Configuration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stable-model encoding of selections, defaults, and configuration constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) be a finite configuration model. An answer-set encoding is a finite logic program \(\Pi_P\) and a projection \(\pi\) from stable models of \(\Pi_P\) to configurations. It is sound and complete when each stable model \(A\in\operatorname{SM}(\Pi_P)\) satisfies \(\pi(A)\in\operatorname{Valid}(P)\), and every valid configuration \(c\) equals \(\pi(A)\) for some \(A\in\operatorname{SM}(\Pi_P)\). Integrity constraints exclude forbidden combinations, while choice rules may generate admissible selections.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An answer-set encoding is correct when projections of its stable models are exactly the valid configurations.
assumptions_latex: The grounded program \(\Pi_P\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Valid}(P)\neq\varnothing\iff \operatorname{SM}(\Pi_P)\neq\varnothing.\)

notation.meaning: logic program encoding configuration model P
projection from stable models to configurations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stable-model representation fits answer-set configuration, but the soundness, completeness, and existence equivalence have no cited source or inspectable locator.

children.title: Solver Encoding Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Representational tradeoffs across logical solver targets.

knowledge_statements.title: Solver Encoding Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic equivalence does not imply equal computational behavior.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For two encodings \((E_1,\pi_1)\) and \((E_2,\pi_2)\) of the same model \(P\), semantic interchangeability requires \(\{\pi_1(m):m\models E_1\}=\{\pi_2(m):m\models E_2\}=\operatorname{Valid}(P)\). This equality alone implies no ordering of formula size, propagation strength, solving time, memory, explanation quality, or incremental-update cost. Encoding selection must therefore preserve the projected solution set and separately evaluate the resource and query properties relevant to the intended workload.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equivalent encodings preserve the same configurations but may differ independently in size, propagation, runtime, memory, explanations, and incremental performance.
assumptions_latex: Each encoding has a defined projection from solver models to configurations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{semantic equivalence}\not\Rightarrow\text{computational equivalence}.\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle content_kind fits the tradeoff leaf and the semantic distinction is precise, but no comparative encoding source supports the listed computational and operational dimensions.

children.title: Optimization-Based Configuration
children.top_down_role: Integer, pseudo-Boolean, weighted-constraint, and multiobjective selection models.

knowledge_statements.title: Optimization-Based Configuration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Integer and pseudo-Boolean selection with single or multiple objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent configuration selections by \(x\in\{0,1\}^n\), optional integer attributes by \(z\in\mathbb Z^q\), and validity by \((x,z)\in\mathcal F\), where \(\mathcal F\) is defined by integer, pseudo-Boolean, or weighted constraints. A single-objective configuration minimizes \(f(x,z)\) over \(\mathcal F\). With objectives \(f_1,\ldots,f_k\), a feasible point is Pareto efficient when no other feasible point weakly improves every objective and strictly improves at least one; lexicographic optimization instead minimizes objectives in a declared priority order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Configuration becomes discrete optimization: constraints define valid products, while one objective, lexicographic priorities, or Pareto efficiency selects preferred products.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal F\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\times\mathbb Z^q\) represents exactly the valid configurations.
All objective values are defined on \(\mathcal F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x^*,z^*)\in\arg\min_{(x,z)\in\mathcal F}f(x,z)\) is an optimal valid configuration.

notation.meaning: feasible set of valid encoded configurations

source_refs.locator: 1.1 The concept of a model p. 3

source_witnesses.locator: 1.1 The concept of a model p. 3

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits the optimization-based configuration topic and the mathematics is standard, but the cited introductory modeling section does not specifically support the pseudo-Boolean, Pareto-efficiency, and lexicographic claims. A relevant integer or multiobjective optimization locator is required.

children.title: Knowledge Compilation for Configuration
children.top_down_role: Offline compilation supporting repeated queries, counting, explanation, and interactive response.

knowledge_statements.title: Knowledge Compilation for Configuration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Offline compilation into a query-efficient Boolean representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) encode valid configurations over Boolean variables \(X\). Knowledge compilation constructs a representation \(K\) with \(K\equiv F\). If \(K\) is deterministic and decomposable negation normal form, conditioning by a partial assignment preserves decomposability; consistency is decided by bottom-up evaluation, and model counts are computed bottom-up by multiplying counts at decomposable conjunctions and adding counts at deterministic disjunctions, with corrections for variables absent from a child. The compiled object can therefore serve repeated interactive queries without resolving \(F\) from scratch.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compile the configuration theory once into an equivalent structured circuit that supports repeated conditioning, consistency checks, and model counting efficiently.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a finite propositional theory over \(X\).
The compiled circuit is deterministic, decomposable, and has explicit variable scopes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Mod}(K)=\operatorname{Mod}(F)\), with conditioning, consistency, and counting computable by circuit traversal.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits knowledge compilation for configuration, but the d-DNNF conditioning and model-counting claims require an authoritative knowledge-compilation citation with a specific locator.

children.title: Federated Configuration Reasoning Family
children.top_down_role: Reasoning organized by modules, subsystems, viewpoints, or distributed knowledge sources.

children.title: Modular Configuration Reasoning
children.top_down_role: Reasoning partitioned across configuration modules or subsystems.

assumptions_latex: \(D\) assigns a domain to every variable, and variables shared by modules have the same domain and interpretation in each module.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R=\bowtie_{i=1}^{m}R_i\) is exactly the relation of globally consistent configurations.

notation.meaning: variables owned or referenced by module i
local solution relation of module i

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global configurations assembled from interface-compatible local solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For modules \(i=1,\ldots,m\), let \(X_i\) be the module variables and let \(R_i\subseteq\prod_{x\in X_i}D(x)\) be the relation of assignments satisfying the module's local constraints. A global assignment \(a\) is a modular configuration precisely when \(a|_{X_i}\in R_i\) for every \(i\). Equivalently, the global solution relation is the natural join \(R=\bowtie_{i=1}^{m}R_i\), whose tuples agree on every shared variable. Interfaces may retain the shared variables needed to test this compatibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each module supplies its local solution relation, and the globally consistent configurations are exactly the natural join of local solutions that agree on shared variables.
knowledge_statements.title: Modular Configuration Reasoning

children.title: Distributed Configuration Reasoning
children.top_down_role: Reasoning performed across separated knowledge sources.

assumptions_latex: The module scopes \(X_i\) form a join tree satisfying the running-intersection property.
Every local solution relation \(R_i\) is finite and represented exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bowtie_i R_i\neq\varnothing\) if and only if every local relation remaining after the two message-passing passes is nonempty.

notation.meaning: relation-valued message from module i to module j
neighbors of module i in the join tree
projection of a relation onto variables in S

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact relational message passing on an acyclic module graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the modules form a join tree, and let node \(i\) store a finite local solution relation \(R_i\) over variables \(X_i\). For adjacent nodes \(i\) and \(j\), define \(S_{ij}=X_i\cap X_j\) and \(M_{i\to j}=\operatorname{proj}_{S_{ij}}\!\left(R_i\bowtie\mathop{\bowtie}_{k\in N(i)\setminus\{j\}}M_{k\to i}\right)\). Compute messages inward from the leaves and then outward, and replace each local relation by its join with all incoming messages. Report failure if a resulting local relation is empty; otherwise select compatible tuples and extend them along the tree to construct a global configuration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a join tree of modules, exchange projected separator relations in two passes. An empty reduced relation detects failure, while compatible remaining tuples can be extended to a global configuration.
knowledge_statements.title: Distributed Configuration Reasoning

children.title: Viewpoint Coordination
children.top_down_role: Coordination of configuration decisions across distinct viewpoints.

assumptions_latex: Each interface map \(\rho_i\) preserves the domains and meanings of the shared concepts.
Each declared relation \(K_{ij}\subseteq R_i\times R_j\) has a specified interpretation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Coordination holds if and only if there exist \((r_1,[... ELLIPSIZATION ...]n_latex [

notation.meaning: map exposing viewpoint i on the common interface
declared compatibility relation between viewpoints i and j

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility of heterogeneous local views through a common interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For viewpoints \(i=1,[... ELLIPSIZATION ...]ratorname {
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local viewpoint configurations are coordinated exactly when their interface projections agree and all declared pairwise compatibility relations hold. Without additional pairwise relations, coordination is equivalent to a nonempty intersection of the attainable interface states.
knowledge_statements.title: Viewpoint Coordination

children.title: Cross-Module Consistency
children.top_down_role: Consistency relationships spanning configuration modules.

assumptions_latex: Shared variables have compatible domains and equality semantics across modules.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The module family is jointly consistent if and only if \(\bowtie_i R_i\neq\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: restriction of a global assignment to module i

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global extendability criterion for local module configurations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given module relations \(R_i\subseteq\prod_{x\in X_i}D(x)\), selected local configurations \(r_i\in R_i\) are cross-module consistent when there exists an assignment \(a\in\prod_{x\in\bigcup_iX_i}D(x)\) such that \(a|_{X_i}=r_i\) for every \(i\). Under shared-variable equality semantics, such an assignment exists exactly when the selected tuples agree on every overlap. The module family is jointly consistent exactly when \(\bowtie_iR_i\neq\varnothing\). Nonemptiness of every pairwise join \(R_i\bowtie R_j\) need not imply that the join of the entire family is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Selected module configurations have a common global extension exactly when they agree on shared variables. A family of module relations is jointly consistent exactly when its full natural join is nonempty; separate pairwise joins may all be nonempty while the full join is empty.
knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Module Consistency

children.title: Configuration-Space Analysis
children.top_down_role: Model-level analyses performed independently of a particular completed product.

children.title: Configuration Existence Certificate System
children.top_down_role: Detection of void models and existence of valid products.

children.title: Model Satisfiability
children.top_down_role: Consistency analysis for complete configuration models.

assumptions_latex: \(X\), the encoded domains \(D(x)\), and the constraint set \(C\) are finite.
Every constraint predicate is decidable on a complete assignment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(c(a|_{\operatorname{scope}(c)})=\operatorname{true}\) for every \(c\in C\), then \(P\) is satisfiable.

notation.meaning: total assignment supplied as a satisfiability witness
variables on which constraint c depends

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct witness certificate for existence of a valid configuration.

source_refs.locator: 2.5 Generalized Set Covering: The Satisfiability Problem p. 58

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=(X,D,C)\) be a finite configuration model, where each \(c\in C\) is a decidable predicate on the assignments to \(\operatorname{scope}(c)\subseteq X\). A total assignment \(a\in\prod_{x\in X}D(x)\) is a satisfiability certificate when \(c(a|_{\operatorname{scope}(c)})=\operatorname{true}\) for every \(c\in C\). Verification evaluates every constraint on the supplied assignment. Acceptance certifies that \(P\) is satisfiable. If each constraint can be evaluated in time polynomial in its representation and input sizes, verification is polynomial in the encoded model and certificate sizes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A complete assignment certifies model satisfiability when every constraint evaluates to true. Verification is polynomial in the encoded model and witness sizes when every constraint predicate is polynomial-time evaluable.
knowledge_statements.title: Model Satisfiability

source_witnesses.locator: 2.5 Generalized Set Covering: The Satisfiability Problem p. 58

children.title: Valid Product Existence
children.top_down_role: Existence analysis for products admitted by a configuration model.

assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a finite set of Boolean features.
\(\Phi\) is a propositional configuration constraint over \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Phi\) admits a valid product if and only if \(\mathcal P(\Phi)\neq\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: Set of valid products satisfying the constraint.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: valid configurations are satisfying Boolean assignments, so existence is propositional satisfiability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite Boolean configuration models; attributes and cardinality features require an appropriate finite-domain encoding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each subset \(P\subseteq F\), let \(v_P:F\to\{0,1\}\) satisfy \(v_P(f)=1\) exactly when \(f\in P\), and define \(\mathcal P(\Phi)=\{P\subseteq F: v_P\models\Phi\}\). A valid product exists precisely when there is a subset \(P\subseteq F\) whose induced valuation satisfies every constraint in \(\Phi\); equivalently, \[\exists P\subseteq F\; (v_P\models\Phi)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \mathcal P(\Phi)\neq\varnothing.\] Thus valid-product existence is exactly satisfiability of the configuration constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid product exists exactly when some feature selection satisfies every configuration constraint, equivalently when the model's product set is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.title: Valid Product Existence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition is mathematically precise for finite Boolean configuration models and fits the Valid Product Existence leaf, but no inspectable feature-model or propositional-configuration source is cited. The standard-field rationale supports candidate status but does not satisfy the citation requirement.

children.title: Void-Model Detection
children.top_down_role: Identification of models admitting no valid products.

assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a finite set of Boolean features.
\(\Phi\) is a propositional configuration constraint over \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A refutation of \(\Phi\) certifies \(\mathcal P(\Phi)=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: Set of valid products satisfying the constraint.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: emptiness of a Boolean configuration space is equivalent to unsatisfiability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical voidness of a finite Boolean configuration model, independent of the chosen complete SAT or constraint solver.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The configuration model is void exactly when \(\Phi\) is unsatisfiable: \[\mathcal P(\Phi)=\varnothing\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \nexists v:F\to\{0,1\}\text{ with }v\models\Phi.\] A checkable void-model certificate is any sound refutation accepted by a proof verifier for the encoding of \(\Phi\), such as a resolution derivation of the empty clause from a conjunctive-normal-form encoding equisatisfiable with \(\Phi\). Verifier acceptance certifies that no valid product exists, provided the encoding and proof system are sound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A model is void exactly when its constraints are unsatisfiable; a verifier-accepted refutation of a sound encoding certifies this emptiness.
knowledge_statements.title: Void-Model Detection

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The unsatisfiability characterization and verifier-accepted refutation certificate are sound under the stated encoding and proof-system assumptions, and certificate is the correct content kind. An inspectable source is still required for the configuration-model characterization and certificate framework.

children.title: Existence Witnesses
children.top_down_role: Valid configurations serving as evidence of product existence.

assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a finite set of Boolean features.
\(\Phi\) is a propositional configuration constraint over \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any \(P\subseteq F\) with \(v_P\models\Phi\) certifies \(\mathcal P(\Phi)\neq\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: Candidate selected-feature set and its induced valuation.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: a satisfying assignment is a directly checkable NP witness for configuration existence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct existence certificates for finite Boolean configuration models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An existence witness is a subset \(P\subseteq F\), or equivalently its total valuation \(v_P:F\to\{0,1\}\), such that \(v_P\models\Phi\). Verification evaluates every constraint of \(\Phi\) under \(v_P\). Acceptance establishes \[P\in\mathcal P(\Phi)\quad\text{and hence}\quad\mathcal P(\Phi)\neq\varnothing.\] For a constraint representation whose evaluation time is polynomial in its encoded length, this witness is checkable in polynomial time in the combined size of \(F\), \(\Phi\), and the representation of \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A selected-feature set satisfying every model constraint is a directly checkable witness that at least one valid product exists.
knowledge_statements.title: Existence Witnesses

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A satisfying feature selection is the appropriate existence certificate, and the conditional polynomial-time verification claim is properly scoped. No source with a specific locator supports either the configuration witness terminology or the complexity claim.

children.title: Feature Availability Status Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Analysis of mandatory, optional, dead, false-optional, and conditionally available features.

children.title: Feature Commonality
children.top_down_role: Analysis of features shared across valid products.

assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a finite set of Boolean features.
\(\mathcal P(\Phi)\neq\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\) is common exactly when \(f\in\bigcap_{P\in\mathcal P(\Phi)}P\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: feature commonality is universal membership across valid products
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boolean feature commonality with void models excluded to avoid vacuous universal classification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A feature \(f\in F\) is common in the nonvoid configuration model \(\Phi\) when every valid product selects it. Formally, \[f\text{ is common}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \forall P\in\mathcal P(\Phi),\ f\in P\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \Phi\models f.\] Equivalently, \(f\) belongs to the intersection \(\bigcap_{P\in\mathcal P(\Phi)}P\), or the augmented constraint \(\Phi\land\neg f\) is unsatisfiable. The nonvoidness assumption separates genuine commonality from vacuous entailment by an inconsistent model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In a nonvoid model, a feature is common when every valid product selects it, equivalently when the model entails that feature.
knowledge_statements.title: Feature Commonality

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The universal-membership definition and its entailment and unsatisfiability equivalents are correct for a nonvoid Boolean model. Because feature commonality terminology can also denote a quantitative measure in feature-model literature, a domain source with a specific locator is required.

children.title: Feature Variability
children.top_down_role: Analysis of feature differences across valid products.

assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a finite set of Boolean features.
\(\mathcal P(\Phi)\neq\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\) is variable exactly when both \(\Phi\land f\) and \(\Phi\land\neg f\) are satisfiable.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: feature variability requires realizable selected and unselected states
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic variability of one Boolean feature across the products of a fixed nonvoid model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A feature \(f\in F\) is variable in \(\Phi\) when its selection status differs between valid products. Thus \[f\text{ is variable}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \exists P,Q\in\mathcal P(\Phi): f\in P\ \land\ f\notin Q.\] Equivalently, both \(\Phi\land f\) and \(\Phi\land\neg f\) are satisfiable. Under the nonvoidness assumption, variability is the complement of being forced selected or forced unselected; it concerns semantic product-space behavior rather than whether the feature is drawn as optional in a syntactic model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feature is variable when some valid product selects it and another valid product omits it; both feature states must be feasible.
knowledge_statements.title: Feature Variability

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The selected-and-unselected realizability condition is internally consistent and matches the intended semantic status taxonomy. No inspectable source establishes that this exact notion is called feature variability in the target configuration formalism.

children.title: Dead Feature Analysis
children.top_down_role: Analysis of features absent from every valid product.

assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a finite set of Boolean features.
\(\Phi\) is a satisfiable propositional configuration constraint over \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Unsatisfiability of \(\Phi\land f\) certifies that \(f\) is dead.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: dead-feature analysis reduces to unsatisfiability under forced selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic deadness in a satisfiable Boolean configuration model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f\in F\), dead-feature analysis asks whether selection of \(f\) is impossible in every valid product. The equivalent predicates are \[\forall P\in\mathcal P(\Phi),\ f\notin P\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \Phi\models\neg f\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \Phi\land f\text{ is unsatisfiable}.\] Hence a sound, verifier-accepted refutation of \(\Phi\land f\) certifies that \(f\) is dead. Requiring \(\Phi\) itself to be satisfiable prevents all features of a void model from being classified as dead merely by vacuous entailment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feature is dead when no valid product can select it; a refutation of the model with that feature forced true certifies deadness.
knowledge_statements.title: Dead Feature Analysis

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The dead-feature predicate and refutation certificate are correct for a satisfiable Boolean configuration model, and certificate is a suitable role for this analysis leaf. A feature-model source and a source for the accepted proof-certificate formulation are absent.

children.title: False-Optional Feature Analysis
children.top_down_role: Analysis of nominally optional features present in every valid product.

assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a finite set of Boolean features.
\(\Phi\) is a satisfiable propositional configuration constraint over \(F\).
The feature-model formalism identifies \(p\in F\) as the parent of a syntactically optional feature \(f\in F\).
\(\Phi\land p\) is satisfiable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Unsatisfiability of \(\Phi\land p\land\neg f\) certifies that \(f\) is false-optional relative to the reachable parent context \(p\).

notation.meaning: Reachable parent feature of the analyzed feature.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: false optionality compares syntactic optionality with semantic implication from a reachable parent context
feature-model formalism must specify parent and optional-edge semantics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parent-relative false optionality with an explicitly reachable parent; root-relative conventions may instead reduce the test to global commonality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\in F\) be declared optional under parent \(p\in F\), and assume \(\Phi\land p\) is satisfiable. The feature \(f\) is false-optional relative to \(p\) when global constraints force \(f\) whenever the reachable parent \(p\) is selected: \[\Phi\models(p\rightarrow f)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \Phi\land p\land\neg f\text{ is unsatisfiable}.\] A sound, verifier-accepted refutation of \(\Phi\land p\land\neg f\) certifies this parent-relative false optionality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A syntactically optional child is false-optional relative to a reachable parent when global constraints force the child whenever that parent is selected; refuting parent-selected and child-omitted certifies this.
knowledge_statements.title: False-Optional Feature Analysis

children.title: Conditional Feature Availability
children.top_down_role: Analysis of features available only under specified selections.

assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a finite set of Boolean features.
\(\Phi\) is a satisfiable propositional configuration constraint over \(F\).
\(C\) is a propositional context over \(F\).
\(f\in F\) is the feature under analysis.
\(\Phi\land C\) is satisfiable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\) is available under \(C\) exactly when \(\Phi\land C\land f\) is satisfiable.

notation.meaning: Feature whose contextual availability is tested.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: contextual availability is satisfiability after conjoining a realizable context and the requested feature
availability terminology varies across configuration formalisms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Contextual semantic availability restricted to realizable contexts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a feature \(f\in F\) and a context formula \(C\), assume \(\Phi\land C\) is satisfiable. The feature is available under \(C\) when at least one valid product satisfying \(C\) selects \(f\): \[\exists P\in\mathcal P(\Phi): v_P\models C\ \land\ f\in P\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \Phi\land C\land f\text{ is satisfiable}.\] It is forced under \(C\) when \(\Phi\land C\models f\), and unavailable under \(C\) when \(\Phi\land C\land f\) is unsatisfiable. These cases distinguish possible, necessary, and impossible contextual selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Within a realizable context, a feature is available if some valid product satisfying that context selects it; satisfiability gives the exact test.
knowledge_statements.title: Conditional Feature Availability

children.title: Configuration Model Relation Calculus
children.top_down_role: Comparative analyses between configuration knowledge bases or product families.

children.title: Model Equivalence
children.top_down_role: Comparison of configuration models admitting the same products.

assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a common finite feature vocabulary.
\(\Phi_1\) and \(\Phi_2\) are propositional configuration constraints over \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Phi_1\equiv\Phi_2\) exactly when \(\mathcal P(\Phi_1)=\mathcal P(\Phi_2)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: logical equivalence over a fixed vocabulary is equality of satisfying assignments and hence product spaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic equivalence over the same Boolean feature vocabulary; auxiliary-variable encodings require projection before comparison.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The configuration models \(\Phi_1\) and \(\Phi_2\) are equivalent over \(F\) when they admit exactly the same products: \[\Phi_1\equiv_F\Phi_2\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \forall v:F\to\{0,1\},\ (v\models\Phi_1\leftrightarrow v\models\Phi_2)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \mathcal P(\Phi_1)=\mathcal P(\Phi_2).\] Equivalently, the exclusive-or formula \((\Phi_1\land\neg\Phi_2)\lor(\Phi_2\land\neg\Phi_1)\) is unsatisfiable. If either representation contains auxiliary variables, equivalence must instead compare the projections of its satisfying assignments onto the shared vocabulary \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two configuration models are equivalent when they admit exactly the same products over their shared feature vocabulary.
knowledge_statements.title: Model Equivalence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Equality of product sets is the correct semantic equivalence relation over a fixed vocabulary, and the auxiliary-variable projection caveat is appropriate. No inspectable configuration-model source supports the selected terminology and projection convention.

children.title: Model Implication
children.top_down_role: Comparison of constraints entailed across configuration models.

assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a common finite feature vocabulary.
\(\Phi_1\) and \(\Phi_2\) are propositional configuration constraints over \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Phi_1\models\Phi_2\) exactly when \(\mathcal P(\Phi_1)\subseteq\mathcal P(\Phi_2)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: propositional implication is inclusion of satisfying-assignment sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic implication over a fixed Boolean vocabulary, with the antecedent model providing the smaller product space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Model \(\Phi_1\) implies model \(\Phi_2\) over \(F\) when every valuation satisfying \(\Phi_1\) also satisfies \(\Phi_2\): \[\Phi_1\models_F\Phi_2\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \forall v:F\to\{0,1\},\ (v\models\Phi_1\Rightarrow v\models\Phi_2)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \mathcal P(\Phi_1)\subseteq\mathcal P(\Phi_2).\] Equivalently, \(\Phi_1\land\neg\Phi_2\) is unsatisfiable. A satisfying assignment of that formula is a counterexample product showing failure of implication; a sound refutation certifies implication.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One model implies another when every product valid for the first is also valid for the second; a counterexample is a product satisfying only the first.
knowledge_statements.title: Model Implication

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The implication direction, product-space inclusion, counterexample, and refutation characterizations are mathematically consistent. A source with a specific locator is required to establish this as the intended configuration-model relation.

children.title: Model Refinement
children.top_down_role: Comparison of models linked by strengthened configuration knowledge.

assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a common finite feature vocabulary.
\(\Phi\) and \(\Psi\) are propositional configuration constraints over \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Psi\) refines \(\Phi\) exactly when \(\mathcal P(\Psi)\subseteq\mathcal P(\Phi)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: constraint strengthening refines a model by restricting its admissible products
refinement direction varies by convention and requires a domain source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Product-space refinement by constraint strengthening; this record fixes the refining model as the one with fewer admissible products.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The model \(\Psi\) is a refinement of \(\Phi\) over \(F\) when every product admitted by \(\Psi\) is admitted by \(\Phi\): \[\Psi\preceq\Phi\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \Psi\models_F\Phi\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \mathcal P(\Psi)\subseteq\mathcal P(\Phi).\] The refinement is strict when additionally \(\mathcal P(\Psi)\neq\mathcal P(\Phi)\), and it is conservative with respect to existence only if \(\mathcal P(\Psi)\neq\varnothing\). Thus adding constraints always yields a refinement, although it may yield a void refinement unless consistency is checked separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A model refines another when it admits only products already admitted by the original; strict refinement removes at least one product.
knowledge_statements.title: Model Refinement

children.title: Comparative Product-Space Inclusion
children.top_down_role: Containment relationships between valid product spaces.

assumptions_latex: \(F_1\) and \(F_2\) are finite feature vocabularies.
\(S=F_1\cap F_2\) is the comparison vocabulary.
\(\Phi_i\) is a propositional configuration constraint over \(F_i\) for \(i\in\{1,2\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Projected inclusion holds exactly when \(\pi_S(\mathcal P(\Phi_1))\subseteq\pi_S(\mathcal P(\Phi_2))\).

notation.meaning: Feature vocabularies and their shared comparison vocabulary.
Projection of a product or product set onto the shared vocabulary.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: product spaces on different vocabularies are comparable after projection to a declared shared vocabulary
projection convention and treatment of nonshared features require a domain source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inclusion between models with possibly different vocabularies, compared through existential projection onto their shared features.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(P\subseteq F_i\), define its projection by \(\pi_S(P)=P\cap S\), and extend this pointwise to product sets. Model \(\Phi_1\) has projected product-space inclusion in \(\Phi_2\) on \(S\) when \[\pi_S(\mathcal P(\Phi_1))\subseteq\pi_S(\mathcal P(\Phi_2)).\] Equivalently, for every valuation of \(F_1\) satisfying \(\Phi_1\), some valuation of \(F_2\) satisfies \(\Phi_2\) and agrees with it on every feature in \(S\). When \(F_1=F_2=S\), this condition reduces to ordinary model implication.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Product spaces on different feature vocabularies are inclusively comparable after projection: every shared-feature pattern of the first must be realizable by the second.
knowledge_statements.title: Comparative Product-Space Inclusion

children.title: Configuration-Space Quantitative Exploration
children.top_down_role: Quantitative characterization and representative exploration of configuration spaces.

children.title: Configuration Counting
children.top_down_role: Cardinality analysis of valid configuration spaces.

knowledge_statements.title: Configuration Counting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact and projected counting for finite constraint-defined configuration spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\prod_{i=1}^{n}D_i\) with finite domains \(D_i\), let \(C:X\to\{0,1\}\) be the conjunction of all configuration constraints, and let \(S=\{x\in X:C(x)=1\}\). The configuration count is \(N=|S|=\sum_{x\in X}C(x)\). For a coordinate set \(J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\), the projected configuration count is \(N_J=|\{x_J:x\in S\}|\); assignments differing only outside \(J\) are then counted once.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Configuration counting measures either all feasible assignments or the distinct assignments visible on a selected set of variables.
assumptions_latex: \(n<\infty\) and every \(D_i\) is finite.
\(C(x)=1\) exactly when \(x\) satisfies every configuration constraint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N=\sum_{x\in X}C(x)\), and \(N_J=|\{x_J:x\in S\}|\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: finite model counting and projected model counting definitions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite exact-count and projected-count definitions are mathematically precise and fit Configuration Counting, but no inspectable source with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Configuration Sampling
children.top_down_role: Selection of valid configurations from large product spaces.

knowledge_statements.title: Configuration Sampling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sampling feasible finite-domain configurations from a specified target distribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a finite feasible set \(S\), weights \(w:S\to\mathbb{R}_{\geq0}\) with \(Z=\sum_{x\in S}w(x)>0\), and sample size \(m\), define \(p(x)=w(x)/Z\). Initialize \(T=()\). For \(k=1,\ldots,m\), draw \(X_k\) independently from \(p\) using an exact weighted model-sampling oracle and append \(X_k\) to \(T\). Stop after \(m\) draws and return \(T=(X_1,\ldots,X_m)\). Uniform configuration sampling is the case \(w(x)=1\) for every \(x\in S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact sampler repeatedly draws feasible configurations from a normalized weight distribution; constant weights yield uniform samples.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is finite and nonempty.
\(w(x)\geq0\) and \(\sum_{x\in S}w(x)>0\).
An exact weighted model-sampling oracle is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Pr[X_k=x]=w(x)/Z\) for every \(x\in S\) and each \(k\).

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

review_flags: confirm that the cited restricted-sampling section supports constraint-defined configuration sampling

source_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm correctly specifies independent exact weighted sampling, but the cited restricted-sampling section is not shown to support exact weighted model sampling over constraint-defined configurations. The oracle assumption and distributional conclusion require a directly relevant source.

children.title: Diversity Analysis
children.top_down_role: Characterization of differences among valid configurations.

knowledge_statements.title: Diversity Analysis
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Metric summaries of dispersion within a finite collection of feasible configurations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((S,d)\) be a finite metric space of feasible configurations and let \(T=\{x^1,\ldots,x^m\}\subseteq S\) with \(m\geq2\). Its mean pairwise diversity and minimum-separation diversity are respectively \[D_{\mathrm{avg}}(T)=\frac{2}{m(m-1)}\sum_{1\leq i<j\leq m}d(x^i,x^j),\qquad D_{\min}(T)=\min_{1\leq i<j\leq m}d(x^i,x^j).\] Larger values indicate greater dispersion under the declared metric; comparisons are meaningful only when the same metric and normalization are used.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Diversity can be represented by average pairwise distance and minimum separation among selected feasible configurations.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is a finite feasible configuration set.
\(d:S\times S\to\mathbb{R}_{\geq0}\) is a fixed metric.
\(T\subseteq S\) and \(|T|=m\geq2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_{\mathrm{avg}}(T)\) and \(D_{\min}(T)\) quantify average and worst-pair dispersion under \(d\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The two metric summaries are internally consistent and the representation kind fits Diversity Analysis, but no configuration-diversity source with an inspectable locator is supplied.

children.title: Representative Coverage
children.top_down_role: Coverage criteria for representative configuration subsets.

knowledge_statements.title: Representative Coverage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Metric coverage of the feasible space by a finite representative subset.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((S,d)\) be a nonempty finite metric space of feasible configurations and let \(R\subseteq S\) be nonempty. The covering radius of \(R\) is \[\rho(R;S)=\max_{x\in S}\min_{r\in R}d(x,r).\] For \(\varepsilon\geq0\), the set \(R\) provides representative \(\varepsilon\)-coverage precisely when \(\rho(R;S)\leq\varepsilon\), equivalently when every \(x\in S\) has some \(r\in R\) satisfying \(d(x,r)\leq\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Representatives cover the configuration space at radius epsilon when every feasible configuration lies within epsilon of a representative.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is finite and nonempty.
\(d\) is a metric on \(S\).
\(\varnothing\neq R\subseteq S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R\) has \(\varepsilon\)-coverage if and only if \(\rho(R;S)\leq\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: covering radius of R in S

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The covering-radius definition precisely expresses representative epsilon-coverage and fits the leaf, but it has no cited source with a specific locator.

children.title: Configuration-Space Anomaly Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Redundant relations, unreachable options, contradictory modules, and unintended implications.

children.title: Constraint Redundancy
children.top_down_role: Configuration relations that add no restriction to valid products.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint Redundancy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic redundancy of one constraint relative to the remaining configuration model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be the assignment space and let \(F= igwedge_{i=1}^{m}c_i\). Constraint \(c_j\) is redundant in \(F\) exactly when removing it preserves the feasible set: \[\{x\in X:F(x)\}=\left\{x\in X: igwedge_{i
eq j}c_i(x)ight\}.\] Equivalently, \(c_j\) is redundant when \( igwedge_{i
eq j}c_i\models c_j\), or when \(\left( igwedge_{i
eq j}c_iight)\wedge
eg c_j\) is unsatisfiable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constraint is redundant when all remaining constraints already imply it, so its removal changes no feasible configuration.
assumptions_latex: Each \(c_i\) is a predicate on the same assignment space \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(c_j\) is redundant if and only if \(\bigwedge_{i\neq j}c_i\models c_j\).
review_flags: confirm explicit support for semantic constraint redundancy

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The semantic redundancy equivalences are mathematically correct and the condition kind fits the anomaly leaf. The generic constraint-programming locator is not established as support for semantic constraint redundancy and its entailment test.

children.title: Unreachable Options
children.top_down_role: Configuration choices excluded from every valid product.

assumptions_latex: \(F\) denotes all configuration constraints.
\(a\in D_v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v=a\) is unreachable if and only if \(F\wedge(v=a)\) is unsatisfiable.
review_flags: confirm explicit support for option reachability testing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Option values that occur in no globally feasible configuration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(x)\) be the complete configuration constraint predicate over assignment space \(X\), let \(v\) be a configuration variable, and let \(a\in D_v\). The option \(v=a\) is unreachable exactly when \[\nexists x\in X:\ F(x)\wedge(x_v=a).\] Equivalently, \(F\wedge(v=a)\) is unsatisfiable. If \(F\) itself is satisfiable, this condition identifies an unavailable option rather than global inconsistency of the entire model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An option is unreachable when fixing its variable to that value makes the complete configuration model unsatisfiable.
knowledge_statements.title: Unreachable Options

children.title: Contradictory Modules
children.top_down_role: Configuration modules whose combined knowledge is inconsistent.

knowledge_statements.title: Contradictory Modules
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint inconsistency between individually consistent configuration modules.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let modules \(M_1\) and \(M_2\) be conjunctions of constraints over compatible assignment spaces, with shared variables interpreted identically. They are contradictory when \(M_1\) and \(M_2\) are each satisfiable but their conjunction is not: \[\operatorname{SAT}(M_1)\wedge\operatorname{SAT}(M_2)\wedge\neg\operatorname{SAT}(M_1\wedge M_2).\] More generally, a family \(\{M_i:i\in I\}\) is jointly contradictory when every module is satisfiable and \(\bigwedge_{i\in I}M_i\) is unsatisfiable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Modules are contradictory when each admits configurations alone but their combined constraints admit none.
assumptions_latex: Module predicates use compatible domains for every shared variable.
Each module is considered with its internal constraints included.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Contradiction is certified by satisfiable modules whose conjunction is unsatisfiable.

notation.meaning: predicate asserting that M is satisfiable

review_flags: confirm explicit treatment of modular inconsistency

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record clearly defines pairwise and family-level joint inconsistency while excluding internally inconsistent modules, and condition is an appropriate kind. The cited generic CP section is not demonstrated to support modular contradiction analysis.

children.title: Unintended Implications
children.top_down_role: Unexpected configuration consequences entailed by the model.

knowledge_statements.title: Unintended Implications
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logically entailed configuration restrictions absent from the declared intended consequences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be a configuration theory and let \(q\) be a restriction on configurations. Relative to a declared set \(I\) of intended consequences, \(q\) is an unintended implication when \[F\models q\quad\text{and}\quad q\notin I.\] The entailment is testable by checking that \(F\wedge\neg q\) is unsatisfiable. Whether the implication is unintended is not purely logical: it depends on the externally supplied specification \(I\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A restriction is an unintended implication when the model logically forces it but the declared requirements do not identify it as intended.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) and \(q\) are predicates over the same configuration space.
\(I\) is an externally declared set of intended consequences.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q\) is unintended relative to \(I\) when \(F\models q\) and \(q\notin I\).
review_flags: intent classification requires an external requirements specification
confirm explicit support for implication analysis

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record correctly separates logical entailment from the externally determined judgment of intent, and it fits the anomaly leaf. The cited generic CP section is not established as support for this implication-analysis formulation or the external intended-consequence set.

children.title: Configuration Process Regime Family
children.top_down_role: Configuration processes distinguished by interaction pattern, organizational ownership, and evolution over time.

children.title: Interactive Configuration
children.top_down_role: Incremental user decisions with immediate consistency and completion feedback.

knowledge_statements.title: Interactive Configuration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incremental decisions with immediate consistency and completion feedback.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a base constraint theory \(F\), initialize the current decisions as \(A_0=\top\). At interaction step \(t\), receive a proposed decision \(d_t\) and query satisfiability of \(F\wedge A_{t-1}\wedge d_t\). If satisfiable, set \(A_t=A_{t-1}\wedge d_t\); otherwise reject \(d_t\) and set \(A_t=A_{t-1}\). Report all values \(v=a\) for which \(F\wedge A_t\models(v=a)\), and report completion when \(A_t\) assigns every required variable. On termination, return any model of \(F\wedge A_t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Interactive configuration accepts only extendable user decisions, reports forced values after each step, and returns a feasible completion.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is satisfiable initially.
Each proposed decision is a predicate over configuration variables.
A satisfiability oracle and model extractor are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accepted state satisfies \(\operatorname{SAT}(F\wedge A_t)\), and the returned assignment satisfies \(F\wedge A_t\).
review_flags: confirm support for incremental interactive configuration semantics

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The incremental accept-or-reject procedure matches the stated Interactive Configuration role, and algorithm is appropriate for this operational statement. The generic CP locator is not shown to support the specific incremental semantics, forced-value reporting, and completion behavior.

children.title: Staged Configuration
children.top_down_role: Sequential configuration across abstraction levels, roles, or lifecycle phases.

knowledge_statements.title: Staged Configuration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential configuration across ordered abstraction levels, roles, or lifecycle phases.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a satisfiable base theory \(F\), ordered stages \(1,\ldots,k\), stage decision spaces \(D_t\), and accepted decisions \(A_0=\top\), stage \(t\) selects \(d_t\in D_t\) satisfying \(\operatorname{SAT}(F\wedge A_{t-1}\wedge d_t)\), then commits \(A_t=A_{t-1}\wedge d_t\). A stage may expose only variables assigned to that stage, but its consistency test includes all committed decisions. After stage \(k\), return a complete model of \(F\wedge A_k\); if no admissible \(d_t\) exists, report stage failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Staged configuration commits decisions in order while testing every stage against the base model and all earlier commitments.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is initially satisfiable.
Stages and their admissible decision spaces are ordered.
A satisfiability oracle and final model extractor are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If every stage succeeds, the returned completion satisfies \(F\wedge\bigwedge_{t=1}^{k}d_t\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: sequential commitment with global consistency checking

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm matches sequential configuration with globally checked commitments and fits the Staged Configuration role, but no authoritative staged-configuration source with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Multi-Authority Configuration Coordination
children.top_down_role: Configuration with multiple viewpoints, authorities, or separated knowledge sources.

children.title: Distributed Configuration
children.top_down_role: Configuration across separated knowledge sources or subsystems.

assumptions_latex: Every shared variable has a common domain and interpretation across agents.
Each \(S_i\) contains exactly the assignments locally feasible for agent \(i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Global feasibility is equivalent to membership in \(\Join_{i=1}^{m}S_i\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: relational join representation of distributed constraint satisfaction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global configuration represented by coupled local theories and shared-variable agreements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let agents \(i=1,\ldots,m\) control local variables \(X_i\) and local feasible sets \(S_i\subseteq D_{X_i}\). A distributed configuration is a tuple \((x^1,\ldots,x^m)\) satisfying \[x^i\in S_i\quad\text{for all }i,\qquad x^i_v=x^j_v\quad\text{for every }v\in X_i\cap X_j.\] Thus the global feasible set is the natural join \(S=\Join_{i=1}^{m}S_i\). Additional cross-agent constraints may be represented as further relations included in the same join.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A distributed configuration joins locally feasible assignments that agree on every variable shared by multiple agents.
knowledge_statements.title: Distributed Configuration

children.title: Multiuser Configuration
children.top_down_role: Configuration involving choices from multiple participants.

knowledge_statements.title: Multiuser Configuration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Configuration formed from compatible decisions submitted by multiple identified users.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be the base configuration theory, let users be indexed by \(U=\{1,\ldots,m\}\), and let \(A_u\) be user \(u\)'s submitted decision predicate. A multiuser decision profile is jointly admissible when \[\operatorname{SAT}\!\left(F\wedge\bigwedge_{u\in U}A_u\right).\] A multiuser configuration is any complete assignment \(x\) satisfying \(F(x)\) and \(A_u(x)\) for every \(u\in U\). If the conjunction is unsatisfiable, no jointly acceptable configuration exists without revising at least one submitted decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multiuser configuration is a complete feasible assignment satisfying the submitted decisions of every participating user.
assumptions_latex: All user predicates refer to compatible configuration variables and domains.
\(F\) contains the shared base constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\) is a multiuser configuration exactly when \(F(x)\wedge\bigwedge_{u\in U}A_u(x)\) holds.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: joint satisfiability semantics for multiple users' decisions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The joint-satisfiability definition is precise and fits Multiuser Configuration, but no authoritative multiuser-configuration source with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Authority-Aware Coordination
children.top_down_role: Coordination of decisions subject to distinct ownership or authority.

knowledge_statements.title: Authority-Aware Coordination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Admissibility condition for coordinated assignments under explicit decision authority.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let agents be indexed by \(A\), configuration variables by \(X\), and feasible assignments by \(F\subseteq\prod_{i\in X}D_i\). Each agent \(a\in A\) has authority set \(X_a\subseteq X\), and each variable has an approval family \(Q_i\subseteq 2^A\). A proposal \(x\in F\) is authority-admissible precisely when, for every changed variable \(i\), its approving agents contain some authorized quorum: \[\forall i\in\Delta(x,x^0),\quad \exists Q\in Q_i:\ Q\subseteq\{a\in A:i\in X_a\text{ and }a\text{ approves }x_i\}.\] Thus feasibility alone does not make an unapproved cross-authority change admissible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible configuration is authority-admissible when every changed variable is approved by an authorized quorum assigned to that variable.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) and \(X\) are finite.
\(x^0\) is the accepted baseline configuration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\in F\) and every \(i\in\Delta(x,x^0)\) has an authorized approving quorum.

notation.meaning: variables over which agent a has authority
acceptable approval quorums for variable i
variables whose values differ from the baseline

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the Authority-Aware Coordination leaf and is internally coherent, but the quorum-based authority semantics are a specialized modeling choice with no cited source. A source must establish the authority sets, approval families, and quorum admissibility interpretation.

children.title: Viewpoint Conflict Management
children.top_down_role: Conflicts arising from differing participant viewpoints.

knowledge_statements.title: Viewpoint Conflict Management
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite conflict-diagnosis and correction procedure for stakeholder constraint sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input finite viewpoint constraint sets \(C_1,\ldots,C_m\), immutable domain constraints \(B\), and nonnegative relaxation costs \(w(c)\). Initialize \(R=\varnothing\). While \(B\cup\bigcup_j(C_j\setminus R)\) is unsatisfiable, obtain an unsatisfiable core \(U\), choose \(c\in U\setminus B\) minimizing an agreed cost-and-authority ordering, and set \(R\leftarrow R\cup\{c\}\). Stop when the remaining constraints are satisfiable or when every current core lies inside \(B\). Return a satisfying configuration and the disclosed relaxations \(R\), or return the immutable core as an unresolved conflict certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly diagnose a conflicting core and relax an authorized viewpoint constraint until a configuration exists or an immutable conflict is exposed.
assumptions_latex: All constraint sets are finite.
Constraint satisfiability and unsatisfiable-core extraction are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B\cup\bigcup_j(C_j\setminus R)\) is satisfiable, or an unsatisfiable core contained in \(B\) is returned.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits a conflict-management procedure, and finite termination is plausible because one remaining nonimmutable constraint is removed per iteration. However, the core-guided relaxation procedure, authority ordering, and returned immutable-core certificate have no cited support.

children.title: Configuration Version Transition Regimes
children.top_down_role: Migration of products and decisions when configuration knowledge changes.

children.title: Configuration-Model Evolution
children.top_down_role: Changes to configuration knowledge across model versions.

knowledge_statements.title: Configuration-Model Evolution
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Versioned constraint-model representation with explicit symbol and value translation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent version \(t\) by \(M_t=(X_t,D_t,C_t)\), whose solution set is \(S_t=\{x\in\prod_{i\in X_t}D_{t,i}:x\models C_t\}\). Evolution to \(t+1\) consists of \(M_{t+1}\) together with a partial translation \(\tau_t\) mapping retained variables and their values. The induced partial product translation is \(T_t(x)_{\tau_t(i)}=\tau_{t,i}(x_i)\) whenever both mappings are defined. Added, removed, split, merged, or reinterpreted symbols are precisely those not represented by this direct translation and therefore require explicit migration rules.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Model evolution is a new constraint model plus explicit partial mappings for variables and values retained across versions.
assumptions_latex: Each model has finite variables and domains.
Variable and value translations are type-correct where defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_t\), \(M_{t+1}\), and \(T_t\) jointly represent the version transition.

source_refs.locator: 1.1 The concept of a model p. 3

source_witnesses.locator: 1.1 The concept of a model p. 3

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits the leaf, but Williams section 1.1 supports modeling only in general and does not establish the proposed partial variable/value translation semantics or the treatment of split, merged, and reinterpreted symbols. The mathematical version-transition representation therefore needs a direct source.

children.title: Product Migration
children.top_down_role: Transfer of existing products to revised configuration models.

knowledge_statements.title: Product Migration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimum-change migration of a complete product between model versions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input an old valid product \(x\in S_t\), the new solution set \(S_{t+1}\), a partial translation \(T_t(x)\), and a nonnegative migration cost \(d(y,T_t(x))\) defined on translated coordinates and required additions. Compute \[y^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in S_{t+1}} d(y,T_t(x)).\] If the feasible set is nonempty, return \(y^*\) together with the changed, deleted, and newly assigned coordinates. If \(S_{t+1}=\varnothing\), report that migration is impossible; if the minimum is not attained, report that no optimal migrated product exists under the chosen cost model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Migrate an old product by finding a valid new-version product of minimum declared change cost, with all changes reported.
assumptions_latex: \(x\in S_t\).
The migration cost is well-defined and nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y^*\in S_{t+1}\) minimizes \(d(y,T_t(x))\), when an optimizer exists.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind is appropriate for Product Migration, and the optimization statement is coherent when the cost is defined on every candidate successor product. No source supports minimum-change optimization as the defining migration procedure or the stated reporting behavior.

children.title: Decision Migration
children.top_down_role: Transfer of prior configuration choices across model changes.

knowledge_statements.title: Decision Migration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Migration of recorded configuration decisions without requiring a complete old product.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a decision record be a consistent partial assignment \(p:I\to\bigcup_{i\in I}D_{t,i}\), where \(I\subseteq X_t\). Under a partial version translation \(T_t\), its direct migration is the partial assignment \(p'\) containing exactly the translated pairs \((\tau_t(i),\tau_{t,i}(p(i)))\) for which both mappings are defined and mutually consistent. A completion \(y\in S_{t+1}\) respects the migrated decisions when \(y\) extends \(p'\). Unmapped, multiply mapped, or inconsistent decisions form the exception set and require revision rather than silent transfer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Decision migration translates a partial assignment, preserves consistent mapped choices, and explicitly separates choices requiring revision.
assumptions_latex: \(p\) is a consistent partial assignment in the old model.
Translations are type-correct where defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A respecting migrated configuration is any \(y\in S_{t+1}\) satisfying \(p'\subseteq y\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits the leaf and correctly distinguishes partial decisions from complete products. The exact direct-transfer rule, exception-set semantics, and treatment of multiply mapped decisions are specialized and uncited.

children.title: Cross-Version Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Compatibility relationships between successive model versions.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Version Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility predicate for old and new configurations under declared correspondence constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in S_t\), \(y\in S_u\), and let \(R_{t,u}\subseteq S_t\times S_u\) encode all required correspondences between retained features, identifiers, interfaces, and values. The pair is cross-version compatible exactly when \[(x,y)\in R_{t,u}.\] For a functional translation \(T_{t,u}\) on shared coordinates, this specializes to \(y_j=T_{t,u,j}(x_i)\) for every declared correspondence \(i\mapsto j\), together with any explicit coexistence constraints. Compatibility is directional unless the declared relation is symmetric.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two versioned configurations are compatible exactly when they satisfy every declared cross-version correspondence and coexistence constraint.
assumptions_latex: \(x\in S_t\) and \(y\in S_u\).
\(R_{t,u}\) is explicitly defined and type-correct.

notation.meaning: valid configurations in the two versions
functional translation when one is available

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits Cross-Version Compatibility, but defining compatibility as membership in an otherwise arbitrary declared relation is framework-specific. The functional specialization, coexistence constraints, and directional interpretation require a domain source.

children.title: Configuration Failure Resolution System
children.top_down_role: Conflict, diagnosis, correction, explanation, recommendation, and reconfiguration structures for inconsistent knowledge or requirements.

children.title: Configuration Failure Sources
children.top_down_role: Failure regimes distinguished by whether inconsistency arises in knowledge, requirements, partial decisions, viewpoints, or evolution.

children.title: Configuration Knowledge-Base Inconsistency
children.top_down_role: Contradictions and anomalies internal to product-domain knowledge.

knowledge_statements.title: Configuration Knowledge-Base Inconsistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Satisfiability-based criterion for contradictions internal to configuration knowledge.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\{c_1,c_2,\ldots,c_m\}\) be the product-domain constraints over configuration assignments \(\Omega\), excluding user requirements and provisional decisions. The configuration knowledge base is inconsistent exactly when \[\operatorname{Sol}(K)=\{x\in\Omega:\forall c\in K,x\models c\}=\varnothing.\] This criterion concerns joint inconsistency: individual constraints may each be satisfiable while their conjunction is not. If \(\operatorname{Sol}(K)\neq\varnothing\), any failure caused only after adding requirements or decisions is not an internal knowledge-base inconsistency.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A configuration knowledge base is inconsistent when its domain constraints have no joint satisfying assignment, even before user requirements are added.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is finite.
All constraints in \(K\) have a common assignment semantics over \(\Omega\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K\) is inconsistent if and only if \(\operatorname{Sol}(K)=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: assignments satisfying every constraint in K

children.title: User-Requirement Inconsistency
children.top_down_role: Conflicts among requirements or between requirements and domain constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: User-Requirement Inconsistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes internally conflicting requirements from incompatibility with domain knowledge.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\) be satisfiable domain constraints and \(R\) a finite set of user requirements over the same assignment space \(\Omega\). The requirements are configuration-inconsistent exactly when \[\operatorname{Sol}(K\cup R)=\varnothing.\] They are internally inconsistent when \(\operatorname{Sol}(R)=\varnothing\); they are domain-incompatible when \(\operatorname{Sol}(R)\neq\varnothing\) but \(\operatorname{Sol}(K\cup R)=\varnothing\). This separation attributes failure without assuming that every combined inconsistency originates inside the requirement set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Requirements are inconsistent for configuration when they cannot be jointly satisfied with the domain model; they may conflict internally or only with that model.
assumptions_latex: \(\operatorname{Sol}(K)\neq\varnothing\).
\(K\) and \(R\) share a common assignment semantics.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R\) is configuration-inconsistent exactly when \(\operatorname{Sol}(K\cup R)=\varnothing\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The combined satisfiability condition is mathematically coherent and fits the leaf, but the cited general constraint-programming section does not directly support the asserted attribution split between internal requirement inconsistency and domain incompatibility. That distinction materially affects the local meaning and needs a direct source.

children.title: Partial-Configuration Dead Ends
children.top_down_role: Accepted choices that eliminate every valid completion.

knowledge_statements.title: Partial-Configuration Dead Ends
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extendability-based definition of a dead-end partial configuration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\) be configuration constraints over complete assignments \(S=\operatorname{Sol}(K)\), and let \(p\) be a consistent partial assignment. Its completion set is \[\operatorname{Ext}_K(p)=\{x\in S:p\subseteq x\}.\] The partial configuration \(p\) is a dead end exactly when \(\operatorname{Ext}_K(p)=\varnothing\). It is a choice-induced dead end relative to its immediate predecessor \(q\subset p\) when \(\operatorname{Ext}_K(q)\neq\varnothing\) but \(\operatorname{Ext}_K(p)=\varnothing\), identifying the newly accepted choices as eliminating every valid completion.
