knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A partial configuration is a dead end when no valid complete configuration extends it; a newly added choice may create that condition.
assumptions_latex: \(p\) assigns at most one value to each variable.
Complete validity is defined by \(K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p\) is a dead end if and only if \(\operatorname{Ext}_K(p)=\varnothing\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind and empty-extension criterion exactly fit the leaf. The cited partial-enumeration section may support search over partial assignments, but it does not inspectably support the configuration dead-end definition or the immediate-predecessor attribution; full direct support is needed.

children.title: Multi-Viewpoint Configuration Conflicts
children.top_down_role: Incompatibilities among stakeholder, subsystem, or organizational viewpoints.

knowledge_statements.title: Multi-Viewpoint Configuration Conflicts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint-satisfiability criterion for conflicts among separately coherent viewpoints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\) be satisfiable domain constraints and let \(V_1,\ldots,V_m\) be viewpoint constraint sets. A multi-viewpoint conflict exists exactly when \[\operatorname{Sol}\!\left(K\cup\bigcup_{j=1}^m V_j\right)=\varnothing.\] It is purely cross-viewpoint when every individual viewpoint is domain-consistent, \(\operatorname{Sol}(K\cup V_j)\neq\varnothing\) for all \(j\), but their union is inconsistent. A subfamily indexed by \(J\) is a minimal conflicting viewpoint family when its union with \(K\) is unsatisfiable and deleting any one index from \(J\) restores satisfiability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multi-viewpoint conflict occurs when viewpoint constraints are jointly impossible, even though each viewpoint may be individually compatible with the domain.
assumptions_latex: \(\operatorname{Sol}(K)\neq\varnothing\).
All viewpoint constraints share the configuration semantics of \(K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A conflict exists exactly when \(\operatorname{Sol}(K\cup\bigcup_j V_j)=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: index set of a viewpoint subfamily

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the failure-source leaf, and the joint-unsatisfiability and minimal-subfamily clauses are precise. No source establishes the viewpoint-set formalization or the distinction between general and purely cross-viewpoint conflict.

children.title: Evolution-Induced Invalidity
children.top_down_role: Previously valid products invalidated by changed components, rules, or requirements.

knowledge_statements.title: Evolution-Induced Invalidity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact boundary at which a formerly valid product fails under a successor model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in S_t\) be valid under model \(M_t\), and let \(T_t(x)\) be its defined translation into the assignment space of \(M_{t+1}\). Evolution-induced invalidity occurs exactly when \[x\in S_t,\qquad T_t(x)\text{ is defined},\qquad T_t(x)\notin S_{t+1}.\] Equivalently, some successor constraint \(c\in C_{t+1}\) is violated by \(T_t(x)\). If the translation is undefined because a component or value was removed, the failure is instead a translation gap until a migration rule assigns successor values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A formerly valid product becomes evolution-invalid when its defined successor translation violates at least one constraint of the new model.
assumptions_latex: \(x\in S_t\).
The direct translation \(T_t(x)\) is defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Evolution-induced invalidity holds if and only if \(T_t(x)\notin S_{t+1}\).

notation.meaning: valid configurations before and after evolution

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary kind is appropriate and the statement cleanly separates a defined but invalid translation from an undefined translation. That separation and the claimed equivalence with violation of a successor constraint depend on the uncited version-translation framework and require direct support.

children.title: Configuration Conflict-Correction Certificate System
children.top_down_role: Dual families of irreducible conflicts and minimal changes used to organize explanation and repair.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Consistency-Based Diagnosis of Configuration Knowledge Bases
top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Conflicts and diagnoses
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Consistency-Based Diagnosis of Configuration Knowledge Bases

children.title: Minimal Unsatisfiable Configuration Sets
children.top_down_role: Irreducible conflicting subsets drawn from model constraints, requirements, or decisions.

knowledge_statements.title: Minimal Unsatisfiable Configuration Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Subset-minimal conflicting sets of configuration constraints, requirements, or decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be a finite set containing configuration-model constraints, encoded requirements, and encoded decisions over a common assignment space. A set \(U\subseteq F\) is a minimal unsatisfiable configuration set exactly when \[\operatorname{Sol}(U)=\varnothing\quad\text{and}\quad \forall c\in U,\operatorname{Sol}(U\setminus\{c\})\neq\varnothing.\] Minimality is by set inclusion, not minimum cardinality. Consequently, every member of \(U\) is necessary for that particular conflict, although \(F\) may contain several distinct minimal unsatisfiable configuration sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A minimal unsatisfiable configuration set is jointly inconsistent but becomes satisfiable whenever any one of its constraints is removed.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is finite.
Every member of \(F\) has a common satisfiability semantics.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U\) is minimally unsatisfiable exactly when it is unsatisfiable and every proper one-element deletion is satisfiable.

notation.meaning: assignments satisfying all members of U

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind exactly fits the certificate-system leaf, and the finite-set formula correctly states subset-minimal unsatisfiability rather than minimum cardinality. Nevertheless, the record supplies no authoritative source or inspectable locator for the MUS definition, so it cannot pass source review.

children.title: Minimal Correction Sets
children.top_down_role: Minimal removals or relaxations restoring configuration feasibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Minimal Correction Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Subset-minimal relaxation of designated configuration constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\) be background constraints and \(C\) a finite set of removable configuration constraints, with \(B\cup C\) unsatisfiable. A set \(R\subseteq C\) is a minimal correction set if \(B\cup(C\setminus R)\) is satisfiable and, for every \(r\in R\), the set \(B\cup(C\setminus(R\setminus\{r\}))\) is unsatisfiable. Thus every member of \(R\) is necessary for the chosen correction, although another minimal correction set may have smaller cardinality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A minimal correction set is an inclusion-minimal collection of removable constraints whose deletion restores feasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is finite.
\(B\cup C\) is unsatisfiable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R\) is inclusion-minimal among sets whose removal makes the configuration satisfiable.
review_flags: Authoritative diagnosis reference and exact locator are absent from the supplied inventory.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is mathematically precise, distinguishes inclusion minimality from minimum cardinality, and fits the Minimal Correction Sets container. No source reference or inspectable diagnosis-specific locator is supplied, so the candidate cannot pass evidence review.

children.title: Conflict-Diagnosis Hitting-Set Duality
children.top_down_role: Structural relationship between conflict collections and candidate diagnoses.

children.title: Explicit Conflict-Driven Diagnosis
children.top_down_role: Diagnosis methods organized around enumerated or maintained conflicts.

knowledge_statements.title: Explicit Conflict-Driven Diagnosis
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagnosis by incrementally enumerating conflicts and solving a hitting-set problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input background constraints \(B\), removable constraints \(C\), and a satisfiability oracle. Initialize the conflict family \(\mathcal K:=\varnothing\). Repeatedly choose an inclusion-minimal hitting set \(D\subseteq C\) of \(\mathcal K\). If \(B\cup(C\setminus D)\) is satisfiable, output \(D\). Otherwise extract a conflict \(K\subseteq C\setminus D\) such that \(B\cup K\) is unsatisfiable, insert \(K\) into \(\mathcal K\), and continue. If minimal hitting sets are selected, the first returned set is a subset-minimal diagnosis relative to all generated conflicts.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maintain explicit conflicts, propose a minimal hitting set, test the corrected configuration, and add a new conflict whenever the proposal remains infeasible.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is finite.
The oracle decides satisfiability and can extract a conflict after an unsatisfiable query.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned \(D\) restores satisfiability and hits every generated conflict.
review_flags: Algorithm variant and termination claim require a diagnosis-specific source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conflict-maintenance and minimal-hitting-set procedure fits Explicit Conflict-Driven Diagnosis, and its stated output properties are plausible for finite C. A diagnosis-specific source is required to establish this precise algorithm variant, its conflict-extraction assumptions, and its termination and minimality guarantees.

children.title: Direct Diagnosis
children.top_down_role: Diagnosis methods seeking corrections without prior exhaustive conflict generation.

knowledge_statements.title: Direct Diagnosis
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle-guided search for a correction without exhaustive prior conflict enumeration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input background constraints \(B\), a finite removable set \(C\), and a satisfiability oracle. Search subsets \(D\subseteq C\) directly, querying whether \(B\cup(C\setminus D)\) is satisfiable. Prune any branch containing a previously found feasible correction when subset minimality is required. Once a feasible \(D\) is found, test each \(d\in D\); discard \(d\) whenever \(B\cup(C\setminus(D\setminus\{d\}))\) remains satisfiable. Stop when no element can be discarded, and output \(D\). Conflict enumeration is not a required preprocessing step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Search correction sets through feasibility queries, then delete redundant relaxed constraints until the diagnosis is subset-minimal.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is finite.
The oracle decides satisfiability of each queried constraint set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output \(D\) is a subset-minimal correction restoring satisfiability.
review_flags: A canonical direct-diagnosis algorithm and locator are needed.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The oracle-guided search and redundancy deletion fit Direct Diagnosis, and the finite-set deletion criterion supports subset minimality under monotone constraint satisfiability. The search procedure is presented as a synthesized algorithm without a canonical source or exact locator.

children.title: Conflict–Diagnosis Duality
children.top_down_role: Correspondence between conflict collections and candidate diagnoses.

knowledge_statements.title: Conflict–Diagnosis Duality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite monotone diagnosis with fixed background constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\) be background constraints and \(C\) a finite removable set. Call \(K\subseteq C\) a minimal conflict when \(B\cup K\) is unsatisfiable but \(B\cup K'\) is satisfiable for every \(K'\subsetneq K\). Then \(D\subseteq C\) is a subset-minimal diagnosis, meaning \(B\cup(C\setminus D)\) is satisfiable and no proper subset of \(D\) has this property, if and only if \(D\) is an inclusion-minimal hitting set of the family of all minimal conflicts.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subset-minimal diagnoses are exactly the minimal hitting sets of all minimal conflicts.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is finite.
Constraint satisfiability is monotone under deletion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D\) is a subset-minimal diagnosis if and only if \(D\in\operatorname{Tr}(\mathcal K_{\min})\).
review_flags: Classical duality is stated without a diagnosis-specific authoritative locator.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite monotone conflict-diagnosis equivalence is correctly stated as a duality and matches the terminal container. The supplied inventory contains no diagnosis-specific authoritative source or locator supporting the theorem.

children.title: Minimal Hitting Sets
children.top_down_role: Minimal transversals linking conflict families to diagnosis candidates.

knowledge_statements.title: Minimal Hitting Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inclusion-minimal transversals of a finite conflict family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite ground set \(C\) and a family \(\mathcal K\subseteq 2^C\), a set \(H\subseteq C\) is a hitting set when \(H\cap K\neq\varnothing\) for every \(K\in\mathcal K\). It is a minimal hitting set when it is a hitting set and no proper subset \(H'\subsetneq H\) is a hitting set. Minimality is by inclusion and does not imply that \(H\) has minimum cardinality among all hitting sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A minimal hitting set intersects every conflict and loses that property if any selected element is removed.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) and \(\mathcal K\) are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H\) is minimal exactly when it hits every \(K\in\mathcal K\) and every \(h\in H\) uniquely witnesses necessity against some conflict.
review_flags: A set-systems reference with an exact minimal-transversal locator is needed.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition correctly distinguishes inclusion-minimal hitting sets from minimum-cardinality hitting sets and fits the container. The necessity-witness characterization is also standard, but no set-systems source with a precise definition or theorem locator is cited.

children.title: Solver Evidence Interface Family
children.top_down_role: Use of solver-produced cores, conflicts, and proof artifacts as explanation inputs.

children.title: Solver-Produced Cores
children.top_down_role: Solver cores used as inputs to configuration explanations.

knowledge_statements.title: Solver-Produced Cores
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unsatisfiable cores returned under named constraint assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let each removable constraint \(c_i\) be activated by an assumption literal \(a_i\), and let the solver report unsatisfiability under assumptions \(A\). A returned set \(U\subseteq A\) is a solver-produced unsatisfiable core when the encoded background formula together with the constraints activated by \(U\) is unsatisfiable. The core is independently checkable by replaying precisely those assumptions. It is minimal only if the solver or a postprocessor additionally establishes satisfiability after deleting each \(u\in U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A solver-produced core names assumptions sufficient for infeasibility; replay checks validity, while deletion checks are required to establish minimality.
assumptions_latex: Each assumption literal has a stable mapping to one modeled constraint.
The solver result is sound for the encoded theory.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U\) certifies unsatisfiability of its activated constraint subset, but not minimality by default.
review_flags: Solver-interface semantics require an authoritative SAT, SMT, or CP solver reference.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate role fits Solver-Produced Cores, and the statement correctly avoids claiming minimality by default. The exact semantics of assumption cores, replay validation, and deletion-based minimality require an authoritative solver or SAT/SMT reference with a specific locator.

children.title: Conflict Extraction Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Interfaces exposing solver conflicts to diagnostic components.

knowledge_statements.title: Conflict Extraction Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Contract relating solver-level cores to model-level configuration conflicts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A conflict extraction interface is a pair of maps \(\alpha:C\to A\) and \(\pi:2^A\to2^C\), where \(\alpha\) associates modeled removable constraints with solver assumptions and \(\pi\) projects a returned core to modeled constraints. Its soundness condition is: for every solver core \(U\subseteq A\), the set \(B\cup\pi(U)\) is unsatisfiable. A completeness condition for a requested conflict class \(\mathcal Q\) requires that every \(K\in\mathcal Q\) can be obtained or refined from some returned \(U\) with \(\pi(U)\subseteq K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The interface maps modeled constraints to solver assumptions and projects returned cores back to sound model-level conflicts.
assumptions_latex: Constraint and assumption identifiers remain stable during a solver call.
The projection accounts for every auxiliary assumption used by the encoding.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accepted projected core is a sound model-level conflict.
review_flags: The interface contract is a synthesized formalization needing source validation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Representation is an appropriate kind for this interface container, and the soundness condition is intelligible. The proposed maps and especially the completeness condition are synthesized rather than tied to a recognized solver interface; a source is needed to determine whether the domains, auxiliary-assumption treatment, and refinement direction are correct.

children.title: Proof Artifact Ingestion
children.top_down_role: Transfer of proof artifacts into explanation workflows.

knowledge_statements.title: Proof Artifact Ingestion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validation and registration of solver proof artifacts before diagnosis use.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input an encoded instance \(F\), a claimed solver status, an artifact \(P\), a checker \(V\), and an identifier map \(\pi\). Verify format and instance hashes, then evaluate \(V(F,P)\). Reject the artifact unless the result is valid. If valid, extract its terminal claim and referenced assumptions, project them through \(\pi\), and register the projected conflict only when all identifiers resolve and the claim is unsatisfiability. Output either a checked conflict with its artifact linkage or a structured rejection; an unchecked artifact yields no certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bind an artifact to the encoded instance, independently check it, resolve its identifiers, and register only validated unsatisfiability evidence.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) is sound for the artifact format.
\(\pi\) maps artifact identifiers to modeled constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An accepted output is linked to a valid artifact for the exact encoded instance \(F\).
review_flags: Artifact formats and checker obligations vary by solver and require a selected standard.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The validation workflow fits Proof Artifact Ingestion and algorithm is the appropriate content kind. Its checker contract, terminal-claim extraction, identifier handling, and accepted artifact semantics depend on a selected proof format or solver standard that is not cited.

children.title: Artifact Provenance Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Traceability between solver results, source constraints, and explanation artifacts.

knowledge_statements.title: Artifact Provenance Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identity and derivation metadata binding evidence to an exact model instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a model instance \(M\), encoding \(F\), artifact \(P\), and checker \(V\), a provenance certificate is a tuple \(p=(h_M,h_F,h_P,v_S,v_V,t,\pi)\). It is valid when the recorded hashes equal the canonical hashes of \(M,F,P\), the solver and checker versions \(v_S,v_V\) identify their semantics, timestamp \(t\) is well formed, and identifier map \(\pi\) resolves every referenced artifact identifier to the corresponding model object. Validity binds evidence to inputs and transformations; it does not by itself establish logical correctness of \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Provenance records bind an artifact to exact model, encoding, tools, time, and identifier mappings without replacing logical proof checking.
assumptions_latex: Canonical serialization and a collision-resistant hash function are fixed.
All transformations from \(M\) to \(F\) are version identified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Valid \(p\) establishes artifact identity and traceability, not the truth of its logical claim.
review_flags: The proposed provenance fields require alignment with a recognized provenance standard.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The distinction between provenance and logical correctness is sound, but the proposed tuple and validity rules are an uncited custom schema. A recognized provenance standard is needed to validate the fields and to determine whether this interface leaf should contain a certificate definition or a representation/interface contract.

children.title: Configuration Diagnosis Search
children.top_down_role: Search families for producing one, several, all, or preferred diagnoses.

children.title: Diagnosis Minimality Regime Pair
children.top_down_role: Distinct minimality regimes for correction and explanation.

children.title: Subset-Minimal Diagnosis
children.top_down_role: Diagnoses minimal under removal of individual correction elements.

knowledge_statements.title: Subset-Minimal Diagnosis
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagnosis minimal under proper-set inclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\) be fixed background constraints and \(C\) a finite set of removable constraints. A diagnosis \(D\subseteq C\) is subset-minimal when \(B\cup(C\setminus D)\) is satisfiable and, for every proper subset \(D'\subsetneq D\), the set \(B\cup(C\setminus D')\) is unsatisfiable. Equivalently, feasibility is destroyed by restoring any one removed constraint. Subset minimality compares containment and therefore permits distinct diagnoses of different cardinalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A subset-minimal diagnosis restores feasibility, but every proper subset fails to do so; it need not use the fewest removals.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is finite.
\(B\cup C\) is unsatisfiable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D\) is inclusion-minimal among feasibility-restoring removals.
review_flags: A diagnosis reference with an exact definition locator is absent.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition correctly expresses subset minimality, its single-restoration equivalent for monotone constraint satisfiability, and its distinction from cardinality minimality. It fits the exact terminal container, but no diagnosis reference or exact definition locator is supplied.

children.title: Cardinality-Minimal Diagnosis
children.top_down_role: Diagnoses minimizing the number of correction elements.

knowledge_statements.title: Cardinality-Minimal Diagnosis
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagnosis minimizing the number of relaxed constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\) be background constraints and \(C\) a finite removable set. A diagnosis \(D^*\subseteq C\) is cardinality-minimal when \(B\cup(C\setminus D^*)\) is satisfiable and \[|D^*|=\min\bigl\{|D|:D\subseteq C,\ B\cup(C\setminus D)\text{ is satisfiable}\bigr\}.\] Every cardinality-minimal diagnosis is subset-minimal. The converse need not hold because a subset-minimal diagnosis can contain more constraints than another incomparable diagnosis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cardinality-minimal diagnosis restores feasibility using the fewest constraint removals; it is subset-minimal, but the converse can fail.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is finite.
At least one removal set restores satisfiability.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D^*\) has minimum cardinality among all diagnoses and is subset-minimal.
review_flags: A diagnosis reference with an exact minimum-cardinality locator is absent.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The minimum-cardinality definition and implication to subset minimality are mathematically correct for finite C and fit the terminal container. An authoritative diagnosis source with a precise locator is absent.

children.title: Minimality Regime Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Differences in diagnostic interpretation, search burden, and result selection.

knowledge_statements.title: Minimality Regime Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical relation and separation between inclusion and cardinality minimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite removable set \(C\), every cardinality-minimal diagnosis is subset-minimal, whereas a subset-minimal diagnosis need not be cardinality-minimal. Indeed, if the family of minimal conflicts is \(\mathcal K=\{\{a,b\},\{a,c\}\}\), then its minimal hitting sets are \(\{a\}\) and \(\{b,c\}\). Both are subset-minimal diagnoses under conflict–diagnosis duality, but only \(\{a\}\) has minimum cardinality. Thus inclusion-minimal enumeration may return larger corrections, while cardinality optimization can discard valid incomparable explanations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimum-cardinality diagnoses are subset-minimal, but subset-minimal diagnoses may be larger and preserve alternative incomparable explanations.
assumptions_latex: Diagnoses correspond to hitting sets of the complete minimal-conflict family.
\(C\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Cardinality minimality strictly refines subset minimality in general.
review_flags: The separation example is directly checkable but lacks an authoritative diagnosis locator.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property correctly states the relation between cardinality and subset minimality, and the displayed conflict family gives a valid separation example. The property kind fits Minimality Regime Tradeoffs, but the candidate has no authoritative diagnosis or transversal reference with an inspectable locator.

children.title: Diagnosis Output Cardinality Regimes
children.top_down_role: Output regimes distinguished by requested number and ordering of diagnoses.

children.title: Single-Diagnosis Output
children.top_down_role: Search settings that request one qualifying diagnosis.

assumptions_latex: \(C\) is a finite set of diagnosable components.
Each \(c\in C\) has an associated constraint set \(K_c\), and \(O\) is the current observation.
At least one subset \(\Delta\subseteq C\) makes the retained model satisfiable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is one inclusion-minimal diagnosis, with ties resolved by \(\prec\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale:model-based diagnosis semantics and deterministic minimum selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic selection of exactly one minimal configuration diagnosis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\Delta\subseteq C\), define \(K_{-\Delta}=\bigcup_{c\in C\setminus\Delta}K_c\). A diagnosis satisfies \(K_{-\Delta}\cup O\), and it is inclusion-minimal when no \(\Delta'\subsetneq\Delta\) is a diagnosis. Given a strict total tie-breaking order \(\prec\) on \(2^C\), compute the nonempty set \(\mathcal D_{\min}\) of inclusion-minimal diagnoses and return
\[\Delta^*=\mathop{\operatorname{argmin}}_{\Delta\in\mathcal D_{\min}}^{\prec}\Delta.\]
The procedure stops after certifying minimality of \(\Delta^*\); it does not assert uniqueness of the underlying diagnosis set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Return exactly one inclusion-minimal diagnosis, using a fixed total order to choose deterministically when several minimal diagnoses exist.
knowledge_statements.title: Single-Diagnosis Output

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the leaf, but no cited evidence supports the diagnosis semantics or selection procedure. The model, rather than a diagnosis, is satisfiable, and the order-qualified argmin notation is nonstandard.

children.title: Ranked Diagnosis Lists
children.top_down_role: Diagnosis outputs ordered by preference, likelihood, cost, or relevance.

assumptions_latex: The finite diagnosis set \(\mathcal D\) is nonempty.
The score \(s:\mathcal D\to\mathbb R\) and strict total tie-breaker \(\prec\) are fixed.
The requested list length satisfies \(1\le k\le |\mathcal D|\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The result is the first \(k\) diagnoses in nondecreasing lexicographic order of \((s(\Delta),\Delta)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale:finite top-k ranking with explicit tie-breaking
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite top-\(k\) diagnosis ranking with deterministic ties.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define \(\Delta\triangleleft\Gamma\) precisely when either \(s(\Delta)<s(\Gamma)\), or \(s(\Delta)=s(\Gamma)\) and \(\Delta\prec\Gamma\). A ranked diagnosis list of length \(k\) is the sequence \(L_k=(\Delta_1,\ldots,\Delta_k)\) of distinct members of \(\mathcal D\) satisfying
\[\Delta_1\triangleleft\Delta_2\triangleleft\cdots\triangleleft\Delta_k\]
and
\[\forall\Gamma\in\mathcal D\setminus\{\Delta_1,\ldots,\Delta_k\},\quad \Delta_k\triangleleft\Gamma.\]
Thus the list is a reproducible ordered prefix rather than an unordered collection of low-scoring diagnoses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A ranked list contains the k best distinct diagnoses by score, with a fixed total order resolving all equal-score ties.
knowledge_statements.title: Ranked Diagnosis Lists

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation precisely defines a deterministic top-k prefix and fits the leaf, but it has no citation with an inspectable locator.

children.title: Multiple-Diagnosis Enumeration
children.top_down_role: Production of several distinct diagnoses for comparison or downstream use.

assumptions_latex: \(C\) is finite, and diagnosis validity is decidable by a satisfiability oracle.
Only inclusion-minimal diagnoses are requested.
The blocking mechanism excludes an emitted diagnosis and all of its strict supersets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Upon termination, the emitted set equals the complete set of inclusion-minimal diagnoses.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complete enumeration of finite inclusion-minimal diagnoses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(E=\varnothing\). Repeatedly ask the diagnosis oracle for a diagnosis \(D\subseteq C\) satisfying the blocking predicates \(D\not\supseteq\Gamma\) for every \(\Gamma\in E\). If none exists, return \(E\). Otherwise minimize \(D\) by deleting components while diagnosis validity is preserved, obtaining an inclusion-minimal \(\Delta\); emit \(\Delta\), update \(E\leftarrow E\cup\{\Delta\}\), and add its blocking predicate. Since \(C\) is finite, every iteration emits a new minimal diagnosis and the procedure terminates after exactly as many successful iterations as there are minimal diagnoses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly find and minimize an unblocked diagnosis, then block it and its supersets; termination yields every inclusion-minimal diagnosis exactly once.
knowledge_statements.title: Multiple-Diagnosis Enumeration

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits, but decidability alone does not ensure that deletion minimization and superset blocking enumerate all minimal diagnoses. Diagnosis validity must be assumed upward-monotone, and authoritative support is absent.

children.title: Diagnosis Diversity Control
children.top_down_role: Control of redundancy and coverage within multi-diagnosis outputs.

assumptions_latex: Diagnoses are subsets of a finite component set \(C\).
A symmetric dissimilarity \(d:2^C\times2^C\to\mathbb R_{\ge0}\) is fixed.
The required separation threshold is \(\tau\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every two distinct reported diagnoses have dissimilarity at least \(\tau\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale:pairwise distance constraint for diverse subset selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pairwise diversity constraint for set-valued diagnosis output.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A reported family \(S\subseteq\mathcal D\) satisfies \(\tau\)-diversity exactly when
\[\forall\Delta,\Gamma\in S,\quad \Delta\ne\Gamma\Longrightarrow d(\Delta,\Gamma)\ge\tau.\]
For set-valued diagnoses, one admissible choice is normalized symmetric-difference distance,
\[d(\Delta,\Gamma)=\frac{|\Delta\mathbin{\triangle}\Gamma|}{|\Delta\cup\Gamma|},\]
with \(d(\varnothing,\varnothing)=0\). Diversity-controlled selection may optimize a ranking objective over all \(S\subseteq\mathcal D\) satisfying this predicate, but ranking quality does not replace the pairwise separation requirement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A diagnosis family is diverse when every distinct pair meets a specified dissimilarity threshold; symmetric-difference distance is one concrete choice.
knowledge_statements.title: Diagnosis Diversity Control

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role and pairwise diversity predicate fit the leaf and are internally coherent, including the empty-set convention, but no inspectable citation supports this diagnosis-diversity formulation.

children.title: Adaptive Diagnosis Interaction Calculus
children.top_down_role: Reuse of diagnostic state as requirements and user decisions evolve.

children.title: Incremental Diagnostic State Reuse
children.top_down_role: Reuse of conflicts, candidates, and search state across successive diagnostic instances.

assumptions_latex: The diagnostic theory is represented by a solver state \(S_t\) at interaction step \(t\).
The next state changes the active constraint database from \(F_t\) to \(F_{t+1}\).
Learned information is retained only when valid for \(F_{t+1}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The updated state is logically equivalent to solving \(F_{t+1}\) from scratch while reusing only sound artifacts.

notation.meaning: Active constraint database at step t

review_flags: standard_field_rationale:incremental constraint solving with sound artifact retention
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sound reuse of diagnostic search state after interactive changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given edits \(A_t\) and \(R_t\), form \(F_{t+1}=(F_t\setminus R_t)\cup A_t\). Partition the artifacts stored in \(S_t\) into retained and invalidated sets using
\[L_{t+1}=\{\ell\in S_t:\operatorname{valid}(\ell,F_{t+1})\}.\]
Initialize \(S_{t+1}\) from \(L_{t+1}\), retract diagnoses or conflicts whose derivations depend on removed constraints, add the new constraints, and resume propagation and search. Stop when the requested diagnosis output is established for \(F_{t+1}\). Soundness requires every retained artifact to be entailed by, or independently valid for, the updated database.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Update the active constraints, discard state invalidated by removals, retain only sound learned artifacts, and resume diagnosis from the filtered state.
knowledge_statements.title: Incremental Diagnostic State Reuse

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits, but the solver state is treated as an artifact set without definition, and sound retained artifacts alone do not establish equivalence to a complete from-scratch solve. A sourced incremental-diagnosis model is required.

children.title: Interactive Query Guidance
children.top_down_role: User-facing queries that discriminate among competing diagnoses.

assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal D\) is a finite posterior distribution over diagnoses.
Each admissible binary query \(q\) partitions diagnoses into answer classes \(\mathcal D_q^+\) and \(\mathcal D_q^-\).
Query cost \(c(q)>0\) is known.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected query maximizes expected entropy reduction per unit cost.

notation.meaning: Answer random variable for query q

review_flags: standard_field_rationale:information-gain query selection over diagnosis partitions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cost-sensitive information-gain guidance for binary diagnostic queries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every admissible query \(q\), derive its answer probabilities from the current diagnosis probabilities and compute
\[\operatorname{IG}(q)=H(D)-\sum_{a\in\{+,-\}}\Pr(A_q=a)H(D\mid A_q=a).\]
Select
\[q^*\in\mathop{\operatorname{argmax}}_q\frac{\operatorname{IG}(q)}{c(q)},\]
using a fixed tie-breaker. Ask \(q^*\), condition the diagnosis distribution on the observed answer, remove diagnoses incompatible with that answer, and repeat. Stop when a diagnosis reaches the prescribed confidence threshold, only one diagnosis remains, or no admissible query has positive information gain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Ask the affordable binary query with greatest expected entropy reduction, update diagnosis probabilities from the answer, and repeat until the stopping criterion holds.
knowledge_statements.title: Interactive Query Guidance

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits, but the assumptions conflate a diagnosis set with a posterior distribution and require deterministic exhaustive binary answer classes. The entropy-guided procedure needs an authoritative interactive-diagnosis source.

children.title: Evolving Requirement Handling
children.top_down_role: Diagnostic continuity when configuration requirements change.

assumptions_latex: At step \(t\), requirements form a finite constraint set \(R_t\).
Added and removed requirements are explicitly identified.
Diagnosis validity is evaluated against the updated requirements.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: After each edit, reported diagnoses are exactly valid for the current requirement set.

notation.meaning: Requirement set at interaction step t

review_flags: standard_field_rationale:dynamic constraint-set update followed by revalidation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagnosis maintenance under explicit requirement additions and removals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Update the requirements by
\[R_{t+1}=(R_t\setminus B_t)\cup A_t.\]
Invalidate every cached conflict, diagnosis, or bound whose justification is not valid under \(R_{t+1}\). Revalidate each retained diagnosis \(\Delta\) by checking satisfiability of the system obtained after applying \(\Delta\) together with \(R_{t+1}\); discard invalid diagnoses and resume search for missing ones. The update terminates when the chosen output regime is complete relative to \(R_{t+1}\). Requirement removal may restore previously inconsistent configurations, so merely filtering the old diagnosis set is not complete in general.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply requirement additions and removals, invalidate unsupported artifacts, recheck retained diagnoses, and search again because removals can create newly valid explanations.
knowledge_statements.title: Evolving Requirement Handling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits, and the warning about requirement removals is plausible, but exact output maintenance depends on an unspecified output regime and search-completeness guarantee. No authoritative source is cited.

children.title: User Decision Incorporation
children.top_down_role: Integration of user confirmations, rejections, and preference feedback.

assumptions_latex: The current candidate diagnosis family is \(\mathcal D_t\).
A user decision is encoded as a constraint \(u_t\) with unambiguous acceptance semantics.
The user decision is treated as hard unless explicitly assigned a soft penalty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The next diagnosis family contains exactly the candidates compatible with the incorporated decision.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale:constraint-based filtering and re-solving after user commitments
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hard-constraint incorporation of explicit user choices into diagnosis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Translate the user's accepted choice into a hard constraint \(u_t\) and update the active diagnostic theory to \(F_{t+1}=F_t\cup\{u_t\}\). Filter known candidates by
\[\mathcal D_{t+1}^{\mathrm{keep}}=\{\Delta\in\mathcal D_t:F_t[\Delta]\cup\{u_t\}\text{ is satisfiable}\}.\]
Invalidate incompatible search nodes and learned artifacts, then resume search under \(F_{t+1}\) to obtain any additional diagnoses required by the output regime. A rejected choice is incorporated through its logical negation. Stop only when the maintained output is complete for the updated theory, not merely filtered from old candidates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Encode an accepted or rejected user choice as a hard constraint, remove incompatible diagnoses, and resume search to restore completeness.
knowledge_statements.title: User Decision Incorporation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits, but the statement introduces undefined F_t and F_t[Delta]. The conclusion suggests mere compatibility filtering, whereas the statement permits newly found diagnoses after re-solving; authoritative support and a consistent claim are needed.

children.title: Federated Diagnosis Algorithm Family
children.top_down_role: Diagnosis organized around modular knowledge, independent components, or parallel search.

children.title: Parallel Diagnosis Search
children.top_down_role: Concurrent exploration of diagnostic candidates or search regions.

assumptions_latex: The diagnosis search space is partitioned into finitely many pairwise disjoint regions \(P_1,\ldots,P_m\).
Each worker applies a sound and complete local diagnosis procedure to its region.
A coordinator performs global duplicate elimination and minimality checking.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The merged output is the same diagnosis family that exhaustive search would produce over the union of all regions.

notation.meaning: Search region assigned to worker i

review_flags: standard_field_rationale:complete partitioned search with coordinated global filtering
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Partitioned parallel enumeration with global minimality control.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Choose regions satisfying \(P_i\cap P_j=\varnothing\) for \(i\ne j\) and \(\bigcup_{i=1}^mP_i=2^C\). Worker \(i\) enumerates valid local candidates \(E_i\subseteq P_i\) and streams them to the coordinator. For every received \(\Delta\), the coordinator rejects it if an accepted \(\Gamma\subsetneq\Delta\) exists, otherwise removes accepted strict supersets and inserts \(\Delta\). Workers exchange newly discovered global blocking constraints when supported. After all workers certify exhaustion of their regions, return
\[E=\min_{\subseteq}\left(\bigcup_{i=1}^mE_i\right),\]
where \(\min_{\subseteq}\) denotes inclusion-minimal members.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Search disjoint regions concurrently, merge candidates centrally, and apply global duplicate and minimality checks before declaring complete enumeration.
knowledge_statements.title: Parallel Diagnosis Search

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits, but C is not introduced and local completeness over each region is not formally connected to the streamed sets E_i. The global equivalence claim requires authoritative support.

children.title: Modular Knowledge Diagnosis
children.top_down_role: Diagnosis organized around explicit knowledge-base modules.

assumptions_latex: The global theory decomposes as \(K=K_1\cup\cdots\cup K_m\).
Module interfaces contain every variable shared between modules.
Each module can characterize the interface assignments extendable to a local diagnosis.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Compatible local diagnoses compose to a global diagnosis, and every global diagnosis projects to compatible local diagnoses.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale:exact decomposition through complete shared-variable interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact modular diagnosis through complete interface summaries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each module \(i\), compute pairs \((\Delta_i,	heta_i)\), where \(\Delta_i\) is a local diagnosis and \(\theta_i\) is an assignment to \(I_i\) extendable to a model of the repaired module \(K_i[\Delta_i]\). A tuple of local pairs is compatible when
\[\theta_i|_{I_i\cap I_j}=\theta_j|_{I_i\cap I_j}\quad\text{for all }i,j.\]
Every compatible tuple yields the global candidate \(\Delta=igcup_i\Delta_i\). Retain candidates satisfying the complete global theory and apply the requested minimality criterion. Exactness requires interfaces to expose all cross-module dependencies; otherwise compatible summaries need not imply global consistency.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Diagnose each module with an interface assignment, join mutually consistent interface summaries, unite their local diagnoses, and check global validity and minimality.
knowledge_statements.title: Modular Knowledge Diagnosis

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The statement contains the invalid command \igcup. It also combines a modular construction with an exactness theorem, so generic representation is not a clean role match. The composition claim needs sourced repair semantics and complete interface hypotheses.

children.title: Distributed Diagnostic Coordination
children.top_down_role: Coordination of diagnostic work across separate computational or organizational participants.

assumptions_latex: Agents hold local theories whose union is the global diagnostic theory.
Messages are delivered reliably and carry conflicts, candidates, bounds, or termination acknowledgments.
Every global dependency is represented by some communication interface.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Termination is declared only when all agents are passive and no relevant message remains in transit.

notation.meaning: Local diagnostic state of agent i

review_flags: standard_field_rationale:distributed fixed-point coordination with global termination detection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Message-driven coordination to a distributed diagnostic fixed point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Initialize each agent's state \(S_i\) from its local theory and set the shared monotone knowledge store \(G=\varnothing\). Each active agent performs local propagation or search, publishes newly derived interface conflicts, diagnosis candidates, and valid bounds, and incorporates received items into \(S_i\). Globally, updates have the form \(G\leftarrow G\cup M\), where \(M\) contains only sound derived information. An agent becomes passive when no local transition or unsent message remains. A termination detector returns the coordinated diagnosis result only when
\[\forall i\in A,\quad i\text{ is passive},\]
and the communication system certifies that no relevant message is in transit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Agents exchange sound diagnostic information until every local state is passive and a termination detector confirms that no relevant messages remain in transit.
knowledge_statements.title: Distributed Diagnostic Coordination

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits, but reliable delivery and passivity do not by themselves define a correct distributed termination detector, and no soundness or completeness condition for the returned diagnosis family is supplied. An authoritative distributed-diagnosis source is required.

children.title: Cross-Component Conflict Handling
children.top_down_role: Conflicts whose causes or corrections span multiple modules.

assumptions_latex: Components are partitioned among modules \(C_1,\ldots,C_m\).
A conflict is a component set that cannot all be healthy under the observations.
Local solvers can emit conflicts involving interface components.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every reported global diagnosis hits every discovered local and cross-component conflict.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale:conflict-hitting certificate with global consistency validation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global handling and certification of conflicts spanning module boundaries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Aggregate all sound local and cross-component conflicts into \(\mathcal C\subseteq2^{\cup_i C_i}\). A candidate \(\Delta\subseteqigcup_iC_i\) passes the conflict certificate exactly when
\[\forall Q\,\in\mathcal C,\quad \Delta\cap Q\ne\varnothing.\]
When a combined local solution violates an interface constraint, extract a sound conflict \(Q\) from the participating module assumptions, add \(Q\) to \(\mathcal C\), and broadcast its projections to affected modules. Continue until the candidate hits every known conflict and the repaired global theory is satisfiable. Inclusion-minimality is certified by additionally checking that \(\Delta\setminus\{c\}\) fails the certificate or global consistency test for every \(c\in\Delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Broadcast conflicts that span modules; a global diagnosis must hit every conflict, satisfy the repaired theory, and fail after any deletion to certify minimality.
knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Component Conflict Handling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate role fits, but the statement contains invalid \igcup commands. Hitting only discovered conflicts is not independently a complete diagnosis certificate unless the conflict family is complete; the added global satisfiability test needs a sourced diagnosis-semantics specification.

children.title: Configuration Explanation Families
children.top_down_role: Explanations organized by user question, supported decision, and underlying certificate.

children.title: Inconsistency Explanations
children.top_down_role: Explanations of why a model, requirement set, or partial configuration has no completion.

knowledge_statements.title: Inconsistency Explanations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A constraint-subset certificate explaining why a partial configuration has no feasible completion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be the constraints of a finite-domain configuration model and \(P\) the constraints encoding a partial configuration. An inconsistency explanation is a set \(E\subseteq F\cup P\) such that \(E\) is unsatisfiable. It is subset-minimal when every \(e\in E\) satisfies that \(E\setminus\{e\}\) is satisfiable. The displayed constraints constitute a checkable certificate because a sound constraint solver can verify the infeasibility of \(E\); minimality additionally requires one satisfiability check for each single-constraint deletion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inconsistency explanation is an unsatisfiable subset of model and partial-configuration constraints; it is minimal when deleting any one member restores satisfiability.
assumptions_latex: \(F\cup P\) is a finite set of constraints over finite-domain variables.
Constraint satisfiability is decided by a sound solver.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(E\) certifies that \(F\cup P\) has no satisfying completion.
review_flags: Specialized configuration-explanation formulation lacks a directly supporting source locator.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate formulation is mathematically coherent and fits the inconsistency-explanation container, but no source reference or inspectable locator supports the specialized configuration-explanation definition or its verification claims.

children.title: Selection Consequence Explanation Family
children.top_down_role: Explanations for required, excluded, or automatically selected options.

children.title: Forced-Choice Explanations
children.top_down_role: Explanations for options that must be selected under the active constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Forced-Choice Explanations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate that exactly one currently admissible option can extend the given selections.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be a configuration theory, \(P\) the current selections, and \(O=\{o_1,\ldots,o_m\}\) a finite set of mutually exclusive Boolean options. A forced-choice explanation for \(o_k\) consists of satisfiability of \(F\land P\land o_k\) together with, for every \(j\ne k\), an unsatisfiable set \(E_j\subseteq F\cup P\cup\{o_j\}\). Hence every feasible completion satisfying exactly one member of \(O\) must select \(o_k\). Subset-minimal explanations require every \(E_j\) to be subset-minimal unsatisfiable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An option is forced when it remains feasible and every competing mutually exclusive option has an inconsistency certificate under the current selections.
assumptions_latex: \(F\land P\models \sum_{j=1}^{m}o_j=1\).
Each \(o_j\) is Boolean.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\land P\models o_k\).
review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports forced-choice explanation certificates.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate role fits the leaf and the exact-one assumption is sufficient for the conclusion, but no cited source with a specific locator supports this forced-choice explanation construction.

children.title: Required-Option Explanations
children.top_down_role: Explanations tracing why a configuration requires a particular option.

knowledge_statements.title: Required-Option Explanations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate that a designated option occurs in every completion of the current partial configuration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be a configuration theory, \(P\) a consistent partial configuration, and \(r\) a Boolean option. A required-option explanation for \(r\) is an unsatisfiable subset \(E\subseteq F\cup P\cup\{\neg r\}\) that contains \(\neg r\). Since \(F\land P\) is satisfiable while \(E\) is not, no feasible completion of \(P\) can set \(r\) to false. The explanation is subset-minimal when deleting any constraint from \(E\) makes the remainder satisfiable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A required-option explanation shows that the current configuration is feasible but becomes inconsistent if the designated option is forbidden.
assumptions_latex: \(F\land P\) is satisfiable.
\(r\) is a Boolean option.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\land P\models r\).
review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports required-option explanations.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The unsatisfiable subset containing the negated option is a coherent certificate for a required option, but the record supplies no source or inspectable locator for this configuration-explanation notion.

children.title: Excluded-Option Explanations
children.top_down_role: Explanations tracing why a candidate option cannot be selected.

knowledge_statements.title: Excluded-Option Explanations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate that selecting a designated option would destroy extendability of the current configuration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be a configuration theory, \(P\) a consistent partial configuration, and \(x\) a Boolean option. An excluded-option explanation for \(x\) is an unsatisfiable subset \(E\subseteq F\cup P\cup\{x\}\) containing \(x\). Thus no satisfying completion of \(P\) under \(F\) can select \(x\). The explanation is subset-minimal if \(E\setminus\{e\}\) is satisfiable for every \(e\in E\); otherwise it remains a valid, potentially redundant exclusion certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An excluded-option explanation proves that adding the option to an otherwise feasible partial configuration makes the relevant constraints inconsistent.
assumptions_latex: \(F\land P\) is satisfiable.
\(x\) is a Boolean option.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\land P\models \neg x\).
review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports excluded-option explanations.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The formulation correctly certifies exclusion under a feasible partial configuration and the certificate content kind fits the leaf, but no supporting citation or specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Implication Explanations
children.top_down_role: Explanations for selections or exclusions propagated from prior decisions.

assumptions_latex: \(F\land A\) is satisfiable.
\(A\) and \(q\) are formulas over the configuration variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\models A\Rightarrow q\).
review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports implication explanations.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraint subset certifying that selected antecedents logically force a configuration consequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be a configuration theory, \(A\) a conjunction of selected literals, and \(q\) a consequence literal. An implication explanation for \(A\Rightarrow q\) is a subset \(E\subseteq F\) for which \(E\land A\land\neg q\) is unsatisfiable. Equivalently, \(E\models A\Rightarrow q\). It is subset-minimal when no proper subset of \(E\) has this entailment. A solver verifies the certificate by checking unsatisfiability after adjoining the antecedent and negated consequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An implication explanation is a subset of model constraints that becomes inconsistent with the antecedent selections and the negation of the claimed consequence.
knowledge_statements.title: Implication Explanations

children.title: Corrective Explanations
children.top_down_role: Explanations paired with feasible changes restoring completion.

knowledge_statements.title: Corrective Explanations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An inconsistency explanation paired with a verifiable modification that restores a feasible completion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be a configuration theory and \(P\) an inconsistent set of user requirements. A corrective explanation is a pair \((E,\Delta)\), where \(E\subseteq F\cup P\) is unsatisfiable and \(\Delta=(D,A)\) specifies requirements \(D\subseteq P\) to delete and consistent requirements \(A\) to add, such that \(F\land(P\setminus D)\land A\) is satisfiable. It is inclusion-minimal when no pair \((D',A')\) with \(D'\subseteq D\), \(A'\subseteq A\), and at least one strict inclusion restores satisfiability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A corrective explanation identifies an inconsistent constraint subset and a deletion-addition repair whose application admits at least one valid completion.
assumptions_latex: \(F\land P\) is unsatisfiable.
\(F\), \(P\), \(D\), and \(A\) are finite constraint sets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\land(P\setminus D)\land A\) is satisfiable.
review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports corrective configuration explanations.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Pairing an inconsistency subset with a satisfiability-restoring modification fits the corrective-explanation container and certificate role, but no source with a specific locator supports the proposed definition or minimality convention.

children.title: Contrastive-Counterfactual Explanation Pair
children.top_down_role: Comparisons between selected and alternative configurations or outcomes.

children.title: Contrastive Configuration Explanations
children.top_down_role: Comparisons between a selected configuration and a designated alternative.

assumptions_latex: \(F\land P\) is satisfiable.
\(B\) specifies the intended alternative rather than an arbitrary negation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(E\land H\models q\) and \(F\land P\land B\models\neg q\).
review_flags: The literature contains multiple inequivalent notions of contrastive explanation; no supporting locator was supplied.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate answering why the realized configuration occurs rather than a specified feasible alternative.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be a configuration theory, \(P\) the factual selections, and \(B\) a contrast condition. For a factual consequence \(q\), a contrastive explanation is a pair \((E,H)\) with \(E\subseteq F\), \(H\subseteq P\), such that \(E\land H\models q\), \(F\land P\land B\models\neg q\), and \(F\land P\land B\) is satisfiable. Thus the explanation identifies sufficient factual selections and constraints for \(q\), while the stated alternative is a feasible contrast in which \(q\) does not hold. Minimality may be imposed on \(E\cup H\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A contrastive explanation gives sufficient reasons for the factual consequence and verifies a feasible nominated alternative where that consequence is absent.
knowledge_statements.title: Contrastive Configuration Explanations

children.title: Counterfactual Configuration Explanations
children.top_down_role: Explanations of outcomes under hypothetical configuration changes.

knowledge_statements.title: Counterfactual Configuration Explanations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A minimal intervention producing a feasible configuration with a specified changed outcome.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be a configuration theory, \(P\) a factual partial configuration with \(F\land P\models q\), and \(I=(D,A)\) an intervention deleting \(D\subseteq P\) and adding constraints \(A\). A counterfactual explanation for changing \(q\) is an intervention satisfying \(F\land(P\setminus D)\land A\land\neg q\). It is valid when this formula is satisfiable and inclusion-minimal when no intervention formed by strict componentwise subsets of \(D\) and \(A\) remains valid. Any satisfying assignment is a witness configuration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A counterfactual explanation is a minimal deletion-addition intervention admitting a feasible configuration in which the factual outcome is reversed.
assumptions_latex: \(F\land P\) is satisfiable.
\(F\land P\models q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\land(P\setminus D)\land A\land\neg q\) is satisfiable.
review_flags: No supplied locator fixes the intervention semantics for counterfactual configuration explanations.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The intervention and satisfying witness form a plausible counterfactual certificate, but the treatment of deletion-addition interventions and componentwise minimality depends on semantics not fixed by any cited source.

children.title: Alternative Baseline Selection
children.top_down_role: Choice of reference alternatives for meaningful explanation comparisons.

knowledge_statements.title: Alternative Baseline Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimization rule selecting a feasible, relevant, and minimally distant contrast configuration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a configuration theory \(F\), factual assignment \(x\), admissible alternative set \(B\), and nonnegative distance \(d\), solve \[y^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{y}\{d(x,y):y\models F\land B\}.\] If the feasible set is empty, return that no admissible baseline exists. Otherwise return \(y^\star\), breaking ties by a fixed deterministic ordering or a declared secondary objective. When \(d\) is a weighted Hamming distance, \(d(x,y)=\sum_i w_i\mathbf 1[x_i\ne y_i]\) with \(w_i\ge0\), the baseline minimizes the weighted number of changed decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select the admissible feasible alternative closest to the factual configuration under a declared distance, with explicit tie-breaking and failure when none exists.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) has finitely many configurations.
\(B\) precisely encodes admissible alternatives.
\(d(x,y)\ge0\) is computable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Returned \(y^\star\) minimizes \(d(x,y)\) over all \(y\models F\land B\).
review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports alternative-baseline optimization for configuration explanations.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The optimization procedure is internally coherent and the algorithm content kind fits baseline selection, but no source establishes that nearest feasible alternatives under the declared distance are the intended baseline-selection rule for this container.

children.title: Alternative Feasibility Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits separating attainable alternatives from infeasible counterfactuals.

knowledge_statements.title: Alternative Feasibility Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary separating reachable feasible alternatives from contrast conditions incompatible with the configuration theory.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be a configuration theory, \(P\) factual selections, and \(B\) an alternative condition. The alternative is feasible exactly when \(F\land P\land B\) is satisfiable. If this formula is unsatisfiable, no configuration preserving all of \(P\) realizes \(B\). A boundary certificate is an unsatisfiable subset \(E\subseteq F\cup P\cup\{B\}\) containing some factual constraints. Any alternative intervention must remove or weaken at least one member of \(E\cap P\); otherwise the unchanged certificate remains unsatisfiable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An alternative lies beyond the feasibility boundary when it conflicts with the theory and preserved facts; every successful intervention must break the displayed inconsistency certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(F\), \(P\), and \(B\) use a common configuration vocabulary.
Satisfiability is interpreted over the declared configuration domains.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(E\) is unsatisfiable, every feasible intervention removes or weakens some constraint in \(E\cap P\).
review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports alternative feasibility boundaries.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The satisfiability boundary and unsatisfiable-subset argument are plausible, but the conclusion is reliable only when interventions may modify factual constraints while leaving the model and requested contrast fixed. That intervention scope is not made fully explicit or supported by a cited locator.

children.title: Preference-Aware Reconfiguration
children.top_down_role: Repair and recommendation families ranking feasible changes by user, business, or engineering preferences.

children.title: Cost-Sensitive Repair Regime Family
children.top_down_role: Corrections ranked by penalties, costs, or explicit priorities.

children.title: Weighted Requirement Repair
children.top_down_role: Repairs ranked using importance weights attached to requirements.

knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Requirement Repair
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimum-penalty deletion of soft requirements sufficient to restore consistency with hard configuration constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be hard constraints and \(R=\{r_1,\ldots,r_m\}\) soft requirements with weights \(w_i\ge0\). Introduce retention variables \(z_i\in\{0,1\}\) and solve \[\min_{x,z}\ \sum_{i=1}^{m}w_i(1-z_i)\quad\text{subject to}\quad x\models F,\qquad z_i=1\Rightarrow x\models r_i.\] Return the feasible configuration \(x^\star\) and deleted set \(D^\star=\{r_i:z_i^\star=0\}\). If the hard constraints are infeasible, report that no requirement-only repair exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Retain a maximum-weight satisfiable subset of soft requirements, equivalently deleting minimum total weight, while never relaxing hard configuration constraints.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) and \(R\) define a finite configuration problem.
\(w_i\ge0\) for every requirement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D^\star\) has minimum total weight among requirement deletions restoring satisfiability with \(F\).
review_flags: Standard weighted repair formulation, but supplied locators do not directly document it.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The weighted retention formulation correctly represents minimum-penalty deletion of soft requirements and the algorithm kind fits the leaf, but no authoritative source with a specific locator is cited for the formulation.

children.title: Cost-Based Repair
children.top_down_role: Repairs ranked by explicit modification or operational costs.

knowledge_statements.title: Cost-Based Repair
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Least-cost sequence of permitted configuration edits that restores feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) be the current requirements, \(F\) the hard configuration theory, and \(\mathcal E\) a finite set of permitted edits. For an edit set \(S\subseteq\mathcal E\), let \(S(P)\) denote the modified requirements and let \(c(S)\ge0\) be its declared cost. Compute \[S^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{S\subseteq\mathcal E}\{c(S):F\land S(P)\text{ is satisfiable}\}.\] Return \(S^\star\) and a satisfying completion. If the feasible edit family is empty, report that the permitted edits cannot repair the configuration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose a permitted edit set of minimum declared cost whose application makes the requirements jointly satisfiable with the hard configuration model.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal E\) is finite and its edits have defined composition semantics.
\(c(S)\) is computable and nonnegative.
Satisfiability of \(F\land S(P)\) is decidable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S^\star\) has minimum cost among all permitted repairs restoring satisfiability.
review_flags: Standard minimum-cost repair formulation, but supplied locators do not directly document it.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite minimum-cost repair optimization is coherent and appropriately classified as an algorithm, but the permitted-edit and composition semantics are generic and no cited source with a specific locator supports this formulation.

children.title: Penalty Aggregation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Alternative ways to combine penalties across repair decisions.

knowledge_statements.title: Penalty Aggregation Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard scalar aggregations of requirement-violation penalties over a finite feasible repair set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R\) be a nonempty finite set of feasible repairs, let \(I\) index soft requirements, and let \(v_i(r)\ge 0\) be the violation of requirement \(i\) under repair \(r\). Common penalty regimes select a repair from \[\operatorname*{argmin}_{r\in R}A(v(r)),\] where, for weights \(w_i>0\), \(A\) is respectively the weighted sum \(\sum_{i\in I}w_i v_i\), the bottleneck penalty \(\max_{i\in I}w_i v_i\), or the weighted \(p\)-norm \(\bigl(\sum_{i\in I}w_i v_i^p\bigr)^{1/p}\) for \(1\le p<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Feasible repairs are ranked by a scalar aggregation of violations, such as weighted total, worst weighted violation, or a weighted p-norm.
assumptions_latex: \(R\) is finite and nonempty.
\(v_i(r)\ge 0\) and \(w_i>0\) for every \(i\in I\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{r\in R}A(v(r))\) defines the selected penalty-minimal repairs.

notation.meaning: violation of soft requirement i by repair r

review_flags: Confirm that the cited section supports the stated aggregation variants.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits the Penalty Aggregation Regimes leaf, but the local file exposes only a table-of-contents entry for the cited penalty-function section, so support for the weighted-sum, bottleneck, and weighted-p-norm variants cannot be inspected. In addition, I must be declared finite and nonempty for the displayed finite sums and maximum to be unconditionally defined.

children.title: Cost Sensitivity Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Changes in preferred repairs as cost assessments vary.

knowledge_statements.title: Cost Sensitivity Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parametric boundaries for linear weighted repair costs on a finite repair set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R\) be a finite feasible repair set and let each repair have feature-cost vector \(c(r)\in\mathbb{R}^m\). For weights \(w\in W\subseteq\mathbb{R}^m_+\), define \(C_w(r)=w^\top c(r)\). The set of optimal repairs is constant on every connected component of \[W\setminus\bigcup_{r\ne s}\{w\in W:w^\top(c(r)-c(s))=0\}.\] Hence an optimal-repair change can occur only on a tie hyperplane, or where such a hyperplane meets the boundary of \(W\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With finitely many repairs and linear weighted costs, the optimizer changes only where two repairs tie or at the admissible weight region’s boundary.
assumptions_latex: \(R\) is finite and nonempty.
\(C_w(r)=w^\top c(r)\) for \(w\in W\subseteq\mathbb{R}^m_+\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{r\in R}C_w(r)\) is locally constant away from pairwise tie hyperplanes.
review_flags: Confirm coverage of discrete parametric tie boundaries.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property and its finite parametric tie-hyperplane formulation fit the Cost Sensitivity Boundaries leaf and are mathematically plausible. The cited local file contains only the table of contents, however, and the locator is a general sensitivity-analysis section rather than inspectable support for constancy of a discrete argmin on cells of a hyperplane arrangement.

children.title: Priority-Ordered Repair Regime Family
children.top_down_role: Repairs governed by ordered requirement classes or stakeholder priorities.

children.title: Lexicographic Repair
children.top_down_role: Repairs selected through ordered comparison of multiple objectives.

knowledge_statements.title: Lexicographic Repair
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional lexicographic minimization of ordered repair-violation criteria.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R\) be a nonempty feasible repair set and let \(g(r)=(g_1(r),\ldots,g_K(r))\in\mathbb{R}^K\), with smaller components preferred and index \(1\) having highest priority. A repair \(r^*\in R\) is lexicographically optimal if no \(r\in R\) has an index \(k\) such that \(g_j(r)=g_j(r^*)\) for every \(j<k\) and \(g_k(r)<g_k(r^*)\). Equivalently, it is obtained by successively minimizing \(g_k\) over the minimizers retained at earlier levels.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lexicographic repair first minimizes the highest-priority criterion, then each lower-priority criterion without worsening any earlier optimum.
assumptions_latex: \(R\) is nonempty.
Each sequential minimum is attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r^*\in\operatorname*{lexargmin}_{r\in R}(g_1(r),\ldots,g_K(r))\).
review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports lexicographic repair.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition matches Lexicographic Repair, introduces the ordered criteria and attainment assumption, and keeps the finite-dimensional regime explicit. No source or inspectable locator is supplied for the definition or its sequential-minimization equivalence.

children.title: Priority-Class Repair
children.top_down_role: Repairs governed by ranked classes of requirements or stakeholders.

knowledge_statements.title: Priority-Class Repair
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Repair minimizing violations by ordered classes of equally ranked requirements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition the soft requirements into ordered classes \(P_1,\ldots,P_K\), where \(P_1\) has highest priority. For a feasible repair \(r\in R\), define the class loss \(G_k(r)=\sum_{i\in P_k}w_i v_i(r)\), with \(w_i>0\). A priority-class repair is any \(r^*\in R\) that lexicographically minimizes \((G_1(r),\ldots,G_K(r))\). Requirements within one class are aggregated together; no improvement in a lower-priority class may compensate for worsening an already minimized higher-priority class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Requirements are grouped into ordered priority classes; losses are aggregated within each class and minimized lexicographically across classes.
assumptions_latex: \(P_1,\ldots,P_K\) partition the soft requirements.
\(R\) is nonempty and the classwise minima are attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r^*\in\operatorname*{lexargmin}_{r\in R}(G_1(r),\ldots,G_K(r))\).

notation.meaning: aggregated loss of class k under repair r

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports priority-class repair.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits Priority-Class Repair, but its specific convention of weighted-sum aggregation within each class followed by lexicographic minimization is unsupported. A source with a section, definition, theorem, or page locator is required.

children.title: Priority-Level Tie Handling
children.top_down_role: Selection among repairs that are equivalent at higher priority levels.

knowledge_statements.title: Priority-Level Tie Handling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic secondary selection among repairs tied under primary priority criteria.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a finite nonempty feasible set \(R\), ordered primary losses \(G_1,\ldots,G_K\), and a deterministic tie score \(h:R\to\mathbb{R}\), initialize \(S_0=R\). For \(k=1,\ldots,K\), set \[S_k=\operatorname*{argmin}_{r\in S_{k-1}}G_k(r).\] After all priority levels, output any \(r^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{r\in S_K}h(r)\), using a fixed total order if this set is not a singleton. The tie rule cannot remove a repair before all primary levels have been optimized.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Successively retain minimizers at every priority level, then break any remaining tie by a secondary score and fixed deterministic order.
assumptions_latex: \(R\) is finite and nonempty.
\(h\) and the final total order are fixed independently of the search.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output \(r^*\) is primary-lexicographically optimal and deterministically selected.

notation.meaning: repairs surviving through priority level k

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports the tie-handling algorithm.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm is correctly placed in Priority-Level Tie Handling and clearly separates primary lexicographic filtering from secondary deterministic selection. No source with a specific locator supports the algorithm or the claimed preservation of primary optimality.

children.title: Priority Override Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Cases where lower-ranked gains cannot compensate for higher-ranked losses.

knowledge_statements.title: Priority Override Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact boundary for representing bounded lexicographic priorities by finite scalar weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let integer-valued losses satisfy \(0\le G_k(r)\le B_k\) on a nonempty repair set \(R\). The weighted objective \(\sum_{k=1}^K W_kG_k(r)\) respects the lexicographic priority order whenever \[W_k>\sum_{j=k+1}^K W_jB_j\quad\text{for every }k<K.\] If this inequality fails at level \(k\), a one-unit worsening of \(G_k\) can be offset by admissible lower-level improvements, so scalar minimization need not be lexicographically valid.
